items.quote: The Max plant is running at 36% capacity utilization as expected . We were expecting 50% capacity utilization is lower than their expectation to 36 % because of the muted demand in quarter 2, but this year end we are looking at a much better capacity utilization going forward.

items.statement: Domestic demand muted in H1 due to 15% export decline in H1 (40% from 2023 peak) and incessant rains; October demand slightly better than last year
items.quote: It has been weak domestic demand which got impacted largely by lower exports, which means that material was being dumped into India and also incessant rains across the country between July, August and September.

items.statement: Project sales mix shifted from 20% to 25% of total; project segment growing ~25% YoY driven by government and private projects
items.quote: last we were at 80% retail, this year, we would be at 75% retail. So, I don't have the growth if that 5% goes up in project, which is between government and private projects. So, government also, I think the only people spending in the Indian industry right now, the government, so that is going up and with the RERA coming in the better builders we have started supplying more products to, so the mi

items.statement: Key downside risk to guidance is EBITDA improvement may not materialize if gas prices spike; balance sheet strong with net debt-free standalone position
items.quote: So, the downside risk is, let us say , it is lower than expected hypothetically. We are a net debt free company. Our balance sheet is strong, our cash flows are strong. Raw material prices are completely under check, namely gas and also other raw material prices. So, the downside risk is that we won't be able to increase our EBITDA from 1%-1.5%. It would probably be at the same EBITDA level.

items.statement: Invested Rs. 3.7 crore in Solar SPV, expected to yield Rs. 1.5-2 crore annual benefit pending Haryana government approval
items.quote: We have made an investment of Rs. 3.7 crores in the Solar SPV, which should give us the benefit of Rs. 1.5-Rs. 2 crores. This is now pending government approval , Haryana government approval as you know, the election was around the corner.

items.statement: Consolidated debt at Rs. 315 crore; Rs. 200 crore term loans with Rs. 40 crore maturing this year; standalone net debt-free
items.quote: The total debt stood at Rs. 315 crores, 70% of that debt is in two names which is Suda Somany which is our house plant which expanded 15 months ago, 18 months ago and the Max plant which started 9 months ago. The total term loan is Rs. 200 crores out of which we have a maturity of Rs. 40 crores this year. So, the net would remain at Rs. 160 at the end of the year and the working capital is at 115,

items.statement: Gross margin declined 1.9% YoY to 33.3% due to capacity utilization dropping to 77% from 88% YoY
items.quote: The gross margin declined by 1.9% from 35.2% -33.3% basically on the back of capacity utilization. The capacity utilization was down on a console level by 4% from 81% in Q1 to 77%.

items.statement: Export volumes improving from August low of Rs. 1,280 crore/month to ~Rs. 1,350 crore; FY25 annualized exports estimated at Rs. 14,000-15,000 crore vs Rs. 20,000 crore last year
items.quote: August was 1,280. I believe this has improved to about 1350, which is what my information is from Morbi, but nothing beyond, which means that the export this year will be anywhere between Rs. 14,000-Rs. 15,000 crores annualized compared to Rs. 20,000 crores last year.

items.statement: Bathware sales grew 10% YoY in Q2 (sanitaryware +9%, bath fittings +12%), outperforming tiles growth of 2.6%
items.quote: The other highlights are that the gas price largely remained the same in Q2 and the bathware sales grew by 10%, which was better than the tiles growth of 2.6%.

items.statement: Brand spend maintained at 2% in H1; guided to remain at 2.5% for full year
items.quote: The brand spend remains at the same level of 2% and the guidance says that it will remain at 2.5%.

items.statement: Expect HAL JV production to start in Q4 FY25 and Prague JV gradual pickup in commercial operations
items.quote: For HAL, we are expected to start production in Q4 FY25 and on Prague, we expect a gradual pick in already commercial operations.

items.statement: Base business capex expected at INR3.5 crores for FY25 and INR5.5 crores for FY26
items.value: INR3.5 crores for FY25 and INR5.5 crores for FY26
items.quote: We expect a capex for the base business to be around INR3.5 crores for the FY25 and INR5.5 crores for FY26.

items.statement: HAL JV total capex for FY25 expected at INR35-40 crores
items.quote: For the HAL venture, we expect the total capex for FY25 to be around INR35 crores to INR40 crores.

items.statement: HAL JV peak revenue expected at INR105-110 crores with current product mix
items.quote: Regarding HAL, we expect a peak revenue of around INR105 crores to INR110 crores.

items.statement: HAL JV EBITDA margin expected around 19%
items.quote: So EBITDA margin, we are looking at around 19%.

items.statement: Prague JV EBITDA margin expected at 25-30%
items.quote: Around 25% to 30% is the margin that we are looking at.

items.statement: Base business growth outlook remains optimistic driven by geographic expansion, penetration and new launches
items.quote: On the base business, we continue to remain optimistic on the growth, outlook going ahead. This will be driven by increasing presence with geographies, increasing penetration in existing geographies and of course new product launches.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 product mix: injectables 50%, tablets 42.6%, nutraceuticals 7.4%
items.quote: I'm sorry. I would like to correct myself. Injectables stood at 50 and tablets at 42.6. The numbers were reversed.

items.statement: Raw material prices normalizing, no major increase anticipated in normal operating environment
items.quote: Overall raw material prices which had increased during lockdown period have been normalizing over the last few quarters. We have seen this trend continuing even in this quarter. We do not anticipate major increase in the raw material prices in the normal operating business environment.

items.statement: Shipping challenges persist with freight costs 2-3x regular rates due to Middle East conflict impacting Suez Canal and China routes
items.quote: So there are two ways basically we ship. One is through the central part, which goes via the Suez Canal. And that is impacted due to the Middle East conflict. And the other one is through China. So on both fronts, we are looking at increasing freight costs to the tune of sometimes 2x to 3x of our regular freight.

items.statement: Prague JV revenue estimated at EUR3.5-4 million annually next year, potential EUR8-10 million in couple of years
items.quote: Looking at what we have estimated and what we are discussing right now, around EUR3.5 million to EUR4 million we are looking at from a top-line perspective on an annual basis.

items.statement: HAL JV capex came under budget due to successful negotiations
items.quote: No, it has actually come under what we had estimated to be. We did have quite a few good round of negotiations and we have managed to save a bunch on it.

items.statement: Target 15-20 product launches annually, 6 done this year with 5 more in works
items.quote: Usually we target around 15-20 products that we launch every year. In this year, we have gone ahead with around 6 launches till now and another 5 are in the works as of now.

items.statement: New product launches initially have lower margins but improve as supply chain establishes and products offered to multiple buyers
items.quote: Initially the margins are less, but once we have a product developed and in our kitty, we can start offering this to multiple buyers across the world. So, that will definitely show as a bump in our margins as and when time progresses.

items.statement: Bombay plant capacity utilization 70-75%, Dehradun 45% with slight improvement
items.quote: So it remains the same as we did the last quarter, around 70%-75% in the Bombay plant and around 45% in Dehradun. We did see a little bit improvement in Dehradun on account of our own products increasing.

items.statement: HAL JV exhibit batches expected end of November or first week of December, on track for full revenue quarter in calendar Q1 2025
items.quote: Yes, towards the end or the first week of

items.statement: Near-term NIM expected to be broadly stable until rate cut cycle starts
items.quote: Our expectations of near-term NIM is that they will broadly be stable until the rates cut cycle starts.

items.statement: Deposits and credit growth expected to grow in tandem
items.quote: But to your point, we do expect deposits and credit growth to be growing in tandem and both are equally important.

items.statement: NIM was 4.27% in Q2-2025, down from 4.36% in Q1-2025
items.quote: Net interest margin was 4.27% in Q2-2025 compared to 4.36% in Q1-2025 and 4.53% in Q2-2024

items.statement: NIM movement includes seasonal impact of higher days in quarter, expected to reverse in Q4
items.quote: The movement of the NIMs in Q1 to Q2 includes an impact of a higher number of days in the quarter, which should seasonally reverse in Q4.

items.statement: Personal loan growth moderated to 17.3% YoY from 40% in Sep'23; credit card growth at 27.9% YoY
items.quote: In fact, if you look at what was the growth rate in June'24 was about 25% and in September'23 was about 40%.

items.statement: Unsecured loans (personal loans + credit cards) represent ~14% of total advances; well within internal thresholds
items.quote: So, yeah, the personal loan and credit card are essentially the unsecured portion, which represents about 14% of our total advances

items.statement: MFI exposure not material; comfortable with MFI and self-help group portfolios within defined thresholds
items.quote: Given the size of our loan portfolio, our total exposure to MFI is not really material. We have some exposure. So, to that extent, we will continue to monitor this and overall basis both for MFI and self-help groups, we are comfortable, and they are well within our defined threshold.

items.statement: BB and below corporate portfolio reduced to ₹3,386 crore (0.2% of advances) from ₹4,164 crore
items.quote: Loan and non-fund based outstanding to performing corporate borrowers rated BB and below reduced to ₹3,386 crore at September 30, 2024 from ₹4,164 crore at June 30, 2024

items.statement: Contingency provisions maintained at ₹13,100 crore (~1% of total loans)
items.quote: The Bank continues to hold contingency provisions of ₹13,100 crore at September 30, 2024

items.statement: Will continue investments in technology, people, distribution and brand building
items.quote: We will continue to make investments in technology, people, distribution and building our brand.

items.statement: CD ratio at ~85%; comfortable with current deposit mobilisation to fund credit growth
items.quote: We have a CD ratio of about 85% and we continue to look at it.

items.statement: Deposit rates could have peaked, but dependent on competitive environment and liquidity
items.quote: We do believe that the deposit rates could well have peaked, but it is largely a function of a competitive environment and liquidity.

items.statement: I-Sec merger approved by NCLTs; appeal filed with NCLAT; dilution <1% and not material
items.quote: On the first question on I -SEC, I think NCL T both Ahmedabad as well as Mumbai have given approval. So, there has been an appeal filed with NCLAT and we will see how this progresses, and we do hope that this get’s approved soon. On this one- the dilution- is just about less than 1% of the overall thing. So, from a dilution point of view, it is not going to be really material

items.statement: RBI draft guidelines on subsidiaries not expected to have material impact; reviewing regulations
items.quote: I don't think so this will have a material impact on us.

items.statement: No specific guidance given for loan growth, deposit growth, or NPA trends; focus on risk-calibrated growth
items.quote: As I did mention, you look at the NPA numbers. At this point of time, they are benign, which you can see from an overall angle.

items.statement: Expect margins to be broadly stable in H2 relative to H1 until a rate cut cycle starts.
items.quote: On the overall, I would say on the margins, we would expect it to be broadly stable in H2 relative to H1 is the way we would look at it until a rate cut cycle starts.

items.statement: No expectation of retail deposit rates going up too much from current levels.
items.quote: So, we would not expect retail deposit rates to go up too much from here.

items.statement: Marginal increase in cost of term deposits possible; overall cost of deposits rose 4 bps this quarter.
items.quote: I think this quarter the overall cost of deposits went up by 4 basis points, which is a little bit of increase in the cost of term deposits and a little bit of reduction in the average CASA ratio.

items.statement: Yield on advances lower due to 30/360 day count convention in longer quarter; impact ~7 bps on yield.
items.quote: See the total impact on yield is seven basis points or so. So, it will be something within that.

items.statement: Opex growth for H1 FY25 ~8.5% YoY; could be slightly higher in H2 due to festive and tech spends, broadly around this level give or take a couple of percentage points.
items.quote: For the first half this year, while the Q2 number is indeed year-on-year growth is very low at 6.6%, for the first half this year, it's about 8.5% or so. And it could be slightly higher in the se cond half, given all the festive season -related spends and other 16 technology spends, etc., that we have planned out. But broadly, around this level, give or take a couple of percentage points is where

items.statement: Business banking growth driven by credit underwriting investment, branch network enablement, digital adoption; market share not saturated, long runway for growth.
items.quote: I don't think that our market share is saturated at all. I think we have a long way to go in terms of entities, we can tap and cover and reach. And there are lots of very large potential customer base out there, both in terms of people and their existing banking plus this is also a segment which is growing.

items.statement: Unsecured loans (personal loans + credit cards) ~14% of loan book; delinquencies normalized upward over last 3-4 quarters but stabilized sequentially in current quarter; overall credit cost 40-50 bps.
items.quote: Overall, the unsecured piece, these two products put together are about 14% of the loan book. So, some increase in delinquency or credit costs in these segments has contributed to the path towards some kind of normalization of credit costs. But even after that, if you look at it, we are still in the 40-50 basis point range on an overall basis.

items.statement: Credit cost normalization gradual; could inch up over time but nothing alarming to suggest substantial increase beyond 50 bps.
items.quote: It's very difficult to say with that k ind of precision. We have consistently been saying that there will be a gradual normalization, but it is anyway much below historical level and we will see it as it comes. I don't think there is anything today which is alarming us in terms of causing us to believe that it will go up very substantially, but could it inch up over a period of time? It could

items.statement: Personal loan YoY growth down from 40% to 17%; will trend down further over next couple of quarters; credit cards continue robust growth.
items.quote: On the personal loan side, the growth on a year-on-year basis has actually come off pretty significantly. Last year in the September quarter, the year-on-year growth was 40% and this year it is down to 17% or so. But in this portfolio, over a period of time, the slippages have gone up. I would say that in the current quarter, we have not seen them go up further on a sequential basis, but we will c

items.statement: Branch count increased by 90 in H1 FY25 to 6,613; branch additions organic, not target-driven; expect materially higher additions in H2.
items.quote: Our branch count has increased by 90 in H1 of current year. We had 6,613 branches as of September 30, 2024.

items.statement: Retail deposit rates up ~15 bps in current calendar year (10 bps in Q4 FY24, 5 bps in Q1 FY25); feeds into 1-2 bps deposit cost increase over time.
items.quote: If you look at the retail deposit rates, I think they have gone up in the current calendar year by about 15 bps or so, I think about 10 bps in Q4 and 5 bps in earlier this quarter. And that will feed into the increase in the cost of deposits by 1 basis point, 2 basis point over a period of time.

items.statement: Treasury gains of Rs 6.8 bn in Q2 FY25 driven by trading operations and mark-to-market gains on fair value through P&L portfolio under new investment guidelines.
items.quote: On the treasury, actually, as you know from 1st of April, the revised investment guidelines came into force whereby a lot of the positions are mark-to-market now other than the HTM portfolio and most of, other than the SLR book and subsidiaries and things like that, most of the portfolio is held either in the AFS or fair value through P&L and the mark-to-market on the fair value through P&L portfo

items.statement: BB and below corporate portfolio declined to Rs 33.86 bn (0.3% of advances) from Rs 41.64 bn; provisions held Rs 6.26 bn vs Rs 8.41 bn prior quarter.
items.quote: The loan and non-fund based outs tanding to performing corporate borrowers rated BB and below was 33.86 billion Rupees at September 30, 2024 compared to 41.64 billion Rupees at June 30, 2024. This portfolio was about 0.3% of our advances at September 30

items.statement: Builder portfolio at Rs 542.16 bn (4.2% of loans); BB and below or NPL portion 1.9% vs 2.1% prior quarter.
items.quote: About 1.9% of the builder portfolio at September 30, 2024 was either rated BB and below internally or was classified as non-performing, compared to 2.1% at June 30, 2024.

items.statement: Write-offs of Rs 33.36 bn in quarter were fully provided loans (technical write-offs); recoveries from written-off accounts adjusted in provisions line.
items.quote: Yes, these were all 100% provided loans. And the way we do write-offs is that, on broadly retail portfolios, we have a days past due based write-off policy. Whereas on the corporate and SME portfolio, it's more on a case-by-case basis. And these were from relatively old, fully provided NPLs that we wrote off this quarter, technical write-off.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR11,155 crores as of 30th September 2024, comprising INR6,496 crores Consultancy and INR4,650 crores LSTK; including October orders it is approximately INR12,000 crores.
items.quote: The company has order book worth of INR11,155 crores comprising under Consultancy segment of INR6,496 crores and under LSTK segment of INR4,650 crores as on 30th September, 2024. However, if we consider the order inflow for the up to one month also, then our company is having order book of approximately INR12,000 crores.

items.statement: Management targets FY25 revenue of around INR3,500 crores and says they are on track.
items.quote: We are targeting around this figure.

items.statement: Corporate target is INR5,000 crores annual turnover within the next 2-3 years.
items.quote: And we have corporate target of INR 5,000 crores per month within next 2 , 3 years.

items.statement: Consultancy segment margin maintained at 20-25%; Turnkey (OBE) margin at 5-6%; expects margins to improve in H2 FY25 to match last year's 8.8% EBITDA margin.
items.quote: Yes, we are expecting that margin will be in the same line as last year, over a period of time for the financial year.

items.statement: Big ticket orders have lower margins than small orders but operational efficiency and new mega jobs will improve margins over time.
items.quote: In big ticket order, the margins are low in comparison to the small order where there is intense competition in comparison to the big orders.

items.statement: Major refinery/petchem projects (GAIL ethane cracker, BPCL/ONGC expansions) are in feasibility stage; tenders will come after board approvals.
items.quote: All these projects are still in the feasibility stage right now. They have indicated the capex investment. But right now, these are in the study phase. After the study phase is done, they will go for their investment approval from the board.

items.statement: International order booking from Abu Dhabi office reached INR160-180 crores this year, highest ever; Nigeria Phase 2 and Algeria projects in bidding.
items.quote: We have received this year highest order booking from that place. It's already reached INR160 crores or INR170 crores, INR180 crores. We have already reached from that office.

items.statement: Biofuel refinery OBE order worth ~INR300 crores secured; green hydrogen studies for NRL and NLC in initial phases.
items.quote: One of the recent achievements in this space was the biofuel refinery, biofuel project and the MRPS, which we have quoted on the OBE basis around INR 300 crores worth of that work is there.

items.statement: Guyana refinery and fertilizer projects delayed as government seeks private investors; offshore wind opportunities emerging but still early.
items.quote: They are looking for the investor to invest that project. So that is the hitch right now because it's far delayed. If the government would have invested, it would have been faster

items.statement: RFCL profit share INR22 crores in Q2, INR55 crores in H1; revenue for 46% share INR729 crores in H1; expects >INR100 crores full year.
items.quote: In this quarter, we have received our profit share is INR 22 crores and up to. Up to half year it's around INR54 crores, INR55 crores. So going forward also we expect that we'll be able to get the same share as a profit from the more than INR100 crores.

items.statement: Numaligarh expansion to 9 MMTPA ongoing; revenue and dividend to EIL only after completion, expected mid to end of next year.
items.period: mid to end of next year
items.quote: Expansion is going on but the revenue will be coming only after the expansion is completed. Right now, they are capitalizing whatever they are incurring. So over a period of time, they will be recognizing the revenue as well as the profitability.

items.statement: Revenue recognition for long gestation projects: ~10% in first 1.5 years, 30-35% in years 2-3, balance in year 4+; similar for Consultancy and Turnkey.
items.quote: During the initial phases, maybe for the first 1.5 year, we are able to recognize revenue only around 10%. After that, in the second year and third year, it will be around between 30% to 35%. And balance revenue is recognized over the next year, fourth year and so on.

items.statement: IOCL Paradip Petrochemical two consultancy packages: EIL is L1 and likely to get the job after internal approvals.
items.quote: We have bidded for that and we have become eligible parties for both of those packages. So we are the L1 and we are likely to get this job in short time after their internal approvals.

items.statement: BPC refinery all consultancy packages awarded and work is ongoing.
items.quote: No, all the packages have been awarded. Work is already on, on those packages.

items.statement: Expects to add INR1,000-2,000 crores more order inflow in H2 FY25, taking full year business intake to INR8,000-8,500 crores.
items.quote: So it's just a half year and we are very much hopeful that we'll be able to add more INR1,000 crores or INR2,000 crores further. So let's say around INR 8,000 crores, INR8,500 crores, it should easily reach.

items.statement: Target to surpass Rs 4,400 crore GDV from business development in FY25 and FY26
items.quote: Last year, we did Rs. 4,400 crores of GDV. For us to maintain our growth trajectory, we need to definitely surpass that. So, that's our target, and go beyond what we have done in the past year.

items.statement: H1 FY25 presales at Rs 1,415 crore, up 77-78% YoY
items.quote: We achieved a presale in H1, Rs. 1,415 crores versus last H1, which was Rs. 800 crores. So, this is roughly 77%, 78% growth comparing for the similar period last year.

items.statement: H2 FY25 launch pipeline includes Vista Phase-2 (Rs 1,200+ cr), Codename Navy Malad (Rs 1,000 cr), Crown Phase-2 Pune (Rs 800 cr), Pink Jaipur (Rs 200 cr), Zen 2 Bangalore (Rs 250-300 cr), Alembic Phase-1 (Rs 700-900 cr)
items.quote: Vista, will have more than Rs. 1,000 crores of inventory. I think we haven't decided whether we launch the retail part of it, but the residential part would be between Rs. 1,200-plus minus that will be launched. That's one. The Codename Navy in Malad is roughly Rs. 1,000 crores.

items.statement: Affordable segment slower than premium/mid-premium due to high interest rates; Palghar Phase-2 sold 75 units in quarter
items.quote: On the affordable side, value home side, which you are trying to cover on Kalyan and a little bit on Palghar side, yes. So, I think as we have seen the affordable segment has been slower than premium, mid-premium and let's say even luxury, which we don't participate.

items.statement: H1 FY25 operating cash flow Rs 548 crore, nearly 2x YoY; net debt Rs 477 crore, net debt-to-equity 0.26
items.quote: Cumulatively for H1 of FY '25, we have an operating cash flow of very close to Rs. 550 crores or Rs. 548 crores to be precise, almost 2x of what was recorded in H1 of FY '24.

items.statement: Equity platform sized at Rs 2,000-3,000 crore total (50:50 with partner) for land acquisition
items.quote: I think the equity platform, we are thinking it to be at least Rs. 1,000 crores to Rs. 1,500 crores by each partner. So, Rs. 2,000 to Rs. 3,000 crores is the size of the overall platform, 50% from us, 50% from the partner.

items.statement: Thane project launch delayed 12-18 months due to approval processes and elections
items.quote: My sense is it will take another 12 months to 18 months for us to bring that to the market.

items.statement: Industrial business PAT potential Rs 2,000 crore over next 10 years (company share after minority interest)
items.quote: If you look at overall potential that we have, we believe that this business over the next 10 years has a potential for roughly Rs. 2,000 crores of PAT. So, I just want to repeat Rs. 2,000 crores PAT potential that IC business has in the next 10 years.

items.statement: MMR pricing up 6% YoY, Bangalore pricing up close to 10% YoY
items.quote: Pricing continues to be at 6% growth compared to the same period last Financial Year and similar positive trends that we see in Pune as well as Bangalore. In fact, in Bangalore, what we see is absorption seems to be at one of the highest levels and they are outpacing the new launches. And as a result, the pricing is seeing much higher growth, close to 10% year-over-year.

items.statement: Conservative net debt-to-equity at 0.26, comfortable up to 0.5 threshold; platform equity from internal cash and partner
items.quote: We have in the past mentioned that we want to be conservative here, not go beyond a threshold of, say, 0.5 or slightly higher than that, but we want to be conservative. So, there is legr oom available in terms of fundraise, and that’s where we would look at funding aspect

items.statement: Focus on mid-premium and premium segments (Rs 2-7 crore ticket); will not pursue affordable or luxury segments
items.quote: In the past calls, I have clearly said we will not pursue affordable anymore. So, that segment is out. And while super luxury and all are very exciting, our focus is going to mid-premium and premium.

items.statement: Q2 residential presales Rs 397 crore vs Rs 455 crore YoY due to seasonality, Shradh and deferred launch; expect recovery in Q3/Q4
items.quote: In the quarter, Quarter 2 Financial Year tends to be slow because of multiple reasons, seasonality, there were deals that were lost due to Shradh and many other reasons. So, we will see, we have a Rs. 397 crores in Quarter 2 FY '25 versus Rs. 455 crores in the last Financial Year.

items.statement: Pending land payments: Kandivali Vista ~Rs 100 cr (TDR), Pune ~Rs 60-70 cr near term, Alembic and Good Host outright paid, Saibaba low capital at DA
items.quote: I think the total Kandivali related payment is done. There’s only TDR, like how much is that? Avinash Bapat: About Rs. 100-odd crores. Amit Sinha: Rs. 100 -odd crores is the commitment that we have to close all the Kandivali Vista related payments

items.statement: IC&IC H1 FY25 leasing revenue Rs 163 crore (Q2: Rs 87 crore) from 335 acres across Jaipur and Chennai
items.quote: IC&IC business has done really well for us. It has given us in the H1 as I mentioned, because of the domestic as well as global interest excitement that we are seeing for India. We had Rs. 163 crores of revenue coming from leasing our 335 acres of land across World City, Jaipur and Chennai.

items.statement: Santacruz redevelopment delayed due to alignment issues between two societies; Borivali cluster redevelopment expected faster
items.quote: This is a roughly Rs. 500 crore projects, not very large, but it is an amalgamation of 2 different societies NextEra and Westview. And they have 2 different management committee, 2 different lawyers, 2 different set of stakeholders. And that has taken a lot of time to get alignment with them.

items.statement: Expect more sales action in Q3 and Q4 FY25 to make up for Q2 slowdown
items.quote: To be honest, I feel that there is a lot more momentum in the market than what the Quarter 2 sales numbers reflect. And that's an area that you will see more action in the quarter 3, quarter 4.

items.statement: RIDF proportion to fall well below 5% of total assets by March 2027 from current 11%
items.quote: we've also indicated that by March '27, we expect this proportion to come well below 5% from the current 11%

items.statement: RIDF drag of ~70 bps on NIM will reduce as RIDF book shrinks
items.quote: That's almost 11% of our Total Assets. And currently, just on a pro-forma basis is pulling down the margins by almost 70 basis points.

items.statement: Margins expected to operate at similar levels with positive bias; no formal guidance given
items.quote: we do expect the margins to operate at similar to actually with a positive bias. But again, I'm not giving any real-time guidance on where the margins will end this financial year.

items.statement: Credit card growth to trend lower to 30-32% from current 45%
items.quote: We would be actually looking at a growth of around 30%, 32%. And then we'll be watchful of how the proceedings are actually in the market

items.statement: Unsecured retail slippages at 35-40% of total; stress expected to remain range-bound for next 2 quarters till March 2025
items.quote: we do believe that it will remain in this range for the next couple of quarters till, let's say, March '25

items.statement: Blended savings account cost at 5.7-5.8%
items.quote: on blended SA rate, I think we should be in the 5.7% - 5.8% range.

items.statement: NPA recovery run rate trending toward INR 5,000 crores for full year including technical write-offs
items.quote: I think we basically -- I think we will be in the range of about INR 5,000 crores.

items.statement: Net RIDF reduction of ~INR 5,000 crores expected in H2 FY25 against gross redemptions of INR 10,000-11,000 crores
items.quote: on a net basis, we don't expect INR 11,000 crores of reduction in the net RIDF book. That net reduction should be in the range of about INR 5,000 crores.

items.statement: Retail growth recalibrated: higher growth in affordable home loans, used car loans, credit cards, rural banking; slowdown in personal loans due to tightened underwriting
items.quote: you can see higher growth rates in products such as affordable home loans, u sed car loans, credit cards, et c. contributing products are also registering high growth rates such as Rural Banking and ISB which is our MFI

items.statement: Credit card gross slippages at INR 150-160 crores for Q2 FY25
items.quote: We have about INR 150 crores, INR 160 crores of growth slippage on the credit card book for this quarter.

items.statement: NII sequentially lower due to NPA recoveries and equity dividend accounting; adjusted NII sequentially higher
items.quote: On a sequential basis, we did have some NPA recoveries that were sitting as part of the NII. And also just from an accounting standpoint, there is a dividend that we do get from some of the Equity Investment that did get accounted in the NII as well.

items.statement: CET1 at 13.2%, down 10 bps due to higher risk weights on MFI and LTV adjustments
items.quote: CET-1 actually has moved from 13.3% to 13.2%. Like I mentioned, the reduction is because we have applied higher risk weightage on the MFI and those other products in which we've increased risk weight.

items.statement: PSL shortfall deposit stock targeted below 5% of total assets over next 3 years
items.quote: We remain on track to start seeing a reduction in the stock of aggregate deposits made in view of PSL shortfall starting second half of the FY '25 itself. This balance is targeted to reduce below 5% of our Total Assets over the next 3 years.

items.statement: Cost of deposits contained at 6.1% through service-oriented strategy, not rate competition
items.quote: our Cost of Deposit has not moved in line with some of the other banks. So the Cost of Deposit is limited at 6.1%, and that is largely because we have kept our costs under control.

items.statement: SME and Mid-Corporate advances grew 26% YoY each; Corporate advances grew 22% YoY and 5% QoQ
items.quote: SME and Mid-corporate Advances continue to grow at a faster pace of 26% each on Y-o-Y basis. Further, the momentum in Corporate Advances continued with 22% Y-o-Y and 5% quarter-on-quarter growth.

items.statement: Iron ore production guidance revised from 3 million tons to 2.35 million tons for FY25 due to delayed mining approval

items.quote: So for our 70 megawatt, we are confident about INR200 crores, INR225 crores should be enough -- for setting up 70 megawatts.

items.statement: Pellet realization Q2 average ~INR10,000; Q3 expected at same level ~INR10,000 average, spot prices currently INR10,000 normal grade and INR11,500 high grade

items.statement: Q2 lean season for steel; Q3 post-Diwali demand expected to recover, prices and margins to improve
items.quote: Usually, Q2 is always a lean season for steel. Q3, post Diwali, we hope the demand to come back. And the prices to probably, I would say, the margin will come back and the prices should further go up. That's the whole idea.

items.statement: Pellet grade mix 50% high-grade (66% Fe) and 50% commercial grade (63% Fe) to continue until new plant; new plant will shift mix to 2/3 high-grade, 1/3 normal grade
items.quote: See, currently 50:50 and once we start the new pellet plant, they'll also be producing high grade. So yes, you are very correct. Once we start the new pellet production, hybrid will be 2/3 and the normal grade will be 1/3.

items.statement: Mining expansion approval delayed, now expected by Q4 FY25; beneficiation plant commissioning 6 months post-approval; mines operational from Q1 FY26
items.quote: We now expect the approval for increase in iron ore mining capacity by Q4 FY '25. Once our environmental approval is received, the Crushing & Beneficiation plant is expected to be commissioned within a period of 6 months as we have already done some part of the work on these mines.

items.statement: If mining approval delayed beyond pellet plant commissioning, market iron ore procurement may rise from 20-25% to 30-35%
items.quote: See, if you don't make approval that will surely happen. But we are confident that we will get the approval before we start the pellet plant.

items.quote: has a healthy balance sheet with net cash of INR998 crores and strong Godawari Power and cash flow from operations of INR564 crores during H1

items.quote: In Q2, the volumes were lower because zinc bath was under maintenance. There was a major repair happened in the zinc bath. That is where the volume is lower. items.statement: Recovery guidance maintained at Rs.7,000-7,500 crore for FY25
items.quote: Of course, our guidance will continue to be around the Rs.7,000 crore to Rs.7,500 crore recovery. So we are moving on that direction.

items.quote: We raise the infra bond at a average price of 7.18 % plus there is no CRR , SLR obligation, no DICGC obligation. So if you reduce the cost of around 40bps because of negative carryover it comes to around a 6.8%.

items.quote: This year, our disbursement may go up to INR190,000 crores. Another INR1 lakh crore disbursement is expected in H2.

items.quote: On the Q3 we are targeting 8.25 lakh ton and Q4 we are targeting 9 lakh ton. And Q1 we are targeting 10 lakh ton and Q2 I'm targeting 11 lakh ton and Q2 up to 12 lakh ton.

items.quote: The margin shall expand to normalized level of Rs. 5,000 per ton over the next 2-3 quarters and this margin should remain sustainable throughout FY26 on a quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.quote: The gap between our product and sponge iron pipes is around 5% to 6% today and we can target additional market of 500,000 tons on a monthly basis.

items.quote: If we remove the inventory loss, it was pretty much profitable and going forward we don't expect further inventory losses. So, the EBITDA per ton in his particular category will recover to the previous level which we have been showing around Rs. 2,000 to Rs. 2,200 a ton.

items.statement: Steel price volatility risk: Rs. 7,500 per ton quarterly fall caused inventory losses; but further similar decline unlikely given new capacity and Chinese pressure
items.quote: It is just in Q2 when there was such a sharp decline, Rs. 2,500-Rs.2,000 month-on-month we saw the correction in the steel prices which we have not witnessed in the last 10 years.

items.statement: Employee expenses peaked at Rs. 800 million per quarter (ex-ESOP); per-ton cost to decline with volume growth
items.quote: So, 800 million per quarter is what like we have peaked and as a as the sales volume increases quarter-on-quarter, the per ton cost will keep on going down.

items.statement: Operating leverage potential of Rs. 500-600 per ton from fixed costs (employee, HO, branding) at 300,000 tons monthly volume
items.quote: from the employee cost , from the head office expenses and the advertisement expenses almost Rs. 500-Rs. 600 per ton operating leverage we can ge t if we keep on producing Rs. 300,000 ton of steel pipes e very month

items.statement: Full-year store opening guidance maintained at 55-60 stores for FY25
items.quote: For the full year, we still maintain our guidance of opening around 55 to 60 stores in the current year.

items.statement: Capex spend of INR 35 crores in Q2 FY25 mainly for new store openings and store refurbishments
items.quote: On the capex side, the spend was INR 35 crores majorly towards capex on new store openings and store refurbishments.

items.statement: Opened 16 new stores in Q2 FY25 and 21 new stores during the quarter (16 North, 5 South under Unlimited)
items.quote: We opened 16 new stores and delivered an LTL of 15% with V-Mart growing a healthy 16% and Unlimited at 11%.

items.quote: But otherwise, excluding LimeRoad commission income, the gross margin actually improved by 0.6% year-on-year for the offline business on the back of lower discounting and higher festive sales mix.

items.statement: Offline business EBITDA at 7.1% in Q2 FY25 (V-Mart 6.6%, Unlimited 9.4%); entity EBITDA 5.8% including INR 7 cr LimeRoad loss
items.quote: For the offline business, EBITDA for the quarter was at 7.1%, with Unlimited at 6.6%, sorry, the offline business EBITDA for the quarter total was 7.1% and Unlimited at 9.4%, while V-Mart at 6.6%.

items.quote: There's no price hike that we have taken. We've already addressed that question earlier. So there's purely a mix change which is happening, and also the merchandise change which we have deliberately done to cater to the higher fashion requirement of the customer, w hich is again a mix

items.statement: Consumer sentiment improving in rural and urban post-elections; repeat customer sales ~70%, NPS >60%, Google ratings >4.7
items.quote: We are definitely attracting lot of consumers, a lot of repeat consumers as well, which is also a good thing, which has been showed up, a repeat consumer or the sales from repeat consumers has almost touched 70%.

items.statement: Fashion shift toward oversized, layered looks with heavier fabrics driving 20-25% of products ~10% higher; younger demographic (<23) share increasing
items.quote: So what's happening is the product in the same category, even because the fashion is also going up, because there are the coarser weave fabrics, heavier fabrics, they are in fashion. So what's happening in the overall cost and the whole pricing also is slightly moving because of fashion element.

items.statement: Faster fashion cycles increase obsolescence risk; delayed winters in North India a watch-out; LimeRoad losses to continue for 1.5-2 years
items.quote: So there could be a continued obsolescence for the industry as well going forward because of the speed of fashion chain is becoming much, much faster. So that is one risk which can get activated later on.

items.statement: Target 12-13% square feet growth annually for FY26 onward; focus on ROI and property costs over chasing numbers
items.quote: So we'll continue to add 12% to 13% of square feet in area. That's our goal, and that is what we should continue to do. So you can calculate on the base, wherever we are. We continue to aspire for 12%, 13% growth, but we will always be also cognizant of the fact that we don't want to oversee it on just chasing a number.

items.statement: Aspire to reach pre-COVID EBITDA margin ~8% in 2-3 years; PAT margin impacted by Ind AS adjustments
items.quote: So all of those included whatever you are expecting the pre-COVID numbers, we should be somewhere there in the next 2, 3 years, and then we do believe and we have the confidence that we will be able to reach that number.

items.statement: LimeRoad losses reduced 63% YoY (6th straight quarter improvement); aim to minimize to negligible in 1.5-2 years but no breakeven guarantee
items.quote: LimeRoad continues its improvement journey with 63% reduction in losses year-on-year. This is the sixth straight quarter of continuous improvement in EBITDA losses for LimeRoad.

items.statement: Inventory up INR 241 cr QoQ and INR 70 cr YoY for festive stocking; days of inventory improved 21 days YoY; negative FCF YTD INR 62 cr
items.quote: The inventory increased by INR 241 crores quarter -on-quarter and INR70 crores year-on-year as we st ocked up for the festive season, which was slightly earlier compared to last year. items.quote: We closed 2 V -Marts stores in the current quarter. items.statement: Consolidated growth guided at 12-14%
items.quote: Somewhere between 13% to 14%. Sorry, 12% to 14%.

items.quote: But broadly, we can say that mattress commands anything ranging between 5% to 8% margin higher than the B2B sort of businesses.

items.statement: Target return on equity of 18%+ in three years

items.quote: I'm happy to share with you that the savings of the annual run rate of about INR100 crores per annum is already achieved and we have other initiatives in place which would further augment this annual run rate in Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Target 18,000 crore GWP for FY25 and confident of achieving it
items.quote: Having said that, I think we are very confident on achieving the annual target that we had set out to achieve 18,000 crore and we are also looking forward that the next four years will be good for the company.

items.quote: Out of these four parameters, we are well in control on three parameters. The claims ratio is definitely elevated beyond what we had anticipated due to the seasonal effects which Amitabh mentioned. I think we will be able to deliver the target that we have set for ourselves in terms of improving combined ratio by 100 basis points for this financial year, on the OPEX side of it.

items.statement: Price hikes taken on 10-12% of product GWP; plan to reprice 50-60% of product GWP by year-end
items.quote: As far as the pricing is concerned, we have already taken product repricing in almost 10-12% of our product contribution as we speak and we plan to take in a few other products. As we exit this year I think almost 50-60% of our product GWP will be repriced.

items.statement: Price hike of ~10% average on two products (senior citizen and Young Star); more products this month and next
items.quote: We have already taken a price revision in two products. One is a senior c itizen and one is the young star, but of course, we are also contemplating price increases in a couple of other products this month and the next

items.statement: H1 FY25 combined ratio 101.1% vs 98.4% YoY; claims ratio 70.2% vs 67.1%; expense ratio 30.8% vs 31.4%
items.quote: Our combined ratio for H1 FY'25 stood at 101.1% versus 98.4% in H1 FY'24. Our claims ratio for H1 FY'25 stood at 70.2% versus 67.1% in H1 FY'24. Our expense ratio for H1 FY'25 stood at 30.8% versus 31.4% in H1 FY'24.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 combined ratio 103% vs 99.2% YoY; claims ratio 72.8% vs 68.7%; expense ratio 30.2% vs 30.6%
items.quote: Our combined ratio for Q2 FY'25 stood at 103% versus 99.2% in Q2 FY'24. Our claims ratio stood at 72.8% in Q2 FY'25 versus 68.7% in Q2 FY'24. The expense ratio for Q2 FY'25 stood at 30.2% versus 30.6% in Q2 FY'24.

items.statement: Fresh GWP grew 31% YoY in H1 FY25; policy count growth 14%; agency fresh business up 23% in Q2
items.quote: The fresh growth is gaining strength. While the overall GWP has grown by 17%, outperforming the average industry growth, fresh growth for same period is 31% over last year's H1. The number of policy growth in fresh has been 14%, with overall number of policy growth of 9%.

items.statement: Renewal GWP grew 13% and policy count 7% in H1 FY25; price increases absorbed well, persistency improved
items.quote: Our renewal growth is also picking up. In H1 FY'25 overall renewal increased by 7% by volume, which is number of policies and by 13% by GWP compared to H1 FY'24. Price increases have been absorbed well and renewal persistency has also increased because of our wellness initiatives.

items.statement: Average sum insured of new policies up 6% to Rs 10.3 lakh; Rs 5 lakh+ policies now 82% of retail vs 77% in Q2 FY24
items.quote: The average sum insured of new policies have increased by 6% to Rs.10.3 lakhs per policy. Rs.5 lakhs and above sum insured policies now constitute 82% of the retail health portfolio versus 77% in Q2 FY'24.

items.statement: Launched modular 'Super Star Plan' with 5-year term and customizable coverage for life stages
items.quote: We have launched a modular product, 'Super Star Plan,' a personalized long-term health insurance solution aimed at providing greater value and flexibility for individuals and family.

items.statement: Investing heavily in digital business; app downloads 7.4M (up from 4.4M), MAU up 115%, organic traffic up 27% YoY
items.quote: Our app downloads have reached 7.4 million as on Q2 FY'25 from 4.4 million as on Q2 FY'24. Our monthly active users have increased by 115% compared to Q2 FY'24 and organic traffic to our website has grown by 27% in Q2 FY'25 versus Q2 FY'24.

items.statement: Long-term policy accounting change effective Oct 1: only 1-year GWP/NWP reported for multi-year policies; expense ratio impacted, no underwriting profit impact; long-term share ~4-5%
items.quote: In terms of long-term accounting, it will be effective 1st of October. What will happen is the long-term policy related premium will be reported on a yearly basis. So, if it's a three-year policy, only one year GWP will be reported, one year NWP will be reported.

items.statement: Anti-fraud digital initiatives yielded savings of 3% of claims outgo; cashless claims 74% of count (66% YoY) and 79% of amount in Q2
items.quote: Our anti-fraud digital initiatives which are proprietary to Star Health have yielded savings of 3% of the claims outgo as a direct result of these measures. The proportion of cashless claim with agreed network hospitals have gone up to 74% in Q2 FY'25 versus 66% in Q2 FY'24.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to sustain at H1 level of 32.2% plus/minus 1% depending on capacity additions
items.quote: we have guided Sumit is that over a longer period we will be able to sustain this margin whatever we have shown in H1. So because of a little bit of seasonality. In the quarter first, the margins will be always a little bit impacted because in the hospital there is an operating leverage which gets kicks in, but the business is generally the quarter 1 is the weakest quarter for us and the quarter s

items.statement: 380 beds expected to be added in next 24 months: Rajahmundry 100 beds by Mar 25, Bangalore Hennur 60 beds and Electronic City 90 beds, Coimbatore 130 beds by end FY26
items.quote: So Ritesh, so roughly 380 beds will come which will be Rajahmundry, 100 beds, which we are starting by March 25. And then two hospitals which is coming at Bangalore, which is Hennur and Electronic City roughly 150 beds there. And Coimbatore which will be the fag end of FY26, 130 beds. So total 380 beds are expected in next 24 month's time.

items.statement: Price corrections will continue in mature hospitals; case mix and price-led increases expected to flow through
items.quote: Some price corrections will continue. And obviously, if the demand is high, we will not be shying away from adding the beds. Which we have done in one of our hospital at Hydernagar in Hyderabad. We have added capacity, if we see the robust demand. So we will keep on adding the beds on the existing hospital if the demand is sustainable and we continue to grow.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 revenue target INR4,500 crores with 7% operating EBITDA margin
items.quote: Regarding our guidance for the full year, financial year FY '25, we continue to maintain same guidance as was communicated last quarter, INR4,500 crores of revenue target for the full year and 7% of overall average operating EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Next year revenue growth 35%-40% with EBITDA maintained at 7%
items.quote: For the coming years, as I shared in my Q1 earning call, we maintain EBITDA at 7% and top line growth of 35% to 40% or so.

items.statement: Order book INR4,800 crores with sectoral split: auto 24-26%, industrial 25-28%, consumer 35-38%, healthcare 6-8%
items.quote: Coming to order book visibility, we have a very strong open order book as of now, as o n September 2024 end and it is approximately INR4,800 crores, which comprises almost 24 % to 26% of auto sector, 25 % to 28% of industrial sector, about 35 % to 38% of consumer sector business about 6 to 8% is healthcare and balance is IT and railways

items.statement: FY25 capex INR175 crores spent, additional INR30-50 crores expected in H2
items.value: INR175 crores spent; INR30-50 crores additional
items.quote: Coming to capex, during the year , we had spent almost INR175-odd crores with a large part of being utilized in readiness of our new campus facility in Pune that was inaugura ted last week. With this, we expect large part of our capex is already behind us and again we may incur another INR30 crores to INR50 crores in the H2 of this year broadly

items.statement: INR130 crores unutilized IPO proceeds to be spent over 1-1.5 years on Pune and Hosur facilities
items.quote: We have approximately INR130 crores of IPO proceeds still unutilized, which we will be spending in the next 1 to 1.5 years broadly. And this will be going towards further upgrading the Pune facility and developing our facility in Hosur, which was planned at the time of IPO.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 180 bps YoY to 25% in Q2; operating EBITDA margin 8.8% in Q2, 6.4% in H1
items.quote: This quarter, we had a strong rebound in the margins also , led by expansion into the gross margin on the back of change in product & business mix, our continuous effort on th e operational efficiency and also stable overhead costs. Our gross margin for the quarter is about 25% with an expansion of almost 180 bps on year -on-year basis

items.statement: High-volume consumer business gross material margin remains below 10%, no accretion or depreciation seen
items.quote: We have not seen any accretion of margins in the high volume consumer business. And they continue to hover with the figures which we had said was less than 10%, 9%, 10% gross material margin.

items.statement: Net working capital reduced to 56 days, target to sustain below 60 days
items.quote: Coming to our working capital performance, we have been successfully able to bring it down to 56 days of net working capital, almost 70 days of net working capital investment from the start of the year. Again, we target to keep it below 60 days on a sustained basis going forward.

items.statement: Pune campus commissioned with 130,000 sq ft on 26 acres; total potential 1.2 million sq ft; INR100 crores invested so far
items.quote: This is a shift in our strategy. So far, we have always built the factories which were exactly mapping the requirement from the customers. This one is a shift where we are investing ahead of time. It's a large campus with approximately 26 acres of land and our first building with 130,000 square feet has been commissioned.

items.statement: Long-term vision: exports to constitute one-third of revenue, requiring 20-25% annual export growth
items.quote: Our long -term vision is that exports should constitute one -third of our revenues. Now, if the exports have to constitute one-third of our revenues, it is very, very imperative that we at least grow by 20% to 25%, or maybe in one year we have a bump-up.

items.statement: Capacity installed till September supports INR5,000+ crores revenue; with Pune expansion, capacity for INR6,000-6,500 crores
items.quote: Whatever we invest in Pune would be beyond that. So I think with Pune expansion being in place, we are well sort of the capacity we have created should enable us to cross the INR6,000 crores, INR6,500 crores mark.

items.statement: Advances growth target of 13% for FY25 and at least 15% for FY26
items.quote: We hope to close the year with a 13% growth in advances per se and I think we are looking to grow at least 15% in the coming year.

items.quote: Currently, I think our deposit is, the NRI deposit segment is contributing just about 4%. And this is something through opening of this, we expect to ramp it up to over 10%.

items.quote: I think it's inching towards I don't have a number exactly, but it's inching towards 80% more or less.

items.quote: Incremental Xanthine capacity will get operational by end of next fiscal. So we will have, the entire project should complete by Q3 of next financial year. And of course, it may take another six, eight months to completely or two, three quarters for us to completely operationalize.

items.quote: Yes, so highest would be CDMO/CMO, then API and then Xanthine. And overall gross margin this time was 65% gross margin. So they range between 35 to 65, across all the segments.

items.quote: Volume growth current quarter, we had little bit of muted deliveries for one customer, but barring that, overall the production did happen at rated capacity, and it will continue to happen as we have announced the future expansion, currently we are fully utilizing our capacity.

items.statement: Saffola edible oils took at least 15% price increase after import duty hike

items.statement: Digital-First brands ARR crossed ₹525 crore in Q2 FY25; expect exit ARR of ~₹600 crore in FY25
items.quote: Premier Personal Care maintained its strong momentum this quarter driven by the Digital-First portfolio, which crossed 525 crore in annual recurring revenue. In Q2, we expect to clock an exit ARR of circa 600 crores this year.

items.statement: Project SETU expanded to 10 states; three-year commitment to transform GT sales infrastructure
items.quote: SETU extended to more states taking the tally to 10 states. Implementing mindset and operating model changes at this scale can be time consuming, especially when significant consumption tailwinds are absent. However, we believe given the early trends, this three -

items.statement: H1 FY25 operating margin held at 21.6%; full-year margin target maintained with possible 40-50 bps compression
items.quote: If you look at H1, we have been able to hold the margins at 21.6%. The earlier guidance was that at a full year level, we will try and hold the margins. Now if you look at the cost pressures, it is definitely higher than what we had anticipated.

items.statement: Sequential uptick in domestic volume growth led by steadying trends across majority of portfolios; >80% of business gained or sustained market share on MAT basis
items.quote: The sequential uptick in domestic volume growth was led by steadying trends across a majority of our portfolios, which also reflected in the healthier trends in off-take growth, as more than 80% of the business either gained or sustained market share and penetration on a MAT basis.

items.statement: Pricing growth likely to pick up in H2 FY25 aided by sequential rise in commodity prices
items.quote: Pricing growth is likely to pick up in H2. In view of the sequential rise in commodity prices, which will further aid domestic revenue growth through the course of the year.

items.statement: Reiterated flattish revenue growth for FY25 and 16% EBIT margin exit rate by Q4 FY25
items.quote: We are still confident that we have a line of sight towards a flattish year. So the 2 things that we talked about, the flattish year and a 16% EBIT margin. We do have a line of sight towards that, and we're quite confident that we will get to flattish and 16%.

items.statement: Expect Q3 FY25 revenue to be stronger than Q2 FY25 and H2 FY25 better than H1 FY25
items.quote: So we expect Q3 to be stronger than Q2, and we also guided in the past that our H2 will be better than H1. I think we still hold on to the same view now.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 DET EBIT margin at 14.2%, up 75 bps QoQ driven by revenue growth and efficiency improvements
items.quote: The Q2 FY25 DET EBIT margin stood at 14.2%, up by 75 bps quarter -on-quarter. This quarter-on-quarter positive movement was driven by revenue growth and efficiency improvement which helped mitigate the wage hike s during the quarter for enabling margin

items.statement: Previous guidance of Q4 FY25 exit EBIT margin at 16% maintained
items.quote: And the previous guidance we have given, Bhavik, on the Q4 exit margin at 16% EBIT, we're still sticking with that. We still have a line of sight to that. That is what we believe we will exit Q4.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 order intake at $156.8 million, down 14.7% YoY, expected to significantly improve in H2 FY25
items.quote: As far as order intake is concerned, we have received over $156.8 million order intake, which is about minus 14.7% compared to the last year same quarter. We expect this to significantly improve during H2.

items.statement: Board approved close to $100 million outlay for semiconductor business, mostly for inorganic acquisitions
items.quote: The Board has approved the $100 million outlay close to $100 million outlay, I'd say. Some of that money is also being used for debt repayment. So that's one element. Now the second element is if you look at why the business has not grown according to its potential, it's because the real value in this business is not just in the design, but it's in the design and supply of chips.

items.statement: Raised INR 875 crore from partial divestment of 11.5 million shares in Cyient DLM, stake now 52.16%
items.quote: We sold about 11.5 million shares for a consideration of approximately INR875 crore. Our stake in Cyient DLM now stands at 52.16%.

items.statement: Long-term debt reduced from $47 million at end of Q1 FY25 to $9 million at end of Q2 FY25 using divestment proceeds
items.quote: Part of the proceeds from this transaction was utilized to retire long-term debt which helped optimize our debt position from $47 million at the end of Q1 FY25 to $9 million at the end of Q2.

items.statement: Semiconductor business launched as wholly owned subsidiary CSPL; acquired 27.3% stake in Azimuth AI for turnkey ASIC design
items.quote: In this quarter, we set up a wholly owned subsidiary, CSPL or Cyient Semiconductors Private Limited to drive dedicated focus on turnkey ASIC design and chip sales through a fabless model. Towards this initiative, we have reached an agreement to acquire 27.3% stake in Azimuth AI, a fabless custom ASIC company known for its expertise in energy and industrial applications.

items.statement: Acquired Abu Dhabi & Gulf Computer Establishment (ADGCE) to strengthen energy business presence in UAE/Middle East
items.quote: To accelerate this initiative, we have reached an agreement to acquire Abu Dhabi & Gulf Computer Establishment, (ADGCE), an Abu Dhabi-based technology consulting and digital services provider primarily catering to the energy sector.

items.statement: Connectivity grew 3.9% QoQ CC, Transportation 3.4% QoQ CC, NGA 9.7% QoQ CC; Sustainability declined 6.4% QoQ CC due to European holidays
items.quote: Connectivity business grew by 3.9% Q-o-Q in constant currency. Transportation business grew by 3.4%, while NGA grew by 9.7% Q-o-Q in constant currency. This robust growth in our key segments helped us mitigate the seasonal headwinds in Sustainability segment, which owing to vacation period in Europe, degrew by 6.4% in constant currency along expected lines for the quarter.

items.statement: All segments expected to grow sequentially in H2 FY25; Sustainability to be better in H2 vs H1
items.quote: say so for all the segments going forward for H2. Sulabh Govila: Sorry, can you repeat that? Prabhakar Atla: To just extrapolate it we can say the same thing that all segments will experience, or we expect all segments to grow in H2

items.statement: Auto vertical faces potential softness for next 3-4 quarters due to macro challenges, electrification slowdown, Chinese competition
items.quote: So there are multiple things at play and there could be p otential softness for the next three, four quarters a nd hopefully it comes back by next year

items.statement: Sustainability vertical has recurring Q2 seasonality due to European holidays (July-Sept) from Citec acquisition; Q3/Q4 historically stronger
items.quote: Any business which has a significant bias of countries like Finland, Norway, Germany and France and Sweden, I think you will find that most of them have a significant vacation period between July to September. items.statement: DET FCF at INR 177 crore in Q2 FY25 with 100% FCF to PAT conversion; Group PAT up 24.5% QoQ, 4.6% YoY
items.quote: The Q2 FY25 DET FCF stood at INR177, a positive movement Q-o-Q, translating into 100% FCF to PAT conversion for the quarter.

items.statement: Interim dividend of INR 12 per share declared for FY25
items.quote: We're also very pleased to inform you that we're announcing an interim dividend payout of INR12 for FY25.

items.statement: Full-year volume expected 255,000-260,000 tons, down ~10% from 292,000 tons last year
items.quote: It looks to be a 10% lower revenue volume either way, whichever way you slice it for this full year. So, closer to 260,000-ton , 255,000 ton to 60,000-ton mark for the full year.

items.statement: Sales decline of 20,000-30,000 tons this year, cyclical not structural, 5-10% overall sales decline
items.quote: On a very realistic note, we see a reduction in sales to the extent of may be 20, 000, 25,000, 30,000 tons this year, which as I elaborated is cyclical in nature, nothing structural.

items.statement: Capex planned at INR 250-260 crores for renewable power, rubber liner plant, and 36,000-ton grinding media expansion
items.quote: We have planned for capex of about INR 250 crores, which includes our equity investment in renewable power, the rubber liner plant that we are setting up, and the 36,000-ton expansion for grinding media.

items.statement: Mining customers destocking, offtake lower than expected, more than 3-4 large customers deferring orders
items.quote: More than three or four large customers are going through a destocking process. So, material that was supposed to be invoiced and shipped out is being deferred to later quarters.

items.statement: Supply chain and freight issues causing customer hesitation, some strategic uncertainty delaying new business
items.quote: We ar e seeing some pushback from customers on saying there is strategic uncertainty on account of the supply chain and want some more time before they go back to business with us

items.statement: Margins remain robust despite volume decline
items.quote: Having said that, margins continue to remain robust. Everything else, opportunity -wise, everything else remains to be robust.

items.statement: Mining sales outside India at 39,800 tons in Q2, up from 36,700 in Q1 but down from 52,000 in Q2 last year; non-mining flat
items.quote: Our mining sales outside of India is at 39,800, slightly up from 36,700 from the first quarter, but down from 52,000 tons in the second quarter of last year.

items.statement: US litigation ongoing, business continues as is with interim CVD applied; constrained in public comments
items.quote: The matter is subjudice. But our business there broadly continues as is. I mean, there are nuances there. But, I mean, we are using the disclosure that we made about the interim CBD that has been applied.

items.statement: Board seriously debating overseas plant expansion as supply chain mitigation; no decision yet
items.quote: This is something which we at the board level are very seriously debating over last couple of quarters. Even in today's board meeting, we had extensive discussions, some technical presentations.

items.statement: Net cash INR 3,212 crores after buyback; small debt INR 120 crores
items.quote: Our net cash is at INR 3,212 crores, which is after the buyback pay-out that has been done. There is a small debt of about INR 120 crores, and the net cash figure is after that.

items.statement: Other expenses higher due to legal and trade defence costs for US litigation milestones in last two quarters
items.quote: Other expenses include professional and legal expenses and a lot of our legal trade defence costs in this two quarters, because a lot of work for the US has happened in those milestones in this quarter.

items.statement: South America remains market of interest; Brazil anti-dumping duty terminated, CVD portion still active
items.quote: Brazil anti-dumping, there's only the CVD portion, as they call it, there's one portion that's still active. The dumping has been, the duty has been terminated in Brazil.

items.statement: No guidance for next year until three-quarter results provide clarity on new initiatives
items.quote: On a conservative note, we don't want to give any guidance about next year till maybe we reach the three-quarter, results, and we have a little clarity on the new initiatives that we are working.

items.statement: Management expects Q3 and Q4 margins to be much better than H1 due to inventory provision reversals and KSA recovery
items.quote: Overall, we think it will be definitely much better than H1.

items.statement: Inventory provisions of 12 bps in Q2 FY25 impacted gross margin; expected to reverse in Q3 and Q4
items.quote: That delta had an impact in terms of gross margin, which we think is more within transitionary short term, and we should get that back in Q3, Q4 time.

items.statement: Gross margin pressure from mix shift to mobility, large deals, and KSA inventory provisions; PAT margin maintained at 1.34% ex-Arena
items.quote: Our profit after tax grew 10% quarter -on-quarter and 2% year -on-year with a PAT of 1.34%.

items.statement: India and UAE grew 25% and 24% YoY respectively; West Africa showing double-digit growth recovery
items.quote: Other large markets, India and UAE, which constituted almost 60 -plus percent of our business, had stellar growth with growth rates of 25% year-on-year from India and 24% year-on-year from UAE.

items.statement: KSA enterprise demand outlook remains strong; expect recovery over next few quarters after government IT reprioritization
items.quote: The enterprise demand outlook remains strong, Aejas. And even on KSA, we expect that to come back.

items.statement: Cloud business grew 54% YoY driven by hyperscaler subscription software; mobility grew 26% YoY with NPI momentum
items.quote: cloud business unit being our stellar performer with a 54% top line growth year-on-year, driven by the continued success in the hyperscaler business in the subscription software in our portfolio.

items.statement: Investing in cloud platform to create ecosystem with partners and ISVs; targeting SaaS and subscription business
items.quote: Second is, it requires investment on a cloud platform, which requires to create an ecosystem with our partners and ISVs. So we're going to work on all of those.

items.statement: Turkey market declined 18-20% in PC business; high inflation and interest rates persist though inflation below 15%
items.quote: So there is a clear decline of around 18% to 20% on the PC business from a market opportunity and a market size perspective.

items.statement: Working capital improved to 25 days in Q2 FY25; guided steady-state range of 35-40 days
items.quote: The business team and operations did an excellent job of working capital, and we achieved one of the best-in-class working capital of 25 days.

items.statement: Interest cost dropped 50% YoY to INR88 crores; ex-Arena interest cost fell 59% to INR30 crores
items.quote: So the overall interest cost -- and the second question is just the overall interest cost, which is interest in the balance sheet plus factoring cost for the quarter is INR88 crores, vis-a-vis INR174 crores Q2 of last year, a drop of 50%.

items.statement: ProConnect revenue at ~INR250 crores/quarter with 7% YoY growth and 4x profit growth; operating profit ~10%
items.quote: We are now tracking close to INR250 crores revenue a quarter. So I mean a lot of things are going well there.

items.statement: Paynet divestment awaiting Competition Commission and Central Bank approvals in Turkey; expected closure by end of year
items.quote: Applications are made and there are follow-ups that are getting done. It was expected it will take 2, 3 qua rters. So we are doing the needful and we are waiting for the approvals to come.

items.statement: Optimistic on Q3 outlook driven by festive season, NPI momentum, deal backlog in India and EMEA, and CSG momentum
items.quote: With the festive season in Q3 in India, the NPI momentum across the world, backlog on deals both in India and EMEA, the momentum we have built on CSG, we are optimistic on the Q3 outlook.

items.statement: Cloud business resell margins similar to base business; consumption/workload and professional services offer higher margins
items.quote: But then when I talk about consumption and workloads, we do work with hyperscalers and are able to appropriate more margins on that. And when it comes to professional services, we can get significantly more margin.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions cited as key risk to positive demand trends across geographies
items.quote: Most of the geographies we are in are seeing positive trends outside of any potential geopolitical risk that may come up.

items.statement: Revenue guidance of Rs. 1,000 crore annual revenue expected within next six to seven quarters
items.quote: Regarding our guidance, we have been giving our guidance in Rs. 1,000 crore for the year '26 and we feel in the next six to seven quarters, we should be able to reach our top line guidance of Rs. 1,000 crore.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 15% still on track but will take time due to upfront costs from new customer onboarding
items.quote: Yes, that is still on track, but it is going to take some time because right now our focus, we would want to make sure that we are getting the customers, we onboard them.

items.statement: Booked multiple orders aggregating Rs. 675 crore in Q2 FY25 including largest ever Pune Safe City order of Rs. 430 crore
items.quote: We are pleased to share that we have booked multip le orders this quarter aggregating Rs. 675 crore representing strong accretion to our order backlog.

items.statement: Pune Safe City order revenue to start in Q3 FY25 with majority in Q4 FY25 and Q1 FY26
items.quote: Some of it will start from this quarter, that is the third quarter. Majority of that would come in the fourth and the first quarter next year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin of 11%+ in Q2 FY25 despite non-recurring expenses of Rs. 3 crore for ECL provision and 40th anniversary celebration
items.quote: Despite this increase in other expenses, we have reported an EBITDA margin of 11 plus percentage in this quarter.

items.statement: Margin dip attributed to non-recurring expenses; margin would have been better without ECL provision and anniversary costs
items.quote: So, because of that margin was a littl e thin, but still we have achieved an EBITDA margin similar in line with our earlier quarter.

items.statement: Strong traction in cyber security with continuing demand and growing customer logos; recognized by Equity Masters as one of three key Indian cyber security companies
items.quote: We see a lot of exciting opportunities. As you know, this quarter also we closed a couple of deals on Cyber Security, which we see there is a continuing demand, and we are also growing in our custom er's logos and we see that sector growing more and more over time.

items.statement: Data centre business seeing strong traction with government budget of Rs. 30,000 crore for data centres in India; responding to MIT RFP for AI and cloud
items.quote: Even the government of India, if you have seen, has also given out a budget of about Rs. 30,000 crore for making data centres in India to make sure that the data of Indians are kept inside.

items.statement: Opened Dubai office and hired 65 people for Middle East expansion; first BFSI customer in Abu Dhabi with service delivery started
items.quote: What we have done is opened up our office in Middle Ea st that is in Dubai for expanding our business there. And we are glad to share that we've got our first customer for which service delivery has already started and we have hired about 65 people there

items.statement: Hiring strategy includes proactive hiring for anticipatory projects which incurs initial expense but becomes recoverable quickly upon winning projects
items.quote: The other is to proactively hire base d on anticipatory projects where we are reasonably confident of winnin g them. And so there you incur an initial expense, but that becomes recoverable very quickly as soon as we win those projects

items.statement: Net cash balance increased to Rs. 115 crore as of September 30, 2024 from Rs. 99 crore a year ago; added Bank of Baroda as third banking partner
items.quote: Hence on a net basis our net cash balance has risen meaningfully to Rs. 115 crore.

items.statement: Debtor days improved to 72 days as of September 30, 2024 from 87 days a year ago; continue efforts to improve further
items.quote: Our DSOs continue to improve further, and we are at 72 days as of September 30, 2024 compared to 87 days at the same time last year.

items.statement: Return on capital employed reached double-digit 10%; would increase 3-4% if real estate properties excluded from net worth
items.quote: return on capital employed we have reached around two digit number, 10% we have achieved, but as earlier also we have pointed out our denominator, the networth figure is almost Rs. 600 crore.

items.statement: Expanding into application support and AI roadmap for better margins; engaging more in app support projects
items.quote: We are also engaging more into app support. We have an AI roadmap. So, we see that there are better margins also to be looked into areas where we can flourish more.

items.statement: Five or six large government tenders up for bidding; evaluating which to pursue; multiple advanced stage negotiations with private enterprise customers
items.quote: pipeline front, Q2 & H1 FY2025 Earnings Call Transcript there are about five or six large tenders that are up for bidding. We are evaluating them. We will soon be fi guring out which are the ones that you want to go after and bid for it

items.statement: H1 margins are at the bottom; second half margins should be better and next year better than current year
items.quote: You should assume that the H1 margins are at the bottom and the second half should be better than the first half and the next year should be better than the current year.

items.statement: Private Wealth RM count to reach 700 by end of FY25 from 585 currently
items.quote: We are looking to go from 585 RM to 700 RM by the end of the year and this addition will happen across HNI as well as ultra HNI.

items.statement: Housing Finance RM count to grow strongly for rest of FY25 and FY26 driving disbursement and AUM growth
items.quote: we will continue to invest in our RM capacity for the coming 4 quarters at least and for FY25 & FY26 this should result in a very good momentum in terms of disbursement volume growth and which will then result into a good growth in our AUM.

items.statement: AMC to launch one new product per month to fill gaps in mutual fund suite and create first-of-kind passive products
items.quote: As we go forward, one should expect to see a product launch on the passive side or on the active side every month i.e., one in a month.

items.statement: Private Equity Fund 2 series exit expected in FY26, Real Estate Fund series 2 exit in FY28, then nearly annual exits
items.quote: You should look at the private equity fund 2 series exit in FY26. You should expect the real estate fund series 2 exit in FY28. And from there on, almost on an annual basis, you will have one exit.

items.statement: Investing ~15% of wealth management top line in RM additions with vintage under 3 years
items.quote: We have an investment of nearly 15% of the wealth management top line in these RMs in terms of a drag, which we expect to recoup over the course of the next couple of years.

items.quote: Our Investment Banking business has successfully completed 22 deals with an issue si ze of Rs. 25,000+ cr during H1FY25. The second half pipeline is a multiple of the first half, and we see very strong outlook of this business for the second half

items.quote: the overall yield is lower because we are increasing the retail housing book mix. items.statement: AMC October gross sales and net flows meaningfully higher than September quarter; strong growth across all channels
items.quote: Importantly, October has been a record month again in all the channels and in terms of the overall sales.

items.statement: Alternates monthly gross sales near Rs 1,000 cr in October alone
items.quote: In alternates, we should be at nearly Rs. 1,000 cr monthly gross sales for the month of October alone.
