items.statement: Order book stood at approximately INR21.5 crores as of 30th September with L1 pipeline of more than INR300 crores
items.quote: Our order book, as of 30th September, stood at approximately INR21.5 crores, with an L1 opportunity pipeline of now more idea than INR300 crores

items.statement: L1 pipeline has increased slightly from Q1 and includes sizable international opportunities
items.quote: It has actually gone up a little bit, but we are just currently retaining the position in terms of numbers.

items.statement: Government capex spending slowed in H1 due to general election; resumption and momentum expected in H2
items.quote: However, we are tracking these opportunities closely, and as we approach the second half of this financial year, we anticipate resumption and momentum in government spending that was slowed in the first half due to events like the general election.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margins of 25-30% as pipeline converts, similar to last year's performance
items.quote: Hardik, the EBITDA that we were tracking was about 25% to 30%.

items.statement: No firm FY25 revenue guidance; awaiting order closures to communicate positioning
items.quote: Hardik, we are awaiting the closures on the order that we are tracking. And depending on when these finally get executed in the timeline that we are left with to overall execute, we will come back to you and the overall market as well to communicate our positioning for this year.

items.statement: Lower gross margin in Q2 due to product mix and BOQ of contract signed a year ago; believed temporary
items.quote: The reason for lower gross profit is because of the product mix and BOQ of the product delivered during this period, for contract that was signed about a year back. However, we believe this is temporary in nature

items.statement: Drone-as-a-Service revenue expected to exceed INR1 crore in FY25; meaningful growth expected next year as franchise model matures
items.quote: We do expect to do more than INR1 crore in revenue this year because these are early days for our POCs as well. But next year onwards, we should start seeing good improvement in revenue from products.

items.statement: H1 FY25 gross profit margin 30.7%; Q2 gross profit margin 24.6%; EBITDA negative due to scale and lower quarterly revenue
items.quote: For H1 FY25, gross profit stood at INR37.8 crores, with a gross profit margin of 30.7%. EBITDA for the quarter was minus INR10 crores and INR minus 1.5 crores for H1 FY25.

items.statement: Increased government scrutiny on technology origin and national security creates barrier to entry, benefiting indigenous developers
items.quote: They have to look at the country of origin of the technology. They have to make sure that the national security interest is also kept into mind when building technology. And therefore, we will see that it will mature the industry quite a bit and it will make it a much safer industry from a national security point of view

items.statement: Proactive steps taken for manufacturing capacity and critical supply chain items to fulfill large orders within timelines
items.quote: Further, we have taken certain proactive steps for building capacity and capability for manufacturing and also have secured several critical items from a supply chain point of view so that we can fulfil even large opportunity within anticipated timelines.

items.statement: Global demand uptick due to geopolitical conflicts; adapting products for international deployment methods and pricing
items.quote: So, in fact, slowdown -- it's the exact opposite of slowdown, Sahil, in terms of the market and the opportunity there because the global wars and several of these geographies are participating in those wars. So overall, there is an uptick and there is a huge uptick in preparing for any eventual conflict that is being seen globally.

items.statement: Middle-mile logistics drone targets 100+ kg payload over 100+ km at high altitude; tactical UAV targets 10 kg payload over 50 km
items.quote: The middle mile logistics drone platform is a platform that's going to be about, 10 times heavier than the tactical platform, where we are looking to load up to about 100 plus kilos to 100 plus kilometers.

items.quote: We expect to have business and volumes coming into ATL from Q1 calendar year, which is January to March time of 2025. Mundra, the land that we have acquired, this is outside the Adani SEZ. We expect to have the first phase of construction to be completed in the next nine months to 12 months and business to start coming in from Q3 of FY26.

items.statement: H2 FY25 volume growth expected similar to H1 (~4% YoY) with market share maintained; EBITDA per TEU expected to remain around INR 2,000-2,100 in near term.
items.quote: We expect similar kind of growth going into H2. And if you were to look at how the market has been between Q1 and Q2, Q1, there was significant growth. Q2, there's been a little bit of a tapering down, which I mentioned in my opening remarks saying in September, the volume seemed to have tapered down a little.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA per TEU crossed INR 2,000; gross margin exceeded 33% and EBITDA margin exceeded 17% driven by better yields and operating efficiencies.
items.quote: In this quarter, we were able to cross the INR 2000 mark per TEU EBITDA. The gross margin exceeded 33% and the EBITDA percentage was in excess of 17%.

items.statement: Global maritime trade projected to grow 2% in 2024 and 2.4% avg 2025-29; India EXIM trade grew with exports $213B and imports $350B in H1 FY25.

items.quote: The cost of labor in India is not less than $230 to $240 per person as of now. As the Bangladesh cost is still about 11,000-12,000 Taka which is equivalent to about $120.

items.statement: Green energy share 4-5% currently, targeting 25% in 2 years, possibly 40%; each project expected 15-20% ROCE
items.quote: In the next 2 years, we are trying to reach from 4%-5% to at least 25% of the green energy in next 2 years. And maybe there could be a possibility that we will be crossing this 25% to even 40% also.

items.statement: Next 1.5-2 months critical for cotton procurement strategy as new season arrivals pick up and CCI policy unfolds
items.quote: next 1.5-2 months is more critical from that perspective. It is one of the major component s of our cost and it definitely determines the profitability of the business for the next couple of months

items.statement: Recycling trends in West may reduce virgin fiber demand long-term; Europe law from 2025 bans garment landfilling
items.quote: Europe has passed a law starting next year 25, which will be landfilling through the garmenting is not possible or will not be allowed. So, it has to be recycled, or it has to be resold.

items.statement: Consolidated profit lower than standalone due to dividend from associates/subsidiaries knocked off in consolidation
items.quote: We got dividend from some of our associated companies and subsidiaries which got knocked off while calculating the consolidated figures.

items.statement: Targets 10-11% volume CAGR in carbon black over next 5 years
items.quote: We are very confident that growing at 10%-11% volume CAGR in the next 5 years is not going to be much of a challenge for us, we just need to have capacities.

items.statement: Aims to reach 1 million tonnes carbon black capacity by FY27-28
items.quote: We aim to reach 1 million tonnes capacity in carbon black by FY '27 -'28, possibly we will surpass this target as well.

items.statement: Expects specialty carbon black project of 20,000 MTPA in Mundra and 30,000 MTPA brownfield expansion in Tamil Nadu to commission in Q3 FY25
items.quote: PCBL expects to commission the specialty project o f 20,000 MTPA in Mundra and 30,000 MTPA brownfield expansion of carbon black facility in PCBL, Tamil Nadu i n Q3 FY '25

items.statement: Second phase of Tamil Nadu expansion of 60,000 MTPA to take total capacity to 880,000 MTPA with 134 MW green power in FY26
items.quote: The second phase of PCBL Tamil Nadu expansion of 60,000 MTPA would take the total installed capacity to 8,80,000 MTPA, with a Green Power capacity of 134 MW in FY '26.

items.statement: Aquapharm expansion of 38,000 MTPA likely to commission by March 2025
items.quote: Aquapharm Chemicals is implementing an expansion project of 38,000 MTPA, which is likely to be commissioned by March 2025.

items.statement: Targets debt to EBITDA below 2x, will use surplus cash beyond capex for debt reduction
items.quote: We are not looking at any absolute debt level, but we are not comfortable with our debt to EBITDA beyond 2. So, we will try and bring it down to that.

items.statement: Expects Aquapharm top line growth of 17-18% from FY26, EBITDA margin 20% next year improving to 25% by FY29
items.quote: Growth in terms of top line, we believe that we can grow at around 17-18% from FY '26 onwards. And our margins, we believe that from next year itself we will have around 20% EBITDA margin, which will gradually improve towards 25% by FY '29.

items.statement: Nanovace commercial plant of 2,000 tonnes to commission in FY27, targets Rs 2,000 crore revenue by FY29 at $100/kg realization
items.quote: Once this plant comes up, which should be in FY '27, it will not take us more than couple of years' time to utilize full capacity. So, by FY '29 we should be doing at least Rs. 2,000 crores kind of revenue from this facility.

items.statement: Plans Rs 600-700 crore capex over next 3-5 years for Aquapharm India and USA
items.quote: We expect to invest roughly around anywhere between Rs. 600-700 crore over the period of next three to five years, between Aquapharm India and USA.

items.statement: Carbon black capacity expansion of 430,000 tonnes by 2029 involving capex of Rs 2,500-2,600 crore
items.quote: If we grow at about 10%-11% every year, by 2029 we will require another 430,000 tonnes of capacity, which will involve a CAPEX of about Rs. 2,500-. 2,600 crores.

items.statement: Current carbon black capacity at 770,000 MTPA, specialty at 10,000 MTPA addition annually
items.quote: The carbon black capacity of the Company stood at 770,000 MTPA. PCBL expects to commission the specialty project o f 20,000 MTPA in Mundra and 30,000 MTPA brownfield expansion of carbon black facility in PCBL, Tamil Nadu i n Q3 FY '25

items.statement: Aquapharm capacity utilization at 75% in Q2, targets 82-83% by Q4, full utilization in 4-5 quarters
items.quote: Currently are at about 75% on overall basis, India and USA all combined. We believe that by fourth quarter we should reach around 82-83%.

items.statement: Performance chemicals carry 25% better margins than tyre grade
items.quote: Yes, that's a more fragmented market and carries better margins, about 25% more compared to tyre, which is bulk business for us.

items.statement: Global carbon black market ~15 million tonnes, long-term growth ~3.5%, China consolidating, Russia sanctioned, creating opportunity for Indian manufacturers
items.quote: It's a fairly large market. It's around 15 million tonnes market already. And if you look at the global growth rate, long term growth rate had been around 3.5%, which creates a large opportunity and scope for further increase in volume.

items.statement: Not worried about Chinese competition in Aquapharm, globally #1-2 in phosphonate, confident in capabilities
items.quote: So, fine, let them come up, what is the worry? We are equally efficient and capable. So, we are not too worried about Chinese or any other player. So, Aquapharm globally in phosphonate they are number one, number two.

items.statement: Awaiting Consent to Operate for 30,000 MTPA Tamil Nadu expansion, applied already, expect commissioning soon
items.quote: The project work is almost complete. We are awaiting Consent to Operate. We have already applied for it. And we expect commissioning soon.

items.statement: European market share increased from 3.5-4% in FY22 to ~21% currently, constrained by capacity
items.quote: In FY '22 it was only about 3.5-4%, currently we are doing close to 21% in those markets and the scope is much, much better, we are constrained by capacity.

items.statement: Crude oil down 10% reduces working capital requirement by ~8%, capital efficiency improves with lower crude
items.quote: Crude falls by 10%, and our working capital requirement goes down by around 8%. So, that's a very simple calculation.

items.statement: Generated Rs 700-800 crore cash flow in H1, targets Rs 9,500-10,000 crore over 5 years, not uniform Rs 2,000 crore annually
items.quote: We did speak about Rs. 9,500 - 10,000 crores of cash generation. But cash generation would increase every year with higher capacity and higher sales volume. So, it will not be uniform across every year.

items.statement: Formed Nanovace Technologies JV with Kindia (51:49) for nanosilicon anode additives, PCBL to infuse $44 million over 2 years
items.quote: PCBL has executed a JV agreement with Kindia Private Limited to form Nanovace Technologies Limited for developing nanosilicon products to be used in anodes of lithium-ion batteries. PCBL holds 51% and Ki ndia 49% in Nanovace Technologies. PCBL would infuse $44 million in Nanovace in multiple stages over the next two years

items.statement: Power generation up 25% YoY to 209 MU, external sales 126 MU at Rs 3.56/kWh average realization
items.quote: Power generation increased by 25% from 167 MU in Q2 FY '24 to 209 MU during the quarter, with an external sales volume of 126 MU as against 103 MU in Q2 FY '24. PCBL's average realizations stood at Rs 3.56 Kwh.

items.statement: US oil & gas chemical demand in rough patch, impacting Aquapharm utilization and margins, expanding to Europe to derisk
items.quote: The US market from the point of view of oil and gas sectors is going through a very, very rough patch in recent times, and the demand has come down substantially. That has put a lot of pressure on our capacity utilization as well as on the margin.

items.statement: Jindal Supreme deployed with ONGC on 15 Oct 2024 at $88,859/day, ahead of Nov 2024 timeline
items.quote: This rig commenced operations on 15 October 2024, which is ahead of the deployment timeline given earlier of November 2024.

items.statement: Jindal Pioneer acquisition in final stage, awaiting statutory approval, expected shortly
items.quote: Further, we are in the final stage of acquisition of rig Jindal Pioneer and are still awaiting approval from statutory authorities. There has been some communication between them and us and we expect that the matter will be approved shortly.

items.statement: Jindal Supreme day rate increased from $40,700 to $88,859; incremental rate flows largely to EBITDA as rig is company-owned
items.quote: Originally, the rig was deployed at $40,700 in the previous contract, which concluded in March 2024. From 15th October 2024, it has been deployed on the new contract at $88,859.

items.statement: Jindal Supreme refurbishment cost >INR130 cr due to MODU standard change, amortized over 3-year contract
items.quote: For Jindal Supreme, the total refurbishment expenditure is more than INR130 crores. That is because there was a change in the MODU standard as per the safety requirement.

items.statement: Debt INR173 cr (secured by Jindal Supreme) to reduce to INR132 cr by Mar 2025, then INR66 cr/year for next 2 years
items.quote: Considering the cash flows that we have right now debt position is at INR 173 crores. This will reduce to INR132 crores as on 31st March 2025 and thereafter the repayment schedule is INR 66 crores each in the next two financial years.

items.statement: Net cash improved from INR51 cr (Mar 2024) to INR69 cr (Sep 2024); Discovery I loan fully repaid from internal accruals
items.quote: have improved in September 2024 as compared to the position in March 2024. Our net cash position has improved from INR51 crores to INR69 crores

items.statement: Jindal Explorer (rented) contract ends May 2025; ONGC to issue two tenders by year-end; rig may extend to Aug-Sep 2025 then need 2 months refurbishment
items.quote: Explorer is going to end contracts in May 25. ONGC is in talks for getting two new tenders before the year ends. So, hopefully, we will be participating in both those tenders and expect to gain the contract.

items.statement: Explorer last contract at ~$64,000/day; next rate expected $65,000-$85,000 depending on competition and timing
items.quote: The latest contract was at USD 64000 something. So USD 64000 being the benchmark with ONGC being the last contract.

items.statement: ONGC short of 7 rigs, wants Pioneer back; international rates rising due to war; no risk of idle rigs
items.quote: ONGC, because already in less of seven rigs, is looking for rigs. And definitely, we will be Jindal Drilling & Industries Limited 30 October 2024 participating in the next two tenders that it will be coming out with

items.statement: No significant one-off expenses expected next 4 quarters except unpredictable by nature; Jindal Explorer refurbishment cost sharing depends on new contract negotiation
items.quote: I don't believe there are any significant one-offs expected going forward, but that by nature is the definition of one-off that you cannot predict them.

items.statement: Jindal Pioneer acquisition application submitted Apr 2024; currently 49% JV profit share; full ownership will boost earnings
items.quote: we had submitted our application in April 2024 with the authority for acquisition of this rig. There has bee n some communication with the authority and we are hopeful that it gets concluded shortly

items.statement: Rig segment contributes ~90% of EBITDA; focus on growing company-owned rig fleet
items.quote: The EBITDA mix has been g iven on slide 10 wherein you will note that the rig segment contributes to almost 90% of total EBITDA and that is the area of focus where we want to grow further

items.statement: ONGC expressed interest in getting Pioneer back; does not want Indian operators moving rigs abroad
items.quote: They do not want us to deploy our rigs outside India. When Pioneer, which was built for ONGC went outside, they missed out on a new rig. And they have expressed their interest in getting Pioneer back into ONGC.

items.statement: Jindal Pioneer acquisition pending statutory authority approval; MODU standard change drove Supreme refurbishment
items.quote: Further, we are in the final stage of acquisition of rig Jindal Pioneer and are still awaiting approval from statutory authorities.

items.statement: International markets (Far East) being explored as backup; rigs can wet-tow or dry-carry without dismantling
items.quote: If we do not see any contracts coming up, we are talking to international markets as well. There is a lot of scope in the Far East, and we have been in touch with those parties as well.

items.statement: Started earnings calls and presentations few quarters ago to improve visibility; no direct institutional broker coverage yet
items.quote: That is why we started earning calls and earnings presentation a few quarters ago. And in my assessment, I think it takes around a couple of years of this exercise for the company's visibility to improve as much as we would like.

items.statement: Net debt-free target by end of next quarter (Q3 FY25)
items.quote: As we discussed in our previous update, we remain firmly on track of achieving a net debt -free status by the end of next quarte r, a key strategic objective for Anant Raj Limited

items.statement: Net debt reduced by INR124 crores in Q2 FY25 to INR95 crores as of 30 September 2024
items.quote: I am pleased to report that we have made a substantial progress towards this goal, with a further reduction of our net debt by INR124 crores during Q2 FY25 compared to Q1 FY25. Our outstanding net debt stands at just IN R95 crores as on 30 September 2024

items.statement: Planning INR2,100 crores fund raise (INR100 crores promoter, INR2,000 crores market) for data center cloud expansion

items.quote: Yes, sir. The co-location is INR26 crores and an additional INR100 crores, sir.

items.statement: 28 MW co-location capacity fully tied up; 0.5 MW cloud pilot launched with good response

items.statement: 0.5 MW cloud pilot generating revenue from 7 Oct; full utilization revenue potential INR75 crores annually
items.quote: So this 0.5 will actually generate close to INR75 crores of revenue.

items.quote: We spend about INR100 crores per megawatt. And in these INR100 crores, we build about 150. Number one, the expense, because, when you do co-location, electricity, and all are pass-throughs. Here, you have to pay for all that. So we are talking about a running cost of about INR2 crores per month, which is INR24 crores. So your EBITDA is about INR 126 crores.

items.statement: Strong demand for both private and government cloud; first-come-first-serve allocation

items.quote: Basically, sir, what we've done is we've started with a private cloud and almost 50% of whatever we've set up right now, and the remaining 50% is for a government community cloud, which actually qualifies as a sovereign cloud.

items.statement: Mixture of private and government clients for cloud; NDAs prevent naming
items.quote: Already, sir. We've already started getting private clients. Sorry, there are NDAs in place. We can't take names and it's not even h ealthy to take names like this, b ut now today we have a mixture of all categories of clients

items.quote: So we spend about INR20 crores an acre if we translate it in the money terms, average for this.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 revenue INR524 crores (+54% YoY); H1 FY25 revenue +51% YoY
items.quote: We announced that we have achieved a revenue of INR524 crores, which represents a growth of 54% compared to Q2 of last financial year. For the first half of FY25, revenue growth stood at 51% over H1 FY24.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA INR124 crores (+40% YoY); H1 FY25 EBITDA +49% YoY
items.quote: For Q2 FY25, we recorded an EBITDA of INR124 with a year-on-year growth of 40%. And for H1 FY25, EBITDA rose by 49% compared to the previous year.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 PAT INR106 crores (+75% YoY); H1 FY25 PAT +78% YoY
items.quote: Our profit after tax for Q2 FY25 was INR106 crores, reflecting a remarkable 75% growth year-on-year. With PAT, for the first half of FY25 saw an increase of 78%.

items.statement: Data center co-location Q2 revenue INR8 crores (82% EBITDA margin); same as Q1
items.quote: In this quarter, we have done INR8 crores revenue and the operational expenses is around 18%. So, it is around 82%.

items.statement: Orange partnership: revenue-share technical fees; Anant Raj owns all equipment
items.quote: It is based on the revenue. There is a fixed amount and then it is based on the revenue the company generates. Amit Sarin: But sir, Orange is only entitled to the technical fees because we actually are going to be owning all the equipment, sir

items.statement: Strong operational cash flow enabling aggressive debt reduction
items.quote: This achievement reflects our disciplined approach to debt management and is supported by the strong operational cash flow, which has enabled us to aggressively reduce our leverage over the past few quarters.

items.statement: Delhi 101 acres held; awaiting new master plan notification before development
items.quote: Delhi is expecting a new master plan, and it is public knowledge. The draft master plan is already available on Janta Book Depot. It's a book anybody can buy. It is yet to be notified. So let us see when it is notified.

items.statement: Ashim Sarin (CEO, Data Center Division) joined call to address cloud queries
items.quote: As we were preempting that there will be a lot of questions on the data center, so we requested him to join as well.

items.statement: Management expects 18% year-on-year revenue growth for next three years, targeting ~₹350 crores by FY27 with higher margins
items.quote: We hope that we'll be growing at a rate of 18% year-on-year for the next three years. That is our estimate, of course. We don't know what happens in future, but that is our estimate, and we will try and see that we reach those targets. Maybe we'll be reaching almost ₹350 crores in '26, '27 with higher margins as compared to the current margins.

items.statement: Consolidated margins currently ~21%, expected to reach 22% next year and 23% in FY27
items.quote: Margins as it is, it is more than 20% now. It is almost 21%. And what I feel that next year, it will go up to 22%, and thereafter in '26-'27, it will lead to 23%.

items.statement: Bearing division expansion completed and functional; Alkop division expansion delayed by heavy rains, to be completed by end of December and functional by January
items.quote: Expansion at Alkop division, that is Menon Alkop Limited that is under progress and because of heavy rains, it was delayed to some extent and will be completed within couple of months from now. So, it will be operational by the end of December.

items.quote: It is 4,86,00,000 pieces in bearing division, then 2,500 tons in aluminium division. And in brakes, it will be 2 lakh of brake linings per month.

items.statement: No impact from US anti-dumping scrutiny on aluminium extrusions
items.quote: Nothing special. We are not affected by that.

items.statement: Debt increase due to full disbursement from Bajaj Finance kept as bank deposits (₹22 crores cash); company effectively debt-free
items.quote: see at the same time, you can look at the cash and bank balances, which are ₹22 crores. So total debt that we got from Bajaj Finance. items.quote: Next generation has already reported. Now they are under training. Both the children are under training. One is at aluminium division that is Alkop, and one is coming to Menon Bearings. So both the sons of promoters have already joined, and they are under training now.

items.quote: Actually, what was happening the more emphasis were given or more thrust was given on the business of bearing division. items.quote: We are opt imistic about achieving our esteemed revenue -- our stated revenue target of approximately INR25 crores (Errata: Actual number to be read as INR2,500 crores ) for financial year '25 with an expected EBITDA margin of about 15% to 16

items.statement: FY26 top-line growth guidance of 50% over FY25 with EBITDA margin maintained at 15-16%
items.quote: So in terms of the guidance, earlier also we said this -- we expect a 50% growth in the top line and we maintain the same EBITDA level of 15% - 16%.

items.statement: Total order book INR31,776 crore net of taxes across SPVs and GIC platform for 8-10 years
items.quote: As on 30th September 2024, our total order book, including all SPVs and GIC platform, stands at about INR31,776 c rores net of taxes, and these concessions are for eight to 10

items.quote: Our EBITDA for Q2 was INR81 c rore, up by 232% compared to INR25 crore in Q2 '24. The EBITDA margin improved by 724 basis points to 16.7%, driven by the positive impact of operating leverage

items.quote: If not INR150 crores, INR140 crores, INR135 crores will be a good number.

items.quote: So in terms of manufacturing, exact number I need to see that, but we have done around 2 million meters in quarter two, and installation around -- installation has been 800,000 meters.

items.quote: We are expecting some good orders. But you will see the significant numbers coming from these projects after three to four years.

items.statement: Headcount rising due to in-house HES, MDM, RF development; exact numbers not disclosed
items.quote: Because of that, lot of -- employee strength has been enhanced all across. So this number will further grow.

items.statement: Maintained FY25 volume growth guidance: EXIM 15%, Domestic 25%, Total 18%

items.statement: LLF guidance for FY25 in range of Rs 350-400 crore

items.quote: H1 collections grew 6% YoY to Rs 497 crore

items.statement: Aqua City launch bookings over Rs 500 crore
items.quote: Arvind Aqua City has achieved bookings of more than Rs. 500 crore at the launch

items.statement: New Bengaluru project on ITPL Road with 4.2 lakh sq ft saleable area and Rs 600 crore potential
items.quote: Recently, we’ve signed a new residential project on ITPL Road in Bengaluru with 4.2 lakh sq. ft. of saleable area and a potential of ₹600

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA Rs 91 crore, up 153% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA for H1 grew by 153% to Rs. 91 croreore

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA Rs 83 crore, up 320% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA grew by 320% to Rs. 83 croreore

items.statement: Target EBITDA margin 20-25% on total project value
items.quote: whatever margins we say and we target and the number is absolutely right. 20%-25% is supposed to be on the total value

items.statement: Portfolio EBITDA margin estimated 23-25% on GDV
items.quote: roughly 20, around 25%, plus minus couple of percentage here and there, which varies from quarter to quarter, half to half, year to year. But generally a ballpark is 23% to 25% thereabouts

items.statement: Unrealized operating cash flow from current pipeline exceeds Rs 2,986 crore
items.quote: We estimate an unrealized operating cash flow exceeding Rs. 2,986 croreore coming from the current pipeline of projects

items.statement: Aqua City realization improved ~10% above business plan, base price Rs 7,000/sq yd now Rs 8,300-8,400/sq yd
items.quote: we have exceeded our targets in terms of what average realization we would have got in the number of units sold till date, and this is approximately 10% more than what we had as a business plan

items.statement: Long-term projects see 5-7% annual price inflation plus destination value creation
items.quote: as time passes, inflation etc., etc., itself takes care of 5% to 7% of value increase on an annualized basis. top of that, if you are creating a destination yourself where the whole area develops and becomes better in terms of liability, look and feel, etc., that value is in addition to the inflationary things

items.statement: Net debt negative Rs 195 crore (net cash) as of Sep 30, 2024, improved from negative Rs 58 crore in Jun 2024
items.quote: our net debt decreased to negative Rs. 195 croreore from a negative net debt of around Rs. 58 croreore as on June 30, 2024

items.statement: Sustenance sales low due to low inventory historically; now building inventory with Aqua City and Uplands 2.0/3.0
items.quote: out of 1,800 crore, almost like 700 crore to 800 crore worth of inventory now is coming from AquaCity and Uplands 2.0 & 3.0, which have been launched in last few months of this one or two quarters

items.statement: Industry trend: sustenance sales typically 20-25% of total in high growth environment
items.quote: industry trend is more like a 20%-25% coming for sustenance in a high growth environment

items.statement: Industry inventory overhang comfortable at 12 months; home loan deployments up 40% YoY in FY24
items.quote: Inventory overhang for the industry remains comfortable at 12 months. Further, according RBI data, home loan deployments exhibited a robust 40% YoY increase in FY24

items.statement: Portfolio 70-80% horizontal (plotted); vertical share increasing substantially by year-end
items.quote: 70%-80% of our portfolio is horizontal at this point. Of course, vertical is now becoming bigger and bigger. And as we end the year, it should be substantially higher than what it is today

items.statement: Plotted project completion requires full physical infrastructure: roads, drainage, electrical, pollution NOCs, power charged
items.quote: normally, it's supposed to be ready with all the roads, all the drainage works, all the electrical works, electrical connection should be coming, NOCs from Pollution Board and other relevant authorities, electricity etcetera should come, power should be charged

items.statement: Aqua City Phase 1 development timeline 3-4 years; total project >25 lakh sq yd (~2.5 cr sq ft)
items.quote: It is a very large development. So, the total project is more than 25 lakh square yards, which is almost like 2.5 crore square feet. So, it is 3 to 4 years' time that we have kept

items.statement: Pune Elan project exit expected this year; 20 units left, OC received, handovers started
items.quote: We will be exiting this project this year, hopefully yes. I mean, the number of units, we show only our inventory there, not the landlord's. Okay, 20 units are left and we are hoping that we should be able to exit this

items.statement: Expect mid-single digit volume growth in H2 FY25
items.quote: We may achieve a mid-single digit kind of growth in the 2nd half.

items.statement: Target 13-15% volume growth and 1-2% value growth from FY26 onwards
items.quote: But hopefully, next year onwards, we will keep our guidance for volume growth at 13 -15% and 1 -2% for value.

items.statement: Expect FY25 capex of Rs 40-50 crore, FY26 Rs 100-125 crore, FY27 similar
items.quote: FY25 we are anticipating because we will be start the construction soon. So, I think we will finish the CapEx and this year around 40 in the range of ₹40 crore to ₹50 crore for the whole year and in the next year again the similar way where we will be spending ₹100 crores and ₹125 crore each year.

items.statement: Spent Rs 11 crore in H1 FY25; delayed land deals in Bangalore, Chennai, Mumbai
items.quote: On the Capital Expenditure side, we spent almost around Rs. 11 crore in H1, because fortunately, unfortunately, we were not able to crack any land deal, which we anticipated at either on Bangalore or Chennai or Mumbai; we were not able to get that.

items.statement: Construction at Kolkata and Ahmedabad sorting centres to start in Q3/Q4 FY25
items.quote: So, I think in Q3 and or Q4, we will be start the construction and next year FY26, we will be able to complete the construction in these big two center like each one is more around 2 like square feet plus

items.statement: Overall fleet utilisation 83% in Q2 FY25 vs 82% in Q1; target 84-85% when volumes normalize
items.quote: in this quarter. And in this quart er, our capacity utilization of the overall fleet is 83% and in the last quarter it was 82%. So average it is around 82.5%, which is still below the expected numbers as we wanted to achieve atleast 85%. When the volume starts to normalize, we will achieve 84-85% again

items.statement: EBITDA margin fell to 13% in Q2 from 16% YoY due to higher toll, labour, admin costs and lower utilisation
items.quote: EBITDA margin has also come down from 16 to 13% due to like other costs like salary and some admin costs, which have increased.

items.statement: Air express cost up 100 bps in Q2 due to airline consolidation, airport privatisation, network expansion; unable to pass on to customers
items.quote: That cost is still on a higher side due to consolidation of airlines and secondly, privatization of the airports. Third, we're also expanding our direct network, as I mentioned in the last call. So, that is going on. The cost has increased, but we were not able to pass that on to the customer because the customer too is not ready to accept a high cost.

items.statement: No price hikes taken yet; will attempt in Q4 FY25 but not optimistic due to high inflation and muted volumes
items.quote: we have not yet taken any price hikes and we will start that effort in the last quarter i.e. Q4, actually. But still, we are not much optimistic about this price hike because of the high inflation and muted volumes. So really, I don’t exp ect high increase on that

items.statement: Rail Express now has 5,000+ customers across 150+ routes; repetitive business growing profitably
items.quote: Rail is really growing very fast. And now we have a 5,000 plus customer base in this segment. We are present in more than 150 routes, which is increasing day-by-day. It’s good that repetitive cus tomers are giving business to us and it is profitable

items.statement: Multi-modal services target 20-22% of revenue in 2-3 years; currently ~17-18%
items.quote: Our Rail Express service is gaining traction with the customers, contributing positively to margins and is essential as we aim for the Multi-Modal services to make up 20 to 22% of revenue over the next 2-3 years.

items.statement: Receivable days 55, payable days 33, net working capital cycle 22 days; debt-free
items.quote: Like you see, receivable days are maintained at 55 days, and payable days is in the range of 33. And accordingly, networking cycle is 22 days. So we have a very robust profile and we are continuously in a debt-free status.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free; ICRA A1+ and CRISIL AA- ratings reaffirmed
items.quote: ICRA and CRISIL ha ve reaffirmed our ratings. It’s AA - by CRISIL for the long term, and A1+ on ICRA which is the highest for the short term. We were also Certified as Great Place to Work for 2024-25

items.statement: Consultant for branch expansion completed work; contract ended; cost not significant
items.quote: So, basically that consultant was hired for expanding the branch network and all and they already did work on that and then you know they have also given their reports on where we have to be like more focused on that

items.statement: Toll tax up 8-10%, labour costs rising due to government wage standardization; both pressuring margins
items.quote: Second part like, high increase of toll is never anticipated because government is now allowing to increase to 8% to 10% is becoming significant amount for the overall journey cost. Third part like because as a volume you know labor cost is also government want to standardize there and want to increase their wages and all.

items.statement: Diesel consumption grew only ~1% YoY in H1, indicating muted freight demand
items.quote: Diesel consumption, as I mentioned, is hardly 1% growth over the same period last year. So, I think demand would be similar. It won't be much and would be rather moderate.

items.statement: Pune sorting centre automation reduced turnaround time 30-40%; Ahmedabad and Kolkata next
items.quote: Automation remains a key focus, exemplified by our newly automated Pune sorting centre, which has improved operational efficiency and reduced turn down time by almost 40%. We are extending next automation to be in Ahmedabad and Kolkata centre to better handle increasing volumes.

items.statement: Money-back guarantee launched across Surface, Rail, Air; well received by new customers
items.quote: This year, we introduced a money back guarantee, reflecting our confidence in timely delivery across surface rail and air modes. This offering has been well received by customers and strengthens our position in express logistics.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margins excluding non-recurring items improved 70 bps YoY in Q2 FY25; excluding Astec, improvement was 130 bps.
items.quote: Godrej Agrovet continues to deliver improvement in profitability, with the exception of Astec LifeSciences and the Poultry business. EBITDA margins, excluding non -recurring items, improved in Q2 FY25 by 70 bps and by 130 bps, excluding Astec's, as compared to Q2 FY24.

items.statement: Animal Feed segment margins improved from 4.6% to 5.9% YoY in Q2 FY25; EBIT per metric ton rose from ₹1,531 to ₹1,953.
items.quote: In Animal feed, the segment margins improved sharply from 4.6% in Q2 FY24 to 5.9% in Q2 FY25 on account of favorable commodity positions and cost optimization measures. Further, EBIT per metric ton improved significantly from ₹ 1,531 in Q2 FY24 to ₹ 1,953 in Q2 FY25.

items.statement: Standalone Crop Protection segment margins improved from 30% to 43% YoY in Q2 FY25 due to lower doubtful debts and fixed cost control.
items.quote: The Standalone crop protection segment results witnessed strong growth in Q2 FY25. Our segment margins improved significantly from 30% in Q2 FY24 to 43% in Q2 FY25, primarily due to lower doubtful debts and control over fixed costs.

items.statement: Dairy segment EBITDA margins improved by 140 bps YoY in Q2 FY25 driven by operational efficiency and improved milk spread.
items.quote: In Q2 FY25, our Dairy segment continued to demonstrate margin expansion, with EBITDA margins improving by 140 basis points. This enhancement was primarily driven by operational efficiency-led gains and an improved milk spread, despite a flat top line.

items.statement: Animal Feed cattle feed volumes declined marginally YoY due to subdued milk prices; layer and broiler feed volumes grew sequentially and YoY.
items.quote: While there was a marginal degrowth in volumes of cattle feed due to subdued milk prices, the layer and broiler feed volumes grew sequentially and also year-on-year.

items.statement: Standalone Crop Protection revenues fell 24% YoY in Q2 FY25 due to erratic rainfall reducing spraying opportunities and higher herbicide sales returns.
items.quote: However, segment revenues were lower by 24% due to the erratic rainfall in key states, which reduced spraying opportunities and resulted in higher sales returns in the herbicide category.

items.statement: Astec LifeSciences faces pricing pressure in enterprise products and lower-than-expected CDMO volumes due to cautious customer approach.
items.quote: Astec LifeSciences continued to experience pricing pressures in the enterprise products business and lower-than-expected volumes in the CDMO category due to a cautious approach adopted by our CDMO customers.

items.statement: Poultry segment revenue declined in Q2 FY25 due to lower live bird volumes as focus shifts to branded business; margins hit by unfavorable channel and product mix.
items.quote: In a seasonally weak quarter, the Poultry segment recorded a decline in revenue, primarily due to lower volumes in the live bird business, as we continued to focus on branded business and reduce our exposure to the live bird business. Segment margins were adversely impacted due to unfavorable channel and product mix.

items.statement: ACI Godrej (Bangladesh JV) revenues declined 6% YoY in Q2 FY25 due to volume contraction and pricing pressures amid challenging political and economic environment.
items.quote: GAVL's joint venture in Bangladesh, ACI Godrej, recorded a decline in revenues of 6% year -on-year in Q2 FY25 due to volume contraction and pricing pressures in the backdrop of a challenging political and economic environment.

items.statement: Astec CDMO revenue targeting ~₹400 crore in FY25, implying ~50% YoY growth over FY24 base of ~₹270 crore.
items.quote: Yes, very near to ₹ 400 crores we are targeting . This means we will be achieving that ₹ 400 crores.

items.statement: Astec CDMO FY25 revenue guidance of 50% YoY growth maintained; H1 was lower but H2 catch-up expected due to seasonal shift in buying behavior.
items.quote: But overall, the earlier guidance remains the same, we'll see a 50% growth over last year.

items.statement: Astec Herbicide 2 plant commissioned on time in Q2 FY25; expected to run at ~30% capacity in FY25, reaching 60-70% utilization only in FY26.
items.quote: Normally, it takes around three years to have a full capacity. This year, we'll be using around 30% of the capacity. And one of the improvement reasons for H2 will be this additional capacity also.

items.statement: Astec Herbicide 2 plant capacity utilization assumptions pushed by 1-2 years; upwards of 60-70% utilization expected only in FY26.
items.quote: And I feel that probably it will be only in FY26 that we will see upwards of 60%-70% utilization of this plant.

items.statement: Dairy value-added products (VAP) salience fell to 32% in Q2 FY25 from 42% in Q1 due to seasonality (rains), but expected to finish FY25 above 40%.
items.quote: On Dairy, yes, value-added products contributed 32% of total sales. But one of the reasons why Q2 is less than Q1 is because of seasonality. You know that when it rains, and it rained a lot in Q2 this year, the curd, the buttermilk, the lassi, the cold drinks, etc., their sales go down.

items.statement: Poultry focusing on branded business (Real Good Chicken, Yummiez) and reducing live bird exposure; branded share increasing.
items.quote: In a seasonally weak quarter, the Poultry segment recorded a decline in revenue, primarily due to lower volumes in the live bird business, as we continued to focus on branded business and reduce our exposure to the live bird business.

items.statement: Consolidated working capital days at ~50 days end-September; expected to reduce to 40-42 days by March FY25 with steep fall in October.
items.quote: By the time March comes, we should exit about 40, 42 days of working cap ital, which is at the end of September was about 50 days. So, this is the kind of reduction. Some of it has already happened, but we believe that it is further going to reduce.

items.statement: Targeting debt-to-equity below 0.3x by March FY25; H1 FY25 weighted average cost of debt at 7.36%.
items.quote: Absolutely. I think debt equity will come down, by March to less than 0.3.

items.statement: H1 FY25 weighted average cost of debt was 7.36%.
items.quote: For H1, the average cost of debt was around 7.36.

items.statement: Vegetable Oil segment: higher end-product realizations offset by lower FFB arrivals; margins improved on better OER and downstream value addition.
items.quote: Our Vegetable oil segment revenues in Q2 FY25 were flat, as higher realizations of end products were offset by lower fresh fruit bunch arrivals. Segment margins improved on account of better oil extraction ratio, OER, and accretive downstream value addition.

items.statement: Oil Palm H2 FY25 expected to be better than H2 FY24 due to delayed season tapering; expecting ₹13-15 crore upside at current prices, though 70-80% shared with farmers.
items.quote: We are expecting an upside of ₹ 13 crores to ₹ 15 crore at today's prices in the second half.

items.statement: Astec enterprise product prices remain low due to Chinese competition and Latin American inventories; demand picking up but pricing pressure persists.
items.quote: In terms of enterprise business, yes, the demand is slowly picking up, but the prices are much lower because of the Chinese pressure and a little bit of inventories and baptism in the Latin American countries. Prices are not picking up, yes, but overall, it is slightly better than, say, last four or five quarters.

items.statement: Poultry Q2 FY25 costs hit by high chicken meat prices (disease incidents, mortality, poor growth) and seasonal high raw material prices in off-season.
items.quote: So, one of the chief reasons for cost increase is that this is the off-season for raw materials. So raw materials prices are at the highest in Q2. And second thing is that there were some disease incidences because of which there was mortality and poor growth , which added to the cost.

items.statement: Animal Feed EBIT per metric ton improved from ₹1,531 to ₹1,953 YoY in Q2 FY25.
items.quote: Further, EBIT per metric ton improved significantly from ₹ 1,531 in Q2 FY24 to ₹ 1,953 in Q2 FY25.

items.statement: Balram Yadav (MD) retirement due end-FY25; succession process underway with candidate interviews ongoing; smooth transition expected.
items.quote: We have good processes in place for succession planning, and we are actually interviewing candidates, and they are being examined. We will soon come to a conclusion, and we expect a smooth transition.

items.statement: Astec CEO Anurag Roy exited; Arijit Mukherjee (COO) overseeing business; hiring CDMO specialists and overseas consultants; CEO recruitment will take time.
items.quote: Yes, definitely, I think we will have to find out a CEO eventually. But at present, we are more focused on augmenting the team with CDMO specialist talent on our roles and also consultants overseas, because we want to push this. The recruitment and hiring of the CEO will take some time, but I think our priority is to develop this CDMO team and give some acceleration to this process. In the meantim

items.statement: Astec CFO replaced; senior R&D exit in August; management says exits don't affect business due to SOPs, committee-based negotiations, and conglomerate support.
items.quote: So, I think the two exits you are talking about, the CEO and CFO. So definitely, CFO has been recruited and already in place. And I must tell you that whenever businesses have some tough time and they go through severe ups and downs, definitely we have seen, not only in this business, but several other businesses also, that people leave. But the way we are structured is that neither power nor know

items.statement: Portfolio cleanup underway; first step was acquiring 49% stake in Tyson JV (Godrej Tyson); further JV decisions to be taken as opportunities arise.
items.quote: So, I think the idea is to clean up the portfolio because we have so many joint ventures, etc. The first step, we have already taken by acquiring 49% shares of Tyson. As and when the opportunity comes, I'm sure that we will take decisions either way.

items.statement: Astec turnaround uncertain; China pricing pressure severe across sector; green shoots seen before but not sustained; not confident of exit from woods in 1-2 quarters.
items.quote: So, I would not say with confidence that things have really turned around. And I must tell you that China is hammering us very badly in several categories. Not only Astec LifeSciences, but a lot of companies in this sector. So, I think, until some sanity prevails in their pricing of products , it is not easy to say that we will be out of the woods in next one or two quarters.

items.statement: Astec high-cost inventory largely cleared; remainder to move out in Q3 FY25.
items.quote: Majority of the high -cost inventories have moved out. So, whatever remaining is there will be Q3, which will be moving out.

items.statement: Astec targeting break-even in H2 FY25 (profitable in Q4) if 1-2 more CDMO contracts under negotiation materialize.
items.quote: We are trying very hard and with one or two more contracts, if they come our way, which are under negotiation, we are hoping to break even in H2 , which means that we will be profitable in Q4.

items.statement: Cattle feed volumes jumped 10% in October over September; strong growth expected in H2 FY25 as rains recede.
items.quote: What we are seeing is a 10% jump in cattle feed volumes in October over September. So, we strongly believe that, the growth will be back in cattle feed in the second half.

items.statement: Astec CDMO: 1 new molecule introduced in FY25 (total 9); R&D now engaged in early-stage co-development with innovators under NDAs; Metconazole developed at record time.
items.quote: So, total this year we have introduced one new molecule and total molecules will be nine. Eight was for the past and one new molecule , and in case of R&D, we are in discussion with several companies for new projects but these falls under NDAs would not be able to disclose the number, but I think this will be significant enough to run the R&D right now.

items.statement: Implant business targets $100 million revenue by FY28-29 (5 years from now)
items.quote: Yes, so on the implant business, we still stick to a path of trying to get to the $100 million business by 5 years' time from now. So, 2028-29 is when we see a $100 million business coming into picture.

items.statement: Hospital business expects continued high double-digit revenue growth in FY25
items.quote: For the hospital business, we are always delivering the higher double digit growth kind of thing and we are going ahead with the same kind of direction right now.

items.statement: Standalone ROCE expected around 20% by end of FY25
items.quote: So, we can see somewhere by the end of the year it will be around 20% kind of thing.

items.statement: Hospital segment EBITDA margin expected 21-23% for next financial year including Sanar
items.quote: So, we are seeing that trend will continue of around 21% to 23% for the next financial year.

items.statement: Sanar Hospital expected EBITDA positive single digit in current year, double digit next year
items.quote: In the current year, we are seeing it will be the EBITDA positive in the single digit kind of thing. Next year, it will be on the move into the double digit kind of profitability with the growth in occupancy and the revenue.

items.statement: Asha Parekh Hospital Mumbai capex ~Rs 250 crore over 36 months from lease filing
items.quote: So, Asha Parekh Hospital in Bombay, we are looking at around Rs. 250 crores kind of a number from the investment perspective. That will again be kind of spread across 36 months from the day that we file the lease agreement with the charity commissioner.

items.statement: Sanar Hospital expansion from 130 to 200 beds planned, 12-18 months after permissions
items.quote: We will add around 60 to 70 beds, so taking the capacity to around 200 beds.

items.statement: FOSO franchise capex Rs 3-5 crore for 25-60 beds, FOSM asset-light with no capex
items.quote: FOSO sometime maybe we have to do the CAPEX in the range of Rs. 3 to Rs. 5 crores, but that depends upon the situation but this entire franchise model is an asset light model.

items.statement: Sanar Hospital currently 130 beds at 25% occupancy, targeting 50%+ occupancy
items.quote: Shalby Sanar is presently operating at 25% occupancy level and it will increase gradually in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Implant manufacturing capacity increased from 2,700 components/month (April) to 7,500+ (September)
items.quote: We were manufacturing approximately 2,700 components in April. We have been able to manufacture 7,500 plus components in September.

items.statement: Q2 surgeries down 7% YoY due to heavy monsoon flooding in Gujarat and Rajasthan
items.quote: Our revenue has been de-grown by 2.4% on a YoY basis due to reduction of surgeries by 7% on a YoY basis. Rajasthan and Gujarat have witnessed a major rainfall in the current quarter where most of the districts in Gujarat and Rajasthan have experienced heavy flooding which has resulted in patients postponing elective surgeries.

items.statement: October showing growth with spillover from postponed surgeries despite Diwali impact
items.quote: In the month of October from what we have seen, we definitely see growth and that spillover effect coming in this quarter despite three or four days of the month being impacted due to the festive season of Diwali.

items.statement: Implant COGS reduced 30% QoQ and 35% YoY to $77 per component from $109
items.quote: When it comes to cost reduction, our cost of goods manufactured has gone down by 30% over the previous quarter. And we are currently at $77 against $109 of last quarter.

items.statement: Implant business: 3,184 constructs sold in Q2 FY25 (up 46% YoY), 6,644 in H1 FY25 (up 85% YoY)
items.quote: The total constructs sold has grown by 46% from 2174 units to 3184 units in Quarter 2 financial year 25. It's grown by 85% from 3585 to 6644 in H1 of financial year 25.

items.statement: Franchise target: 40+ hospitals across India in next 4-5 years
items.quote: Our primary focus remains on utilizing our expertise and excellence in orthopedics with the goal of establishing more than 40 franchise hospital across India within the next 4 to 5 years.

items.statement: ARPOB improved 7.3% YoY to Rs 38,779; ALOS improved to 3.6 days from 3.92
items.quote: ARPOB and ALOS has shown an improvement at 38,779 and 3.6 respectively, compared to 36,136 and 3.92 in the same period of the previous year. ARPOB on YoY basis has been grew by around 7.3%.

items.statement: ARPOB historically grows 5-7% per quarter or 10-12% annually; Sanar international patients to boost blended ARPOB
items.quote: As we have mentioned, the ARPOB is keep growing on the quarter-on-quarter basis. As Sanar occupancy will grow, that will also contribute into the ARPOB because the international patient, we have the higher ARPOB. So, the way we have seen historically, it is growing every quarter 5% to 7% or every year around 10% to 12% on a basis.

items.statement: Payer mix: 36% self-pay, 41% insurance, 23% government; insurance share down from 44.2% due to lower Gujarat surgeries
items.quote: The peer mix of the current quarter is 36% from the self-patient, 41% from insurance, and 23% from the government business.

items.statement: Sanar: 54% revenue from international patients; group international revenue Rs 15.3 crore
items.quote: In the current quarter, 54% of the revenue contribution of Sanar has been generated from the international patient. Revenue from international patient on the overall group basis is Rs. 15.3 crore, which includes Sanar as well as Shalby Limited.

items.statement: CKS Gold implant launch pending US FDA approval, expected Dec-Jan
items.quote: It's gone for the US FDA approval. So, we are waiting for the US FDA approval to come through. So, expecting the approval to come anywhere between December and January.

items.statement: Sanar Hospital received AACI (American Accreditation) accreditation to drive institutional international business
items.quote: And also we have got recently accredited by AACI which is an American Accreditation company. Now this accreditation will help us in getting some institutional business from different countries.

items.statement: Shalby Krishna Hospital obtained bone bank license in September 2024, operational in Q3 FY25
items.quote: In September 2024, Shalby Krishna Hospital has got a license of bone bank and has successfully operationalized in the ongoing quarter three of FY25.

items.statement: Consolidated debt Rs 405 crore (up from Rs 313 crore) due to implant working capital and Sanar acquisition
items.quote: So, the reason if you can see this is majorly as you can see the growth is coming into the implant business. We are investing into the implant, the new product is going to be launched into the upcoming quarter. So, that is the working capital utilization mainly into the implant business and some part into the Sanar business.

items.statement: Comfortable with net debt:equity 1:1 or 3x EBITDA; expect internal accruals to fund expansions with minimal new debt
items.quote: From the perspective of the peak debt, very honestly, we would be comfortable at about, internally speaking, net equity ratio 1:1 or maybe 3x EBITDA. But very honestly, we don't see ourselves going there. The reason being that we are already generating anywhere between Rs. 200 to Rs. 250 crores of annual EBITDA and that number is also growing on an annual basis. So, I believe that our internal acc

items.statement: No equity raise planned; strong cash position (Rs 74 cr net cash standalone) and bank borrowing capacity suffice for Mumbai/Delhi expansion
items.quote: In terms of the hospital, we are not looking for any kind of equity infusion right now because our cash position on the standalone basis is suffice to take care for our expansion for Delhi as well as Mumbai location. Apart from that, our balance sheet is so strong that we can raise the further fund from the bank.

items.statement: No plan to hive off implant business; expects it to deliver higher double-digit profit in coming years
items.quote: In the current quarter, you can see there is a 90% growth in terms of the topline and as we will progress in the coming quarter, implant will start delivering the profit and in the coming years, it will deliver the higher double digit profit. So, it is a profitable venture for us and there's no possibility that we will look forward for any kind of hive off for that.

items.statement: Occupied beds up 2% YoY to 680; target 710-730 in upcoming quarter; long-term 70-75% occupancy sustainable
items.quote: From 680 what we have right now the occupancy, we are going to see very shortly in the upcoming quarter it will be ranging between 710 to 730.

items.statement: Home Care patients up 15.3% YoY to 9,000+; revenue up 7% YoY to Rs 3.9 crore
items.quote: We serve 9000 plus patients in the current quarter versus around 7800 plus patients in the Quarter 2 of the last year with a growth of 15.3% patient counting the similar period of the last year. Revenue from the Home Care business is Rs. 3.9 crore in the current quarter versus Rs. 3.6 crore in the same quarter of the last year which is 7% growth on the YoY basis.

items.statement: Ayushman Bharat senior citizen scheme impact minimal; only 2 hospitals empaneled
items.quote: See out of the hospitals that we operate, only two of the hospitals are Ayushman Bharat empaneled for us, for any which way the impact will be very minimal. For the rest of the hospitals, I mean we are unable to kind of give you an assessment of the overall impact but I can tell you for us it won't be a significant impact.

items.statement: MAT regime continues till end of FY25 or Q1 FY26; consolidated tax rate elevated due to no deferred tax on implant/Sanar losses
