items.quote: Now if you look at the product level for Hollow PVC, uPVC window and WPC products, demand was there but we were not able to cater the demand on appropriate time due to supply constraint where we would have done by supplying the products on time.

items.statement: Roofing sheet demand not up to mark; spreading awareness to improve demand
items.quote: For roofing sheet, demand is not up to the mark, and we are trying to spread awareness and benefit of uPVC roofing sheet and hoping to get good demand for the product in the coming time.

items.statement: Doors contribute 15% of revenue, furniture 85%
items.quote: And for the doors, we are largely into furniture now, doors is a small part. I mean, 15% of the total revenue is door, and 85% is furniture.

items.statement: 100% sales through dealer/distributor network; no direct developer relationships
items.quote: Our 100% billing is through dealers only.

items.statement: Regional sales split: Gujarat 60%, Telangana 8-9%, Karnataka 6-7%, Maharashtra 5%, Rajasthan 3-4%, others 13-14%
items.quote: Yes. Gujarat is 60%, and Telangana is 8% to 9%, Karnataka is 6% to 7%, Maharashtra 5%, Rajasthan is 3% to 4%, and others around 13% to 14%.

items.statement: Dhabriya Polywood identified as key listed competitor in same space
items.quote: Precisely, you can say, Dhabriya Polywood is our competitive. I mean, they are in the same space.

items.statement: Market largely unorganised; organised players few; company claims market leadership in Gujarat
items.quote: We can say, largely it is unorganised market. There are small players, the numbers of players you can count on there, those are into the organised market are few. So, it is a bigger market, I think.

items.statement: Current portfolio not export-oriented; SPC flooring to be export-oriented product
items.quote: So current product portfolio is not meant to export, but definitely, SPC flooring will be the export-oriented product only.

items.statement: Debtor days 40-50; inventory days currently 70, targeting 90 days to enable 2-3 day delivery
items.quote: So, overall, the debtor days are almost 40 to 50 days, and inventory, we wish to keep more because there are lots of sizes and colour and textures are there. So, we want to cater the demands in two to three days, what we want to achieve. So, for that, we have to keep the materials in our store. So, it will increase. I mean, it is 70 days as of now. So, it will be around 90 days, what we are thinki

items.statement: PVC furniture 20-25% cheaper than wood panel alternatives
items.quote: It depends, but generally, you can say 20% to 25% will be cheaper in PVC.

items.statement: Advertising budget 5-6% of sales; currently using shutter painting, wall painting, hoardings, radio and movie partnerships
items.quote: Percentage of sales, you can say 5% to 6%.

items.statement: Electricity supply issue at new plant resolved; continuous power needed for extrusion process
items.quote: So, this is the extrusion method, what we are using for the production. And for that, we need continuous supply of the power. So, at our new factory, we did not have the power supply that which is continuous.

items.statement: BIS regulation impact not yet assessed
items.quote: That I need to check. I haven't seen that.

items.statement: No major risk seen currently due to real estate boom and product diversification into SPC flooring and PEB
items.quote: So, hopefully, we have in India, as of now real estate is booming, and we are targeting affordable housing, renovation of the houses and offices. So, for the PVC product as of now, there is no risk as such we are looking for. And even though we have added new products to cope up with the risk if it emerges in the future.

items.statement: Labour and operators provided food and accommodation at new premises; office staff work remotely from Ahmedabad head office
items.quote: I mean, for labourers and operators, we already we are providing them the food and accommodation that we have created for them at the new premises also. And for the office staff, they can work remotely in at the head office sitting in Ahmedabad.

items.statement: H1 FY25 sales growth 10% YoY and 15% HoH
items.quote: In this period, sale growth was 10% year-on-year and 15% half-on-half.

items.statement: uPVC window installation plant started in September 2024; previously only supplied profiles to dealers
items.quote: Now from September onwards, we have started the installation plant for uPVC window. So that is the scenario.

items.statement: Shashwat appointed CEO designate, to take over as MD & CEO on Jan 1, 2026; Gopal Vittal to become Vice-Chairman & MD then Executive Vice Chairman
items.quote: Shashwat will be appointed CEO designate and will take over the role of MD & CEO on January 01, 2026.

items.statement: Capex for FY25 will be lower than FY24; no specific number given
items.quote: I have always said that this year you will see a moderation in overall capex for the year and that we stand by. We have not given a specific guidance but we will certainly see capex going down from last year.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 capex was Rs 6,260 Crores; FY25 capex expected to moderate from elevated FY24 levels
items.quote: Capex for the quarter was 6,260 Crores.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 54.8%, up 1.1% sequentially
items.quote: EBITDA margins came in at 54.8% , an improvement of 1.1% .

items.statement: Airtel Finance AUM at Rs 2,500 Crores; annualized loan disbursal rate Rs 3,000 Crores
items.quote: We are trending at an annualized loan disbursal rate of 3,000 Crores and our AUM stands at 2,500 Crores.

items.statement: Mobility lost 2.9M customers due to SIM consolidation from tariff repair; normalization seen in October with customer adds
items.quote: In the mobility business we experienced a loss of 2.9 million customers due to sim consolidation triggered by the tariff repair, but this decline was milder than what we observed in earlier rounds.

items.statement: ARPU rose to Rs 233 from Rs 211 in Q1; full benefit of tariff repair expected in coming quarter
items.quote: ARPU came in at Rs.233 compared to 211 in Q1 maintaining an industry-leading growth.

items.statement: Rolled out ~5,000 network sites and ~9,800 route km of fiber in Q2; 5G user base reached 105M
items.quote: We ended the quarter with a 5G user base of 105 million .

items.statement: Broadband added ~6 lakh customers; FWA expansion driving growth; live in 2,000+ cities via FWA and FTTH
items.quote: In the broadband segment we added nearly 6 lakh customers, a step jump from previous quarter s.

items.statement: Postpaid net adds steady at ~0.8M; Airtel Black customers up ~65% YoY; Xstream customers up 55% YoY
items.quote: Postpaid net adds remain steady at about 0.8 million.

items.statement: Payments Bank monthly transacting users ~86M, up 20% QoQ; annualized revenue run rate >Rs 2,600 Cr, up 58% YoY; deposits >Rs 2,950 Cr, up 43% YoY
items.quote: The monthly transacting users stood at just over 85 million, actually a shade under 86 million, with a strong growth of 20% sequentially.

items.statement: Prepaid Rs 32,000 Cr of high-cost spectrum dues in last 5 quarters; India net debt/EBITDA 2.6x vs 3.1x a year ago
items.quote: In the last five quarters we pre paid over 32,000 Crores of high -cost spectrum dues.

items.statement: Highest ever quarterly operating free cash flow (EBITDA minus capex) of ~Rs 11,000 Cr
items.quote: We delivered the highest ever quarterly operating free cash flow, which is EBITDA minus capex of 11,000 odd Crores.

items.statement: Curative petition on AGR dues rejected; review petition pending; moratorium period not yet started
items.quote: No I think that was the last recourse on this particular matter.

items.statement: India mobile ROCE still very low at 11.2%; further tariff repair needed to improve returns
items.quote: At the same time the ROCE of the India business is still very low at 11.2%. The only way to improve this is further tariff repair.

items.statement: Africa revenue share 25% of consolidated; constant currency growth 7.7% sequentially
items.quote: Africa now accounts for 25% of revenues , India mobile is at 60% and India non-mobile is at 15%.

items.statement: Signed agreement with Sparkle for Blue & Raman Submarine Cable Systems capacity between India and Italy
items.quote: To boost our global connectivity offerings we s igned an agreement with Sparkle for Blue & Raman Submarine Cable Systems capacity between India and Italy .

items.statement: Paid Rs 5,000 Cr dividends from cash generation in Q2
items.quote: In addition, do note that we paid out 5 ,000 Crores of dividends from our cash generation.

items.statement: Solarized 3,500+ sites in Q2; ~24,800 sites in last 5 quarters; diesel savings >2M litres/month; 5.8 tonnes CO2 eliminated monthly
items.quote: We solarized over 3,500 sites in the quarter and about 24 ,800 sites in the last five quarters.

items.statement: Won all five 5G network experience awards on OpenSignal; best experience in India
items.quote: Airtel was awarded all five awards on 5G network experience on open signal , a testimony to the hard work done by all at Airtel.

items.statement: FWA unit economics now comparable to FTTH; CPE costs dramatically reduced via OEM/chipset partnerships
items.quote: As far as the unit economics is concerned, the unit economics are now comparable between both FTTH and FWA.

items.statement: Moving FWA to standalone 5G by December; trials underway for better uplink performance
items.quote: We are moving to standalone 5G on FWA by December we are in the midst of doing some trials and we want to just test whether we are able to get better uplink performance with SA for a fixed wireless access.

items.statement: Bharti Hexacom revenue ~Rs 2,100 Cr, up 9.8% QoQ; ARPU Rs 228, up 11.3%; EBITDA margin ~50%; op FCF ~Rs 600 Cr
items.quote: We have delivered revenue of close to 2,100 Crores growing sequentially by about 9.8%.

items.statement: Bharti Hexacom net debt/EBITDA improved to 2.03x despite Rs ~1,000 Cr spectrum debt addition
items.quote: Consequently net debt-to-EBITDA improved to 2.03 despite addition of the spectrum debt of close to 1,000 Crores.

items.statement: Bharti Hexacom spectrum CWIP fully capitalized; amortization to flatten from Q3 run-rate
items.quote: Of course the millimeter wave continues to be there, but whatever we have purchased now, everything has got capitalized and put to use.

items.statement: Bharti Hexacom smartphone adds 143k vs 703k prior quarter; customer base impacted by tariff repair, normalizing in couple of quarters
items.quote: Smartphone customer addition was about 143,000 as compared to about 7 03,000 in the previous quarter.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated jewellery EBIT margin guidance revised to 11%-11.5% from earlier 11.5%-12.5%
items.quote: I think FY25 looks like more between 11% and 11.5%.

items.statement: Q2 jewellery margin dropped 270 bps mainly due to Rs 290 crore customs duty loss, lower studded mix, higher gold coin sales, and weak large solitaire demand
items.quote: We had two-three impacts on margin this quarter. One was a substantial part of it is on account of the one-time custom duty loss, which has flown in already part of it in this quarter and partly in the next.

items.statement: H2 FY25 jewellery margin expected to improve over H1 due to better demand, stabilising diamond mix, and CaratLane margin trajectory
items.quote: H2 is therefore expected to be certainly better than H1 and certainly for diamond stud ded, even more so. And that gives us the confidence that it would be a better margin play in H2

items.statement: Gold coin and bullion purchases surged in Q2; studded share lower due to gold rush and weak large solitaire demand
items.quote: There was a gold rush of sorts in quarter two. Therefore, the gold component was much higher, including a substantial rise in gold coins and bullion purchases.

items.statement: Competitive intensity on gold rates increased; Tanishq offered gold price discounts for first time, distributed payouts between making charges and gold rate
items.quote: The competitive intensity on gold rates itself has gone up. Thanks to the very high price of gold. And many local players have been either on their own or sometimes in response to other national players or chains come out strongly with gold price offers.

items.statement: Tanishq added 22 stores in Q2, 10-11 more in October; target 40-50 for FY25. Mia to reach 250 stores by FY25 end. CaratLane at 301 stores, net addition 29 YTD, targeting 20 more by March
items.quote: We have added in Tanishq 22 stores. In fact, in this month itself, in October, we have added another 10 or 11 stores, rather. We have added 33, therefore, up to 30th October and our aim is to add between 40 and 50.

items.statement: Watches analog segment growing double-digit on premiumization and product innovation; wearables share correcting, analog share rising
items.quote: Analog is seeing good growth in the last few quarters, and it is on the back of very strong product design and innovation. Also, on premiumization.

items.statement: Watches EBIT margin guidance maintained at 13%-14% range
items.quote: I would go back to what we had said during the investor day that 13%-14% is definitely in the range that we will commit to.

items.statement: GST hike proposal on watches above Rs 25,000 under review; proportion of such sales currently not very high but rising with premiumization
items.quote: So, right now, it is a proposal. I think the group of ministers has recommended to the GST Council. So, we will have to wait and see how it actually pans out.

items.statement: Golden Harvest enrolments strong despite competitor schemes; Tanishq launched new variant with gold rate fixation feature
items.quote: No, in fact, we ourselves have innovated a little bit on the golden harvest. We have launched another version which also enables customers to fix their gold rate, etc. , a nd the benefit is different from the Golden Harvest usual

items.statement: Customs duty loss estimated at Rs 275-280 crore in Q3 FY25; not included in normalized margin guidance
items.quote: actually our current estimate, which is much more firmer is that quarter 3 may witness about ₹275 - ₹280 crores kind of number

items.statement: Lab-grown diamond strategy not disclosed; monitoring consumer interest but no store inquiries beyond clarification that diamonds are natural
items.quote: We continue to observe. We are not seeing inquiries across our stores other than clarifying that all the diamonds we are selling are natural, etc., We continue to observe and study the customer and keeping a close track of it.

items.statement: EyeCare strategy executing well with strong customer acquisition across affordable fashion, progressive lenses, premium frames
items.quote: The strategy that we started executing about 8-9 months back continues to be in full swing and the customer acquisition rate continues to be at a very satisfying level.

items.statement: Taneira targeting blockbuster FY26; IRTH first EBO launched in Mumbai; international business and TEAL performing well
items.quote: The foundation of Tane ira has become stronger and stronger and stronger. And we expect certainly FY26 to be a sort of blockbuster year for Taneira

items.statement: M&HCV market softened from Q1 into Q2; recent retail uptick seen; Q3/Q4 expected stronger with OEMs carrying moderate inventory
items.quote: Like Nagaraja mentioned, we continue seeing softening of market from Q1 into Q2 as well. Most of this was expected to some extent after the general election and the monsoon. And the recent few days have shown some uptick in the retail sales, which is a positive trend.

items.statement: Full-year M&HCV industry volume forecast at 90,000-95,000 for Q3 and 100,000+ for Q4, implying ~5% dip vs last year
items.quote: So, in all likelihood, we should end up Q3 and then around 90,000 to 95,000, that is our current forecast. And Q4 will be like last year at the higher note, around 100,000 plus. This will still be a dip compared to last year about 5%.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin 11.4% vs 11.9% YoY; H1 FY25 EBITDA 11.6% vs 11.2% YoY; operating performance improved despite volume drop
items.quote: And EBITDA, by and large, you look at it, we are at 11.4 versus 11.9. Though the drop of sales is about 15%, the drop in EBITDA is lower. However, it's not as low as the drop in sales, that's mainly due to the better operating performance and middle-class performance during this quarter.

items.statement: New Axle MS 185 SOP started and ramping up well for Ashok Leyland; bus axle and 177 axle planned for launch in next few quarters
items.quote: And also, as we mentioned in the previous quarter, we introduced our new Axle MS 185 to Ashok Leyland. And not only have we started the SOP, but we are also able to ramp up the production very well.

items.statement: Share of business with Ashok Leyland currently 63-65%; targeting 65%+ with new product launches (MS 185, bus axle, 177)
items.quote: So, our current share is around 63% to 65% depending on the product mix. Typically, that is where we range. And with the new products that we are planning to launch in a couple of months, we should be 65% plus, that is what we are aiming for.

items.statement: Exports grown ~25% vs FY22; focus on intra-company exports to Meritor global units; new products (177, 185) are global platforms enabling export
items.quote: And your question earlier on the growth, I just pulled out some numbers, which may not be very accurate, but we have grown about 25% compared to 2021-22 to the current year. And all the new products also what we are now working on, we are bringing them to the global standard.

items.statement: Aftermarket sales benefited Q2 from last quarter's backlog completion; aftermarket contribution close to double digits annually
items.quote: And second is about this quarter we had some better benefits coming from sales to the aftermarket, which was probably one of the last quarter's backlog, and we completed this quarter.

items.statement: Metal cost performance focus over last six years yielding benefits; fixed cost under-absorption main margin headwind at current volumes
items.quote: Only what we are a little suffocating at this moment of time is basically the fixed cost absorption. So, as I said that, we continue in market at the same level, you can see the same level of performance of EBITDA in the next six months.

items.statement: Investments focused on manufacturing automation and debottlenecking to improve operating efficiency; capacity upgrades aligned with new product launches
items.quote: As Nagaraja was talking about the investments, the investments is basically meant to automate and debottleneck the issues in the production and on towards so the investment to the new products and so on and so forth.

items.statement: Bharat Forge acquisition of American Axle India CV business announced but not completed; transaction subject to legal/anti-competition approvals; management declines comment until details available
items.quote: There is just an announcement that has come, but this transaction is not complete. It goes through all the legal proceedings, including anti-competition and everything. So, that's why we said that it is probably premature at this point of time to make any comments on this.

items.statement: ROCE currently ~21%; could improve to 24-25%+ with volume growth; axle business has higher engineering content and margins than brakes
items.quote: Overall basis, you really see that our ROCE is at around 21%. As the volume grows, we can able to overall the ROCE can improve much beyond 24 or 25.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; leadership team includes President & WTD Nagaraja, CFO Ranganathan, Meritor India President Kishan Kumar
items.quote: We have with us Mr. Nagaraja – President and Whole-Time Director, Automotive Axles; Mr. Ranganathan S. – CFO, Automotive Axles and Mr. Kishan Kumar – GM, Meritor of India.

items.statement: Targets 25-30% revenue CAGR over next 5 years with exports ~40% of revenue
items.quote: Paramount is now expected to grow its top line with a CAGR of minimum 25 %-30% over the next 5 years with its exports mainly through our distribution network in the US accounting for around 40% of the total revenue.

items.statement: Expects INR1,800 crore revenue by FY26 from existing plants after brownfield capex
items.quote: So in terms of tonnage, we are looking at roughly 33,000 tons of metal processing capacity , by FY '26 and this should mean revenues of roughly INR1,800 crores.

items.statement: Expects US exports to cross INR500 crore in FY25
items.quote: we should be crossing INR500 crores in exports to the US this year

items.statement: Spent INR62 crore in FY24 and INR27 crore in H1 FY25 on brownfield capex to debottleneck existing plants
items.value: INR62 crores in FY24 and INR27 crores in H1 of FY25
items.quote: The company has incurred a capital expenditure payment of INR62 crores in FY24 and INR27 crores in H1 of FY25.

items.statement: Targets 33,000 tons metal processing capacity by FY26 via brownfield expansion of two existing plants
items.quote: So in terms of tonnage, we are looking at roughly 33,000 tons of metal processing capacity , by FY '26

items.statement: Order book of INR619 crore as of Oct 1 2024 (INR427 cr domestic, INR192 cr export); firm-price orders limited to 4-month delivery
items.quote: The pending order as on 1st of October 2014 was INR619 crores out of which domestic cable orders was INR427 crores and the export orders were INR192 crores pending.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin 9.38% vs 9.13% YoY; H1 FY25 EBITDA margin 9.31% vs 8.94% YoY; PAT margin compressed due to first-time tax incidence
items.quote: Our EBITDA is INR33.6 crores with a margin of 9.38% as against INR23.2 crores with a margin of 9.13% in the same quarter of the previous year

items.statement: Strong power cable demand driven by infrastructure capex (renewables, metros, private sector); railway signaling and telecom (BharatNet) provide additional tailwinds
items.quote: Power cable has got currently the strongest tailwinds, number one. The reason is that there is so much activity happening in the country.

items.statement: Power cables 50% of Q2 cable sales (up from 39% YoY); railway, house wire, telecom, others comprise rest; mix shifts opportunistically based on margin and volume
items.quote: By the way, the power cable sales have constituted roughly 50% of the total cable sales for the company in this quarter, as against 39% of the previous year quarter.

items.statement: US exports INR271 cr in FY24 (down from INR400 cr in FY23 due to price/freight drop, volume -4%); 8 distributors now vs 2 in 2020; US market ~$47 bn
items.quote: We achieved US exports of INR400 crores in FY23 and INR271 crores in FY24

items.statement: Working capital days improved from 137 days (Mar 24) to 109 days (H1 FY25); higher than peers due to limited channel financing on small B2C/distribution sales (INR56 cr H1)
items.quote: our H1 working capital days have come down to 100, just let me put out my notes. So our working capital has come down from 137 days for 31st March 24 to 109 days in -- for H1

items.statement: Became debt-free in Aug 2024 after prepaying ARC dues; only INR15 cr small loans (insurance policy surrender value, vehicle loans); debt-equity 0.02
items.quote: In August 24, we prepaid all our dues to the ARC, the Asset Reconstruction Company and since then we have become a debt-free company.

items.statement: Raised ~INR274 cr via fresh equity in past two years; promoters infused INR128 cr since 2010 (INR45 cr in last two years)
items.quote: Paramount raised approximately INR274 crores during the past two years from investors by way of fresh equity.

items.statement: Firm-price export orders hedged by booking metal next working day; distribution sales too small (INR56 cr H1) to cause margin compression from metal volatility
items.quote: we are always booking our metal practically on the next working day of finalizing the order with our distributors there in U.S.

items.statement: US exports face 5% duty vs zero for Korea, Vietnam, Cambodia, Mexico; would benefit if uniform duty imposed
items.quote: My competitor from South Korea gets zero duty, my competitor from Vietnam gets zero duty, my competitor even from Cambodia gets zero duty. And Mexico gets zero duty, I pay 5%.

items.statement: PAT growth muted for ~3 quarters due to YoY comparison with zero-tax periods; tax incidence started Q2 FY25
items.quote: I think to my guess is that for the next two quarters, we will see a similar position, because every quarter will be compared with the previous year's quarter in which there is zero tax

items.statement: Metal consumption (volume proxy) grew 53% YoY in H1 FY25 to 10,757 tons vs 7,035 tons
items.quote: The company consumed a total of 10,757 tons of metal in this H1 FY '25 as against 7,035 metric ton for the last year, showing a growth of 53%.

items.statement: Plans new Greenfield facility (capacity equal to existing two plants) or acquisition for FY27 growth beyond INR1,800 cr limit of current plants
items.quote: we would need to set up a new Greenfield facility with a capacity roughly equal to the existing two plants.

items.statement: Promoter stake below 50%; no family resources to increase stake; prefers smaller share of larger company
items.quote: I would love to have my stake go up to 50% plus. I don't think currently I see any of the promoter family having the resources to try and increase our stake.

items.statement: Revenue guidance of INR 750 crores for FY25 and INR 1,500 crores for FY28 with 30%+ EBITDA margin maintained
items.quote: Correct. Yes, so there is no revision to any guidance that we shared previously.

items.statement: Second half of FY25 expected to be stronger than first half with Q2 as softest quarter
items.quote: The second half of the year has always been stronger for MPS, if you go even years back and whether Q3 is stronger or Q4 is stronger, ends up being a debate every year, but the second half of the year is the strongest for MPS.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 30.11% in Q2 FY25, expected to improve further by Q4 FY25
items.quote: EBITDA margins bounced back to 30.11% in Q2 FY '25 and overall EBITDA grew by 31.90% in Q2 FY '25 compared to last year.

items.statement: Content Solutions EBITDA margin expanded to 38.36% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Revenue in the Content Solutions business grew by ~37% in Q2 of FY '25 compared to last year. EBITDA margins expanded to 38.36% as AJE settled well into MPS.

items.statement: Platform business EBITDA margin at 28% of consolidated revenue and 40% of consolidated EBITDA
items.quote: Revenue quality is also improving with platforms responsible for 28% of the consolidated revenue and even more impressively 40% of the consolidated

items.statement: eLearning EBITDA margin recovered to 19% in Q2 FY25, would have been 22.8% without currency impact
items.quote: Revenue grew by 8.8% in Q2 FY '25 compared to the same period last year, and EBITDA margins recovered to 19% in the quarter.

items.statement: AJE already PAT-positive with high double-digit EBITDA margin, improving incrementally in Q3 and Q4
items.quote: From AJE's perspective, we are already PAT-positive. The business is performing well. There is already a high double-digit EBITDA margin. And yes, it will improve incrementally between Q3 and Q4

items.statement: Target eLearning EBITDA margin of 27%-28% near-term, 30%-32% long-term
items.quote: In the long run, we want the business to be as close to the average EBITDA margin of the company, which is 30%- 32%. Even if it doesn't go all the way to 30%-32%, achieving 27%-28% would be a very strong step.

items.statement: Content Solutions revenue grew ~37% Y-o-Y in Q2 FY25, journals and OWL education business driving growth
items.quote: Revenue in the Content Solutions business grew by ~37% in Q2 of FY '25 compared to last year.

items.statement: Platform revenue grew ~67% Y-o-Y in Q2 FY25 primarily due to AJE acquisition
items.quote: Primarily due to the acquisition of AJE, the platform business grew by ~67% in revenue in Q2 of FY '25, compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: Content business expected to grow 10%-12% reliably, Platform 12%-14%, eLearning 14%-15% organic growth from FY26
items.quote: To summarize, content 10%-12%, platform 12%-14%, and then eLearning 14%-15% organic growth.

items.statement: Won new logo away from largest Content Hosting Platforms competitor, seeing influx of RFIs and RFPs
items.quote: Another highlight was the success of our business development efforts. For example, earlier this financial year, we won a new logo away from our largest Content Hosting Platforms space competitor.

items.statement: Exhibition project Phase 1 consulting report this calendar year, Phase 2 execution in calendar 2025 for marquee Indian customer
items.quote: So, our assessment is this calendar year, we will submit our consulting report on what that experience center should look like, and then calendar year 2025, we will be executing on the experience center.

items.statement: Top 10 customers now contribute 48% of revenue, down from higher concentration in 2012
items.quote: Our top 10 customers now contribute to 48% of our revenue, a much lower customer concentration than when we started this journey in 2012.

items.statement: 15 new logos acquired in eLearning in H1 FY25, each meeting strategic criteria (10k+ employees, $3B+ revenue, or strategic sector)
items.quote: As Archana described, we have already onboarded 15 new logos in MPS Interactive alone in the first half of the year.

items.statement: Large Australian banking customer reactivated at Liberate, now back in top 10 accounts
items.quote: At Liberate Learning, the top 10 accounts now include a Large Banking Customer that was dormant for the past several months due to their internal corporate development activities.

items.statement: Reinvestment primarily into MPS Labs (R&D hub) to drive organic growth while maintaining 30% EBITDA margin
items.quote: Most of our reinvestment goes into MPS Labs, which is our R&D hub. And that allows us to future-proof ourselves but also allows us to future-proof our customers.

items.statement: Transitioning eLearning to gig/contractor model from full-time employees, headcount stabilizing at new lower level
items.quote: We are consciously transitioning from a model that is heavily reliant on full-time employees to a more flexible and elastic delivery structure where we leverage contractors and gig workers.

items.statement: Content Solutions headcount declining due to MPS Labs automation while revenue per FTE increases
items.quote: With MPS Labs' larger intervention in the content business, based on the automation that's getting unlocked, we are seeing a steady decline in the headcount in the content solutions space while the revenue per FTE is increasing.

items.statement: Corporate learning budgets slower decision-making but education/training gets boost in slowdown, outsourcing increases when customers reduce headcount
items.quote: We are having to work much harder for the same level of order book. So, I think decision-making is slower. Having lived through '08, '09, and other experiences like this, typically, education and training get a boost when there is a slowdown.

items.statement: Expanding hedging to Australian dollar and Chinese Yuan, forwards booking expected from Q1 calendar year
items.quote: As that is changing, we now have exposure to both the Australian dollar and the Chinese Yuan. And we are actively working to create some protection around, that we will start to see from next calendar year onwards.

items.statement: Consolidated DSO improved to 44 days, eLearning DSO at 36 days, collections improved
items.quote: The theme of improvement in the quality of revenue can also be observed through improvement on DSO to 44 days.

items.statement: Deferred liability from Liberate acquisition caused 4.3% EBITDA impact (INR 1.5 crores) in Q2 due to exchange fluctuation

items.quote: On the number front, for this quarter, equipment sales reached ₹22.5 crore, with a margin of ₹5.7 crore. Of this, approximately ₹17 crore in revenue and ₹4.7 crore in direct margin came from the Middle East, significantly contributing to our overall performance.

items.statement: Multiplex screen count increased from 1,565 in 2020 to 2,122 currently, while total screens slightly declined from 3,792 to 3,735 due to single-screen closures.
items.quote: In 2020, we had 3,792 screens, with 1,565 of those being multiplexes. Today, while our total screen count is slightly lower at 3,735, our multiplex count has increased to 2,122.

items.statement: Ad revenue share with exhibitors increased due to acquisitions of ~400 southern screens in January with higher minimum guarantees; share dropped from 85% in Q1 to 69% in Q2.
items.quote: For instance, if revenue per screen is around ₹4.5 lakh, the share could be approximately 60–65%. As we approach higher revenues per screen, closer to ₹8–9 lakh, the share would drop to around 40–45%. You can actually observe this trend in our numbers: in Q1, the share was nearly 85%, and by Q2, it has reduced to 69%.

items.statement: Consolidated cash at end of Q2 FY25 was Rs. 998 million; net cash was Rs. 409 million after outstanding debt.
items.quote: The consolidated cash at the end of quarter was at Rs. 998 million and the net cash was Rs.409 million after considering outstanding debt.

items.statement: No buyback discussions; technically not possible due to accumulated losses from earlier periods despite current net cash position.
items.quote: However, there are no discussions around a buyback, and technically, it isn’t possible due to accumulated losses. So, even though th ere’s no buyback consideration, our focus is on getting the business back on track

items.statement: Caravan Cinema business sees traction with state government support and events like elections; activity drops in monsoon, expects uptick in winter.
items.quote: As winter approaches, we expect to see an uptick in this business, particularly in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Nova Cinemas launched one property in Uttar Pradesh; second set to open during Diwali alongside major releases Singham and Bhool Bhulaiyaa.
items.quote: We recently launched one property in Uttar Pradesh, with a second set to open during Diwali alongside major releases like "Singham" and "Bhool Bhulaiyaa".

items.statement: Digital cinema advertising is less than 1% of overall ad spend; requires substantial effort to regain advertiser mindshare as 99% budgets allocated elsewhere.
items.quote: To put it into perspective, digital cinema currently makes up less than 1% of the overall advertising expenditure, So, what that means is 99% of adver tising budgets are already allocated elsewhere.

items.statement: Ad minutes sold per show per screen at 2.68 in H1 FY25; management sees potential to double volume and pricing, with 55-60% of incremental revenue flowing to PBT.
items.quote: For instance, if I were to double my current 2.7 minutes of advertising per show and double my pricing, I could theoretically see four times my existing sales. Importantly, this increase would not come with a proportional increase in expenses like sharing . Therefore, around 55 -60% of my incremental revenue would directly contribute to profit before tax (PBT).

items.statement: Merger of 100% subsidiaries (formed for DCI business) approved by NCLT in January; streamlines corporate structure, saves operational costs, no impact on consolidated numbers.
items.quote: Regarding the merger, it involved some of our 100% subsidiaries, formed for spe cific purposes, primarily related to our DCI business. One of these companies was acquired in 2011 -12 and later became a 100% subsidiary. The purpose of the scheme was to streamline our corporate structure, merging these entities back into the holding company.

items.statement: NCLT order approving amalgamation scheme received in Q4 FY24; prior year Q2 numbers restated for apple-to-apple comparison.
items.quote: The effect was applied immediately after the order was received, which was in Q4 of last year. The issue her e is that we are comparing Q2 of the current year with Q2 of last year. However, in Q2 of the previous year, the order had not yet been received, so last year's Q2 numbers did not reflect the impact of this order.

items.statement: Total revenue up 11% YoY in Q2 FY25 driven by 7% theatrical revenue growth and 79% YoY growth in Sale of Product, offsetting 17% YoY ad revenue decline.
items.quote: However, a 7% increase in theatrical revenue and a 79% YoY growth in Sale of product supported overall performance, resulting in an 11% YoY increase in total revenue this quarter.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY25 stood at Rs. 968 million vs Rs. 871 million in Q2 FY24; H1 FY25 revenue Rs. 1,913 million vs Rs. 1,725 million in H1 FY24.
items.quote: The consolidated revenue for Q2 FY25 stood at Rs. 968 million, as against Rs. 871 million in Q2 FY24, primarily driven by Sale of Product.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 net loss of Rs. 9 million vs net profit of Rs. 33 million YoY; improved from net loss of Rs. 42 million in Q1 FY25.
items.quote: The company reported a net loss of Rs. 9 mn in Q2FY25, compared to a Net profit of ₹ 33 mn in Q2FY24 and improved from the net loss of Rs. 42 mn in

items.statement: H1 FY25 net loss of Rs. 50 million vs profit of Rs. 58 million in H1 FY24.
items.quote: On the PAT front, the company reported a net loss of Rs. 50 mn in H1FY25 against a profit of Rs. 58 mn in H1FY24.

items.statement: Middle East equipment sales steady; Saudi Arabia market opening last year resulted in decent uptick, expecting volumes to remain high.
items.quote: In the Middle East, particularly, the opening of Saudi Arabia's market last year resulted in a decent uptick, and we expect volumes to remain high in this region.

items.statement: 470 movies released (including versions/languages) in Q2 FY25 vs 484 in Q2 FY24 and 476 in Q1 FY25.
items.quote: In total, 470 movies were released (including versions/languages) during the quarter, compared to 484 in Q2FY24 and 476 in Q1FY25.

items.statement: FY25 revenue guidance of around INR725 crores with EBITDA margin around 21%
items.quote: I'm pleased to inform you all that we have delivered a strong quarter with 48% increase in revenues Q-o-Q basis and 122% increase in EBITDA Q-o-Q, in line with the guidance given in Q1. The second half is expected to be stronger than the first half. We expect to achieve revenues of around -- overall revenues for the year for around INR725 crores with a margin around 21% by end of FY '25.

items.statement: Sequential margin improvement expected in H2 FY25 due to operating leverage and batch production ramp-up in MNC Aerospace
items.quote: We anticipate EBITDA margins will improve in H2 because of higher operating leverage due to increased revenues and optimization of costs driven by the improved operational efficiencies once we enter into batch production in MNC Aerospace division and also other verticals.

items.statement: Closing order book at end of Q2 FY25 around INR940 crores; targeting INR1,400-1,500 crores by end of FY25 including Kaiga 5&6 orders
items.quote: So the overall order book as of end of Q2, I think, is around INR940 crores. And the orders that we have won for this quarter is around INR247 crores in all. So that's what it is. And by end of the year, as I mentioned earlier, that we're looking at INR1,400 crores to INR1,500 crores.

items.statement: Bloom Energy closing order book stands at INR493 crores; expecting similar execution in H2 FY25
items.quote: The closing order book for Bloom Energy stands at INR493 crores. We are expecting similar execution in H2.

items.statement: Bloom Energy increased forecast from 3,000 to 4,000 units for calendar year 2025; potential for further upward revision
items.quote: We are optimistic about growth in clean energy in FY'26 as Bloom gave an indication for execution of 4,000 units in calendar year 2025 as against an initial indication of 3,000 units.

items.statement: Nuclear sector expecting more than INR500 crores of orders in H2 FY25 from Kaiga 5&6 and reactor refurbishment
items.quote: As I said, we're ex pecting more than INR500 crores worth of orders coming in from nuclear in the second half of this year

items.statement: Clean energy vertical executed INR192 crores in H1 FY25 with 1,808 hotbox units and 36 electrolyzers dispatched
items.quote: In clean energy, we have executed around INR192 crores of orders in the first half of the year. We have dispatched 1,808 units of hotbox units and 36 units of electrolyzers.

items.statement: MNC Aerospace vertical delivered INR17 crores in H1 FY25; expecting INR45 crores execution in H2 FY25 with 45% revenue growth over next 3-4 years
items.quote: We have witnessed a substantial growth in space in line with our predictions in the first half where we have delivered around INR17 crores of orders in MNC aerospace for the first time. We expect to execute around INR45 crores of orders from MNC aerospace with H2.

items.statement: Civil nuclear power plant execution expected INR60 crores in FY25; 40-45% growth projected for FY26 backed by refurbishment and Kaiga 5&6 reactors
items.quote: So, we expect to deliver around INR60 crores of orders in FY '25 in this sector on a cumulative basis. This sector is expected to witness a 40% -45% growth in FY '26 backed by robust order book and strong order pipeline from refurbishment of reactors and Kaiga - five and six reactors.

items.statement: Products vertical executed INR71 crores in H1 FY25; targeting nearly INR140 crores annual revenue by end FY25 with >30% growth predicted
items.quote: We have registered a final growth in products with INR71 crores of execution in the first half. We expect to execute nearly INR140 crores of revenue from products on an annual basis by end of FY '25. This vertical is predicted to register a growth of more than 30% over the coming quarters.

items.statement: New exclusive aerospace facility in Hyderabad to be commissioned by end of December 2024 for MNC customers
items.quote: We are establishing a new exclusive aerospace facility by end of December this year. We are doing -- we are taking all the required steps to achieve what we are trying to tell us that's the goal for the company.

items.statement: Net working capital days at 247 days in Q2 FY25; targeting reduction to 220 days by end of FY25
items.quote: Our net working capital to revenue days are 247 days and we are targeting to reduce to 220 days by end of financial year FY25.

items.statement: Long-term debt reduced by INR16 crores from INR142.5 crores to INR126.4 crores; total repayment obligation of INR45 crores by end of FY25
items.quote: The company has reduced the long-term debt by INR16 crores bringing it down to INR142.5 crores to INR126.4 crores, out of the total repayment obligation of INR45 crores by end of this year.

items.quote: Already a lot of first articles have been done. We are moving into the batch production like we're looking Buikling Nation with at voice, we're looking at Andritz, GE, Regen Power is another company which has joined us. So we are adding a lot of clients

items.quote: See, the good news is that we have finalized various agreements with very good MNCs, as we have said earlier, with I AI, with GKN Aerospace and stuff like that. So we are continuing to work on various projects with them on the first artical basis.

items.statement: Outsourcing costs (plasma coating in US) to come down drastically as in-house qualification progresses; other expenses to normalize in next two quarters
items.quote: Now, we have the equipment coming in and the qualification is going on. So, a lot of a ctivities happening in that area to reduce our costs drastically down. If you look at the other expenses those things are going to come down drastically moving forward

items.statement: Q2 FY25 revenue INR190.2 crores (48.3% QoQ growth); EBITDA INR36.8 crores (121.7% QoQ growth); EBITDA margin 19.3%
items.quote: Quarter-on-quarter, when it comes to quarter-on-quarter performance, we achieved a robust quarter with revenue growth of 48.3%, reaching INR190.2 crores in Q2 FY 2025 compared to INR128.3 crores in Q1 FY 2025. EBITDA improved significantly, standing at INR36.8 crores in Q2 FY '25, up to 121.7% from INR16.6 crores in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Clean energy FY25 revenue projection INR380-400 crores; Space FY25 revenue projection INR55-60 crores
items.quote: So, as I said, we're looking at about -- in the clean energy segment, probably we'll doing around INR380 crores to INR400 crores, INR380 crores odd for FY '25. And in the space sector, we're looking at around close to about INR55 crores to INR60 crores of revenues coming in, in the space segment as such.

items.statement: Bloom Energy forecast revisions occur quarterly; 4,000 unit forecast for CY2025 may increase further by end of Q3 FY25
items.quote: See, they normally -- presently, they're releasing orders based on quarter-to-quarter basis, but they give forecast for the calendar year, in fact. So right now, from 3,000, they have increased it to 4,000 units for next calendar year, which can even go up further.

items.statement: Roller Screws certification delay due to rigorous defense testing for 100% import substitute; only paperwork remains pending
items.quote: Yes, there has been a delay but the issue here is that to certify a product which is a 100% import substitute they have to do all the trials to ensure that it is at par with the import product what they're getting it right now which they have now it's been done so the process itself took that much time.

items.statement: Defense JV not yet finalized; focusing on direct agreements with MNCs like IAI and GKN Aerospace instead
items.quote: Not as yet. See, the good news is that we have finalized various agreements with very good MNCs, as we have said earlier, with I AI, with GKN Aerospace and stuff like that. So we are continuing to work on various projects with them on the first artical basis.

items.statement: Cash flow from operations INR18 crores in Q2 FY25; targeting to surpass FY24 annual cash flow of INR57.4 crores by end of FY25
items.quote: Cash flow from operations stands at INR18 crores in Q2 FY25 with the goal of surpassing FY24's annual cash flow of INR57.4 crores by end of FY 2025 with increased revenue projections.

items.statement: Project more than doubling volume in Andhra Pradesh from FY24 level of 1.7 million cases on annualized basis
items.quote: We project more than doubling our volume in AP state from FY24 level of 1.7 million cases on an annualized basis.

items.statement: Expect 300 basis point improvement in EBITDA margins over three years from capex projects
items.quote: In current year FY25 we'll be incurring about what we expect a 300 basis point improvement in the EBITDA margins over the same period and would be ROCE accretive.

items.statement: Expect H2 ENA prices to be 2-3% higher than H1
items.quote: We are expecting the H2 ENA prices to be about 2%-2.5%. I mean, this is just a broad estimate at this point of time, but we expect it to be higher between 2%-3% in H2 versus H1.

items.quote: So overall we will be investing about INR525 crores of capex over a period of three years which will be funded through a combination of internal accruals and debt.

items.quote: So, of the INR527 crores, year one is INR185 crores. Year two will need about INR220 crores, and year three will need about the balance INR120 crores.

items.quote: The gross margin improved to 42.9% in quarter 2 of FY '25 as Allied Blenders and compared to 38.7% in Q1 of FY '25 and 39.2% in Q2 FY '24

items.statement: EBITDA margin at roughly 12% in Q2, targeting 15% industry parity over 2-3 years from capex projects
items.quote: if you see our Q2 EBITDA is roughly 12%. So the incremental EBITDA that this project will deliver is roughly 300 basis points.

items.statement: Expect price increases in coming financial year to be no different than current year at mixed level
items.quote: So for now as we see things, I think even for the coming financial year, we expect price increases to be no different than what we have seen in the current financial year.

items.statement: Anticipate positive shift in consumer sentiment in festive season driving market growth
items.quote: First a little bit about the industry as we move into the festive season, we anticipate a positive shift in consumer sentiment which is expected to drive market growth.

items.quote: The growth was led by premiumization of the portfolio with continued increase in P&A volume salience to 39.7% in Q2 FY '25 as compared to 36.9% in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Telangana receivables at INR350 crores, expect significant reduction by Q4 FY25 as payments now coming daily
items.quote: So at the end of Q2, the overview are by and large in the same range, about INR350 odd crores. So there has been some change, but not significant. And again, if we were to go by the guidance that we received from Telangana, we do expect a significant reduction.

items.statement: Peak debt for capex projects expected at INR200 crores, overall debt to come down as Telangana overdues get paid
items.quote: So, like I said earlier the INR525 crores of debt is spread across three years. INR185 crores in year 1, INR220 crores in year 2 and about 100 balanced debt in year 3. items.statement: Launched Zoya gin in Goa and Rajasthan, planning two new flavors and key markets in Q3 FY25, expanding to UAE

items.quote: Earlier, we have given the guidance of 100 bps reduction. But now we have revised the EBITDA margin guidance, 100 bps improvement over last year.

items.quote: I feel that farmer is going to have a good recovery for Kharif sales and Rabi acreages, and Rabi opportunity is appearing very positive, in fact, very bright.

items.quote: ITI index is 16.3% -- 16.09% in this half year basis as compared to last year's 16.39%.

items.quote: LaNevo from Nissan, Dhanuka is exclusive. Purge again from Nissa n, Japan, Dhanuka is exclusive. MYCORe SUPER is Dhanuka's exclusive product. Zanet is exclusively available to Dhanuka.

items.quote: Rs. 600 crores to Rs. 650 crores anywhere in between is what we are trying to target.
