items.quote: We saw INR27 increase in our PAPMs, with learning additions increasing by 23%.

items.statement: Specialized staffing EBITDA up 18% YoY and 26% QoQ in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Even though our revenue dipped slightly, our profitability has improved over the last few quarters. EBITDA is up by 18% year-on-year and 26% sequentially, largely due to cost-saving efforts and some onetime sourcing and absorption benefits.

items.statement: Specialized staffing had INR80 lakh one-time absorption fees in Q2 FY25
items.quote: So in specialized staffing this quarter, we had close to about INR80 lakh of absorption fees, so which is a onetime sourcing fee that we get from clients.

items.statement: HR Services target 6-8% EBITDA margin FY25, 8-10% sustainable in coming years
items.quote: So at annual level, we should be able to make 6% to 8% EBITDA margin in other HR Services this year, and that can improve to 8% to 10% sustainable margins in the coming years.

items.statement: Standalone staffing potential to expand margins up to 1.5% over 18-24 months
items.quote: even on a stand-alone basis, staffing has a potential to expand margins up to 1.5%. But again, that's subject to whether it is going to happen in the 18 months or 24 months is subject to external behaviors as well.

items.statement: General staffing growth driven by consumer, telecom, early BFSI recovery in H1 FY25
items.quote: Our core growth driver in H1 that consumables, telecom and early-stage recovery within BFSI, each contributing significantly to our performance.

items.statement: Quick commerce and organized retail boom driving associate additions
items.quote: We have also benefited from the boom in quick commerce and organized retail. This structural shift towards compliance and productivity and workforce management in some of these sectors has helped us grow our head count.

items.statement: Telecom benefiting from nationwide network upgrades and infrastructure investment
items.quote: In the telecom vertical, continues to benefit from the nationwide expansion, which is taking place in network upgrades. With additional investments in infrastructure and network growth, this sector remains promising for sustained associate additions in the month ahead.

items.statement: BFSI seeing measured revival in microfinance, payments, affordable housing but cautious on Q3
items.quote: We are seeing a measured revival within micro finance, payment services and affordable housing. It's too early to call it. We'll have to wait and see how it plays out in Q3.

items.statement: Specialized staffing tech talent demand showing gradual improvement, GCCs growing
items.quote: From a specialized staffing standpoint, we see that the tech talent demand is showing gradual signs of improvement. However, with the current focus in the industry on resource optimization and upskilling, we don't expect a big surge in open positions right away. On a positive note, we are seeing growth in many of the GCCs we partner with and further nontech industry by ramping up the digital trans

items.statement: IT services hiring closures taking longer (18-24 months), growth from GCCs and non-tech
items.quote: On the IT services hiring bit, while there are a lot of open positions that are coming in, closures are actually taking slightly longer than what it used to happen earlier. I'm talking about 18 to 24 months time frame. So we don't -- so we have not done an addition on the IT services hiring. Most of the hiring has come from GCCs and the nontech sector, at least in Q2.

items.statement: GCC contribution to specialized staffing revenue grew from 40% (18 months ago) to 60% now
items.quote: GCC contribution, about 18 months back, was at 40% on revenue. And about the year back, it's at 50%. So we are consistently adding numbers and clients on GCC front, and that's also helping us to improve margins overall.

items.statement: Partner with 65 GCCs, added 10 new GCCs in H1 FY25
items.quote: Today, we have about 65 GCCs that we partnered with. We believe that this number is going to grow. In fact, over the last 2 quarters, H1, we signed about 10 new GCCs that are getting onboarded right now as we see.

items.statement: RBI KYC strictures may suppress BFSI hiring outlook for Q3 FY25
items.quote: there is some strictures, which are coming across specific to KYC that RBI is calling out. So we are anticipating is it possible that there might be some sort of a unit response coming in from largely BSFI sector.

items.statement: PM Internship Scheme and UGC AEDP guidelines creating tailwinds for Degree Apprenticeship
items.quote: the employment -linked incentive under the constituent of the Prime Minister's Internship scheme, the PMIS, were the key initiatives that were launched in Q2. So this scheme aimed at reaching 10 million youth in 5 years, offers a very promising path for industry -aligned skills and draws more youth on corporates into apprenticeship opportunities. So in addition, the UGC also launched the draft gui

items.statement: Free cash INR340 crore as of 30 Sep 2024, working capital metrics steady
items.quote: Balance sheet metrics, like receivables ratio, DSO, working capital ratio, ROCE, are all steadily maintained. There is an increase in working capital borrowing at EdTech business level, which is in line with the business growth. Free cash stands at INR340 crores as of 30th September 2024.

items.statement: Increase in working capital borrowing at EdTech business in line with growth
items.quote: There is an increase in working capital borrowing at EdTech business level, which is in line with the business growth.

items.statement: Evaluating M&A options to expand HR Tech product portfolio and client base
items.quote: In HR Tech vertical, we are evaluating M&A options to expand our product portfolio and client base.

items.statement: Looking at inorganic additions to complement HCM business
items.quote: HCM is the only one where we continue to make investments. We're lo oking at complementing the HCM business with some element of inorganic additions also so that it gets heft and product portfolio

items.statement: FTE productivity improved 1.7% in H1 FY25, FTE per recruiter up 2% to 387
items.quote: During H1, FTE, full-time equivalent productivity improved by 1.7%. FTE has improved by 2% to 387 headcount, owing to a 6% increase in associate headcount in Q2, enabling us to manage a larger workforce effectively and support more clients without additional overhead.

items.statement: Group headcount 3.5 lakh+, added 18,000 in Q2 FY25 vs 13,000 YoY
items.quote: At a group level, we added nearly 18,000 head count, largely coming in from across sect ors in the Staffing and DA

items.statement: Hired 26,000 associates in Q2 FY25 via internal/external channels, up 29% QoQ and 16% YoY
items.quote: We hired nearly 26,000 associates during Q2 through our sources, which is a 29% increase quarter -on-quarter and a 16% incre ase from the same period last year

items.statement: 80JJAA tax benefit continues with no sunset, effective tax rate 0% for standalone for 3-5 years
items.quote: On 80JJAA, as of now, there is no sunset. So we continue to claim this benefit under our staffing business. So in stand-alone TeamLease financials, our effective tax rate can be 0 going to 80JJ benefit for at least for the next 3- to 5-year time frame.

items.statement: IT reassessment of FY16-17 80JJAA claims due to 8-year time-bar limit, no outstanding demands
items.quote: However, reopening the assessment of 2016 and '17 is more likely going with the time buying of income tax assessments, bec ause 8 years is the time barring limit. So that's the reason we believe those were reopened and kept, but whatever queries that have been given to us, we have been providing the documentation and addressing them. So we are not seeing any kind of challenge with respect to the c

items.statement: On track to meet FY26 revenue target of 3200 crores through organic and inorganic growth
items.quote: We are pretty much on track to meet our numbers as a combination of organic and inorganic, we are very much on track to meet our numbers.

items.statement: Capex plan of 600 crores over 3 years, with 200 crores this year and 150-180 crores next year
items.quote: I have always maintained that we are looking at around 600 crores of CAPEX over 3 years. And we are on track on the 600 crores of CAPEX and we are continuing to maintain the same outlook. And this year would again be about 200 crores. Correct me if I am wrong. I am requesting my CFO to correct my statement and next year will be about 150 to 180 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 13-13.5%, exports recovery could add 50 basis points
items.quote: I have always maintained in many quarters that our 13 to 13.5% EBITDA is what we intend to maintain and what looks reasonable for our set of products. Margins will be a little better when exports resume. Exports, this was probably the weakest quarter in many quarters, so when exports resume or comes back, margins will go up about 50 basis points.

items.statement: Domestic 2-wheeler demand muted, Q3 expected very weak, exports muted due to US elections
items.quote: Demand is very muted in the industry. My industry peers also tell me that their performance is also very muted. And as usual, the Q3 Quarter, which traditionally is the lowest quarter in the automotive industry, will remain very muted, but a little more muted than normal. In terms of exports, because of the Elections in the US, and the policies of the Republican government that have come in, expor

items.statement: Exports at 6.5% of revenue vs 9% last year, US election impact on export demand
items.quote: Same quarter last year was about 9% and this year is about 6.5%.

items.statement: May raise up to 300 crores debt for acquisitions, currently debt-free with cash reserves
items.quote: We are a debt-free company. We have cash reserves. But depending on the size of the acquisition, we are not only looking at this. We are looking at other inorganic play also, safe inorganic play in allied areas and as I have maintained in my earlier calls, up to about 300 crores of debt, we are looking at probably raising based on the kind of acquisition.

items.statement: Management expects revenue to go up in H2 FY25 after closing non-core businesses
items.quote: No, now it should go up only. But whatever was there earlier because of the non-core businesses like a lot of product businesses which were there in colour, retail and other product businesses which we have closed down, which we have statistically decided not to pursue, so those have been closed.

items.statement: Banks floated RFPs for over 21,000 ATMs and CRMs in H1 FY25
items.quote: In H1 FY '25, banks have floated RFPs of more than 21,000 plus ATMs and CRMs. We expect this trend to persist furthermore, as digitalisation shapes banking trends like digital banking units, UPI integration, CRMs i.e Cash Recycling Machines and cassette swapping present new revenue streams, enabling us to further strengthen our cash payment portfolio.

items.statement: Tenders for around 25,000 new ATMs and CRMs seen in H1 FY25 with larger volumes expected in H2
items.quote: So, on the redeployment of ATMs and the new ATMs, if you look at it in the H1, we saw tender coming for around 25,000 new ATMs and CRMs and most of the deployment are in those regions across. So, we normally see an H2 which is higher than H1. So, we expect still larger volumes coming on to H2.

items.statement: Average monthly cash withdrawal per ATM increased from INR1.35 crore to INR1.43 crore YoY
items.quote: According to industry data, average monthly cash withdrawal from ATMs increased from INR1.35 crores in financial year 2022- 2023 to INR1.43 crores in financial year '23-'24, underscoring the continued demand for ATMs and CRMs as cash remains a preferred mode of transaction for many.

items.statement: Group EBITDA margin was 29.2% in H1 FY25 with steady margins due to no non-recurring expenses
items.quote: During H1-25, we reported a total income of INR7,197 million with EBITDA of INR2,100 million representing a 29.2% margin and a PAT of INR290 million.

items.statement: Securevalue India EBITDA margin improved from 17.1% to 20.1% YoY in H1
items.quote: The EBITDA has improved from INR 383 million to 429 million, which shows a margin gross from 17.1% to 20.1% margin. So, I think from that perspective, the numbers are good.

items.statement: Digital payment segment accounted for 14% of total revenue in Q2 FY25
items.quote: This quarter, our digital payment segment accounted for 14% of total revenue, reinforcing our steady growth within digital channels.

items.statement: Extended contract with Indian Bank for reconciliation services with projected revenue of INR50 crore over 3 years
items.quote: We have also successfully extended contract with Indian Bank for the reconciliation of card and non-card transactions. The projected revenue generation is expected to be about INR50 crores over the next three years.

items.statement: Managing prepaid platform for Indian Oil's XtraPower program with estimated revenue of INR58 crore over 5 years
items.quote: Additionally, we are providing end-to-end platform and management services, including prepaid card issuance for Indian Oil Corporation Limited's flagship program, XtraPower. This prepaid program is accepted at 25,000 IOCL fuel retail outlets, processing annual fueling transactions worth more than INR60,000 crores. This is a fixed income contract with an estimated revenue of about INR58 crores over

items.statement: Ongo contactless fueling pilot expanded to over 60 fuel outlets in Mumbai with 2,000 fleet vehicles onboarded
items.quote: Our ongoing pilot of contactless fueling solution on the Ongo app has expanded to over 60 fuel outlets in Mumbai, and we have onboarded about 2,000 fleet vehicles. This one-of-its-kind open-loop fueling solution by Ongo, which is expected to go live very soon and will be followed by a pan-India expansion.

items.statement: Plan to roll out Ongo fueling to 500 outlets by end of year with city-wise pan-India expansion
items.quote: So, we expect to roll out city-wise, maybe by 500 outlets by the end of the year.

items.statement: Issued around 60,000 NCMC cards to date targeting 25-30 lakh cards in 2-3 years
items.quote: To date, we have issued around 60,000 NCMC cards. The NCMC offers a unified payment solution for various modes of transport, including metro, buses, ferries, as well as parking and toll payments.

items.statement: ATM/CRM network of 70,000+ as of Sep 2024, servicing 32,151 ATMs including 7,230 CRMs under managed services
items.quote: As of 30 September 2024, we have installed, maintained or managed a network of approximately 70,000-plus ATMs and CRMs. We are servicing about 32,151 ATMs, including 7,230 CRMs under our managed services and outsourcing portfolio.

items.statement: Securevalue India services 31,093 ATMs/CRMs with daily replenishment of INR19.33 billion across 446 vaults and 2,370+ cash vans
items.quote: As on 30 September 2024, we have serviced about 31,093 ATMs and CRMs, replenishing daily average amount of INR19.33 billion. Securevalue India accounts for 446 vaults and spoke locations. We have about 587 pickup and doorstep banking points and a network of 2,370 plus secure cash vans across 1,800 plus cities and towns.

items.statement: Trade receivables increased due to new PSU bank order execution and milestone-linked payments; collection expected from Q3
items.quote: One, definitely we have executed a new order of one of the large public sector banks, where we have executed and delivered the project and now the realisation will happen in the quarter three. So, that is one aspect where we see the receivable will definitely start getting collected in the quarter three onwards.

items.statement: Net debt at INR6,839 million with reverse factoring and INR6,092 million without; term loans have confirmed repayment schedule
items.value: INR6,839 mn (with RF), INR6,092 mn (without RF)
items.quote: The net debt position of the company stood at INR6,839 million along with the reverse factoring and INR6,092 million without reverse factoring.

items.statement: Converted large contracts from transaction model to hybrid model to cover declining transactions and costs
items.quote: So, if you look at it in our commentary ahead, we have said that we have converted large contracts from a transaction model to an hybrid model across, so that we at least see what the transactions which are getting declined are covered and our costs are covered in the hybrid model across.

items.statement: ATM redeployment shifting from metros to semi-urban/rural areas where cash transactions remain high
items.quote: But the penetration of digitalization is only constrained to cities and metros. That's what I said across in my response to a query that a lot of redeployment of ATM is happening from metro to semi-urban and rural, where still transaction or cash is the mode of any payment.

items.statement: Management sees no credit risk on receivables as customers are renowned banks and PSUs
items.quote: From a credit risk perspective, I think we are dealing with very renowned customers including banks and public sector undertaking. So, we do not see any challenge with respect to credit risk on those customers.

items.statement: Hybrid model currently at 35%; will grow but large high-transaction contracts kept on transaction model
items.quote: So, if you look at it, our large contracts which have used transactions, we have still maintained it on transaction model, because we are seeing enough attraction and transaction because most of them are getting redeployed from a metro where transaction decline has happened, to semi-rural and urban areas. So, their transaction in those areas are still quite high to support a transaction-based mode

items.statement: Banks expect heavy transactions in semi-urban/rural for next 3-4 years per recent PSU RFP for 21,000 ATMs
items.quote: So, if you look at the recent public sector RFP, which came in for 21,000 from a single bank. So, they are expecting transactions to be heavy in semi-urban and rural for at least for the horizon of next 3 to 4 years.

items.statement: Other income driven by lease accounting write-backs, insurance income on cash losses, and interest on cash/FDs
items.quote: So, in case of other incomes, there are two-three major heads that come. One is definitely since we are having a lot of leases in our books of accounts. So, we have lease accounting that happens and there are write-backs of lease income that comes on those parts. That is one of the major income that comes in leasing. Then there are insurance incomes because of various cash losses that are pertaini

items.statement: Q2 revenue grew 6.25% YoY to Rs 347 cr despite bad monsoon and fewer wedding dates; festive mood drove recovery
items.quote: In this quarter, our company did a revenue of about Rs. 347 crores compared to the last year of Rs. 326 crores, which is a growth of about 6.25%.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 51 bps YoY to 42.17% in Q2; PAT grew 1.7%
items.quote: Our gross margin in this quarter also grew by about 51 basis points to 42.17% compared to last year's 41.6% and our PBT levels of the quarter significantly grew compared to the last quarter and our PAT levels grew by 1.7%.

items.statement: Added 16,000 sq ft via two new Varamahalakshmi stores in Q2; total retail area ~6.7 lakh sq ft across 63 stores in 17 cities, 4 states
items.quote: In this quarter, on the operations front, we have opened about 16,000 square feet of retail space, adding two new Varamahalakshmi Silks stores, and that takes our total retail area close to 6.7 lakh square feet.

items.statement: Planning 25,000 sq ft per quarter in Q3 and Q4 FY25 (45,000-50,000 sq ft total H2); all Varamahalakshmi format, 6-8 stores
items.quote: Rest of the year we are planning at the rate of Rs. 25,000 square feet per quarter. as you are aware in H1 we have added about Rs. 23,000 and odd and for Q3 and Q4, we are planning at the rate of Rs. 25,000 plus/minus each, that should be in the range of Rs. 45,000 to Rs. 50,000 per square feet henceforth.

items.statement: FY25 full-year revenue/EBITDA guidance deferred to end of Q3; FY26 target ~8 lakh sq ft total retail area; long-term 10-12% sq ft CAGR
items.quote: Probably by end of Q3 we will have a much more meaningful sense and probably that will be the right time for me to give you better guidance.

items.statement: Sales per sq ft annualised: Varamahalakshmi Rs 42,000-45,000, KLM ~Rs 12,000, KMR Rs 19,000-20,000; Varamahalakshmi store EBITDA 32-34%, KLM 23-24%
items.quote: On an annualized basis, we are expecting would be in the range of, in respect of, Varamahalakshmi it should be in the range of anywhere between Rs. 42,000 to Rs. 45,000 andnd KLM would be in the range of about Rs. 12,000 or so, and KMR should be in the range of about Rs. 19,000 to Rs. 20,000.

items.statement: Varamahalakshmi gross margin 43-45%, store opex ~11% vs company avg 15-16%; store EBITDA 32-34%
items.quote: Store level EBITDA for Varamahalakshmi will be in the range of about 32% to 34%.

items.statement: October SSG positive and much higher than expected; Q3 has ~7 extra wedding dates vs last year, Q4 ~9 extra; H2 wedding-heavy
items.quote: October has been good, especially if you see the calendar compared to last year and this year, Pitra Paksh calendar which is supposed to be the inauspicious period last year started from September 29th and went until October 15th or so. But this year, if you see, ended by September itself, so October onwards, both Dussehra festivity mood and Diwali festivity mood has kicked up.

items.statement: H1 SSG -6.5% (Q1 -20%, Q2 marginally negative); targeting full-year FY25 SSG +1-2%
items.quote: H1, as you are aware, the first quarter we had a negative of 20, minus -20 was there in SSG for Q1. Q2 we have improved, and overall if you take for H1 it was approximately minus -6.5 and H2, we are expected to recover the SSG, in fact recover from the negative of the H1 also. I am hoping that for the year end we should be at least 1% or 2% positive on SSGs.

items.statement: Shifted ad spend from print to digital; Q2 digital ad spend ~Rs 2.2 cr (doubled YoY); overall A&P down QoQ
items.quote: On an average, I think this quarter we spent about Rs. 2.2 crores.

items.statement: Budgeting Rs 4 cr for renovation of ~3 stores in FY25 from internal accruals
items.quote: Broadly, we are budgeting about Rs. 4 crores on renovation of approximately three stores. That will be met out of the internal generations of the company.

items.statement: Expect at least 100 bps margin improvement in H2 driven by wedding season
items.quote: There's a scope of margin improvement by about at least 1% or 100 basis points. So, this is what we are basing on. Considering that wedding season is kicking in, I think we should be able to deliver that.

items.statement: Added innerwear (male & female) as SIS in KLM stores; yielding strong results; planning more categories to make KLM one-stop family destination
items.quote: We have already started off with innerwear as a category and that category has been doing well. We will continuously try to see if we can add more categories in the entire value chain ecosystem to help KLM as a one-stop family destination store.

items.statement: 60% of saree revenue from weddings (65% for Varamahalakshmi); bride-focused; gifting & festivity balance
items.quote: If you take the entire, the way we look at the data, the way we analyze this, if you have to take between wedding and non -wedding wear, non-wedding meaning your festivity and any other occasions, at least 60% of the entire business comes from weddings.

items.statement: Rain impact in Tamil Nadu (Madurai) and Andhra (Vijayawada) ~Rs 10-15 cr revenue loss in H1
items.quote: Broadly about Rs. 15 crores. Generally, about Rs. 10 crores to Rs. 15 crores maybe clubbing together the impact in Andhra and Tamilnadu – a part of which was in Q2 also Overall for H1.

items.statement: Average rent Rs 80-85/sq ft (range Rs 60-140); rent-to-revenue ~4-4.5%
items.quote: Overall, in terms of when you take an average of Tier-1, Tier-2, Tier-3 put together, it ranges anywhere between Rs. 60 per square feet it went all the way to about Rs. 140 to Rs. 135 per square feet. So, average we have about Rs. 80, Rs. 85 is our average currently in the stores that we have opened.

items.statement: Lease tenure 9-15 years (avg 11-12 years); employee cost up due to pre-hiring/training for upcoming store pipeline
items.quote: So, the lease tenure anywhere goes from nine years to 15 years onwards, but average lease if you look at, At 11 to 12 years will be the average lease life that we currently have in the company.

items.statement: Tax raid in May 2023; accepted Rs 4.8 cr additional liability for 3 years in Q2; similar amount possible for remaining 3 years
items.quote: There was a tax raid on the company in May '23 . Though there was no major issues pointed out. As a practice they will do the reassessments for a period of six years. So, out of that, for the three years reassessment we had accepted an additional tax liability of Rs. 4.8 crores, which was taken into this quarter's books.

items.statement: H1 SSG negative due to negligible wedding dates and Pitra Paksh shift; H2 recovery dependent on wedding calendar execution
items.quote: If you see the current wedding calendar, which stands to be the single most important factor for our business, in H1 there are negligible dates and that's the reason why our SSG levels have been negative.

items.statement: FY25 total sq ft addition ~75,000 (vs initial 90,000 target); 15,000-20,000 sq ft spillover to Q1 FY26
items.quote: Totally I think close to 75,000 square feet we will be able to add in this financial year. There will be, as we initially planned, we have rolled over around 15,000 to 20,000 square feet for Q1 of next year.

items.statement: Long-term expansion beyond South India (North, East, West) over 10 years; cluster-based approach; quality over quantity
items.quote: So, if you want us to talk about 10 years down the line, definitely yes, our retail store presence will go much beyond South India. We actively wanted to move towards other regions of North, East and West as well.

items.statement: Sarees 70-72% of sales; Varamahalakshmi saree-heavy; customizing mix per region using decade-built software analytics
items.quote: Currently majority of our products are sarees, so 70%, 72% of what we currently sell is sarees. But also, there's a considerable amount of revenue contribution with respect to other categories such as women's kurtas, salwars, lehengas, men's wear, kids wear.

items.statement: Tamil Nadu Varamahalakshmi stores outperforming core AP/Telangana markets in revenue/sq ft and margins; expanding in Trichy, Tirunelveli, Pondicherry
items.quote: Tamil Nadu Varamahalakshmi Silks' average is higher than the other markets. And the newer stores that we have added also is doing as per the same averages only, irrespective to the fact that it's in Tier-1, Tier-2, Tier-3.

items.statement: FY26 may add 1-2 Kalamandir stores but majority Varamahalakshmi; FY27 ~10-12% sq ft growth on FY26 base
items.quote: As of now, we do not have any provision for Kalamandir stores, but majority of it will come from Varamahalakshmi, maybe one or two stores in the provision we are looking at in two active areas.

items.statement: New Varamahalakshmi stores mature in one full financial year (two seasons); launching expenses depress margins for first 6-8 months
items.quote: One full financial year, that means we are leaving out the year in which it has come into operation. We will assess one full year of operations of the store, that is, it would have seen two seasons.

items.statement: Capex guidance maintained at INR200 crore annually on base case; exploring other manufacturing footprint options
items.quote: I think our initial guidance was, on a basc case, INR200 crores annvally. But we arc also cxploring other options from a manufacturing footprint standpoint. So we maintain our guidance

items.statement: Capex incurred in Q2 FY25 was around INR43 crore
items.quote: The capex during this quarter is at around INR43 crores.

items.statement: Plant 6 at Unit 2 Ambernath commissioned adding 120 KL capacity for PI and contrast media segments; commercial production for cardiovascular PI started mid-September
items.quote: This facility adds 120 KL of additional capacity which will cater to our customers in the PI and contrast media segments. Commercial production of our PI client in cardiovascular therapy commenced in mid-September.

items.statement: Incremental 80 KL capacity in same block for NCE MRI contrast media intermediate; validation batches ongoing, commercial supplies expected from Q3 FY25
items.quote: As indicated in the previous call, we are commissioning incremental capacity of about 80 KL in the same block, and as we speak, the validation batehes for an advanced intermediate orientated towards the NCE in the MRI space are ongoing. We expect commercial supplics to commence from this capacity in quarter three onward

items.statement: Small volume plant at Unit 2 for proof of concept and clinical supplies expected to commission in Q1 FY26
items.quote: At Unit 2, we are also building a small volume plant, which we envisage will be ready for commissioning in quarter one of FY '26.

items.statement: Unit 3 at Mahad for contrast media backward integration expected to commission in Q1 FY26; effluent treatment plant ready for trials
items.quote: We believe that this new capacity will get commissioned, as we had indicated in the past, in quarter one, FY '26.

items.statement: Demand remains robust across all three product categories, specifically PI/CDMO category; Plant 6 capacity will support effectively
items.quote: Engagement with existing and new clients continue to be promising, with strong forecasts across all three product categories, specifically PI or CDMO category. Demand remains robust, which our Plant 6 capacity will support effectively.

items.statement: Contrast media demand expected to stabilize from Q4 FY25 onwards
items.quote: For contrast media category, Q2 supplies were steady, and we expect the demand for customers to stabilize from Q4 '25 onwards.

items.statement: Confirmed orders for full Plant 6 capacity for cardiovascular PI product
items.quote: Absolutely, we have confirmed orders on this particular candidate.

items.statement: Strong order book on NCE molecule for contrast media; new product launch expected in Q4 FY25
items.quote: And we have got a strong order book on the NCE molcetie also. So, we should be in a position to improve our performance in H2

items.statement: Gross margin at 57% in Q2 FY25, up 2% sequentially and sustained year-over-year; EBITDA margin at 33% in Q2
items.quote: For the same quarter, we recorded a gross margin of 57%, higher by 2% sequentially, and we were able to sustain similar margin on year-over-year basis.

items.statement: Steady-state gross margin expected around 53-55% for current product mix; Q2 margin marginally higher due to goods in transit capitalization
items.quote: See, based on the current portfolio, I would believe the margin would be in a similar range, maybe plus or mimus 2%. So, this quarter, because of a higher goods in transit, normally the overhead gets capitalized. So, the margin is marginally higher. So, T would actually take it somewhere around 53% to 55

items.statement: No significant price erosion in contrast media; volume discounts offset by rupee depreciation; key raw material prices stable
items.quote: In contrast media, technically, we have not seen any significant price erosion. So generally whenever there is a volume discount, it is generally offset by rupee depreciation. So we have actually not seen any meaningful price erosion in contrast media.

items.statement: Better product mix expected in H2 FY25 with 5-6 products getting traction including new NCE launch in Q4

items.quote: Generally, in case of hybrid power, the per unit cost saving is around INR4. And we are sourcing close to 30% of our power requirement for our Bharuch plant from these hybrid projects.

items.statement: Strategy of making more value-added filament yarn products helping reduce China dumping impact
items.quote: The strategy of making more value-added products has helped in reducing the impact of China

items.statement: Capex on value-added filament yarn products ongoing; incremental impact on margins expected to be marginal
items.quote: We are spending capex on value addition. Last year also, we did some capex on value-added products. And this year also, we are doing some capex. So that should help. But these are incremental capex only and will have a very marginal impact on the margins.

items.statement: Industry pushing for quantitative restrictions on imports; also rationalizing costs to improve competitiveness
items.quote: So we are, along with other industry participants, pushing for some quantitative restrictions. So that is an industry effort, which has been made. And the other side, we are trying to rationalize our costs and see -- to become more competitive with our own business.

items.statement: Filament yarn import duty 5.5% (5% + surcharge); Tyre cord duty 20%; most imports under advance license
items.quote: So duty in case of filament yarn is 5.5%, which is 5% plus surcharge. For tyre cord, it is 20% duty. So tyre cord, there is good duty protection, which is there. Most of the imports, which comes to India is against the advanced license where tyre companies have done the exports.

items.statement: Carrying higher raw material inventories due to supply chain situation; will cause mark-to-market impact in Q3
items.quote: Of course, because of the supply chain situation, we are carrying some higher inventories of raw material. So there will be some impact in Q3.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 operating revenue INR 536 crores (+35% YoY); EBITDA INR 38 crores (+300% YoY); EBITDA margin 7.07%; PAT INR 21 crores (+400% YoY); PAT margin 3.99%; Total volume 20,368 MT (+27% YoY)
items.quote: For the Q2 operating results, our operating revenue stood at INR536 crores, which grew by almost 35% year-on-year. EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR38 crores, which grew by 300% year-on-year. EBITDA margins were reported at 7.07%.

items.statement: H1 FY25 operating revenue INR 1,064 crores (+29% YoY); EBITDA INR 79 crores (+156% YoY); EBITDA margin 7.41%; PAT INR 46 crores (+157% YoY); PAT margin 4.29%; Total volume 40,908 MT (+27% YoY)
items.quote: For the first half of FY '25, operational revenue stood at INR1,064 crores, representing a growth of 29% year-on-year. EBITDA stood at INR79 crores, which increased by 156% year-on-year. EBITDA margin for the period was 7.41%.

items.statement: Q3 filament yarn volumes expected to be good
items.quote: Yes, Q3 should be good for filament yarn in terms of volumes.

items.statement: Supply chain normalization leading to higher imports creating pressure in Q3; container freight normalized but some congestion delays remain
items.quote: They are almost normalized. So container freight, which was almost double to triple, has now been normalized. And there are some delays because of congestion, which got created in the last 4, 5 months.

items.statement: Manpower cost reduction efforts: cutting non-viable capacities and not replacing retiring employees
items.quote: And manpower also, we are trying to cut down on capacities, which are not viable and not to take new manpower, which is -- or where people are retiring, we are not taking new manpower.

items.statement: Exploring technical textile opportunities and adjacencies; may provide more details next year if board approves plans
items.quote: Yes. We are looking into these opportunities. One is that we are doing capex on value addition. There is existing value addition also, which has been done, and we are looking to do more capex there. And then some of the other areas which are there in terms of adjacencies, there also we are working.

items.statement: Expects double-digit revenue growth for full year FY25
items.quote: Regarding the sales outlook for the full year 2024 -'25, we expect to have double-digit revenue growth over the fiscal year.

items.statement: Domestic sales grew 47% YoY and 7% QoQ in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Domestic sales at INR2,008 crores are higher by 47%. Exports at INR440 crores are lower by 13%.

items.statement: Gross margin dip due to project business mix, not CPCB IV+ cost pass-through
items.quote: This is largely due to the mix that plays out for us. When we -- in this quarter, there is a large share of the projects business, as we call it, where we do installation and commissioning for some of our gen sets in the -- and so because of that, it's the mix playing out.

items.statement: Installed capacity utilization at 60-65%; manned capacity over 90%
items.quote: There are -- so there's a large -- there's a wide range of products that we manufacture in our plants. And our capacities are utilized quite well at this point in time, more than -- on an average, more than 60% to 65% utilization.

items.statement: PowerGen domestic sales INR896 cr (84% YoY); Distribution INR658 cr (20% YoY); Industrial INR406 cr (35% YoY)
items.value: INR896 cr, INR658 cr, INR406 cr
items.quote: For the domestic business, Power Generation domestic sales were INR896 crores, 84% higher compared to last year; and 12% higher compared to last quarter. Distribution business sales were INR658 crores, 20% higher compared to last year and 1% higher compared to last quarter. Industrial domestic business sales were at INR406 crores, 35% higher compared to last year and 9% higher compared to last qua

items.statement: CPCB IV+ applies up to 800 kW; above that CPCB II continues; both contribute to PowerGen
items.quote: CPCB IV+ is below 800 kilowatts, and above that is CPCB II range. So there is a mix there of CPCB II and CPCB IV+.

items.statement: Data center segment growing; QSK60 predominant node in India; no migration to higher nodes yet
items.quote: Data centers around the world as a segment is doing very well given the AI boom across the world, as is the case in India. And we have products which are rightfully positioned for that segment. So most definitely, we are quite focused on that segment, and we see the growth of that segment around the world as we see it in India.

items.statement: First to launch full CPCB IV+ range; strong brand and supply chain; competitors now launching products
items.quote: We work amongst one of the first few players to launch the full range of products in the market. In the meantime, we have continuously worked on improving our supply chain, makin g sure that our product is well accepted in the market. We do have a strong brand in the market. So we do think we are pretty well positioned in the CPCB IV+ space in the market

items.statement: Construction equipment emission norms change from Jan 1, 2025; pre-buying expected
items.quote: Yes, there will be an emission norm change in that segment. The construction segment from a demand perspective has been doing well. As with any other emission change, there is some prebuy that happens in the market,

items.statement: Channel inventory for CPCB IV+ at adequate levels; no CPCB II inventory remaining
items.quote: We continuously evaluate inventory in the channel. And for CPCB IV+ as well, we have evaluated the inventory, and we are at adequate stock availability in our channel for CPCB IV+. So that's where the inventory levels are.

items.statement: Strong balance sheet; well positioned to sustain growth trajectory
items.quote: And with a strong balance sheet, world-class infrastructure on the ground for manufacturing, our best-in-class talent, we are very confident of sustaining our growth trajectory.

items.value: INR452 cr, INR178 cr, INR199 cr, INR68 cr, INR146 cr, INR105 cr, INR32 cr, INR58 cr

For the Industrial business, the breakup into different segments, construction around -- construction is INR146 crores, rail INR105 crores, mining at INR32 crores, compressor at INR58 crores

items.statement: CPCB IV+ product largely localized at launch; continuous cost improvement via ACE program
items.quote: A large part of our CPCB IV+ product range and what goes in those products is localized. And we are continuously working on where we do not have indigenized parts yet. So it's a continuous endeavor, but I can tell you that the large part of that product range is already localized at the time of launch.

items.statement: Auto SUV volume growth target 15-18% for full year
items.quote: we should hence hit for the full year 15-18% growth for the SUV portfolio.

items.quote: we did have F19 as a good benchmark , where the auto business was roughly at around 10% margin, PBIT . And that remains, let us call it a medium-term goal for the business to first hit.

items.statement: EV capacity addition of 10,000 units annually in Phase I
items.quote: The EV capacities of course will start kicking in as soon as we start production, and that in Phase I we will be adding 10K.

items.statement: ICE capacity constrained on some models; evaluating need to strengthen ICE manufacturing footprint
items.quote: We are capacity constrained right now on some of the ICE models. We are not sure exactly what we are going to do, but we will be working on what we need to do by way of strengthening the ICE manufacturing footprint as well.

items.quote: The dealer stock is way below 30 days , a nd we are at a very, very comfortable level of dealer stock as we ended October and have gone into

items.statement: LCV demand turning positive from October with mandi arrivals up 20% in late October

items.quote: Tech M has seen traction in BFSI. EBIT is up almost 5 percentage points, yes, from a low base and there is more to do on that front.

items.statement: Renewables business Susten added ~1 GW in Q2 vs 2 GW full year prior; 5 GW in 5 years target accelerating
items.quote: our renewables business Sust en, we had talked about 5 gigawatts in 5 years, s o 1 gigawatt a year. In this last quarter, in one quarter alone , we got almost 1 gigawatt, and that's coming off 2 gigawatts last year

items.quote: The date for TREM V as of now is April ‘26. It's still at a draft level , and we would be very surprised if it happens in April 2026. It's for all the product, between 25 to 50 19 HP

items.quote: we continue to have discussions across our group companies with various opportunities , a nd if we feel at any point in time that an opportunity makes sense, it's profitable for us, meets the conditions we've laid out , then we will have a further

items.quote: the end losses have continued to come down in Mahindra finance. And so , that's going to result in overall credit costs coming down in the second half.

items.statement: Services profit contribution exceeded Farm profit contribution in Q2; inflection point for services portfolio
items.quote: Our Services business has contributed more to M&M's profits than our tractor business has in this quarter. And, while that has been the case sometimes in the past as well, we're starting to see that uptick again.

items.statement: Born Electric SUVs BE 6e and XEV 9e to be revealed in November 2024; market launch early 2025
items.quote: we're finally ready to reveal the two, we're calling it now 'electric origin SUVs '. We're naming them B E 6e and XEV 9e. So , these two products will be revealed in November and will be in market in early part of 2025.

items.statement: Turned net debt free as of September 2024, ahead of March 2025 target
items.quote: At the outset, I am pleased to share that as of September 2024, we have turned net debt free well before our stated target of March 2025.

items.statement: Targeting mid-teen volume growth in H2 FY25
items.quote: With these recent developments, we are now targeting mid -teen volume growth in H2 FY25.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin expanded 422 bps to 17.6%; adjusted EBITDA margin up 188 bps to 15.3%
items.quote: EBITDA margins expanded by 422 basis points to 17.6%, and adjusted for the subsidy income, EBITDA stood at Rs. 56 crore at a margin of 15.3%, showing a 188-basis points margin expansion on adjusted EBITDA.

items.statement: Maintenance capex Rs 15-20 crore per year; grain distillery recommissioning ~Rs 45 crore
items.quote: Our maintenance CAPEX could remain anywhere in the range of Rs. 15 to Rs. 20 odd crore on a yearly basis. That's the maintenance CAPEX. And as and when we do take a call on the distillery, we will let you all know, but that will be an investment of around Rs. 45 crore.

items.statement: Plan to recommission 100 KLPD grain distillery at Shrirampur
items.quote: No, we will be recommissioning the 100 KLPD plant.

items.statement: Telangana overdue receivables ~Rs 80 crore out of Rs 130 crore total; expect regularization in 3-4 months
items.quote: The total receivables in the state would be around Rs. 130 crore and around Rs. 80 crore of this would be overdue.

items.statement: ENA price fell to ~Rs 69/litre in Q2 from Rs 70/litre in Q1; packing material costs softening
items.quote: On the ENA front, we've seen for the quarter ENA prices for us reducing by another rupee per litre. Whilst in the previous quarter in Q1 the average price was around Rs. 70 a litre, right now we are looking at around Rs. 69.

items.statement: Karnataka volumes hit record highs in September and October after excise duty cut
items.quote: I am happy to share that the month of September saw us clocking our highest ever primary and secondary volumes in the state, and even happier to share that October beat this mark comfortably as well.

items.statement: P&A saliency in CNB family portfolio rose to 38% in Q2 FY25 from 32% in Q2 FY24

items.statement: Andhra Pradesh currently 30% of sales; expect mid-teens growth there over next 2-3 years
items.quote: Currently it is 30% of sales and totally Andhra I think mid -teens growth would be reasonable to expect.

items.quote: Our revenue guidance would be a couple of 100 basis points more than our volume guidance, but this is based on our existing business perspective.

items.statement: Usership agreement with Spaceman Spirits to sell Samsara Gin and Sitara Rum in select states in India and internationally starting H2 FY25
items.quote: Through the usership agreement, we will start selling both these brands in certain states in India and internationally. This will be followed by a few more launches soon.

items.statement: Telangana collections not yet normal; overdue at ~10 weeks vs historical 8-9 weeks low
items.quote: We are at roughly 10 weeks overdue in Telangana, and in terms of pricing, I think they have set up a pricing committee to fix the price of beer.

items.statement: Dividend policy evolving; distributed dividends for three years; no immediate change announced
items.quote: We have just about started our dividend distributions, over the past couple of years now, it's been three years that we've been distributing dividends, in the recent past.

items.statement: Telangana overdues improved from peak 18-19 weeks to ~10 weeks; expect regularization in 3-4 months
items.quote: Historically, around 8 to 9 weeks would have been low and I think it has gone up to 18 to 19 weeks.

items.statement: Mansion House Whisky positioned vs Royal Stag, Royal Challenge in semi-premium segment; sees room despite large incumbents
items.quote: Comparable brands would be Royal Stag, Royal Challenge. These would be our comparable brands.

items.statement: Packing material inflation easing; ENA prices stable near-term; no meaningful COGS inflation expected
items.quote: While packing material costs have seen some level of softening, we continue to be cautious about ENA prices. We expect that there will be no meaningful inflationary impact on COGS in the near-term.

items.statement: Flandy at ~7% of Mansion House saliency in relevant states; Green Apple flavor launched in Telangana and AP
items.quote: We've kind of maintained the same saliency for this quarter. It is around 7% of overall Mansion House saliency that we have in the relevant states.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 revenue was INR 753 crores, up 10% YoY, driven by domestic demand while exports were subdued.
items.quote: So generally, the Q2 '24-'25 performance highlights where we got the best September quarter with INR 753 crores, which was a 10% Y-o-Y growth comparing to the same quarter last year. Demand was largely driven by the domestic, so -- which was the plus and in exports were minus.

items.statement: PBT margin was 16.4% in Q2 FY25 vs 18% YoY and 16.6% QoQ, impacted by unfavourable product mix due to lower rail sales.
items.quote: Our PBT margin was 16.4% compared to 18% in the prior year period, and last quarter was 16.6. Rigid margin performance in the quarter despite unfavourable product mix.

items.statement: Bharuch plant capex of INR 600 crores approved; building up, machines received, 66 kVA line energization expected in 10 days, commissioning targeted for Q1 FY26.

These are imported into India. And then civil construction, you pay only after finishing. Then 10% still there and all that. So we will be obviously consuming the capex, every order is placed, machines are coming.

items.statement: New Bharuch facility to produce spherical and cylindrical roller bearings; commissioning targeted first quarter-ish, full ramp-up to 80-85% utilization expected in 24-30 months.
items.quote: So we are working towards as fast as possible, some months here and there, but endeavour is first quarter-ish, somewhere like that.

items.statement: Rail segment sees steady order book; last quarter of fiscal year traditionally strongest due to wagon industry contract completions.
items.quote: Generally, the rail, always the last quarter is generally best because the wagon industry pushes the wagon manufacturing, they have to complete their contracts. So if you see all years, in the last 5, 10 years, the last quarter of the fiscal year is always the best, and there will be no change to that, that will remain there.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 revenue mix: rail 22%, mobile 18%, distribution 19%, process 21%, exports 19%.
items.quote: So Mr. Jain, the revenue mix for the Q2 '24-'25, this quarter was out of the total pie, the rail was 22%, mobile was 18%, distribution was 19%, process was 21% and exports were 19%.

items.statement: Exports largely to North America (50-60%); US heavy truck weak but October showed improvement; Americas rail decent; Europe rail market small.
items.quote: Largely our exports are North America. We export to Australia. We export to even China. But largely it is US followed by Europe and followed by India and rest of...

items.statement: Gross margins around 39% vs 41-42% earlier due to mix, inflation, energy, labour, and steel cost volatility; passing cost increases faces huge resistance in automotive.
items.quote: Obviously, my boss is asking the same question. So it is sort of a mix of everything. It is a mix of inflation, it is partly because of the mix, partly because of inflation, energy cost, labour cost, and then steel is going up and down here and there.

items.statement: Wind energy demand picking up domestically (Adani, Suzlon) and for exports (gearbox manufacturing by ZF, Flender, NGC); steel not at full capacity but improving; cement and infra traction starting post-elections.
items.quote: Wind for domestic use is picking up definitely. And we see Suzlon, Adani for Indian market doing a good job. But the manufacturing of the gearboxes in India for the ZFs of the world or the Flenders of the world is okay.

items.statement: CV market expected to improve in Q4 FY25 (Jan-Mar) post-elections and monsoon; construction equipment market projected to reach USD 10 billion by 2030.
items.quote: On CV, particularly, I think, January, February, March might be a lot better than the previous 2, 3 quarters.

items.statement: Freight rail market leader in India; passenger rail market leader; intend to maintain position through technology and supply chain.
items.quote: On freight, we are the market leaders in India. On passengers, we are the market leaders, and we intend not to lose any ground to anybody.

items.quote: We are operating 28 MILLTEC sites in India. So, we are winning more sites in India, and we intend to promote that model not only in steel, we want to take it from MILLTEC to Caster-Tech to Power-Tech to Cement-Tech.

items.quote: Timken supplies sensors bearing to Ford for many, many years. We produce a railway sensored bearing. I gave a presentation to Railways 30 years back or 25 years back. items.statement: Evaluating business case to leverage parent's acquired technologies (belts, chains, lubrication, robotics, linear motion, Cone Drive slew drives) in India via M&A, greenfield, or supply chain; will be sold through Timken India.

items.statement: Balance sheet remains debt-free with robust cash flow; continuing strategic investments including Bharuch project.
items.quote: And overall, our balance sheet is debt free. Cash flow is robust. We are continuing strategic investments.

items.statement: Parent holding at 51.05%; no information on plans to increase or decrease stake.
items.quote: The parent is currently at 51.05%. And currently, we are at 51.05%. And that is it. I have no further information on that. Neither going down, neither going up. No information available with us.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainties across end markets; US market subdued, China mining down, Australia down; heavy rains/flooding delayed Bharuch construction.
items.quote: Obviously, there is geopolitical situations, and there are uncertainties across multiple end markets. US market has been subdued. China is down, so which -- China is down, mining is down, Australia is down, we export to these markets -- America.

items.quote: I don't see any reason to be pessimistic as I look for the October to March, 2 quarters in general. I think people who run business should be optimistic. And there is no cause of being pessimistic in approach.

items.quote: We h ave announced chlorine downstream projects of 100 TPD Aluminium Chloride & 225 TPD Calcium Chloride in Bharuch with a capex of Rs 310 crore at a new site near our existing plant. These projects will get commissioned by Q1 FY27 and will enable a chlorine sink of upto 225 TPD

items.quote: The ECH plant faced some pre -commissioning delays which are being addressed by our technology partners and we are confident of commissioning the plant by Q4 FY25.

items.statement: Caustic soda demand remains good, but excess capacity in India at 75% utilisation creating chlorine price pressure
items.quote: The segment continues to see good demand of caustic, however excess capacity in India is creating pressure on product prices especially in Chlorine.

items.quote: And on your point of the ROCE, given that their capital employed is negligible and their EBIT will be in excess of Rs. 200 crore, so it's like abnormal number, it's very high.

items.quote: The Board announced an interim dividend of 100% amounting to Rs. 31.19 crores.

items.quote: Prices are expected to remain rangebound for the FY 2024 -25 between Rs 3850 - 3950/Qtl, which are not commensurate with the increase in the cost of production ow ing to increase in SAP and climatic conditions in the last season
