items.statement: October volumes strong: 1,783 tillers vs 1,200 YoY, 680 tractors vs 289 YoY
items.quote: In the month of October, we have sold 1,783 tillers as against to 1,200 in October 2023. Similarly, for tractors, we have sold in the month 680 tractors, which in October '23 it was 289.

items.statement: H2 FY25 expected strong due to good monsoon, reservoir levels, MSP, acreage
items.quote: acreage has gone up, monsoon has been great, reservoirs are full, minimum support prices are better. So, in every sense of the word, it looks positive.

items.statement: Higher HP tractor mix pressuring margins temporarily; power weeder growing rapidly
items.quote: As our higher horsepower volumes are growing and especially when it is a new product, there is a bit of a margin pressure when the product is new for a few months before it normalizes

items.statement: Appointed 56 dealers for VST Zetor in North markets in H1 FY25
items.quote: in the northern markets, very happy to say that in the first half of this year, we have been able to appoint 56 dealers

items.statement: Power weeder segment seeing larger competition; power tiller competition limited
items.quote: Definitely more and more players are entering that segment, but we don't see too much of effect in the power tiller space, but you can see larger competition in power weeder segment.

items.statement: Receivables at 70 days due to government orders, expected to normalize to 45-50 days by end Q3
items.quote: receivables have gone up purely because of the government orders we have received and the supply which is in process. So, I would say that by the end of Q3, it would normalize and come back to the normal levels of around 45 to 50 days of receivables.

items.statement: Short-term debt of Rs 7 crore for better capital and working capital management
items.quote: Yes, better capital management, better working capital management. We had looked at, see, how to use some debt when it is usable instead of looking at kind of taking funds from our treasury.

items.statement: Kobashi JV on hold due to technology transfer delays; evaluating inorganic opportunities
items.quote: that project is on hold right now. It is not dropped, but because a JV partner Kobashi is taking more time in terms of moving certain technologies in certain products which we wanted in the JV, that decision is not yet made

items.statement: Couple of inorganic opportunities on anvil, nothing to announce yet
items.quote: We have a couple of things are on the anvil, but nothing to announce at this moment in time.

items.statement: Key risk: commodity price spike from geopolitical events; execution acceleration challenge
items.quote: the one concern that I have is on the bottom line. So, while I am saying to the earlier caller that the commodity prices shouldn't come under pressure in the coming quarter, which doesn't look like because demand is slowed down almost across markets. I hope that doesn't reverse itself and the commodity prices shoot up because of an extended war or the Gulf War or whatever reason.

items.statement: International business grew from 3% to 13%, targeting 25-30% in 2-3 years
items.quote: two years back or three years back, we were at about 3% of international business. Last year we closed at about 13% of international business. We are going to take it to about 25% to 30% of our business.

items.statement: R&D team expanded to 80-90 personnel working on multiple platforms
items.quote: Today, we are a 80-90 strong R&D personnel. We are working on multiple platforms including our entry into the U.S. market, developing platforms of various kinds of engine.

items.statement: Interest cost run rate targeted at Rs 75-80 crore per quarter
items.quote: I would say the interest cost should be in the range of Rs.75-80 crores is something that we have been working on, saying that it should not go beyond Rs.75-80 crores in terms of a run rate of the interest cost.

items.statement: Global OFC demand contracted marginally till Sep 2024; CRU projects 4.3% annual growth to 652 mn fkm by 2028, 7% ex-China
items.quote: As per latest CRU projections, the medium term demands the optical fiber volumes is to go up steadily to 652 million fiber kilometers by 2028. This projects a healthy 4.3% annual growth in the annual demand and a strong 7% annual demand growth for ex-China during 2023 to 2028.

items.statement: India AI data center GPU capacity expected to reach 5.2 lakh GPUs by 2026, requiring 36x more fiber than CPU racks
items.quote: As per initial estimates, India is expected to boost its GPU based server capability in these AI led data centers to 5.2 lakh GPUs by 2026. These GPU heavy data centers will require 36 times more fiber than CPU racks, driven by an increase in server density and higher bandwidth requirements.

items.statement: Open order book Rs 8,630 crore at end of Q2 FY25, well diversified across customers and businesses
items.quote: Despite of increased quarter on quarter revenue and significant order descoping our open order book stands at Rs.8,630 crore at the end of Q2 FY25, backed by steady order wins.

items.statement: STL Digital order book over Rs 336 crore with healthy pipeline
items.quote: We continue to work with our customers for growing our business in the US, Europe and India across technology and service verticals and expect the future growth to be driven by robust order book of more than Rs.336 crores.

items.statement: Optical networking Q2 FY25 EBITDA Rs 133 crore at 12.9% margin, improved QoQ but lower YoY due to lower OFC volumes and mix change
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stand at Rs.133 crores, at 12.9% of revenues. EBITDA margin reflects substantial improvement on quarter-on-quarter basis and stands lower on Y-o-Y basis because of lower of OFC volumes and change in product mix.

items.statement: Global services Q2 FY25 EBITDA Rs 24 crore at 6.7% margin, steady revenue QoQ
items.quote: Our selective order intake and execution focus has helped us achieve Q2 FY25 EBITDA of Rs.24 crores and EBITDA margin of 6.7%.

items.statement: STL Digital Q2 FY25 revenue Rs 64 crore, EBITDA loss Rs 15 crore, losses trending down YoY and QoQ
items.quote: In line with our expectation and tough industry environment, with a focus on profitable growth, we have achieved a Q2 revenue of Rs.64 crores. The EBITDA losses for Q2 stand at Rs.15 crores, despite the lower revenues, EBITDA losses trending downward Y-o-Y and quarter on quarter basis.

items.statement: Manufacturing facilities strategically located with completed capacity expansions and CAPEX cycle
items.quote: As we have been sharing with you, our strategically located manufacturing facilities, completed capacity expansions and CAPEX cycle, and our continuous focus on cost structure optimization, product development and innovation, emphasis on data center portfolio and tier one customer approvals.

items.statement: Optical fiber cable utilization currently ~50%, target to return to 75-80% for meaningful EBITDA performance
items.quote: And that's something that we want to continue to see that how we drive these utilizations up from this current 50% levels and take this really back to that 75-80% levels, where then we have meaningful EBITDA performance.

items.statement: Optical connectivity attach rate 22% in Q2 FY25, highest ever quarterly revenue; some customers at 100%+ attach rate in UK/Europe
items.quote: Our optical connectivity product line continues to demonstrate strong growth momentum, as we noted, our highest ever quarterly revenue for optical connectivity products an attach rate of 22% during last quarter.

items.statement: Launched AI-DC portfolio at India Mobile Congress 2024; target 25% of optical business revenue from data center segment in medium term
items.quote: We have taken a target that 25% of our optical business revenue should come from this segment in the medium term, that's the whole thought process.

items.statement: Won new orders from leading American customer, UK telecom operator, Italian optical fiber cable orders, Indian private telecom for FWA, and long-term fiber supply order
items.quote: To highlight the few key events, we won the new orders from leading American customer and from leading UK telecom operator. For optical connectivity and fiber solution we have received new orders in Italy for optical fiber cable and specialty cable products.

items.statement: STL Digital acquired large strategic global customer in Europe; robust new deal flow from marquee customers across US and India
items.quote: We acquired a large and strategic global customer in Europe as well. We continue to work with our customers for growing our business in the US, Europe and India across technology and service verticals.

items.statement: Optical cable ex-China market share 8% in H1 CY, dipped to 6% in H1 CY24, recovered closer to 8% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Basis the CRU global consumption data, H1 calendar year, we had 8% market share on optical cable ex China. On H1 CY24 market share seem to be 6% amidst a challenging demand environment. Our Q2 FY25 market share, however, seems to have come back closer to 8%.

items.statement: BEAD program main volumes pushed to H2 CY2025, peaking 2026-2027; BharatNet Phase III results expected this quarter, 3-5 year execution
items.quote: In terms of BEAD probably, versus where we were 4-6 months ago, we do see that the larger volumes of BEAD related cable demand and connectivity demand is probably got pushed out by a few months. So while we have started winning a few initial projects linked to BEAD, the main significant volumes are now expected probably second half of calendar year 2025 and then with it peaking in 2026 and 2027 ca

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty in Europe: no supply disruption; European facility scaling up, lowering manufacturing cost and improving profitability
items.quote: So Nikhil, from the supply chain perspective absolutely there is no impact because whatever customer orders are being placed, we have been able to serve all of them without any kind of disruption. So, which is very positive. However, we have seen that in terms of as we scale up our European facility, we are able to bring down the overall manufacturing cost, and we are able to see the higher profit

items.statement: North America expected 12-15% annual growth; Europe flattish but UK, Germany, Eastern Europe, Middle East steady; US inventory normalizing in 1-2 quarters
items.quote: But thematically, what you mentioned in terms of demand in North America, we do see all of those sectorial themes do play out over the next 12-15 months. And of course, from a longer-term perspective as well, North America continues to be probably the most positive growth territory globally, where anywhere between 12-15% annual growth is expected.

items.statement: Raised Rs 1,000 crore in Q1 via QIP, repaid major part of debt; debt-to-equity 0.74; service business demerger to transfer Rs 550-600 crore net debt
items.quote: So, with reference to the debt, as you have rightly mentioned, we raised about Rs.1000 crores in Q1 which has been used to repay the debt and successfully we repaid the major part of the debt from the procedure that we have received. The current net debt that we have is about Rs.2169 crores and our debt-to-equity ratio is about 0.74 at this point in time.

items.statement: Global services demerger: shareholders/creditors approved July 2024; NCLT hearing Oct 11, 2024; final order expected Q3-Q4 FY25 (3-4 months); resulting companies to list
items.quote: We are progressing steadily on a demerger process. The shareholders and creditors of STL India have approved the scheme of arrangement in a meeting dated 10 July 2024 basis the approval, demerger petition has been filed with the NCLT, and the hearing was conducted on 11 th October 2024 with NCLT. We are awaiting the order from this particular hearing from NCLT. The date for the final petition is p

items.statement: STL Digital new CEO Naveen joined, implemented significant cost cutting to drive EBITDA break-even
items.quote: The new CEO, Naveen who's come in, has done fairly significant cost cutting as well to really make sure that focus is there on getting to EBITDA break even.

items.statement: BharatNet Phase III results expected this quarter; T-Fiber project Rs 700 crore fund involvement stuck on forest right-of-way approvals from central/state govt
items.quote: With respect to your specific questions on the fund involvement for this particular project, at this point in time, fund involvement is almost to the extent of Rs.700 crores for this particular project.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 expected sluggish for order inflow due to Nov-Dec winter slowdown; order uptake expected in Q4 as budgets release Jan-Feb
items.quote: Yes, that is correct. Largely because of what I explained that in November, December is typically quite slow, not much of decision making in this period.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 24-28%
items.quote: we will be in the range of 24% to 28% on a n EBITDA for the full year, which we are saying we will .

items.statement: Full-year FY25 absolute EBITDA expected to grow sequentially year-on-year
items.quote: Second, we had said we will show sequential growth year -on-year on the absolute EBITDA number.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 revenue growth target: top quartile among peers
items.quote: And third, we said that we would be in the top quartile of the growth amongst our peer group.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin 27.1%, up sequentially due to revenue growth, utilization, and one-offs
items.quote: EBITDA for Q2 was INR 2,288 million, at a margin of 27.1%.

items.statement: One-offs in Q1 boosted Q2 margin by ~85 bps (sign-on bonuses, 401k, leave provision change)
items.quote: The impact of these one-off on margin is about 85 bps.

items.statement: New facilities in Chandigarh, Pune (Q3) and Mumbai (early Q4) to increase G&A and depreciation by 50-70 bps each quarter
items.quote: we expect max about 50 to 70 bps impact, [as] the percentage of revenue in Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Financial markets demand driven by compliance/regulatory work and market activity; no slowdown anticipated
items.quote: I think our financial markets growth is driven primarily from a compliance and regulatory perspective, so that I think it is a big driver.

items.statement: Digital creative business soft due to low demand from China; likely to continue for next couple of quarters
items.quote: fashion and luxury saw a decline with global fashion houses reporting less client demand, particularly out of China. This is likely to continue for the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: Customer operations demand driven by existing client growth and cross-sell despite industry pressure
items.quote: Despite this, because of our strong delivery, we see continued strength in existing client growth and client diversification.

items.statement: Q2 ACV deal wins INR 28.9 million; roll-offs higher than Q1, full impact in Q3 from short-term project completions
items.quote: ACV of the deal wins for the quarter was a strong at INR 28.9 million. Roll-offs in Q2 were higher than Q1 and the full impact of these roll -offs will be felt in Q3.

items.statement: Normal annual roll-off rate 15-20% of revenue
items.quote: Normal value is about 15% to 20% in a year.

items.statement: New offices in Chandigarh and Pune going live in Q3, Mumbai in early Q4; seat count and costs to rise
items.quote: Our new office spaces in Chandigarh and Pune will go live in Q3 and the new space in Mumbai will go live in early Q4.

items.statement: Exit headcount increased by ~480 to 18,227; attrition at 22%, higher than Q1 as anticipated
items.quote: The exit headcount has increased by about 480 to 18,227. Attrition is at 22% , which is higher than Q1 as we had anticipated.

items.statement: DSO improved to 77 days from 81 days in previous quarter
items.quote: DSO is 77 days compared to 81days in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Top 10 client concentration increased to 63% due to strong growth in financial markets and customer operations
items.quote: the top10 client concentration is now up to 63%, a result of the strong growth in top clients in financial markets and customer operations.

items.statement: Analytics and automation business at USD 19 million, up 10% sequentially
items.quote: Our analytics and automation business is USD 19 million this quarter, up 10% sequentially, which is a positive sign.

items.statement: M&A priorities unchanged: upstream consulting/advisory in financial markets, analytics/creative in digital, Salesforce/Adobe implementation in tech, near-shore in customer operations
items.quote: our priorities remain unchanged. We continue to look for assets which can meaningfully add to what the capabilities that we have.

items.statement: Buyback vs dividend priority to be examined post tax ruling change; no immediate decision
items.quote: I think we will definitely have to examine it, as you say, there is no difference in buyback and dividend anymore other than the reduction in dilution.

items.statement: Senior leadership hiring under CEO completed; further hiring case-by-case for sales and delivery
items.quote: The senior leadership under Kapil , that hiring is done. But under the senior leaders, we will decide on a case-to-case basis on whether we need to strengthen in certain areas, add more sales muscle in other areas and so on, that continues to happen on a case-to-case basis.

items.statement: Quarter-on-quarter aberrations possible; forward-looking guidance not provided; medium-to-long-term outlook positive
items.quote: I think to expect the same growth that we have delivered in Q2, I think it will not be appropriate, and we don't give forward-looking guidance, but in terms of medium to long term outlook stays positive.

items.statement: Q2 operating revenue USD 98.8 million, up 6% QoQ and 12.8% YoY; INR 8,318 million, up 6.4% QoQ and 15% YoY
items.quote: Operating revenue in Q2 was USD 98.8 million, up 6% sequentially and 12.8% year on year driven by exceptionally strong growth in our financial markets business and supported by customer operations business.

items.statement: Q2 PAT INR 1,402 million at 16.6% margin, up 26% QoQ and 3.9% YoY
items.quote: PAT for the quarter was INR 1,402 million at a margin of 16.6%.

items.statement: Employee cost as % of revenue may not decline if shift to higher-cost change/analytics work continues
items.quote: if we are moving into more change and analytics kind of work, then the employee cost in those areas is higher. So, it's kind of hard to say definitively that the employee cost has peaked.

items.statement: Everest Group rated eClerx Major Contender in RPA Products and CXM Services Americas, Aspirant in Finance & Accounting Peak Matrix
items.quote: eClerx was rated as a "Major Contender" in RPA Products and in Customer Experience Management (CXM) Services Americas and as an "Aspirant" in Finance and Accounting Peak Matrix assessment by the Everest roup.

items.statement: Combined technology and analytics under single leadership to improve positioning, agility, and value proposition
items.quote: We have combined technology and analytics under single leadership. This will help us position our services better improve agility and enhance the value proposition for our clients.

items.statement: Cayman outpatient facility commissioned a week ago; full hospital expected in ~4 weeks
items.quote: the outpatient facility of the hospital has been commissioned about a week ago. So, the quarter which results you are seeing, that is Q2, the facility was not commissioned. We've started outpatient services that is doctor consultations and limited diagnostics now. We hope to get approval to start the entire hospital in about next four weeks or so.

items.statement: Cayman margin dilution now expected for 4-5 quarters vs prior 6-8 quarters
items.quote: we'd like to change our estimates from the 6-8 quarters and change it to about 4-5 quarters is when we expect some margin dilution. So, we're more optimistic on the cost front.

items.statement: New hospital cluster revenue ~₹130 cr in Q2 with 13% YoY growth and 11% EBITDA
items.quote: the new hospital cluster has done pretty well in this quarter. It's given a very strong revenue growth around 13% year -on-year, with the revenue crossing around ₹130 crores for this quarter, with an EBITDA of around 11%.

items.statement: H1 FY25 capex ₹530 cr (₹320 cr India, balance Cayman); ₹160 cr for Bangalore land
items.quote: We have spent about ₹530 crores in H1 of which ₹320 crores is in India and balance is in Cayman. Out of this ₹320 crores, ₹160 crores was for the land we bought in Bangalore and the rest was regular Capex.

items.statement: Committed projects: ~700 beds greenfield in Kolkata & Bangalore, ~150 beds brownfield Raipur over 3-3.5 years; targeting ~1500 beds in 4 years
items.quote: We already 5 have committed projects which include greenfield in Kolkata and Bangalore totaling to around 700 beds and the brownfield in Raipur with around 150 beds. This will come up in the next 3-3.5 years’ time. We are also working to close 1-2 more greenfield projects. But all in all, it would be adding around close to 1500 beds in the next four years from now provided there are no material de

items.statement: Kolkata Rajarhat 1000 beds in two phases; first phase ~350 beds
items.quote: The intent is to add 1000 beds in Kolkata but it will go live in two phases. So, the first phase which we are building, is what we have factored right now. Then once those get completely occupied, then we'll go for the second phase.

items.statement: Bangalore greenfield project ~₹500 cr capex (land + build) on land adjacent to current hospital
items.quote: I think the ₹500 crores estimate was given for the greenfield opportunity that we are doing in Bangalore. And there is a land available next to our current hospital and we will be building in that.

items.statement: Cayman Q2 slowdown due to team focus on new hospital commissioning and 7-10 days lost to hurricanes; October back to positive trajectory
items.quote: There were few factors that led to the slowdown, you know, all across its uniform. It's not any particular specialty, a particular category. You know, everybody, the whole team has been focused for the past few weeks on commissioning the new hospital. It's a lot of time to fulfill all the compliance related obligations. We had a couple of hurricanes that led to about 7-10 days of unproductive work

items.statement: India inpatient ARPP grew ~14.5% YoY driven by mix shift to domestic patients, complex procedures, better payor mix; price hikes low single digits (4-5%)
items.quote: Our typical price increase is low single digits, 4-5% every year. So, anything beyond that is all efficiency driven. Efficiency realization, higher order procedures, better payor mix, so everything is driven by that.

items.statement: International patient share declining (Bangladesh down 19% YoY); domestic grew 13.5-14% YoY with higher value per patient
items.quote: the degrowth through these international patients have been to the extent of 19%, but the domestic has grown by around 13.5 to 14%. But, that 14% has contributed to a higher valu e than the degrowth on the international patients to the extent of 19

items.statement: International business expected to trend to zero over next 10 years; focus on domestic 15 km radius
items.quote: the international business is one number that I expect to go to zero over the next 10 years. So we're not spend ing too much time and energy focused on attracting more patients from international geographies, and focused instead entirely within a domestic radius, highest priority within the 15 kilometers of all our

items.statement: Complex procedures growing: record TAVI volumes, 113 robotic cardiac surgeries in quarter; trend expected to continue
items.quote: We did the highest number of robotic cardiac surgery in one quarter. We did around 113 robotic cardiac surgeries in one quarter, and there are some hospitals which have done 500 -600 over 7-8 years period. So, this is the volume of work that happens here, and we will continue to see this kind of high-end work going up in this one.

items.statement: Actively pursuing acquisitions but valuations fully priced; focusing on distress assets in West Bengal & Karnataka; acquired Sparsh hospital and Cayman ENT practice
items.quote: We've spent since '2016 trying to pursue multiple opportunities for Asset Light acquisitions, all of that. It's just that out of absolute compulsion in the absence of finding anything else to do, we have gone for the greenfield. But still we are pursuing few acquisitions, things that are still in discussion both here as well as overseas.

items.statement: Cayman cash reserves netted against debt used to finance new hospital; surplus on net cash basis; evaluating repatriation or other market opportunities
items.quote: although there is a cash balance, it is also significantly netted off against our outstanding debt, which we essentially borrowed to finance the new hospital. So, just looking at only the cash reserves in that market, it should be offset against the outstanding debt there to see on a net cash basis how much we have.

items.statement: Consolidated ETR outlook maintained at 14-17%; Cayman zero tax, India at domestic rates; mix shift drives rate
items.quote: Cayman comes at zero tax and India comes at India taxation rates. So if the share of profit of Cayman in the overall mix goes up, the ETR goes down. So that's the logic. But what we are seeing is that India also has been doing quite well in terms of India's performance itself, and Cayman will come back up after the new facilities commence. So, we would like to maintain the outlook on the tax rate

items.statement: Insurance pilot (Aditi) launched in Mysore, expanded to Bangalore; ₹1.2 mn GWP since inception; building retail distribution
items.quote: We've done about Rs. 1.2 million of premium GWP since we started. But obviously, we're building a retail business and a direct retail business and that takes time to scale up.

items.statement: Bangladesh visa restrictions minimal; only critical patients allowed; no clarity on normalization timeline
items.quote: The situation in Bangladesh, it continues to suffer. The visa restrictions are still in its minimal. Only the critical patients allowed entry into the country. It would definitely take a long period of time for the situation to normalize. We don't even know and have no clarity in terms of the timeline by when it is going to get normalized.

items.statement: Cayman major capex complete; only minor post-commissioning spend remaining
items.quote: the majority of our capital outlay in Cayman is mostly complete. I mean, we have a last few, little bit of expenditure for the new hospital post commissioning. But with this, with the new Camana Bay hospital we're done with any significant capital outlay in that market.

items.statement: Group ROE ~26.3% as of Sep 2024; India slightly higher, Cayman slightly lower due to new capex; not splitting mature vs new assets
items.quote: Our ROE overall as a group, if you would see, as of 30th September 2024, we would be around 26.3%. So that's the number that we've reported out. If you split it between India and Cayman, India is slightly on the higher side and Cayman is slightly on the lower side, but still in that range only, mainly because of the Capex that has gone online in Cayman.

items.statement: Hospital investments take 8-10 years to recover capital; land & building provide perennial asset sweating
items.quote: See, hospitals are a very long-term investment business. So, it takes 8 to 10 years, but you must also appreciate that a lot of the investments outside of biomedical, like the big chunk of the investment goes in land and building. So, your ability to sweat that asset exists almost perennially.

items.statement: Kolkata Rajarhat approvals in progress; expect all approvals in 3-4 months before groundbreaking
items.quote: The applications have all been done. The process approvals are in progress. We expect all the approvals to be sought by the next 3 -4 months' time before we start the groundbreaking there.

items.statement: Cayman October volumes returned to old trajectory; new hospital outpatient started November; expect Q3 growth
items.quote: In fact, we've already seen that in the first month of Q3, which is October. And there will be two reasons for that. One is just a return to normalcy. And also, at least by December of this quarter, the last month of the quarter, we hope to have the early signs of the new hospital with outpatient work and inpatient work kicking in.

items.statement: No specific growth guidance; maintaining healthy pace with focus on EBITDA, ARPP, ALOS reduction
items.quote: We don't normally give out guidance on the growth numbers. We're just trying to maintain a healthy pace of growth, keeping in mind that we're not adding any new beds and we're doing a lot of internal re-optimization, and with a focus on a very healthy EBITDA and focus on improving the realizations per patient and reducing the ALOS.

items.statement: Industry bed additions announced by organized players; high competition, long payback, no infrastructure-like protections
items.quote: The organized players have all announced significant bed additions over the next three years. Viren Shetty: So, all of us are, I would say, expanding to the best of our capabilities, keeping our debt to equity ratios in mind, making sure we don't overstretch and overleverage

items.statement: Cayman new facility expected to reach pre-commissioning margins in 4-5 quarters vs earlier 6-8 quarters
items.quote: We initially anticipated about 6-8 quarters to return to pre-commissioning margins. We now think that will be closer to 4-5 quarters as I had shared earlier as well.

items.statement: Similar integrated care burn rate expected for next 2 quarters as cohorts added
items.quote: Similar burn rate we can assume at least for the next 2 quarters. The logic with which NHIC works is cohort by cohort which means that we start a particular code which is a group of clinics and that cohort breaks even in about 18 months.

items.statement: Cayman Q2 revenue dipped 7% YoY due to hurricane; October already back on growth trajectory
items.quote: As I answered previously, the quarter was a little slower than we expected. There were quite a few small things adding up to lead to a disappointing quarter but then in the month that’s have gone by, that’s October, the first month of quarter 3, we are alr eady back to our previous growth trajectory and a little better as well

items.statement: Cayman Q2 revenue USD 29M vs USD 32M prior quarter; margin decline from new facility costs and lower existing revenue
items.quote: For example there are USD 29 Mn for Q2, the previous quarter was at USD 32 Mn and the one before was at USD 30.5 Mn or so, between USD 30 Mn & USD 31 Mn. You know our margins over there. So that gives you a rough sense of what can be attributed to the revenue decline and what will be on account of the new facility cost.

items.statement: Corporate overheads ~4% of revenue including ATHMA/MEDHA tech investment
items.quote: 4pc of revenue is what we normally clock in as corporate overheads but that also includes a significant investment in technology because we are investing significantly in ATMA and MEDA and including that, we do about 4pc of revenue.

items.statement: Bangladesh revenue share down to 6.5% from 9% post-pandemic; expected to trend to zero over decade
items.quote: Bangladesh was typically around 8-9pc of revenue. We have come down to 6.5pc of revenue. Viren Shetty: Prior to pandemic, it used to be 11pc, then it settled down post pandemic at 9pc, now it has come down to 6-7 but as I indicated earlier, in a decade’s time, this number will go down to 0

items.statement: Cayman Q3 margins to stay pressured: Oct-Nov zero/minimal revenue, full costs; revenue ramp from Dec
items.quote: Because in Q3, we will see all of October again, zero revenue, in November minimal revenue because of just outpatient facility is being commissioned. If all goes according to plan, December is when we will start seeing the revenue but for October, November, we would have incurred very significant costs.

items.statement: ATHMA/MEDHA SaaS revenue minimal for next 2-3 years; focus on adoption and product building
items.quote: As a revenue contributor, it's not contributing anything much now, nor we foresee it will be anything significant in the next 2-3 years. For now, we're just looking to really increase adoption and improve the product.

items.statement: Net interest margin rose from 5.2% to 7.1% for H1 FY25 driven by lending-as-a-service partnerships contributing 47% of AUM
items.quote: While funding costs have also risen modestly, we have seen an increase in our net interest margin, which rose from 5.2% to 7.1% for the half year, given increasing business with these lending as a service partner, which contributes to 47% of total AUM today.

items.statement: AUM grew to ₹12.2 billion from ₹7.8 billion a year ago; 65% gold loans, 34% MSME business and three-wheeler EV loans, 0.6% LAP and personal loans in run-off
items.quote: Our AUM has grown to 12.2 billion, up from 7.8 billion a year ago . 65% of our AUM comprises of gold loans, 34% in MSME business and three-wheeler EV loans and a mere 60 basis points in loan against property and personal loans, which are in run off mode.

items.statement: H1 FY25 disbursements were ₹6.5 billion, up from ₹5.6 billion in H1 FY24, driven by MSME Gold, MSME business loans and three-wheeler EV loans representing over 99% of AUM

So, on an overall basis, no change HL, NHL. On self-employed and salaried as we have guided earlier, we will try to move 1.5% every year.

items.statement: BT out rate improved to 5.8% annualized from 6.5% YoY, no risk of increase from rate hike
items.quote: So, Rinesh, BT out, if I were to compare versus on a Y-o-Y basis, we were in 24, 6.5%. And as we speak for the quarter, we are 5.8%. So that is a substantial improvement on this, on an annualized basis.

items.statement: GNPA at 1.29% with 35% provision coverage, expected to remain in 35-37% range
items.quote: We have managed to maintain good standard of asset quality with GNPA on AUM coming at 1.29% compared to 1.35% same time last year. The net NPA stood at 0.9% in Q2 FY25 versus 0.92% in Q2 FY24. As at September end, the stage 3 provision stands at 35% and as we have mentioned in our previous calls, our provision will be in the range of about 35% to 37%.

items.statement: Deeper impact strategy expanding to Tier 4 cities and small talukas, contributing 5-8% of business
items.quote: Our new initiative, which I spoke about in my opening speech of deeper i mpact, they will contribute 5% to 8% of the business. It's a new initiative, so it will take a little more time to get matured

items.statement: NHB sanction of ~INR 1,000 crores expected in Q3, to be drawn over four quarters
items.quote: Just to give a reference number, last year we had a INR1,000 crores sanction which came in, which was drawn down over a four quarter period.

items.statement: Fee income as percentage of disbursements guided at 2.2% to 2.4% conservatively
items.quote: I think to be conservatively you should model it around 2.2% to 2.4%.

items.statement: Sales team productivity at 3 logins per month and 1.25-1.29 disbursements per month, doubling after 6 months
items.quote: Yes, the productivity of the direct sales team, which is right at the front end, is 3 logins per month and about 1.25 to 1.29 disbursement units per month.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR1,21,532 million as of September 30, 2024
items.quote: Order book and revenue visibility as of September 30, 2024, our order book stands strong at INR1,21,532 million, indicating a healthy book-to-bill ratio.

items.statement: Order inflow of INR2,500 crores from two Ayodhya HAM projects and INR900 crores metro project plus INR143 crores bus terminal in H1 FY25
items.quote: we have received two orders - three orders. Two orders from Ayodhya. One is Northern Ayodhya Bypass and another is Southern Ayodhya Bypass , b oth are HAM projects of the company and with the EPC, the company got a Northern Ayodhya Bypass project at a EPC value of approximately INR1,200 crores and a Southern Ayodhya Bypass project at a EPC value of INR1,300 crores

items.statement: Targeting 15% to 20% revenue growth for FY25 on standalone basis
items.quote: Last yea r, we achieved a turnover of INR 2,952 crores. We are expecting this year turnover in line with our guidance that is 15% growth rate, 15 % to 20% growth rate this year

items.statement: EBITDA margin excluding bonus and royalty at 12.6% for Q2 FY25, standard range 12.5% to 13.5%
items.quote: The EBITDA excluding bonus and royalty for the current quarter stood at 12.6%. The EBITDA for the corresponding quarter last year stood at 13%. So, the pure EBITDA margin from the pure construction activity of the company which the company carries out, it stood at between 12.5 to 13.5.

items.statement: Targeting early completion bonus for Bathinda Dabwali HAM project to improve margins in H2 FY25
items.quote: We are targeting one more bonus which could be for Bathinda Dabwali. I mean, it will be the completed super ahead of schedule. So, with that bonus coming, yes, it will improve.

items.statement: Equity requirement of INR494 crores for Varanasi-Ranchi-Jharkhand projects and INR350 crores for two Ayodhya projects
items.quote: total requirement of equity for Varanasi, Ranchi and Jharkhand project is INR494 crores a nd as far as these two Ayodhya projects are concerned, so total equity requirement for these projects would be close to INR350

items.statement: Debt-equity ratio at 0.21 as of September 2024, expected to remain 0.21 to 0.25 by March 2025
items.quote: As on September 2024 our debt equity ratio stood at 0.21. So, on an average basis on December and March, we are expecting to be in the range of 0.21 to 0.25.

items.statement: Net working capital days at 61 as of September 30, 2024
items.quote: The net working capital days have stood at 61 as of September 30. The days have been calculated considering the inventory days, WIP position, debtor and the vendor.

items.statement: Mobilization advances outstanding at INR252 crores as of September 30, 2024
items.quote: As on 30th September, the total mobilization advance which we have taken, is INR252 crores, which is outstanding as on 30th September.

items.statement: Targeting to start 2-3 new projects in next 1.5 quarters including Ayodhya HAM projects and Jharkhand elevated project
items.quote: We are expecting and targeting to start at least two to three new projects in coming next 1.5 quarter.

items.statement: Ayodhya HAM projects (INR2,500 crores) to start in Q4 FY25, Jharkhand elevated project (INR2,900 crores) Package 1 in Q3 FY25, remaining packages in Q4 FY25
items.quote: We are targeting three, but it's hardly one and a half month left now. And fourth quarter, we are sure that Ayodhya will be started, both the projects. That will really help us in pushing our revenue and everything and Jharkhand, again, I said before, one package is very clear. We should start and the second one, we are trying our level best.

items.statement: Order book composition: 85.7% roads/highways/elevated/tunnels, 12.64% railways/metros, 1.8% bus terminals, 0.48% airport runways
items.quote: Our order composition includes 85.7% from roads, highways, elevated flyovers, tunnels, 12.64% from railways and metros, 1.8% from bus terminals and 0.48% from airport runways.

items.statement: Focusing on specialized structures (elevated, bridges, metros) avoiding highway rat race, 60% of order book is structure work
items.quote: And our structure work order book value is about 60% of our total order book value. And we are bidding for some other specialized projects also, which I can't tell you right now. But once we bag those contracts definitely, it'll be announced to SEBI, but we are avoiding the rat race, going into highway bidding and we are going into specialized bidding.

items.statement: Open to monetizing HAM assets via individual sale or InvIT, no fixed timeline, will decide based on cash flow needs
items.quote: The company has the open plans for monetization of its HAM asset. That can be done in the form of either individual HAM asset sales to any strategic investor or in the form of InvIT. The company would be exercising the due option, considering its cash flow position and the fund requirements for its long-term resources.

items.statement: NHAI revised model concession agreement offers substantial risk mitigation, making BOT model more investment-friendly
items.quote: The revised model reconciliation agreement introduced by NHAI offers a substantial risk mitigation making it more investment-friendly.

items.statement: HAM project Malout Abohar Sadhuwali rated AAA by CRISIL, company overall rating A+ long-term by CRISIL
items.quote: I would also like to highlight that the HAM project has been rated AAA by CRISIL. As of now, the overall credit rating of the company is A-plus long-term, short-term as per CRISIL.

items.statement: Emerging as L1 bidder for two Ayodhya HAM projects worth INR1,299.2 crores and INR1,199.3 crores
items.quote: I am also pleased to announce that our company has emerged as L1 bidder for two new HAM projects. Southern Bypass Ayodhya worth INR1299.2 crores a nd Northern Ayodhya Bypass worth INR1199.3 crores

items.statement: One elevated project in Jharkhand worth INR207 crores is L1 but awaiting award due to state elections
items.quote: Yes, there is one elevated project in Jharkhand which is about INR207 crores which is yet to be awarded. I think there are some elections in the state. So, once the elections are over, then I think they might allot us.

items.statement: Renegotiating with bankers for better pricing on BG charges, funded debt margins, interest rates, and working capital margin reduction from 20% to 10%
items.quote: Since now the company is listed, we are renegotiating with the bankers for the betterment of the pricing, be it a BG charges, be it a margin against the funded debt and also against the rate of interest on the fund-based limit. And the company is also negotiating for the reduction of the margins for the working capital limit from 20% to 10%.

items.statement: Bathinda Dabwali project delayed 3 years due to land acquisition, appointed date issued August 2023 but final land still pending
items.quote: If you see, Bathinda Dabwali we quoted in 2020 October, I think. So, this work got started last year 23 after 3 years around 3 years. August 11th was the appointed date, if I'm not wrong. Appointed dates are always issued by government when they give us the land.

items.statement: Atmanirbhar scheme relaxed milestone payments removed, returning to standard milestone payment schedule affecting cash flow timing
items.quote: The Atmanirbhar scheme was there during COVID, which was a relaxation for milestone payments. Earlier, if we were supposed to get a milestone payment at 10%, 30%, 70%, 50%, because of Atmanirbhar we could get payments in between also. So, the Atmanirbhar sector has been removed now. So, now, back again we have the m ilestone payments. And in EPC milestone

items.statement: Bid pipeline of over INR10,000 crores already quoted, expecting another INR8,000-10,000 crores in next 3-4 months
items.value: INR10,000+ crores quoted, INR8,000-10,000 crores pipeline
items.quote: So, bid pipeline, we have already quoted projects more than INR10,000 crores and we can see a lot of bids coming in the next 3 months, 4 months. Normally, if these bids get received, we would have another INR8,000 to INR10,000 crores.

items.statement: Received INR906 million annuity from NHAI for first HAM project Malout Abohar Sadhuwali completed ahead of schedule
items.quote: The company has received an annuity of INR906 million on a gross basis from NH AI for its first HAM project Malout Abohar Sadhuwali which was completed ahead of schedule

items.statement: Company operates in 13+ states with 11 verticals, enabling geographic and segment diversification
items.quote: We've already crossed 13 states. So, if you're not getting projects in Punjab, it doesn't matter. We'll get it in Jharkhand or Bihar or UP. So, that's about us.

items.statement: Targets 20-25% YoY growth in real estate booking value
items.quote: We are focused on future expansion through a capitalized business model via JDA route and targeting 20% to 25% growth in booking value year-on-year.

items.statement: Expects real estate bookings to reach near Rs 4,000 crore next year
items.quote: Clearly, you can safely assume a 20% growth rate on the bookings every year, year-on-year. So, next year itself, we will be very close to Rs. 4,000 crores.

items.statement: Engineering H2 expected to be better than H1
items.quote: No, it should be better.

items.statement: Residential real estate demand remains strong in Mumbai with 6-8% price growth
items.quote: We are not seeing any signs of demand abating. So, demand is still strong. It's doing well. Prices are also holding well. They are not running away. So, it's a very healthy market today with large volumes and prices remaining more or less steady with 6% to 8% increase year-on-year.

items.statement: Engineering consumables domestic market weak, export market improving
items.quote: However, the domestic market continues to have a little bit challenge. But if I look at the auto ancillary, I think the first six months, as you heard me saying, first six months have been quite a decent number. But we are seeing a little bit weakness right now.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 consolidated EBITDA margin 15.6%
items.quote: And during the quarter, the Company has delivered an EBITDA of Rs. 172 crores in the 2nd Quarter of Fiscal 2025, with an EBITDA margin of 15.6%.

items.statement: Real estate segment EBITDA Rs 112 crore in Q2 FY25
items.quote: The segment reported an EBITDA of Rs. 112 crores in the 2nd Quarter of Fiscal '25 compared to Rs. 47 crores in the 2nd Quarter of Fiscal '24, which is higher as compared to the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Engineering segment EBITDA margin 11% in Q2 FY25 due to product mix change
items.quote: During the quarter, the business reported an EBITDA margin at 11%, mainly due to changes in the product mix.

items.statement: Real estate bookings Rs 562 crore in Q2 FY25 driven by TenX Era, Thane retail shops, Bandra JDA
items.quote: In the 2nd Quarter of Fiscal '25, the Company achieved a strong booking of real estate of Rs. 562 crores, primarily driven by the demand for the TenX Era, sale of retail shops in Thane, as well as in JDA Project of The Address By GS in Bandra.

items.statement: Engineering business operates on order-based production with 3-4 month lead times, no discrete order book disclosed
items.quote: Whatever we produce, it is a B2B business. So, you produce based on the orders only. So, like that, we have always an order book because the lead times of certain products is three to four months and certain products are 30 days.

items.statement: Launched Park Avenue High Street retail project in Thane with 80,000 sq ft RERA carpet area in September 2024
items.quote: In the 2nd Quarter of Fiscal '25, we have launched our commercial project for retail shops Park Avenue - High Street Reimagined Retail in Thane with a RERA carpet area of 80,000 square feet in the September 2024, the first of its kind High Street Retail in Thane, which received an overwhelming response.

items.statement: Thane land bank: 40 acres under development (4 msf, Rs 9,000 cr revenue potential), 60 acres balance (7 msf, Rs 16,000 cr potential)
items.quote: Out of this 100 acres of land, approximately 40 acres is currently under development and there are five ongoing projects adding up to 4 million square feet, generating a revenue approximately of Rs. 9,000 crores, with an additional potential of 7 million square feet on the balance 60 acres to generate another Rs. 16,000 crores of revenues.

items.statement: Four JDA projects in MMR with combined revenue potential over Rs 7,000 crore
items.quote: Additionally, we have signed also 4 JDA projects in Mahim, Sion, and including the Bandra project, the combined revenue from four JDA projects in Mumbai Metropolitan Region is over Rs. 7,000 crores.

items.statement: Total revenue potential from Thane land bank and JDAs is Rs 32,000 crore over next few years
items.quote: With this and the development potential of Thane land bank and 4 JDAs gives the Company a total revenue possibility of Rs. 32,000 over the next few years.

items.statement: Engineering revenue split: ~15% aerospace, ~65% auto components
items.quote: So, if I look at it, roughly 15% comes from the aerospace, and 65% comes from the auto components.

items.statement: EV component revenue is very small at ~1% of engineering
items.quote: As far as EV is concerned, it is a very small portion, very, very small, 1%.

items.statement: Engineering exports ~two-thirds of revenue
items.quote: So, almost two-third is export.

items.statement: Thane market has established competitors for 10-15 years, Raymond is relatively new entrant
items.quote: Every big developer has got a larger than our project in Thane and they have been there for over 10, 15 years. In fact, we are the new ones.

items.statement: Real estate demerger scheme filed with stock exchanges, shareholders to get 1:1 share in Raymond Realty
items.quote: The proposed demerger is progressing well with the demerger scheme filed with the stock exchanges. Upon completion, the new entity will seek automatic listing. According to the scheme of arrangements, each shareholder of Raymond Limited will receive one share of Raymond Realty Limited for every share held in Raymond Limited.

items.statement: Engineering restructuring scheme filed with NCLT to create two subsidiaries for aerospace/defense and auto/consumables
items.quote: In the engineering business, as announced earlier, in the remaining business, two new subsidiaries of Raymond Limited will be created through a scheme of arrangements, one focused on aerospace and defense, the other on auto components and engineering consu mables, each charting its own path for growth and a primary objective of value creation. Currently, we have filed the restructuring scheme with

items.statement: Net cash surplus Rs 685 crore, up Rs 184 crore since March 2024; gross debt Rs 906 crore including MPPL acquisition debt
items.quote: We continue to remain a net debt-free business with a net cash surplus of Rs. 685 crores, an increase of cash of Rs. 184 crore since March 2024. The total gross debt stands at Rs. 906 crores, which includes the debt taken for the acquisition of the MPPL, as well as the existing working capital facilities at MPPL.

items.statement: Cash and cash equivalents Rs 1,591 crore as of September 30, 2024
items.quote: Additionally, we maintain strong liquidity with cash and cash equivalents of Rs. 1,591 crores as of September 30th, 2024.

items.statement: Interest cost Rs 29 crore in Q2 FY25, up Rs 20 crore YoY due to MPPL acquisition debt and MHADA/TMC payment deferment
items.quote: The interest cost in the quarter is Rs. 29 crores, higher by Rs. 20 crores on a year-on-year basis as compared to Rs. 9 crores in the same quarter last year. The rising interest cost can be attributed to the following factors: interest costs of Rs. 14 crores on account of acquisition debt for Maini Precision, as well as working capital debt at Maini Precision; and another Rs. 4 crores interest cos

items.statement: Aerospace growth impacted by production issues at major aircraft manufacturer causing shipment delays
items.quote: Aerospace business growth impacted by ongoing production issues faced by one of the largest aircraft manufacturers, leading to delays in shipment.

items.statement: Auto component sector seeing near-term weakness in certain global pockets
items.quote: Additionally, recent softness in the auto component sector due to weaker market may impact the growth in the near term.

items.statement: JK House property remains with Raymond Limited post demerger
items.quote: JK House is a property of Raymond Limited and stays in Raymond Limited.

items.statement: Pune realty market entry under evaluation, actively looking at deals but nothing signed
items.quote: So, we are currently studying the market and actively looking at quite a few deals, but nothing to report as such. Once we sign something, we will definitely share with you.

items.statement: Gross margin erosion of around 100 basis points due to raw material inflation
items.quote: The impact of rising RMC is felt on the gross margins. There is a margin erosion of around 100 basis points led by the RM inflation.

items.statement: Gross margin uptick expected from November as raw material inventory dilutes
items.quote: And once the inventory dilutes, I think we will see the uptick in the margins, which is expected in the November onwards.

items.statement: Slight pickup in retail secondaries in last two weeks of September and early October
items.quote: But we've seen a huge uptick in our secondaries. However, what we've seen is that the retail ability to stock up, which is our primary sales to the -- in the direct market to the retailer or our distributor sales to the retailer has not been of the level that the offtakes have been there in the second half.

items.statement: H2 volume growth expected between high single-digit to double-digit
items.quote: We believe that we should be between a high single-digit to a double-digit growth.

items.statement: Product mix to remain balanced with marginal adverse impact as mass segment grows
items.quote: So look, I think the mix will be balanced as we move ahead. I believe that, look, we still got scope to grow in premium because in India, the premium consumers tend to consume.

items.statement: Working capital at 5% of revenue supports capex plans and dividend payout
items.quote: Working capital remains efficient and as a percentage of revenue stood at 5%. This has helped to generate healthy cash flows and it supported our capex plans and dividend payout.

items.statement: Price drop impact of almost 3% still affecting revenue growth
items.quote: Because of the price drop at the beginning of the year, there's still an impact of almost close to 3%.

items.statement: No price cuts planned due to volatile raw material costs and currency
items.quote: So keeping this in mind, I don't think we are looking at price cuts at this point of time because I think that will be naive because then you will have to take significant price increases next year to cover the cost of any wage inflation and other things t hat you -- NFT or whatever you ask, right

items.statement: EBIT margin guidance maintained with only 0.5% depletion depending on competitive intensity
items.quote: I stick to the EBIT margin guidances that I've always given. We don't want to deplete our profitability other than 0.5% type of stuff depending on competitive intensity.

items.statement: A&P spend to increase from 2.5-3% to 3.5-4% of revenue with initiatives from January and more pronounced by March
items.quote: A&P, we have been hovering around the 2.5% to 3% of revenue. As I said, our stated intent is to go closer to 3.5%, 4%. You will see various initiatives that Rohit and team will deploying starting January, more pronounced towards March next year.

items.statement: B2B growth driven by focused order book work across businesses
items.quote: I think it's also because we've focused and we've been working hard on our order book across our businesses, right? So I think that with a specific focus in certain sectors is giving us better growth.

items.statement: Collections and overdues becoming challenging across industry due to money crunch
items.quote: We believe that in this industry and many of the other peer industries, overdue and collections have become a bit of a challenging because of some money crunch that we observed in the market.

items.statement: Inventory built up to INR 741 crores ahead of festive season, expected to normalize in 30-45 days
items.quote: The inventory buildup is predominantly ahead of the festive season. We beefed up the inventory, and that has resulted in a spike in inventory, as of 30th September, we were at INR741 crores. It will get normalized over a period of 1 month to 45 days period.

items.statement: Distribution expansion targeting 5,700-6,000 towns in next couple of quarters
items.quote: We are on the anvil of getting close to 5,700 to 6,000 towns between -- in the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: Competitive intensity increased in decorative B2C after new entrant, discounts marginally up
items.quote: So the answer on competitive intensity is, of course, it's increased. I mean, frankly, it has increased over the last 6 months after the new entrant has come in.

items.statement: Management expects FY25 volume growth to exceed 10%
items.quote: I think this year also we hope to cross 10%.

items.statement: Pharma inventory issues easing but agrochemicals remain under pressure from Chinese cost competition
items.quote: within pharma sector we see that this seems to be easing a little bit because the other part of the life science, which is the agro-chemical segment still continue to remain under pressure both from the inventory point of view and also from the cost pressure which is coming in from China

items.statement: Half-year margins squeezed ~2 percentage points as finished goods prices fell 5-6% vs raw material prices down 3-4%
items.quote: the finished good prices have dropped a little more than the raw material prices over the period half year to half year. And therefore, the margins have got squeezed by about 2% at points. So, say the finished good prices have dropped by an average of 5%-6% but the raw material prices have dropped 3%-4%.

items.statement: H2 margin outlook uncertain; focus on volume over margin but aiming for both
items.quote: We are always optimistic that we will try to improve the margin, but we don't want to sacrifice volume because of it. So, our focus will be more volume than margins, but of course at the same time, we try to expand the margins. But it's difficult to say where we will in the end land up.

items.statement: FY25 capex Rs 80-100 cr; FY26 capex Rs 100-120 cr
items.quote: This year it will be around 80 to 100 crores, and next year may be a slightly larger, about 100 to 120 crores may be.

items.statement: Overall utilization 65-70%; Ethylamines new plant has 3-4 years headroom; some products need debottlenecking
items.quote: The existing capacities on average would be 65% to 70% utilization, but it varies from product to product. Some we have very tight where we will be de-bottlenecking and there is some CAPEX involved with that. But of the major products, as we have known the Ethylamines last year, we commissioned the huge plant. So, there is plenty of headroom in Ethyl.

items.statement: Acetonitrile market ~30,000 tons; company utilization ~60% across two plants
items.quote: Well, we have two plants, one in Kurkumbh and one in Dahej, and we use them at maybe I think overall 60% I think capacities would be in that region.

items.statement: Life sciences 65-70% of turnover; domestic/export split ~80/20; pharma share rising slowly over years
items.quote: They haven't changed at all from our regular life sciences accounting for 65%-70% of our turnover and the rest all, as you can see from our website or wherever, it doesn't change dramatically. Even the domestic export sectors are more or less the same 80-20.

items.statement: Chinese overcapacity and weak global agro demand driving pricing pressure across value chain; normalization timeline uncertain
items.quote: I think it is more of a capacity expansion issue. There are overcapacities. They have put on more capacities in the last few years, and the demand has really not picked up too so that all those capacities are utilized, and we see such an immense pressure across the value chain.

items.statement: Anti-dumping investigation on Acetonitrile ongoing; plant inspection and costing review next; final decision in 4-5 months
items.quote: after oral hearing now they will come for investigation of our plant and as well as costing records, and then MoC will issue their findings. After that, MoF generally takes 3 to 4 months. Next 4 to 5 months we should expect something.

items.statement: Working capital days (debtors, creditors) stabilized; no significant change expected
items.quote: I think the working capital cycle, number of days of debtors, number of days of creditors and all have, I think, more or less stabilized, maybe an improvement marginally as volumes go, but nothing significant. I don't think there will be any change in working capital.

items.statement: Continuous yield and specific consumption improvements via process engineering and R&D teams; permanent baseline gains each year
items.quote: every year we have been improving our yields and specific consumptions across products regularly. So, though they may not be very dramatic, there is every attempt to make both through the process engineering group and the R&D group trying to improve our cost structures from point of view of consumptions regularly. It is a constant practice.

items.statement: Europe energy costs and green chemistry push adding pressure on agrochemical customers and industry utilization
items.quote: Europe, for example, is having their own issues with respect to the large energy costs for agro-chemical and chemical production in general as well. And also on the same way, on the user side, they are pushing for more of the so-called green chemistry related products, eco-friendly products.

items.statement: H1 volume growth 8-10% YoY; Q2 volume growth 17% YoY (low base)
items.quote: half-yearly basis the volume growth is about 8% to 10%, and compared to last year quarter, itis 17%.

items.statement: Export share ~20% annually (18-22% quarterly); management cautious on pushing exports given global situation
items.quote: Yes, I think it is on similar levels. What happens is quarter-to-quarter, sometimes we are fulfilling one commitment to the export, so sometimes it goes to 21%-22% and sometimes it drops to 18%, but it is overall about 20% annually, 20%-21%. So, between quarters, there is not much, you know, it is not a significant change. Yes, we would like to push exports, but given the global situation, we don'

items.statement: New Dahej project part of earlier Rs 225 cr plan (now higher cost); two other molecules on hold pending market improvement
items.quote: No, this is a part of that 225 crores project. The other part we are still on the R&D stage. This is one of the two lines of products which we were looking at that time. And in the meantime, of course, costs of plant and machinery have got up. So, I think that 225 crores was an underestimate

items.statement: Q2 FY25 saw slow customer call-offs leading to lower sales bookings; expect reversal before March 2025 as customers remain committed to orders
items.quote: Q2 FY '25 continued to witness slow call-offs by our customers, which led to the lower sales booking in Q2 of FY '25. However, we expect to reverse the situat ion before March of 2025 as the customers remain committed to their orders

items.statement: Extended rainfall in some geographies reduced domestic juice consumption; expect severe summer to boost Q4 demand
items.quote: There is a cost of repetition that all these domestic order book positions, which are there for last so many years, there has not been a single order cancellation. However, the call-offs do happen. So, for the domestic, the specific reason being extended rainfall i n some of the geographies, whereby specifically for Indians -The consumption of a juice is asp irational and it is climate related

items.statement: Order book for mango pulp booked once a year for 15-17 months; no reduction in order booking, slightly up vs last year; delays due to freight and vessel issues
items.quote: Our order is booking once in a year for period of next 15 to 17 months. So there is no reduction in order booking. However, it is slightly up. However, due to the d emand/supply situation in Indian beverage industry as well as across the globe, due to some freight issue, non-availability of the vessels, there is some delay in the shipment, which is a major cause for -- I mean, one of the major cau

items.statement: Production quantities indicated at season start reflect order book; produced 40% more last year and still supplying crop year 2023 inventory
items.quote: Last year, we had produced 40% more than the p revious year. And we are still supplying crop year 2023 inventory as we speak

items.statement: More than doubled tomato processing capacity; new capacity going on stream this month
items.quote: We have more than doubled our tomato processing capacity as we also mentioned about this in the previous conference call and that capacity is going on stream this month.

items.statement: New pastry line doing well; planning to expand by adding two more lines in immediate future
items.quote: Our new pastry line is doing very well and enthused by the market and the response -We are planning to expand the pastry line further by adding two more lines in the immediate future.

items.statement: Spray drying expanded capacity running close to full capacity from October 2024; foresee full capacity utilization for extended capacity in remaining part of year
items.quote: The spray drying expanded capacity Foods & is now running close to full capacity from the month of October, 2024 and we foresee full capacity utilization for the extended capacity in the remaining part of the year

items.statement: Growth in frozen vegetables and snacks category in export markets with expansion of product categories and geographies
items.quote: We continue to witness growth in frozen vegetables and snacks categ ory in the export markets with the expansion of product categories and geographies

items.statement: Tetra Recart product development and testing with brands ongoing; expect traction in coming years
