items.quote: Please understand that we are inundated by the customer requests and new models is the order of the day.

items.statement: Group localised cables and achieved success in charging connectors made in India
items.quote: From our side, as we had mentioned earlier that the group has already started and locali sed the cables, started locali sing and achieved success in the charging connectors completely made here in India.

items.statement: Cannot disclose customer-specific or voltage-type details due to confidentiality
items.quote: Raghunandhan, thing is that we can't give details because our customers don't like it. Once we start to answer this, then you can already assume that it's an electric vehicle or an ICE vehicle or whatever. So we can't -- we are privy to a lot of confidence from the customers, so please understand.

items.statement: Target 13 more store openings before end of FY25, total 25 new stores for FY25
items.quote: Looking ahead we are actively working on adding 13 more stores before the end of FY25.

items.statement: Rs 35 crores capital outlay for 12 stores opened April 2024 to present
items.quote: We have successfully opened 12 stores with a total capital outlay of Rs. 35 crores.

items.statement: October 2024 saw record 47% year-on-year growth, confident about Q3 festive and wedding season
items.quote: In October we had a record month with a 47% year -on-year growth.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin 15.9%, H1 FY25 16.8%; excluding forex Q2 would be 17.5%, H1 17.6%
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 15.9% in Q2 FY25.

items.statement: Forex loss of Rs 4.65 crores in Q2 FY25 due to INR-CHF fluctuation; Rs 2.34 cr in exchange fluctuation, balance in COGS
items.quote: This movement had a notable impact on our financial results resulting in a FOREX loss of approximately Rs 4.65 crores.

items.statement: Exclusive brands 31% of Q2 FY25 revenue; luxury and high luxury share at all-time high in H1 FY25
items.quote: Revenue from exclusive brands stood at 31% of the total revenue in Q2 FY25.

items.statement: Signed exclusive agreements with three new brands since April 2024: ID Geneve, Singer Reimagined, Hautlence
items.quote: We have signed exclusive agreements with three more brands which are ID Geneve, Singer Reimagined and Hautlence.

items.statement: H1 FY25 same store growth 15.5%; ASP Rs 2.16 lakhs vs Rs 1.87 lakhs in H1 FY24
items.quote: Our same store growth for the first half of FY25 demonstrates strong progress, reaching 15.5% in H1 FY25.

items.statement: Certified pre-owned business (Second Movement) billings Rs 43 crores in H1 FY25, 33.6% YoY growth
items.quote: The certified pre-owned business, which is Second Movement, it has experienced a 25% year -on-year growth , reaching billings of Rs. 43 crores in H1 FY25.

items.statement: Messika Jewellery boutique at Chanakya Mall Delhi on track to open January-February 2025
items.quote: Currently in the setup phase, the boutique is on track to open its doors by January or February of 2025.

items.statement: Favre Leuba India launch January 2025 across 40 boutiques; pre-orders over 100,000 CHF at zero discounts
items.quote: From 12th of January onwards the Favre Leuba watches will be available across 40 boutiques in India along with a strong digital marketing campaign.

items.statement: Target 8-10X growth in Rimowa business over 5 years; 8-10 Messika boutiques in 5 years
items.quote: In my opinion over the next 5 years, we are going to at least target an 8X to 10X increase in the business of just Rimowa itself.

items.statement: GST hike to 28% would require 8.5% revenue-neutral price increase; EFTA benefits to start next year
items.quote: The 8.5% is that if you want to remain at the same revenue, net-off taxes, you need to take an 8.5% price increase.

items.statement: Inventory days 177 as of 30 September 2024; cash and bank balance Rs 271.4 crores
items.quote: Inventory days, as on 30 th September stood at 177 days. Cash and bank balance stood at Rs. 271.4 crores as of 30th September 2024.

items.statement: Store count 72 as of October 2024 (70 end Q2, +4 in October); 3 boutiques combined into 1 under renovation
items.quote: As of now the total store count is 72. In October we opened 4 stores.

items.statement: 15-day intensive training + 4-level certification for all frontline staff to maintain service quality in Tier-II expansion
items.quote: Each and every new employee goes through a 15 day intensive training program , post which we've got a certification program. We've got four levels of certification which happen over the employee's tenure in the company.

items.statement: Management confident of maintaining 30% gross margins irrespective of GST hike; discussing with government representatives
items.quote: I do believe that. Again, as I mentioned I don't want to go into something that is when and if it happens, I am sure our management will make sure that our 10-year vision doesn't change.

items.statement: Differentiation via authorized status, pan-India service network, multi-brand inventory, 250k Instagram followers, 60k website orders, concierge service
items.quote: We've got 250k nearly Instagram followers, we get around 60k business through a website. All of those help in terms of building out our entire differentiation with us.

items.statement: Pre-owned segment projected 20% growth for remainder of FY25; focusing on high-value consignment acquisitions
items.quote: We foresee 20% growth in the projected year and the remaining year.

items.statement: Overall business target 10x in 10 years; healthy mix of same store growth and new store additions
items.quote: Our goal is to increase our overall revenue, and our overall business will be 10times in 10 years.

items.statement: H1 FY25 PAT margin 7%; Q2 FY25 PAT Rs 21.2 crores, 14% YoY growth
items.quote: PAT margin stood at 7%.

items.statement: H1 FY25 volume growth 5% YoY; Q2 FY25 volume growth 17% YoY despite heatwaves, elections, rains, shradh period
items.quote: Our overall volume increased by 17% in Q2 FY25 and 5% in H1 FY25 on a YOY basis.

items.statement: India pricing currently 1-4% lower than global on average due to CHF appreciation; some brands already higher
items.quote: Realistically you can go on the websites and see, it's roughly just 1 or 2 maybe 3 % or 4% lower on average.

items.statement: No fund raise mentioned; cash balance Rs 271.4 crores as of September 2024
items.quote: Cash and bank balance stood at Rs. 271.4 crores as of 30th September 2024.

items.statement: Earnings conferences to be held half-yearly going forward
items.quote: Moving forward we will be hosting our earnings conferences half yearly.

items.statement: Expects ethanol supply of 6.5 crore litres for current ethanol supply year 2024-25
items.quote: We expect this year's ethanol supply to be in the region of about 6 crores litres. I think the total ethanol quantity which we have contracted for the current year is 6.5 crores litres.

items.statement: Expects higher cane crushing than last year but no specific number given
items.quote: As I mentioned earlier, I don't want to give any specific number, but I think it would be fair to say we are hoping it will be higher than last year for sure.

items.statement: Expects sugar exports of about 2 million tons plus by government
items.quote: And export also, now we believe there is adequate reason to allow for sugar to about 2 million tons plus of sugar export.

items.statement: Expects clarity on MSP, ethanol prices, and exports in next 1-2 months post Maharashtra elections
items.quote: I would imagine more and more clarity will come in the next 1 or 2 months when they will talk about export. They will give you some guidance on export hopefully. They will give us some guidance on what is their view on MSP. They will give us some guidance on what their view on – ethanol prices are there.

items.statement: Grain-based distillery capex of INR48 crores out of INR94 crores CWIP as of Sep 2024; balance is sugar capacity capex
items.quote: So, against capex of INR60 crores around INR48 crores is of grain. Rest is normal capex. 94, 48, 50 is grain. Rest is normal.

items.statement: Grain distillery to be capitalized by end of Q3 FY25; interest subvention of 50% on INR40 crore loan
items.quote: Out of against that distillery we have INR40 crores loans against which we will get the 50% interest subvention.

items.statement: Ethanol plant utilization expected at 82-85% including levy; 15% idle capacity for opportunistic grain/molasses use
items.quote: Roughly between 82%-85%. It will depend upon the final cane numbers, obviously.

items.statement: Mansurpur plant started crushing; Asmoli and Meerganj to start within a week
items.quote: Only Mansurpur has started. There was no delay. There was delayed Diwali and because of late trend we didn't find any big reason to start earlier than this. Mansurpur has already started crushing. Asmoli is supposed to start in this week and Meerganj probably early next week.

items.statement: Dual feed distillery conversion on track
items.quote: Part of our capacity of our distillery to a dual feed process is on track.

items.statement: Sugar sales volume up 5% YoY to 99,147 tons in Q2 FY25; institutional sales focus improved realization
items.quote: Our sugar sales during Q2 FY25 stood at 99,147 tons, an increase of 5% from 94,870 tons during the previous year during Q2 FY24. Our focus on institutional sales and the increased volume helped us get a little better price over the corresponding quarter last year due to which our overall sugar realisation improved from INR38,152 per ton in Q2 FY24 to INR38,720 per ton in Q2 FY25.

items.statement: Country liquor sales volume up 27% YoY to 7.6 lakh cases in Q2 FY25
items.quote: We sold 7,60,200 cases of country liquor at an average realization of INR274 against 5,96,880 cases of country liquor in Q2FY24.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA negative INR7.4 crores vs positive INR20.5 crores YoY due to lower ethanol sales
items.quote: EBITDA for Q2FY25 stood at negative of INR7.4 crores as against EBITDA of INR20.5 crores in the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA margin 2.1% vs 4.6% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 2.1% as against 4.6% in the corresponding period last year.

items.statement: Sugar segment EBIT loss INR11 crores in Q2 FY25 vs profit INR32 lakhs YoY
items.quote: EBIT loss stood at INR11 crores as against EBIT profit of INR32 lakhs in corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: Biofuels segment EBIT negative INR2 lakhs in Q2 FY25 vs INR14.5 crores profit YoY
items.quote: Biofuels segment , EBIT stood at negative of INR2 lakhs in this quarter as compared to INR14.5 crores in Q2FY24.

items.statement: Sugar realization improved 1.46% to INR38.72/kg in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Our average sugar realization for Q2FY25 increased by 1.46% to 38.72 per kg from 38.16 per kg in Q2FY24.

items.statement: Ethanol prices unchanged for two years: sugarcane juice INR65.61/ltr, B-heavy INR60.73/ltr; C-heavy increased to INR56.28/ltr last year
items.quote: Currently the basic rate for sugarcane juice and B heavy derived ethanol have remained the same which is INR65.61 per litre for sugarcane juice based ethanol and INR60.73 per litre for B heavy molasses. These rates have remained unchanged for the last two years. C heavy molasses derived ethanol prices meanwhile were increased last year from INR49.41 per litre to INR56.28 per litre.

items.statement: Landed cane cost INR82/quintal; SAP INR370/quintal for general variety
items.quote: Landed cost of sugarcane for us. INR82 a quintal of sugar. A quintal of cane. A quintal of cane, sorry.

items.statement: Sugar inventory valued at INR34.12/kg as of Sep 2024 vs INR34.9/kg last year
items.quote: Our inventory as on 30th September 2024 stood at 1.03 lakh tons of sugar valued at 34.12 per kg as compared to 10,364 tons of sugar as on 30th September 2023 which was valued at 34.9 per kg.

items.statement: Cost of production for white sugar INR35.18/kg (excludes admin depreciation and interest)
items.quote: The valuation as of 30th September for white is 35.18 and overall it is 34.4 per kg for the whole of sugar. And for white sugar, it is 35.18 per kg.

items.statement: Contracted 6.5 crore litres ethanol for current supply year; 312 crore litres allocated to sugar segment nationally
items.quote: I think the total ethanol quantity which we have contracted for the current year is 6.5 crores litres.

items.statement: Sugar release mechanism constant at 30,000-35,000 tons per month
items.quote: So, we have been getting about the sugar as per the release order takes into account the people who are balanced. So our sugar releases have been fairly constant between 30,000-35,000 tons.

items.statement: Interest cost rose to INR15.76 crores from INR8.8 crores YoY due to higher inventory and capex deployment
items.quote: Interest cost in this quarter has gone from INR8.8 crores in Q2FY24 to INR15.76 crores in this quarter mainly on account of substantially higher inventory and higher deployment of internal accruals towards capex in the same period.

items.statement: Long-term debt INR239 crores as of Sep 2024; repaid INR34 crores in H1 FY25; debt-equity 0.24x
items.quote: Our long -term loan stood at INR239 crores as on 30th September 2024 as against INR230 crores as on 31st June 2024. We have repaid long term loans of around INR34 crores during the first half. Long term debt equity remained at INR0.24 times.

items.statement: CARE rating A with stable outlook for long-term and short-term
items.quote: Long term and short term rating of the company continues to be assigned by CARE at A with stable outlook.

items.statement: Government allowed ethanol from sugarcane juice, B-heavy, C-heavy molasses for ESY 2024-25; also allowed rectified spirit and ENA from all three feedstocks
items.quote: The Government of India's move to permit sugar manufacturers to produce ethanol from sugarcane juice, B heavy molasses and C heavy molasses for the ethanol supply year 2024 -25 and also allowing mills to manufacture rectified spirit and extra neutral alcohol from all three feed stocks which is sugarcane juice, B heavy molasses and C heavy molasses for the season are positive developments.

items.statement: Supreme Court allowed states to regulate industrial alcohol; UP impact minimal per management
items.quote: See, early days, we don't know, but I think for UP, it was a non -event. Because UP, there have been enough controls with the government exercises directly or indirectly through molasses and through other sort of ways.

items.statement: Policy uncertainty on MSP, ethanol pricing, exports; Maharashtra elections may delay decisions
items.quote: Maybe they will get a little bit more time to consider all this post the Maharashtra election.

items.statement: Maize availability for grain ethanol questionable; 11 million tons needed for current tenders vs national demand
items.quote: I think roughly 11 million tons of maize is required, which I don't think the country has the, I mean, if you look at the entire demand that the country has between poultry and ethanol sectors, I don't think this is the kind of numbers which are going to be produced.

items.statement: Targeting 60-70% non-traditional sugar sales (institutional, pharma, packaged) in next couple of years from ~25% in H1 FY25
items.quote: This year in 6 months I think we've sold about close to 25% of our sugar that we've sold. Roughly 25% is on the non -Asian, non -conventional methodology, non -conventional challenges like institutions, industries and we hope over the next - we hope to continue to have this going up to maybe 60%, 70% in the next couple of years.

items.statement: Pharma-grade sugar commands export premium
items.quote: We have pharma -grade sugar, so we do tend to get a premium for our sugar whenever export comes in.

items.statement: National sugar production estimated 33.6 million tons for SS 2024-25; 3.8 million tons diversion to ethanol; net production 29.8 million tons
items.quote: With the estimated gross sugar production of 33.6 million tons in sugar , for the sugar season 2024-25 and about 3.8 million tons of likely diversion for ethanol , it is estimated -- and the consumption is expected to be in the region of 29.3 million tons and the net sugar production is estimated to be 29.8 million tons.

items.statement: Ethanol blending target 18% for ESY 2024-25; OMC requirement 916 crore litres; 312 crore litres allocated to sugar segment
items.quote: For the current ethanol supply year that is 2024-25, the oil marketing companies have established their total requirement at 916 crores litres which would result in an overall blending of about 18%. items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 26.19% in Q2 FY25 from 15.25% in Q2 FY24 due to line stabilization, better utilization, and procurement efficiency.

items.statement: Management plans to maintain current EBITDA margins for the next 2-3 years, expecting softening only after that as competition increases.
items.quote: You know, it's our plan to maintain similar margins than what they are today. And according to us, we will continue to maintain these margins because the industry, the demand is very robust. We are looking at a little bit of softening the margins only after about 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Capex plans: 1 GW TOPCon cell line (INR670 cr) by Q4 FY25, 4+4 GW cell/module (INR3,300 cr) by FY27, 2 GW wafer facility (INR175 cr) by FY26, and aluminium frame facility (INR230 cr) by FY26.
items.quote: So, for the 1- GW cell line, the capex investment is about INR670 crores. For the 4 GW plus 4 GW, which is coming from the IPO rate, is INR3,300 crores. And on the wafer, it's about INR175 crores.

items.statement: 1 GW TOPCon cell line expansion to be completed by Q4 FY25; 2 GW wafer manufacturing facility targeted for commissioning in FY26; 36,000 MT aluminium frame facility for captive use by FY26.
items.quote: We are executing a 1 GW TOPCon cell line expansion, which will be completed by Q4 FY25. Further leveraging the opportunities for backward integration, we are planning an investment into a wafer manufacturing facility of 2 GW, which is targeted to be commissioned by

items.statement: Order book stands at 3.86 GW (INR6,233 cr) as of Q2 FY25, executable over 10-12 months; Q1 FY25 order book was INR5,700 cr.
items.quote: Q2 numbers is 3860, that's 3.86 GW, INR6,233 crores.

items.statement: Domestic solar demand is robust, driven by PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana (25-30 GW over 3 years) and Kusum scheme (34.8 GW target); DCR demand estimated at 10-15 GW annually and growing.
items.quote: So the demand is anywhere between, as on today, between 10 GW to 12 GW, and this is growing. The pipeline is huge. So, when you talk of pipeline, there is, the Kusum scheme, which has a huge pipeline.

items.statement: Module production is 70-80% TOPCon; lines are technology-neutral (can produce Mono PERC, TOPCon, HJT); DCR and non-DCR mix remains constant each quarter.
items.quote: At the moment, almost 70% to 80% of our production is TOPCon. To move to HJT, the, spend on capex is insignificant. It is just changing some jigs and fixtures. So, it's not material at all. But I'm talking about module line.

items.statement: Revenue mix in H1 FY25: 41% domestic customers, 32% IPPs, 12.2% OEM, 10.3% government, 3.9% exports.
items.quote: So, we have, about maximum sales are, in domestic terms, it is about 41%. And to IPP, this is 32%. We do OEM for customers, that is about 12.2%. And export is about 3.9%. So that's the mix.

items.statement: India TOPCon module prices: USD 0.155-0.16/W (non-DCR) and USD 0.23-0.24/W (DCR); Cell prices: USD 0.13-0.15/W depending on volume.
items.quote: So, as of now, in India, the TOPCon module prices are around USD 0.155 to USD 0.16 for non-DCR and DCR is around USD0.23 to USD0.24.

items.statement: Wafer facility will source polysilicon externally (imports or domestic PLI supply); no plans for polysilicon manufacturing. Aluminium frames will use procured billets (extrusion, anodizing, fabrication).
items.quote: We will be sourcing our polysilicon from outside India. And as and when polysilicon is available in India under the PLI scheme, if we get polysilicon in India, we will buy it in India. But if we don't, we would import polysilicon.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty petition filed by Indian solar firms is in nascent stage; ALCM (Approved List of Cell Manufacturers) expected to be imposed by government in future, which would make all cells DCR-compliant.
items.quote: It's still in the nascent stage. It's just been filed a couple of days ago. So, there is no development or significant update on that as of today.

items.statement: Exports are 2.82% of Q2 FY25 revenue; US JV with Heliene for 1 GW cell facility is in wait-and-watch mode due to US policy uncertainty; no capex deployed yet.
items.quote: Our exports for this quarter were 2.82% of the quarterly revenue.

items.statement: Total debt INR1,248 cr (long-term INR863 cr, short-term INR385 cr) as of Sep 30; cash INR1,520 cr including IPO proceeds; net cash positive ~INR223 cr; interest cost ~9.25% (long-term) and 8.5% (short-term); FY25 interest cost estimated INR
items.quote: So, the interest cost for the company right now on the long-term liabilities is around 9.25% per annum. And for the short-term liabilities, working capital funds, it's in the range of about 8.5%. And for the total long-term debts and short-term debts, as on 30th September, long-term debts are INR 863 crores, short-term debts are INR385 crores. So, 1248 crores is the total debt.

items.statement: IPO proceeds significantly strengthened balance sheet; net debt-to-EBITDA improved from 5.5x in H1 FY24 to net cash positive currently.
items.quote: The proceeds from our IPO have significantly strengthened our balance sheet. Our net debt-to-EBITDA ratio was 5.5 in H1 FY24, and today we are net cash positive.

items.statement: Warranty provisions increased sharply (other expenses up QoQ) due to revenue doubling; modules carry 25-30 year warranty.
items.quote: So that's as per our policy and provisions as the revenue is growing. We have a provision which is there for warranty because modules are sold on a 25-to-30-year warranty. So, because if you look at the revenues, they've almost doubled compared to last year. So that's how that provision has gone up.

items.statement: New cell capacity announcements in India (10-12 GW) will take 2.5-3 years to commission and stabilize; Premier's 14-year experience provides competitive advantage; ALCM implementation could require 40-50 GW cells, extending margin stability
items.quote: If you look at the companies which have been setting up cell line or announced setting up cell line, and if you look at how much time it's taking them to even commission the lines and then to stabilize these lines is not easy.

items.statement: US expansion risk: policy uncertainty under new US administration regarding IRA benefits; company is not dependent on US market and will proceed cautiously.
items.quote: We are a little bit of a wait and watch looking at the political developments. We have signed, you know, an MOU and announced that we'll be setting up a gigawatt of facility along with our US partner that's Heliene.

items.statement: DCR demand estimated at 10-15 GW annually, growing due to PM Surya Ghar (25-30 GW over 3 years) and Kusum scheme (34.8 GW target, 50 lakh pumps by FY26).
items.quote: I would estimate it's been 10 GW to 15 GW as of today, but it's growing.

items.statement: Expect double-digit growth in branded apparel in H2 FY25 and healthy EBITDA margins
items.quote: What we are seeing clearly is that with the wedding season spread out over five months now, that we should see a double-digit kind of a growth happening across apparel or a healthy growth happening across apparel.

items.statement: Target 200 additional stores over next 18 months via asset-light franchising, focusing on Ethnix by Raymond
items.quote: Aligned with our growth strategy, we are progressing towards expanding our retail footprint, targeting 200 additional stores over the next 18 months, primarily following an asset-light franchising model.

items.statement: Expect net working capital to normalize by end of March FY25 as festive and wedding season sales materialize
items.quote: Hence, we believe that by the end of March, we will be in a pretty regularized and normalized space of networking capital.

items.statement: Expect debt reduction by year-end FY25 as working capital eases
items.quote: Yes, that would be a fair assumption to make.

items.statement: Garmenting capacity expansion capex of INR 200 crores, 50% under implementation, balance over next 12 months
items.quote: We have invested INR200-odd crores of capex. 50% of that is already under implementation. Balance 50% will come over the next 12 months.

items.statement: Healthy order book in garmenting; added over 20 new clients across US, UK, Europe; early wins from Bangladesh Plus One
items.quote: In the garmenting business, we have a pretty decent and healthy order book. And I see that going forward in the second half, we should be able to deliver strong growth in the garmenting business.

items.statement: Branded apparel EBITDA margin improved to 13% vs 12.1% YoY; focused on intake margin and sourcing efficiencies
items.quote: The branded apparel segment delivered in a beta margin of 13% v ersus 12.1% in the same quarter of the previous year

items.statement: Branded textile EBITDA margin declined to 18.9% from 22.2% YoY due to operating deleverage from 8% revenue decline
items.quote: The segment EBITDA margin was impacted due to lower revenues primarily, and was at 18.9% in Q2 FY25, as compared to 22.2% in Q2 FY24.

items.statement: October retail optics positive across categories; double-digit growth on Diwali-to-Diwali comparison; wedding season from Nov 12 for 45-48 days
items.quote: The month of October has already shown good optics compared to the previous period and we anticipate this momentum to go ahead as we move through peak wedding and winter season.

items.quote: We have already appointed over 60 distributors, with product pricing positioned attractively between INR500 and INR999.

items.statement: Ethnix by Raymond at 129 stores (136 as of Oct), targeting 150 by end Q3 and 300 over 2-3 years; mass premium positioning
items.quote: We have reached 129 stores already in Ethnix by Raymond. And we are looking to cross 200 stores over the next 6 months to 8 months.

items.statement: Macro headwinds: geopolitical tensions, economic volatility, food inflation, excessive rainfall impacted Q2 discretionary spending
items.quote: Amidst these positive demand indicators, we remain mindful of a challenging ma croeconomic environment marked by ongoing geopolitical tensions and concerns around economic volatility

items.statement: Red Sea logistics challenges increased lead times by 2-3 weeks, delaying garmenting revenue recognition in H1
items.quote: The part of this garmenting result that you see is also due to certain logistics challenges that we got from due to the Red Sea piece, where the lead times have increased by around two to three weeks.

items.statement: Focused on improving sourcing and intake margins in apparel; intake margin efficiencies playing out strongly despite tough demand
items.quote: we have put in some very focused efforts on improving our sourcing and intake margins in apparel. And that is something you have been noticing across our businesses and across result s over the last two years as well

items.quote: Our net debt stood at INR396 crores as of Q2 FY25. This increase is mainly due to a planned rise in working capital, which grew by approximately INR325 crores to INR1,692 crores in September 2024.

items.statement: Commercial Refrigeration disrupted by BIS regulatory changes from March 27, 2024, impacting water coolers and deep freezers
items.quote: From March 27th of 2024, BIS related changes in terms of specification that has disrupted the supply chain and there are difficulties that are being encountered, we will explain to you.

items.statement: Carried-forward order book grew 9.8% YoY to Rs 6,598.20 cr as of September 30, 2024

items.statement: Segment I margin improved to 8.3% in Q2 FY25 from 6.1% in Q2 FY24 due to changing business mix
items.quote: Segment 1 margins saw an improvement in Q2FY25, rising to 8.3% of revenue, compared to 6.1% of revenue in Q2FY24. The improvement in margins is a result of the changing mix of business within the segment.

items.quote: We continue to maintain; the top line growth of 25% to 30% in Room Air Conditioners or the unitary products as a whole and margin guideline remains. There is no change in that at all.

items.quote: I am joined by Mr. Rahul Sheth and we will be happy to take Q&A after that.

items.statement: Double-digit revenue growth expected for FY25, excluding TajSATS impact
items.quote: By excluding TajSATS, we still will do definitely more than 10% top line growth, whether it's 12 or 14 or 15, that the second half month by month we can tell, but this is our belief and confidence.

items.statement: Target to open 25 hotels in FY25, 30 in FY26, with pipeline of ~120 hotels
items.quote: With a target to open 25 hotels in this financial year, going up to 30 in the next financial year and a higher number in the years that follow, with a pipeline of almost 120 hotels.

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR700-800 crores for FY25, with INR344 crores spent in H1

Whatever one-offs we have been doing at some point, either we will keep them or we might do a sale and manage back on a sale and leaseback and recirculate. So there are some one-offs which might increase the total capex to 7% if we don't sell.

items.statement: Signed 42 hotels and opened 14 hotels from April to October 2024
items.quote: In the period of April to October 2024, we have signed 42 hotels and opened 14 hotels.

items.statement: Portfolio reached 350 hotels with 230+ operational, monthly run rate of 6 signings and 2 openings

items.statement: Taj brand achieved double-digit ARR growth, commanding 66% RevPAR premium over industry
items.quote: Taj achieved double -digit growth in average room rates. I repeat, Taj achieved double -digit growth in average room rates, high lighting the strong demand witnessed in domestic luxury travel. This strong performance helped IHCL command a RevPAR premium of 66% over the industry in the Indian market

items.statement: October hotel segment revenue grew 16.5% YoY, driven primarily by ARR growth
items.quote: October figures we already have, which is behind us, and we've had a 16.5% hotel segment revenue growth.

items.statement: Management fee income reached INR100 crores in Q2, up 15% YoY on 11% net unit growth

items.quote: If you see the slide we put out in the deck, it shows that the RevPAR for internationals hotels have grown by 10%. And this is reall y on the back of a very strong performance in the peer, which has done exceedingly well

items.quote: And that is how it caught our attention in how we can scale it to more than 100 properties by 2030 as these are small, experiential boutique properties in all kinds of destinations, which can provide that experiential stay.

items.statement: No debt on company-owned projects, funding from internal accruals, net cash position of ~INR2,500 crores
items.quote: There is no debt. And we will continue to do that where it makes sense, that it's a brand-enhancing opportunity. It comes at a compelling price or is with a very good partner. Then we will do that and push especially our new and reimagined businesses forward so that they become significant contributors in the times to come.

items.statement: Other expenses as percentage of revenue decreased from 27% to 26% in Q2, showing scale benefits
items.quote: If you look at the presentation on slide number 26, you will see that as a percentage of revenues, this has actually come down from 27-odd percent to 26%. And that is a scale which is at work here.

items.statement: San Francisco and Maldives/Sri Lanka international markets remain soft/challenging
items.quote: San Francisco remains challenging, so it's neutral, as good or as bad as last year. London is same level as last year. Cape Town continues to grow. Dubai has been strong. Maldives is soft, and Sri Lanka is soft.

items.statement: Sea Rock redevelopment progress expected over next 100 days, subject to government approvals
items.quote: We remain fairly optimistic that over the next 100 days, we should make a lot of progress. Not a little bit of progress, a lot of progress. That, we can also communicate with all of you.

items.statement: Goa portfolio consolidating after high COVID base, expected bounce back in Q3/Q4 with 50+ units and RevPAR north of INR11,000-14,000
items.quote: Goa has been a winner for us. Together with Amas, we have crossed 50 units in Goa, more than 16 hotels, our latest we've opened today under IHCL selection. items.quote: Right. So, this is going to help us to both make products where our margin should be increased as well as reduce the total number of employees we use in terms of automation.

So, this is the big challenge, if that picked up we would be able to improve and in fact have been better than last year , but this is the challenge the yarn pricing is just not moving right now.

items.quote: Right. So, yes, our inventories have risen by about, 50 crores plus. items.quote: We will be having additional term loan, not a working capital. Working capital should come down over a quarter. items.statement: Government policies restricting imports from China (QCOs) expected to help yarn pricing; potential US tariff differential vs China under new administration could give preferential access
items.quote: Right now we are expecting that all of the policies that the government has taken to restrict some of the imports coming in from China should begin to help, some of the QCOs and other strategies that the government has implemented because , there is a lack of demand there is a challenge from China, and a lot of goods do come into the country, and this causes pressure on the yarn.

items.statement: India's market share in US/EU grew from 5% to 7% (2019-2024); UK stable at 4%; Red Sea crisis and elevated logistics costs persist; hope for improved US access post-election
items.quote: India's market share in the US and the European Union has shown consistent growth, rising from 5% in 2019 to 7% in 2024 . While its share in the UK remains stable at 4%.

items.statement: Technical textile JV (Tesca) revenue Rs 40 cr, PAT Rs 2.5 cr in H1; steady but auto sector slow; optimum potential ~Rs 200 cr yearly (~Rs 50 cr quarterly)

items.statement: Yarn pricing remains key risk to overall margins; uncertainty on when yarn cycle turns; competition intense in automotive fabrics; retail over-the-counter segment weak (Diwali season bad)
items.quote: On the yarn business I can't say there is . On the fabric and garment we do have optimism, but on the yarn business I will not be able to say that there is right now, it is challenging.

items.quote: So, this is going to help us to both make products where our margin should be increased as well as reduce the total number of employees we use in terms of automation. So, the effort of all the modernization is to increase the productivity per employee and to increase the value added per kilogram or per meter.

items.quote: Yes, so we are consuming about 20% of our yarn production in ternally, and if you compare FY24 versus FY25 the internal consumption of yarn has not increased. items.quote: Yes, we have plans to put a plant in Mexico U.S., then it would be around INR250 crores capex.

items.quote: And it's the regular capex here in India, we are doing for the upgradation and -- time to time. Yes, we are doing for the upgradation of the machineries and capacity enhancement.

items.quote: But as soon as we take a decision within 4 months, 5 months the production will start.

items.quote: We are doing the models and the Ford Motor company got added to exports, some models got added.

items.quote: If you see the growth, then export growth is 35%, 36% overall export growth. And volume-wise is at 22%. And in domestic 4% volume-wise growth is there already.

items.quote: It is because of both reasons. Because of increase in exports. Majorly, it is on account of increase in exports.

items.quote: We are only working on higher segments. Lower segments, we are not working. And because of the sales force like that only, automotive sales is not very good.

items.quote: Lot of materials coming from China is under invoicing in spite of increasing the import duty and antidumping duty, still material is coming in very like USD3 material is coming in USD 1. Now when I put up a antidumping duty, where the price doesn't matter it is USD0.46 per meter.

items.quote: Our total INR216 crores total revenue, where the breakup is export general INR25 crores, export OEM INR60 crores, auto OEM INR40 crores, auto replacement INR37 crores, footwear INR43 crores, furnishing INR7 crores and others INR4 crores.

items.quote: The export is INR85 crores out of INR216 crores and domestic is INR132 crores, which is 40% and 60% in ratio.

items.quote: And if we take the OEM supplies total out of INR216 crores, then INR137 crores is OEM supply, which comes to 63% of total sales revenue for the quarter.

items.quote: Actually, it has two impacts. One is, increase in ocean freight because of this Suez Canal issue. items.quote: how is the relation between U.S.A. and Mexico. Becau se USA is not happy with China a nd in Mexico, a lot of Chinese companies are there with which Americans are not satisfied. So how America and Mexico relationship moves

items.quote: In terms of breakup of orders in hand of about INR98 billion, about 62% of the orders in hand we have from the private segment customers, about 32% orders in hand are from the central utilities and PSUs, and about 6% orders in the overall portfolio from the state utilities.

items.statement: HVDC tenders (Fatehpur-Bhadla, Khavda-Nagpur) expected to finalize within 3 months; addressable scope $1-2 billion
