Collectively, these specialties achieved a 13.6% year-on-year growth and accounted for 61% of total hospital revenue.

items.statement: Oncology grew 19%, neurosciences 17%, robotic surgeries up 57% YoY
items.quote: To highlight , the oncology specialty registered a growth of 19%. Neurosciences reported a growth of 17%. This is also reflected in the number of procedures performed in neurosciences with a growth of 21% compared to Q2. Encouragingly, the number s of robotic surgery performed increased by a strong 57% compared to the corresponding previous period.

items.statement: Medical travel revenue grew 6% to INR134 crores, contributing 8% of hospital revenue
items.quote: Our revenue from medical travel grew 6% compared to Q2 of financial year '24 to reach INR134 crores. The revenue contribution of international business stood at approximately 8% in Q2 of financial year '25 on similar lines with Q2 of '24.

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR800-900 crores per year for FY25 and FY26 including maintenance and growth
items.quote: Yes. So we are expecting around INR800 crores to INR900 crores approximate capex, which includes maintenance as well as growth capex for both the years, each year.

items.statement: Net debt-to-EBITDA at 0.16x as of Sep 2024; post Agilus stake purchase debt-to-EBITDA expected below 1.5x by year-end
items.quote: On the balance sheet side, we remain comfortable and healthy with a net debt -to-EBITDA of 0.16x as on September 30, 2024, as against 0.29x on September 30, 2023. Our net debt stands at INR281 crores as of September 30, 2024.

items.statement: Agilus 31.52% stake purchase from PE investors at INR1,778 crores enterprise value, funded via INR1,500 crores NCD
items.quote: Yes, it is in public domain. We have gone for the shareholder approval also for that. I think the number is INR1,778 crores enterprise value.

items.statement: Agilus stake acquisition expected to close by end of November or early December 2024
items.quote: We are in the final stage of finalizing the agreement with the key inve stors. Hopefully, we should be concluding all this thing by this month end. And then we will conclude the deal by this month end and maybe early week of December.

items.statement: Agilus Diagnostics targets 25-26% EBITDA margin by FY27-28
items.quote: So what we are seeing -- what we feel is that by in another 15 to 18 months, we should be able to be in the range of about 25%, 26% kind of margins. In the upcoming quarters, we'll be able to see steady progress on these

items.statement: Agilus expects double-digit revenue growth trajectory from FY26 onwards post brand transition
items.quote: Yes, definitely, that will happen. So we are seeing that trend happening. So I think after this year, you will see that the basis will change because of whatever changes we have done compared to last year, the brand transition, all those things happening now. So those will have a better impact in the coming years.

items.statement: Agilus added 150 customer touch points in Q2 FY25, targets 600-700 for full FY25
items.quote: So this year also, we expect to add close to about 600 to 700 touch points. And we are seeing that improving every quarter. So this quarter, we have added close to about 150 touch points.

items.statement: Diagnostic EBITDA margin improved to 21.5% in Q2 FY25 from 17.2% in Q2 FY24, adjusted margin 24%
items.quote: Operating EBITDA margin in the diagnostic business basis gross revenue have improved to 21.5% from 17.2% in Q2 of financial year '24. Excluding one-off items like rebranding exercises by Agilus first brand transition, reversal of provisions related to certain government businesses and the contingent consideration payment for an earlier lab acquisition, the operating margin stood at 24%.

items.statement: Agilus pricing stable on blended basis, differential pricing across segments and regions
items.quote: No, it's fairly constant. So we have differential pricing across different segments, across different regions. And it's kind of very similar to how the rest of the industry players move.

items.statement: High Court hearings ongoing for forensic matter, next hearing end of month; Fortis brand auction ordered, mechanism to be decided Nov 21
items.quote: Whereas in the matter of brand, the court has ordered for an aucti on of the Fortis brand. So for that on 21st, the court officials will decide on the mechanism and the terms, etcetera. Post that, we will see how we can participate and secure this for us.

items.statement: Onboarded specialists in cardiac, renal, gastroenterology, internal medicine, obstetrics and gynecology in Q2 FY25
items.quote: During the quarter, we further strengthened our medical talent with the onboarding of specialists in the area of cardiac sciences, renal sciences, gastroenterology, internal medicine and obstetrics and gynecol ogy.

items.statement: Evaluating divestment of Sacred Heart hospital in Bangalore (Richmond Road)
items.quote: Another hospital in this category is a very small hospital Sacred Heart in Bangalore, which actually we are planning to divest and get rid of this hospital because it is very small hospital.

items.statement: Legal costs higher in FY25 due to increased hearings, expected to decrease from FY26
items.quote: this year, Atul, we don't expect the legal cost to be low. In fact, this year, the legal costs have been slightly higher than the last year because more number of hearings, etcetera has happened in the high court compared to last year. So the cost has been slightly higher this year, but we expect that to go down from next year

items.statement: Indian real estate sector experiencing robust demand in Tier 1 cities; Tier 2 cities emerging as new investment destinations
items.quote: The Indian Real Estate sector continued to experience a robust demand, with Tier 1 cities witnessing the sturdy demand, while Tier 2 cities are emerging as a new investment destination.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 sales INR1,331 crores, volume 1.53 msf; H1 FY25 sales INR2,500+ crores
items.quote: In Q2 FY '25, our sales were INR1,331 crores, while sales volume was 1.53 million square feet.

items.statement: Customer collections up 18% YoY in Q2 and 27% YoY in H1; quarterly run rate ~INR1,000 crores vs INR350 crores in FY22
items.quote: Customer collections for Q2 increased by 18% year -on-year and for H1 by 27% year -on-year, indicating im proving operating efficiencies.

items.statement: Average realization up 9% YoY to INR8,697/sqft; Puravankara +17%, Provident +15% YoY
items.quote: The average realization was 9% higher year-on-year to INR8,697 per square feet because of the mix of inventory, while Puravankara and Provident saw increase of 17% and 15% year -on-year, respectively.

items.statement: H1 FY25 geographical sales: Bangalore 56%, Chennai 18%, Mumbai & Pune 11%, Kochi 11%
items.quote: The geographical contribution for the first half was Bangalore share of 56%, followed by Chennai at 18%, Mumbai and Pune at 11% and Kochi at 11%.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 deliveries: 591 units, 0.77 msf; H1 FY25: 1,520 units, 1.92 msf
items.quote: On the delivery front, in Q2 FY '25, we have given possession of 591 units, and the area of 0.77 million square feet.

items.statement: Launch pipeline robust: ~12.27 msf new planned projects + 3.44 msf new trade launch = 15.7 msf total; Mumbai & Pune 49% of planned projects
items.quote: Our launch pipeline for the company is robust, with approximately 12.27 million square feet of new planned projects and 3.44 million square feet for new trade launch totalling to 15.7 million square feet.

items.statement: Acquired redevelopment rights for Miami Apartments at Breach Candy, Mumbai (2,000 sqm land); estimated rates INR125,000-140,000/sqft carpet
items.quote: The company acquired the redevelopment rights of a prestigious society, Miami Apartments at Breach Candy in Mumbai, spread across 2,000 square meters of land.

items.statement: Expanded footprint in Lokhandwala, Andheri West: new cluster with GDV INR700 crores; total land ~4.3 acres, combined GDV INR2,350 crores
items.quote: The company expanded its footprint in the Lokhandwala, Andheri West. Adding a new cluster of societies with the potential of GDV of INR700 crores to its existing redevelopment projects, bringing to the total land area in the region to around 4.3 acres with a combined GDV of INR2,350 crores for the project.

items.statement: Signed JDA for 1.95 acre land parcel in Electronic City, Bangalore; saleable area 2.6 lakh sqft, potential GDV INR250 crores
items.quote: The company also signed a JDA for 1.95 acre land parcel at the prime location in Electronic City Market in Bangalore. The land parcel is adjacent to Purva Western project and will be saleable area of 2.6 lakh square feet with a potential GDV of INR250 crores.

items.statement: Net debt INR2,430 crores (Sep 30, 2024); net debt-to-equity 1.29x; cash INR939 crores; debt per sqft under construction down 26% to INR928 from INR1,248 (Mar 2022); cost of debt 11.62%
items.quote: Our net debt stands at INR2,430 crores as on September 30, 2024, with the net debt-to-equity ratio at 1.29. Our cash and cash balance was INR939 crores as on 30th September 2024, which indicates the strong liquidity profile, ensuring stabil ity and operational capability.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 total revenue +36% YoY to INR520 crores; H1 +67% YoY to INR1,195 crores; EBITDA margin 28% (Q2), 24% (H1); net loss INR19.88 cr (Q2), INR5 cr (H1)
items.quote: In Q2 FY '25, our total revenue grew by 36% year-on-year to INR520 crores, and revenue for H1 FY '25 grew by 67% year -on-year basis to INR1,195 crores. Our EBITDA margin stood at 28% for Q2 FY '25 and 24% for H1 FY '25.

items.statement: Invested ~INR945 crores in land with potential GDV INR9,700 crores from 5.8 msf new acquisitions
items.quote: Also, we want to highlight that a total of around INR945 crores has been invested in land, with a potential gross development of value of INR9,700 crores from 5.8 million square feet of new acquisitions.

items.statement: H2 FY25 launch pipeline GDV ~INR13,600 crores; expect to open ~INR8,000 crores for sale in Q3 & Q4; all projects at advanced approval/RERA stage
items.quote: For the new launches, our expectation is in the current quarter and the next quarter, we will launch - the GDV of the launch pipeline is approximately INR13,600 crores, of which we are expecting to totally open for sale approximately INR8,000 crores.

items.statement: Target to launch Thane and Lokhandwala redevelopment projects before March 31, 2025
items.quote: In fact, in this -- in the coming two quarters, we are anticipating we should take Thane and Lokhandwala to market, that's our target before 31st March.

items.statement: >90% end-users (no bulk/multi-unit sales); Provident = first-home buyers; Puravankara = mix of first-home & upgrades; Purva Land = investment for self-build
items.quote: Look, from our point of view, all of them are end users because we don't do any bulk sale, any multiple unit sales. These are all customers who are buying homes, either upgrading or first time.

items.statement: Estimated 65-75% of customers currently taking home loans (up from ~40% self-funded post-COVID)
items.quote: My hazard a guess is -- and don't hold me to it -- would be approximately 65% to 75% of our customers are currently taking loans.

items.statement: No pricing pressure; sustenance projects saw 15-17% price appreciation YoY with 14% sales velocity increase
items.quote: No impact. If you see, at least as a brand in our case, as Neeraj mentioned in opening remarks, we have seen last year to this year, price appreciation in sustenance projects of between 15% to 17% between Purva and Provident.

items.statement: Commercial: 3 msf plan approved; 2.2-2.3 msf completion next FY yielding ~INR150 cr rental income; target INR500 cr rental income over 5 years
items.quote: From the 2.3 million square foot which will be completed in the next financial year, we are expecting rental income of about INR150 crores. The balance will come in the following financial year once we complete the balance phase of those projects.

items.statement: Focused on residential (INR30L to INR35-50Cr/unit) and commercial office; ancillary retail only; no data centers/logistics parks
items.quote: We are absolutely clearly focused on residential. Our residential portfolio cuts across INR30 lakh a unit to now INR35 crores to INR50 crores a unit. We are very focused on that. And secondly, our absolute clear focus is on commercial office.

items.statement: Starworth precast facility: investing to strengthen business; too early to discuss monetization
items.quote: I think we are investing in the business at this point in time to strengthen the business. And I think once we reach an optimal scale where we believe that it can create significant value for the organization, we will evaluate it.

items.statement: Embedded EBITDA margin on presales: JDA 16-17% to Purva Land 35-40%; average 28-32%
items.quote: I think I have mentioned this in the past, that our project level margins range from anywhere between -- on the JDA side as low as 16%, 17% to as high as 35% to 40% for Purva Land. So that's the range of margin. But if you look at an average, we would land up at about a 30% margin between -- EBITDA margin between 28% and 32% on an average.

items.statement: Mumbai redevelopment EBITDA margin 23-24%; Thane ~30%
items.quote: If you look at the redevelopment project, the EBITDA margin will be anywhere between 23%, 24%. And I think it also -- because we believe that Mumbai as a market is a very stabilized market.

items.statement: Lokhandwala realization INR36,500-45,000/sqft; Pali Hill INR105,000-115,000/sqft
items.quote: So in Lokhandwala, you would expect anything between INR36,500 to INR45,000 a square foot. That would be the range of pricing depending on floor rise, PLC, etcetera. And for Pali Hill, we would expect an average realization of anywhere between INR105,000 to INR115,000 square foot.

items.statement: HDFC platform: deployed INR417 crores across 2 projects; expect to deploy ~INR300+ crores shortly; total platform INR1,150 crores
items.quote: So far, we have deployed INR417 crores. That has been deployed between 2 projects, and we are expecting to deploy another approximately INR300-plus crores very, very shortly.

items.statement: Strategic focus on 6 geographies: Bangalore, Hyderabad, Chennai, Mumbai, Pune, NCR (Gurgaon/Delhi); 80% focus here, 20% opportunistic in existing markets (Goa, Kochi, Coimbatore)
items.quote: The strategy for us is to focus on these 5 or 6 geographies, which is Bangalore, Hyderabad, Chennai, Mumbai, Pune, and in NCR, we are looking at Gurgaon and Delhi. So these are 6 locations we are focusing on.

items.statement: NCR entry: asset-light JDA model; conservative approach; 12-24 months for first contribution; focus Golf Course Road area in Gurgaon, South Delhi; avoid Dwarka Expressway/Yamuna Expressway
items.quote: NCR is going to be, as I mentioned in the past, that it will be an asset-light investment opportunity where we are looking for JDAs. We're not looking at large outright commitments, at least for next year to 2 years, and we are very, very -- we'd like to be a little conservative in our approach there from the market perspective.

items.statement: Presales 3-year CAGR ~57% (last 3 years); target land bank 45 msf over 2-3 years (from 15 msf net after launches); aim for 22.5 msf annual launch capability
items.quote: Our CAGR for the presales number over the last 3 to 4 years has been about -- in fact, 3 years has been 57%. But if you take the year before that, it would be in mid 30s or early 30s.

items.statement: Debt target: maintain sub-1.0x net debt/equity long-term; keep absolute debt stable near-term; aim to reduce net debt toward zero over 3-4 years as collections scale
items.quote: keep it sub-one. Obviously, temporarily, it may go up and down because it's a way of business. There are multiple action points that we take -- undertake to bring the debt down because that's a constant process. But our goal will be to maintain similar absolute number of debt over a period of time. And eventually, because we can't compromise growth at this point in time. However, over the next 2 t

items.statement: Management maintains sustainable EBITDA margin guidance of around 15%
items.quote: We should be delivering around 15% margins on sustainable basis.

items.statement: Management reiterates 15% EBITDA margin guidance for the market
items.quote: Yeah, 15% is our guidance to the market.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin at 14.1% with revenue of INR 867 crores
items.quote: In Q2 FY 2025, RHI Magnesita India reported revenue from operations of INR 867 crores, a 1.3% decline quarter-on-quarter. The EBITDA for the quarter was at INR122 crores with margins at 14.1%

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA margin improved to 16% from 14.9% in H1 FY24
items.quote: The EBITDA for the first half year was at INR279 crores, while EBITDA margins improved to 16%, up from 14.9% in the previous corresponding period.

items.statement: Raw material cost pressure from alumina-based materials and chromite sands impacted Q2 margins
items.quote: increasing raw material costs, especially for alumina-based materials and chromite sands exerted pressure on margins.

items.statement: Pass-through of alumina price increases takes 2-3 months with zero net impact over time
items.quote: We will negotiate, it will take two, three months, but when that round year price goes down, it also takes two, three months to reduce the prices. So it is zero net impact, I would say.

items.statement: Steel industry growth estimated at 2.7-2.9% vs market estimates of 6-7%
items.quote: If you check JSW's announcement, it is 2.7% growth in steel in India. And we have our calculation 2.9% growth, right?

items.statement: Cement industry slowdown in H1 but positive outlook for H2 with planned commissioning
items.quote: Meanwhile, the cement industry has seen slowdown. However, the outlook for the latter half of the fiscal year remains positive, with anticipated growth led by our customers' planned commissioning of their projects and infrastructure initiatives.

items.statement: Strong order book in iron, pellet, DRI making with 4 Blast Furnace Cast House contracts and 6 new Taphole Clay customers
items.quote: We have a strong order book in the iron, pellet, DRI making business. In iron making, we have seen a good order momentum in Blast Furnace Cast House. We have four contracts and added six new customers in Taphole Clay.

items.statement: Advanced discussions with OEMs for long-term coke oven and blast furnace stores association
items.quote: We are also in advanced discussion for long-term association with OEMs for coke oven and blast furnace stores. We should strengthen our order books in the coming quarters as well.

items.statement: Annual capex run rate of INR 70-80 crores expected for next 2-3 years
items.quote: So we are doing something like INR70 crores, INR80 crores every year from last 2, 3 years. And this is the pace we assume next 2, 3 years also, okay?

items.statement: Capacity utilization improved to 67% in Q2 FY25 from 61% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Capacity utilization also improved to 67% in Q2 FY 2025 from 61% in Q1 FY 2025, highlighting our ongoing operational enhancement and efficiencies in the acquired plants and the shipment growth that we did.

items.statement: Production volume increased 10.8% QoQ to 86.2 kilotons in Q2 FY25
items.quote: In terms of volumes, we produced 86.2 kilotons in Q2 FY 2025 compared to 77.8 kilotons in Q1 FY 2025, higher by 10.8%.

items.statement: Net debt/EBITDA ratio reduced to 0.3x from 0.6x at start of year
items.quote: We are proud to inform that due to operational efficiencies in first half of the year, we managed to reduce our net debt EBITDA ratio to 0.3x from 0.6x in the beginning of the year.

items.statement: Import dependence reduced from 40-45% to 30-35%, targeting 80% local-for-local production
items.quote: maybe two years back, it was 40%, 45% import, now, it has come Sensitivity: Internal down to 30, 35%. And in coming days, it will further come down. And our target is to take it to 80% roughly for local-for-local

items.statement: One-time impact from incoterm change increased traded goods purchase in Q2
items.quote: There's a change of incoterm and we have a lot of material in the pipeline, I would say, but it doesn't have any long-term material impact.

items.statement: Exports remain weak with no material improvement expected in next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: No, it is really weak. Rather in last quarter also, it was a dip, small dip in our percentage, I would say. And I don't see next two, three quarters it will have any material impact or substantial increase in our exports.

items.statement: Chinese refractory dumping at $650-700 CIF impacting commodity ladle business volumes
items.quote: Yes, of course, when you are having a lot of pressure from neighboring country, China, on commodity business, particularly ladle business, and they are dumping like anything, they are selling at $650, $700 CIF.

items.statement: Flow control products 80-85% alumina-based; cement bricks also high alumina-based
items.quote: All flow control products, maybe 80-85% flow control products are based on high Alumina raw material. Okay. And all cement bricks -- Alumina -- high Alumina cement bricks are based on Alumina based raw materials.

items.statement: Resumed business with Dalmia Cement this year
items.quote: Yes, we have resumed and this year we are getting orders from Dalmia as well.

items.statement: Key steel customers JSW, Tata, ArcelorMittal, JSPL, SAIL planning expansions
items.quote: You know, you take the name of all big four, whether it's the JSW Group, Tata Group, ArcelorMittal, JSPL and SAIL. Everybody is planning to expand.

items.statement: Volume growth target of 1-2% above steel industry growth maintained
items.quote: I still maintain that statement. We want to grow 1% or 2% more than the industry.

items.statement: Geopolitical risks (Trump sanctions on China) could increase Chinese dumping in India
items.quote: If, you know, there's no change in global geopolitical situation, headwind, I don't want to sound political, but you know, with Mr. Trump on the top in US, if he puts some sanctions on China, more sanctions on Chinese refractory, then China will have overcapacity, more overcapacity. And then they will start dumping whatever they are dumping out more in India, which will have impact.

items.statement: Steel and cement plant pricing pressure makes raw material cost pass-through challenging
items.quote: So you must understand if steel plants, cement plants are under pressure on pricing part, to getting price increase will not be a cakewalk. It will happen, but we need to really put our efforts. And it will take time.

items.statement: Management expects exports from India to the US to increase drastically over the next two years and sees potential respite from the Ukraine war boosting Europe trade.
items.quote: I think we are looking at least for the next 2 years, the exports from India to the US will increase drastically and we are really looking forward to that business growth which will be coming over.

items.statement: Order book and pipeline are good, and growth momentum from recent quarters is expected to continue.
items.quote: So, coming quarters, they are looking good, the order book is good, the pipeline is good and we feel that the growth in last few quarters will continue.

items.statement: No major capex planned; short-term borrowings are purely for working capital due to business growth.
items.quote: We are not looking at any major big investment in this. We want to continue on the same growth path which we have and that is working well for us.

items.statement: Actively looking at acquisitions in the LCL space, targeting a mid-size company with 100+ crore topline for majority stake and management control.
items.quote: We are looking at some acquisition in the LCL space which we have mentioned earlier also because we feel that LCL is one product that we don't have with us and we are willing to acquire a mid-size company which will augment our growth overall.

items.statement: Acquisition target size is around 100+ crores revenue; aim to provide growth capital and purchasing power while retaining majority control.
items.quote: So, we are looking at a company which has closer to around maybe 100 plus crores of business topline where we can acquire. We don't want to run it ourselves. We want the company, maybe have management control, we have a majority stake in that.

items.statement: Ocean freight margins are increasing and getting better despite rate fluctuations linked to the Chinese market.
items.quote: Margins are increasing, and margins are getting better. I would say that rates are fluctuating still because sometimes, now Indian market on the ocean flight is completely dependent on the Chinese market.

items.statement: Air freight volumes grew 4.5x YoY after becoming an IATA agent, gaining direct booking capability and better buying power.
items.quote: We were not IATA agents earlier. We were outsourcing this activity through other IATA agents. But as you know that last year, we became IATA agents ourselves and because of that we were able to focus on this business more ourselves.

items.statement: Air freight will grow but remain secondary; focus stays on sea freight where the company holds position on key trade lanes.
items.quote: Yes, air freight business, we feel that it will be growing, but to be very honest, since we are a sea freight company, we don't want to put too many resources into the air freight business.

items.statement: Import logistics is picking up, currently ~20% of mix vs 80% exports; management expects import share to grow significantly.
items.quote: At the moment in percentage wise, I would still say that export contributes a major 80% or so, but I think that like 20% still remains imports, but we see that imports getting bigger and bigger in coming quarters.

items.statement: Evaluating EV trailer fleet for green logistics to transport export containers; capex is large and profitability under review.
items.quote: We are looking at having EV trailers for the movement of export containers. So, we are working on it though the CAPEX is big in that. So, we are still trying to evaluate, look at the profitability, look at how this will work out.

items.statement: Short-term borrowings increased substantially in H1 FY25 solely for working capital as business grows and credit periods extend.
items.quote: Borrowing is only working capital. There is no CAPEX. There is nothing of any other usage, but it is purely being used for working capital.

items.statement: Any future debt will only be overdraft for working capital; no asset or capex borrowing planned.
items.quote: Any debt which will be there if we have will be in the form of an overdraft towards working capital only. We are not looking at any asset, any CAPEX or any such thing in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Ocean freight Q-o-Q dip is seasonal due to monsoon halting commodity movement (rice, cotton, wheat); long-term business wins offset volume decline.
items.quote: Yes, of course, because during this time, in the monsoon time, there is no movement of commodities, rice and cotton and wheat and all does not move in this quarter. So, there is a slight dip in the volumes because of that.

items.statement: Ocean freight rates fluctuate with Chinese market; rates softened in Q2 but started picking up in late October.
items.quote: So, now what we were seeing in the first quarter of this financial year, the freights in China were very good. So, the rates really got very high in India also, but in the second quarter, it was a soft market, so the rate started getting lower.

items.statement: Renewed government sector contracts with BHEL, BEML, HAL, BNPL and similar long-term partners.
items.quote: We have been able to get some good contracts and get our old contracts renewed, especially in the government sector contracts. This includes contracts with BHEL, BEML, HAL, BNPL and other similar government organizations.

items.statement: Revenue grew 58.3% Q-o-Q in Q2 FY25 driven by new trade lanes, import growth, air freight, and Freight Jar opening customer doors.
items.quote: So, ma'am, as I mentioned earlier, overall business is growing because we are focusing on new trade lanes, we are focusing on acquiring new businesses, which has contributed in this overall growth.

items.statement: Freight Jar 2.0 adoption is low but opens doors to new customers; digital platform showcases capabilities while brick-and-mortar model retains business.
items.quote: Freight Jar overall is doing good for us, but I would like to say that surely the acceptance is low. People are very willing to know as to what is the new product, what is the new age business, and what are the new options which are available to them, but the adoption is still low.

items.statement: No major headwinds or challenges seen in coming quarters; hopeful that war resolutions and easing fuel prices will support international trade.
items.quote: I think we are not even forcing any major challenges which we don't see in the coming quarters. So, overall, we are very hopeful and positive and bullish about the business in coming months.

items.statement: Management declines to give specific revenue targets but confirms business is on right path and expects to exceed expectations; H1 run rate ~Rs 262 cr.
items.quote: That will be a very bullish number to say, but it is always good to always keep on doing better and always setting more records. But that will be very bullish to say at this point of time. But yes, the market is looking good, and the business is looking good. So, you have the numbers with you that we have already crossed last year's turnover and we continue to grow on

items.statement: Investing significantly in IT to improve efficiency and reduce costs across the system.
items.quote: Especially in the IT sector, we are investing a lot, so that we can get some better efficiency in the IT sector.

items.statement: IATA accreditation provides direct airline access, own airway bill stock, and better purchasing power versus competitors using agents.
items.quote: So, when we have the IATA accreditation, then we can deal with the shipping lines directly and book the shipment directly through the airlines. So, that is the biggest advantage which we have now that we can deal with the airlines directly.

items.statement: Chennai park expected to be operational by end of Q3 FY26
items.quote: I am also pleased to share that the Chennai project construction is progressing well and expecting to be operational by end of Q3 FY26.

items.statement: Fundraising of Rs 500-800 crore via QIP or private placement approved for next 7-8 years of projects
items.quote: Aligned with our expansion plan, our board has approved fundraising through a qualified institution placement or private placement up to Rs. 800 crores supporting our projects for the next 7 to 8 years.

items.statement: Total capex of Rs 1,500-2,000 crore planned for future parks, funded by equity, debt and internal accruals
items.quote: We have a total CAPEX of roughly Rs. 1,500 crores to Rs. 2,000 crores and we are proposing to raise only Rs. 500 to Rs. 800 out of that through equity. The rest there will be a combination of debt and then internal accruals.

items.statement: QIP expected to be completed before end of current financial year
items.quote: Hopefully before the end of this financial year.

items.statement: Mature parks expected to deliver 3-5% footfall growth and pricing growth equal to inflation
items.quote: If the matured park will give anywhere between 3% to 5% of footfall growth and then pricing maybe equal to the inflation rate in the country, so that is what we follow on with respect to the matured park.

items.statement: Bangalore park expected to see low single-digit footfall growth and 5-8% ARPU growth per annum over next 5 years
items.quote: 5 years is hard to predict, but I think we can expect low single-digit growth in Bangalore in percentage terms and ARPU growth, you can expect between 5% to 8% per annum, kind of thing you can take, conservatively.

items.statement: Bhubaneswar park expected to close first year with 3-4 lakh visitors
items.quote: So, we were expecting about 3 to 4 lakhs of footf all in the full year of operation. But we are a new entrant to this particular region. So, we need to wait and see the impact by the end of this

items.statement: Rs 15 crore invested in new rides at Hyderabad park during Q2 FY25
items.quote: As part of our continuous investment strategy, we also added multiple rides at our Hyderabad Park at a cost of approximately Rs. 15 crore and was open to public by the Telugu superstar Naga Chaitanya.

items.statement: Bhubaneswar park built in under 16 months for less than Rs 200 crore
items.quote: If you are able to build a park in under 16 months for a full-fledged park if we are able to do for less than Rs. 200 crores, I think that is a remarkable achievement and we want to capitalize on those kinds of opportunities.

items.statement: Large tier-1 parks cost Rs 700-800 crore each; tier-2 parks under Rs 200 crore
items.quote: if you have to build a large park, it's going to cost us, one park will cost us between Rs. 700 crores to Rs. 800 crores, especially if you're in a city like Delhi or Bombay. So, it depends on the kind of park s that we finally build . If we build in a tier 2 city like Indore or Mohali, we'll do something under Rs. 200 crores

items.statement: Company can build 2-3 parks simultaneously; each large park needs 18 months construction with 1,000 workers daily
items.quote: Two to three. Two, we can easily do. Three also is possible, but I think it's still building that capability because we need a large team to work on each project. Each of our parks needs construction time of at least 18 months. It's a 50-acre parcel of land. At least thousand people have to work on site every day for 18 months for it to complete.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 footfall declined 9% to 4.5 lakh due to unpredictable weather and heavy rainfall
items.quote: Our footfall declined by 9% to 4.5 lakh and leading to a 13% drop in income, which stood at Rs. 71.23 crores compared to Q2FY '24.

items.statement: Diwali and Dussehra festival seasons were good for footfalls
items.quote: It was good, Diwali season was good. Dussehra and Diwali, both the festival seasons were good.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin 4% (Rs 2.8 crore), down 90% YoY due to revenue drop, higher marketing spend and employee additions
items.quote: EBITDA including other income for the quarter stood at Rs. 2.8 crores, down by 90% YoY. EBITDA margins for the quarter stood at 4%. The degrowth in EBITDA was about Rs. 24 crores which is predominantly attributable to reduction in our revenue by Rs. 8 crores. Increase in our marketing spend by Rs. 6 crores and expansion of employee base by adding approximately 210 people across location and corpor

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA margin 40% (Rs 98.7 crore), down 34% YoY due to revenue drop, marketing spend and employee additions
items.quote: EBITDA including other income for the quarter stood at Rs. 98.7 crore, down by 34% Y oY. EBITDA margins for the quarter stood at 40%. The degrowth in EBITDA was about Rs. 50 crores, which is predominantly attributable to reduction in our revenue by Rs. 19 crores, increase in our marketing spend by Rs. 11 crores and expansion of employee base by adding approximately 210 people across location and c

items.statement: Hyderabad park delivering ~45% EBITDA margin; new parks cause temporary margin compression but stabilize over time
items.quote: We are getting almost 45% EBITDA margin from Hyderabad. If you exclude COVID years, Hyderabad is only five years old. So, it's still not as mature as the other two parks that we have. So, it's still giving very good footfalls and revenues. So, I think there is still growth possible from Hyderabad.

items.statement: Corporate team building 90% complete; new parks may cause 1-2 percentage point EBITDA margin shrinkage initially
items.quote: Corporate level, we already completed most of the recruitments. Apart from that, almost like 90% we have already completed the recruitments and then the team building activities and all, so now it's only thing is like that you have to add parks and then only for that particular park we need to add certain people so it will not create so much of problem maybe from second and third year for a new pa

items.statement: Online bookings grew 48-50% YoY in H1 FY25 due to digital marketing initiatives
items.quote: Compared to last year, so we were able to see about some 48%, 50% of growth in online alone. This is mainly because of various digital spending initiatives and marketing, other things we are doing through our marketing department.

items.statement: Deferred tax liability reduced by Rs 24 crore due to capital gains tax rate cut from 20% to 12.5% in budget
items.quote: Previously, we had recorded a deferred tax when we did a revaluation of our land. So, now after this current budget, there is a reduction in the capital gain tax from 20% to 12.5%. Accordingly, the deferred tax also reworked and then adjusted as on 30th of September, which amounts to about some Rs. 24 crores.

items.statement: Board approved QIP/private placement up to Rs 800 crore; quantum of equity dilution not finalized (Rs 500-800 crore range)
items.quote: We have not decided the quantum of equity that we will dilute. This depends on what we get. It's still early days. We have not really decided, I mean, it could be anywhere between Rs. 500 crores to Rs. 800 crores.

items.statement: Unpredictable weather events (rain, floods, heat waves) affect discretionary spending and footfalls; business sees cyclical growth patterns
items.quote: I mean the rain and all that we can't predict. And obviously anything to do with rain, floods and heat wave and all that, obviously will affect any kind of discretionary spending where people have to get out of the house, right? So, that we can't predict but the rest of it I think we are more or less confident that it will work because it's already been proven in three cities, fourth city we've ju

items.statement: Industry size projected to grow from Rs 11,000 crore to Rs 25,000 crore in 4-5 years at 10-11% CAGR per industry reports
items.quote: Add on to this point if you see the industry size as well because if it is growing from 11,000 crore to about some 25,000 crore in next to 4-5 years as per some of the industry reports, which is showing a CAGR of about some 10% to 11%.

items.statement: No plans for land revaluation before QIP; last revaluation at IndAS transition added Rs 400 crore to land value
items.quote: That we already did it at the time of transferring from the old Ind AS from the Indian GAAP to the IndAS time. So, where we recorded about some Rs. 400 crores of revision in the land value, we don't want to do that valuation as of now

items.statement: Future expansion to use long-term leases where possible; not averse to buying land if lease rental and land cost are similar
items.quote: it. Wherever possible we will not buy land, but if land is available and I mean, we are not averse to buying land, because if the lease rental and the cost of land is similar, we might as well buy it. Depends on state to s tate it varies, so it's hard to predict that, but wherever possible we would like to keep the CAPEX low and do the lease

items.statement: EBITDA margin guided at 12-14% for the quarter; actual came in at 12.6%
items.quote: Our EBITDA has also been in the guided range of 12% to 14%, coming at 12.6% for the quarter after investments, as Ravi was highlighting.

items.statement: Core lubricant volume grew 8.8% YoY; excluding factory fill, growth was double-digit
items.quote: we've also seen a lot of our segments growing, and we have –recorded a volume growth of 8.8%. If you take out the factory fill, which is th e new vehicles, mainly commercial vehicles where we are also involved, our growth is actually double digit in this quarter

items.statement: Industry volume growth estimated at 3-4%; company growing 2-3x market
items.quote: We don't have data validated, but by whatever we are gauging, the industry is growing by 3% to 4%. I think that is where some people say 4% to 5% because of Baz aar growth or different segments, but for us, the 3% to 4% growth is what the industry is getting in terms of volu me. I think we are continuing to look at two to three times of that.

items.statement: Gross margin increased ~100 bps YoY; EBITDA at 12.6% within guided 12-14% range despite higher A&P and staff costs
items.quote: At the same time, we have also been able to deliver good increase in the gross margin by nearly 100 basis points. Our EBITDA has also been in the guided range of 12% to 14%, coming at 12.6% for the quarter after investments, as Ravi was highlighting.

items.statement: B2B segment growing double-digit; channel OEM business grew double-digit; agri segment highlighted
items.quote: We have seen that the channel OEM business in particular did very well, and the agri segment is the highlight there. We have seen that a lot of our sales and marketing initiatives undertaken during the quarter were really working for us.

items.statement: Annual capex for lubricant business ~INR20-30 crore; no additional equity needed for Tirex at this stage
items.quote: Also considering that our capex requirement for lubricant business also is around INR20 crore, INR25 crore-INR30 crore annually. We continue to generate good cash, and we have increased the payout already to 55%, 60%.

items.statement: Pre-bought inventory due to global refinery shutdowns in Oct-Nov; led to higher borrowings
items.quote: As I mentioned in my opening remarks, Mr. Ramesh, we have had to store higher inventory because as I was mentioning in one of the earlier questi ons, some of the refineries where we have a term contract, were going for a maintenance shutdown during October, November we had to prebuy some of the inventories and that's where you see increase in the borrowings.

items.statement: Base oil prices linked to crude ($75-80/bbl currently); comfortable maintaining gross margins at current crude levels
items.quote: But on a ballpark, I can give you that if crude remains at the current level, which is $75 to $80 range. Of course, it sometimes goes to $85 also during the quarter. It went up to $90 in April; and it went up to $85 in July. It is volatile thing and difficult to comment, but if it remains at the current levels, we are comfortable to maintain our gross margins.

items.statement: Premium range growing at double the company growth rate; motorcycle segment up 2% in mix; diesel engine oil ~39%, personal mobility ~22%, industrial ~18%
items.quote: We continue to focus on our premium range of products. And again, we are happy to share that this has contributed to the overall kitty by notching up double the growth rate, though it is a small contribution in terms of percentage, but this is growing at double the rate which we are growing which augurs well to our strategy of profitable growth.

items.statement: Market share: diesel engine oil 8-9%, motorcycle 8-9%, other segments 5% or below; aim to grow 2x in strong segments
items.quote: If you look at the segments, we are strong in diesel engine oils. We have close to 8%, 9% market share there. Similarly, motorcycle, we are 8% to 9%. I think this is where we are. In most of the other segments, we are 5% or below.

items.statement: Exports now 6-7% of portfolio, up from 3-4% earlier and 5% stabilized level
items.quote: Yes, I think we are now at around 6% -7% in terms of our export as a percentage. While earlier it used to be 3%-4% and then we stabilized around 5%. Now it has gone to 6%-7%.

items.statement: H1 FY25 cash generation INR147 crore vs INR140 crore last year; inventory up due to refinery shutdowns
items.quote: On cash flow side, we have been able to continue to generate good cash. You can see from the cash flow published that INR147 crore of cash has been generated during H1 FY’25, which is more than even the last year H1 of INR140 crores.

items.statement: No additional equity investment planned for Tirex; working capital loans from banks if needed
items.quote: At this stage, we do not see any need to put more money for the growth of the business. Of course, some working capital loans can be availed from the bank if we want to.

items.statement: Tirex (51% stake) revenue INR14 crore in Q2, INR24-25 crore in H1 (vs INR24-25 crore full FY24); target INR500-700 crore in 5 years, doubling annually
items.quote: For Q2 FY '25, it was around INR14 crore, and for the H1 FY’25, it is around INR24 crore-INR25 crore, which in the last full year turnover was around INR24 crore-INR25 crore for Tirex. They've achieved the last year number in H1 FY’25 itself. We have been also guiding in the past that we want to at least double the turnover every year for the next few years.

items.statement: Dividend payout increased to 55-60% from 35-40% three years ago; may increase further if cash deployment opportunities not visible
items.quote: We have been currently paying out roughly 55%, 60% as dividend payouts. That we have increased over the last two, three years from 35%, 40% to now 55%, 60%. Obviously, ROCE is impacted partly because of keeping the cash for the investment for future. If we see that there are opportunities that are not immediately forthcoming, and we increase the payout, then ROCE obviously can improve.

items.statement: Employee costs up sequentially due to team building for future growth
items.quote: Yes, absolutely, right.

items.statement: AdBlue realization ~INR45/litre (down from ~INR50); margins mid-single digit; YTD double-digit growth, minimum stability 10,000 kl/month
items.quote: It has been around INR45 realization fo r Q2 FY’25, which was earlier around INR50. And the margin remains roughly similar, mid-single digit.

items.statement: Battery segment turnover INR20 crore in Q2
items.quote: The battery turnover was INR20 crore for the quarter.

items.statement: PM e-drive scheme (effective Oct 1) provides incentives for charging infrastructure; benefits Tirex business
items.quote: The recent PM e-drive, which was announced in August and is now effective from October 1st, is again, talking about giving a lot of incentives to increase the charging infrastructure. helps us and the Tirex business.

items.statement: Short-term margin expansion uncertain due to competitive intensity despite stable input costs; medium-term target to increase gross and EBITDA margins
items.quote: Considering all this, it's difficult to say that in the short term, there can be a benefit of the lower crude sustained, but over a longer-term trajectory, over the next one to two years, obviously, our endeavour is to increase our gross margins and increase our EBITDA margins to the higher trajectory.

items.statement: A&P spend typically 3-4% of revenue; Q2 elevated by 40-75 bps due to mega campaign 'The Unstoppables'; spillover into Q3 expected
items.quote: Just to add, Nitin, we have already guided that our usual advertisement is in the range of 3% to 4%, as Ravi highlighted. In a normalized way, we would be towards the lower end of this band. In this quarter, we are on the higher side of this band. That's where the delta is, anywhere between 50 basis points to 75 basis points in given quarters.

items.statement: EV fluids volume to remain single-digit even at maturity; present with 9-10 EV OEMs; 3-wheeler EV penetration 50%, 2-wheeler 6-7%
items.quote: As you know, the penetration is going up from 3%, 4% to even 50% in three -wheelers. I think it's going to be a growing segment. We want to be part of it beca use we are there. We already have a good partnership with few OEMs, but not a very large volume. It will still be a very small volume of the overall pie.

items.statement: Data center cooling products under development globally
items.quote: Yes, we have started. We have products. We are developing them globally.

items.statement: Tirex targets EBITDA neutral to marginally positive in current year; at scale, EBITDA margins similar to lubricant business (not margin dilutive)
items.quote: We believe that once we reach a size and scale, it should deliver at least a similar EBITDA margins as our lubricant business. It will not be a margin diluting business on a consol basis.

items.statement: Unlock 2.0 strategy: accelerate (grow 2-3x market, gain share in low-share segments), premiumize (value growth double volume growth), transform (digital, EV charging, organizational)
items.quote: We have shared with some of you earlier, to achieve the next level of growth and success, we have embarked on the theme, Unlock 2.0, which is accelerate premiumize and transform. For acceleration, we are not only growing ahead of the market, we are also focusing on growing more in areas where our market share is lower.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY25 is INR 800-1,000 crores
items.quote: No, we'll be incurring the capex will be around INR 800 crores to INR 1,000 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance revised to 5-6% range going forward
items.quote: I think our EBITDA margins would be in the range of 5% to 6% now going forward.

items.statement: Volume growth guidance maintained at 5-7% YoY for FY25 subject to price volatility
items.quote: I think last time also, we gave a guidance of around 5 to 7 percentage. We stick to that guidance, subject to the price volatility and the demand increase, which is going to happen based on that.

items.statement: Morbi industrial volumes expected to grow to 3.5-4 mmscmd in Q3 FY25 from 2.86 mmscmd in Q2
items.quote: I think in quarter 3, we are looking at a growth of around 3.5 to 4 mmscmd.

items.statement: CNG sales grew 12% YoY in Gujarat and 25% YoY outside Gujarat in Q2 FY25
items.quote: In Q2 FY '25, CNG sales in Gujarat increased by 12% year-over-year, while outside Gujarat sales surged by 25% year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Domestic customer additions of 0.4 lakh in Q2 FY25 despite monsoon season
items.quote: Despite the monsoon season where construction is a bit challenging, GGL has still managed to maintain the growth rate and have been able to add 0.4 lakh customers in the current quarter.

items.statement: EBITDA per SCM improved to INR 6.86 in Q2 FY25 from INR 6.14 in Q2 FY24
items.quote: In terms of EBITDA per SCMD, it stands at close to INR 6.86 against INR 6.14 in the previous quarter of the previous year.

items.statement: Higher CNG share (now >40% of portfolio) and gas sourcing portfolio driving margin improvement
items.quote: One is CNG is definitely there because we are growing at close to 12 percentage in CNG. And the other thing is basically the portfolio of gas, which we are sourcing, that is also giving us a benefit advantage to the rest of the people over here.

items.statement: Capex of INR 130 crores in Q2 FY25, INR 330 crores in H1 FY25 for gas infrastructure
items.quote: During the quarter, the company invested close to INR 130 crores into the gas infrastructure, aggregating to INR 330 crores up to the half year of this financial year.

items.statement: Added 9 new CNG stations in Q2 FY25, total network at 820 stations
items.quote: During this quarter, we have added 9 new CNG stations, enhancing accessibility. Overall, we have achieved CNG sales volume of 2.93 mmscmd in this quarter.

items.quote: We have issued nearly 400 LOIs, out of which 125 have been accepted by the applicants. And apart from that, they have already submitted the bank guarantee of INR10 lakhs for those LOIs from those 125 locations.

items.quote: During the quarter, we had to increase the industrial prices by approximately INR 2 per SCM. The increase was mainly on account of significant increase in LNG prices.

items.statement: Evaluating CNG price increase to offset higher gas procurement costs from APM cut
items.quote: Yes, we are evaluating options to increase the CNG prices in near future to basically offset the increased cost of gas procurement.

items.quote: So for the quarter ended September '24, we were getting I mean, the shortfall was approximately 26% which was being fulfilled through spot. So -- and after that there has been a further reduction in APM gas. The reduction is now approximately 50%.

items.quote: That is basically we procured the volume was close to 8.9 mmscmd was there. So if you look at the average price of spot, that's around INR 37.4 per SCM.

items.statement: BG LNG contract (2.5 mmscmd) expiring mid-2025, in discussions for replacement with oil/Henry Hub linked contracts
items.quote: So that LNG contract will expire somewhere in the middle of 2025. And we are right now in discussions for a new LNG contract to replace those volumes.

items.statement: CNG and domestic share increased from <20% to >40% of portfolio over last few years
items.quote: See, I think if you look at the last few years, the growth of CNG and the domestic has increased in our portfolio from close to less than 20%, it is more than now 40 percentage.

items.statement: Non-Morbi industrial volumes grew to 2.05 mmscmd in Q2 FY25 from 1.9 mmscmd in Q2 FY24
items.quote: The non-Morbi volume of 2.05 mmscmd for quarter ended 30th September 2024 has grown from 1.9 mmscmd during the same period in the previous financial year.

items.statement: Targeting 2-3.5 mmscmd potential in Surat, Ankleshwar, Bharuch, Vapi, Valsad, Ahmedabad Rural, Dahej, Silvassa
items.quote: I think these areas have a potential to increase to almost 3 mmscmd to 3.5 mmscmd. We are putting up networks in Ahmedabad rural and Dahej and Silvassa.

items.statement: Morbi market size 7.5-8 mmscmd, current consumption ~6.5 mmscmd including propane, GGL share 2.86 mmscmd
items.quote: The market size would be around 7.5 to 8 mmscmd. And right now I think because of various issues in Middle East and all, I think, the consumption would be close to 6.5 mmscmd, including propane consumption.

items.statement: Propane price INR 43.6/SCM vs PNG INR 44.7/SCM, differential narrowed to INR 1-1.5/SCM driving switching
items.quote: Propane prices have actually gone up. The differential is now INR 1 to INR 1.5 per SCM.

items.statement: Delhi High Court stay order protects GGL from PNGRB common carrier regulations for 20 GAs
items.quote: What we have done as GGL management is we have immediately moved Delhi High Court again and obtained a protection order, a favorable order from Delhi High Court. So this prevents PNGRB from taking any coercive action against GGL.

items.statement: Over 98% of collections through digital mode
items.quote: Further, our focus on digital drive, we are happy to state that more than 98% of our collections are coming through digital mode for which we would like to thank our customers.

items.statement: Credit rating reaffirmed at AAA stable by CARE and India Ratings, CRISIL AAA under developing watch
items.quote: After the recent corporate announcement, Gujarat Gas continues to have a credit rating of AAA stable and a short-term rating of A1+, which has been reaffirmed by CARE and India Ratings. CRISIL has maintained the AAA rating and under the developing watch category.

items.statement: Scheme of arrangement filed with BSE/NSE to eliminate GSPC Group layered structure, expect stock exchange clearance by November 2024
items.quote: We have filed the scheme with BSE and NSE, and we expect to get clearance from stock exchanges during November 2024, followed by submission of scheme with SEBI.

items.statement: APM gas likely to be gradually replaced by new well gas at market-linked prices over next 3-4 years
items.quote: So that's what we hear from the market that APM gas would gradually be replaced by maybe new well gas as they call it. So basically, gradually, there will be a gradual abolishment of or there will be a gradual reduction of APM gas and that gas would ultimately be replaced by new well gas.

items.statement: CNG maintains 47% price advantage vs petrol and 15% vs diesel
items.quote: CNG maintains significant price advantages being approximately 47% cheaper than petrol and 15% cheaper than diesel.

items.statement: Matchmaking billing expected to return to growth in Q3; revenue to decline due to muted Q2 billing. Both billing and revenue growth expected to improve in Q4. Marriage services expected at similar level to Q2.
items.quote: On the billing and revenue outlook for Q3, the matchmaking billing expect to come back to the growth levels in Q3. However, there will be revenue decline due to the muted billing growth in Q2. In Q4, we expect both billing and revenue growth to move to a better levels. Marriage services, we expect to be at a similar level of Q2.

items.statement: Consolidated profit after tax expected to be lower in Q3 than Q3 last year due to investments in new areas.
items.quote: On the outlook for Q3 margins, we expect the profit after tax to be lower than the levels of Q3 of last year due to the investments in the new areas.

items.statement: Marketing expenses for matchmaking optimized to Rs 45.2 cr in Q2 from Rs 47.1 cr in Q1 and Rs 46.1 cr YoY.
items.quote: Marketing expenses for matchmaking in Q2 is at 45.2 crores as compared to 47.1 crores in Q1 and 46.1 crores a year ago. So, you would have observed we have optimized the marketing expenses a bit in this quarter.

items.quote: We have also taken Anil Kapoor as a brand ambassador exclusively for the northern and western markets. So, we intend to invest in northern market in particular. items.statement: Cash balance at Rs 379 cr, declined slightly from Q1 due to dividend payout.
items.quote: Our cash balance is at 379 crores, declined slightly as compared to Q1 due to the dividend payout.

items.statement: Second buyback announced at a premium; board decision to reward shareholders.
items.quote: Basically, the board evaluates the various ways to reward the shareholders, and so these are the second buyback and we discussed with the board and we thought it's better to set at certain second premium and it was a board decision on the buy back. items.statement: Matrimony.com certified as Great Place to Work by Great Place to Work India based on associate feedback.

items.quote: We may expect some increase in ARPU possibly from Q4 onwards and volume may also increase. But we are not giving a number at this point in time. items.statement: Management expects double-digit healthy revenue growth in FY26 versus FY25 driven by export order execution.
