items.statement: Strong pipeline in performance coatings from high-end approvals (railways, bridges, oil & gas, metro, Vande Bharat)
items.quote: Based on these initiatives in the performance coating divisions, we have done well and witnessed very strong traction and also have a strong pipeline.

items.statement: EV penetration: 4-wheeler 2-3%, 2-wheeler 7-8%, 3-wheeler >50%; Nerolac EV market share matches conventional
items.quote: If you look at electrical vehicles, the penetration in the 4-wheeler is just about 2% to 3%, and in 2-wheelers, it's about 7%, 8%. So it is going up, but with a slower pace. 3-wheeler, more than 50%. And our reach penetration in the electrical vehicle is as good as the conventional system. And we are holding the higher market share in this segment also.

items.statement: Staff costs increased to support initiatives; expected to be absorbed as revenue growth accelerates
items.quote: And fortunately, because the top line growth is low, as and when the market growth picks up, I think that will get absorbed, because cost has gone up because we have given the support to our initiatives.

items.statement: Management expects to achieve 10% overall sales growth for FY25 despite flat H1 revenue
items.quote: But we should be able to have that 10% overall sales. Let's see.

items.statement: Glass container capacity utilization was approximately 93% in Q2 FY25 despite furnace relining
items.quote: Despite a scheduled furnace relining, we maintained a strong glass container capacity utilization of approximately 93% this quarter.

items.statement: No greenfield projects in progress; growth dependent on HNG acquisition and debottlenecking of fuel efficiency, productivity, product quality
items.quote: But obviously, the acquisition of HNG is in pipeline. So we hope that things will work out well in our favour, and we hope to add up the capacity in the very near future because of this inorganic growth.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 27% in Q2 FY25 driven by cost efficiency and product mix optimization
items.quote: Despite a scheduled furnace shutdown, the Company reported Total Income of ₹611 crore while EBITDA increased 20% year -on-year to ₹166 crore, with a 27% margin.

items.statement: Soda ash prices relatively stable; freight costs increased due to geopolitical tensions offsetting minor commodity price declines
items.quote: Because of the demand and supply, the soda ash, basic prices have little come down. Because of this, it is almost balanced out with, I think, small 2%, 3% here and there, it normally happens.

items.statement: Specialty glass plant (154 tons/day) on track and contributing significantly; still has upside potential
items.quote: Yes, I think we are on the track. And certainly, in these set of numbers, this specialty glass has contributed quite a lot.

items.statement: Exports currently less than 5% of revenue; priority is domestic market; UAE subsidiary established as conduit for Middle East exports
items.quote: It's close to around 5% or less than 5%. Because as a marketing strategy, we are here to serve the domestic market on first priority basis.

items.statement: HNG acquisition pending Supreme Court decision; next hearing Wednesday; NCLT can move fast if ruling favorable
items.quote: The matter is continuously heard, and we feel that hearings should get completed in other 1 or 2 days whenever the next hearing is, next hearing is on coming Wednesday and after which the courts will take a decision.

items.statement: HNG tax losses (₹1,200 cr) usable only within HNG until merger; not available for AGI consolidated profitability
items.quote: Post the acquisition, HNG will have its own set of profitability and AGI will have its own set of profitability in the respective tax shields.

items.statement: Festive demand now spread throughout year; October performance satisfactory; optimistic on H2 continuation
items.quote: Sir, we are very lucky in India, we have the festive season throughout the year. So Diwali has finished and now Christmas and New Year is about to come.

items.statement: Furnace relining behavior unpredictable; normally takes a quarter to stabilize volumes post-relining
items.quote: The reason is when you reline the furnace, the behaviour of the furnace is a little difficult to predict. And since this furnace, we have started in the month of August and we just started our firing the furnace and September onwards, they start selling.

items.statement: No furnace relining scheduled for next 24 months; last relining completed August 2024
items.quote: We don't have furnace relining for to the best of my knowledge for around 24 months now.

items.statement: Not competing with Firozabad cluster; different technology, processes, and sustainability commitments yield superior margins
items.quote: I do not think we are competing with the Firozabad cluster at all. Firozabad cluster has a different way of working. There product may be same, the process is different, the commitments are different and everything is different.

items.statement: Specialty glass global market share less than 1%; niche segment requiring high technology and skilled manpower
items.quote: Okay, then, in the specialty products, on a global scale, we may be less than 1%.

items.statement: Other expenses fluctuate due to HNG litigation costs; expected to phase out post-adjudication
items.quote: There was a lean period in between. And now I think since the hearing is going on in almost all the courts. In short term, you may see some trend going up. But ultimately, it will phase out once the adjudication is done.

items.statement: HNG acquisition funding details confidential until NCLT approval; will disclose upon court order
items.quote: There are some things which are right now confidential because the entire resolution plan proceedings are confidential in nature until it is approved by the adjudicating authority, which is NCLT.

items.statement: Sustainability focus includes employee well-being and empowerment; received SEEM National Sustainability Award Gold 2023
items.quote: We are proud to receive SEEM National Sustainability Award Gold 2023 for our community contribution towards our manufacturing plant, focusing on climate change, water stewardship, waste minimisation, employee well-being and empowerment.

items.statement: Incorporated Sun Reach Pack (FZE) in UAE in October 2024 to expand global footprint and increase exports
items.quote: In October '24, we incorporated Sun Reach Pack (FZE), a wholly owned subsidiary in the United Arab Emirates to expand our global footprint and increase exports.

items.statement: Green electrical energy has small commercial benefit over normal electrical; sustainability primary driver not cost savings
items.quote: I think normal electrical and green electrical has a very small delta of the benefit, on the commercial benefit. It is more towards the environmental and sustainability commitments.

items.statement: Export onboarding takes time due to customer trials, ethical verification, and history checks; UAE entity enables local presence and service
items.quote: They are going to take a trial. They will also do all sort of confirmation about our company, about our ethical working, our old supplies, our history and everything.

items.statement: Glass packaging gaining share over PET long-term due to sustainability trends; constant interchange between materials in overlapping segments
items.quote: As such, globally, there is a clear signal that things should change to more sustainable packaging, which is a glass packaging. PET has gained a bit of points, but I don't think so on a long-term basis, they have any bright future in the times to come.

items.statement: No specific debt commentary; focus on HNG acquisition funding structure pending court approval
items.quote: We'll be disclosing this upon the order from the court once the NCLT approves it. Then at that time, we'll make the appropriate disclosures as per the requirement of the laws.

items.statement: JLR maintains full-year guidance of GBP30bn revenue, >=8.5% EBIT margin, and net cash positive, though headroom is tighter than desired
items.value: GBP30bn revenue, >=8.5% EBIT, net cash positive
items.quote: We have mentioned Q2 was hurt by factors largely out of our control, and we expect to bounce back strongly in H2. Though the headroom to holding these commitments, which are GBP30 billion worth of revenue, greater than or equal to 8.5% EBIT and net cash positive, they are still our commitments.

items.statement: JLR FY26 EBIT margin target of 10% still possible but getting tighter due to D&A effects from extended ICE lifecycles
items.quote: Yes, FY26 follows a similar thought pattern, to be entirely honest with you. 10% is still possible, particularly as the D&A effects of extending out the end point of our ICE products will still be very relevant in that year. But again, it is getting tighter.

items.statement: JLR Q2 production limited to 86,000 units due to Novelis aluminum flood and 6,000 unit quality hold; expects strong H2 bounce-back as constraints ease
items.quote: So the summary for JLR is that we were held back by outside forces in Q2, particularly the flood at Novelis, which restricted our production to 86,000 units in the quarter.

items.statement: JLR Q2 EBIT margin 5.6% (down 190bps YoY) due to operating deleverage from lower volumes; expects recovery in H2 to hit 8.5% full-year target
items.quote: EBIT at at 5.6%, down 190 bps and profit before tax and exceptional items at ~Rs. 5,800 crores, down about Rs. 400 crores.

items.statement: JLR EBITDA margin only 12% in Q2 (very low); expects majority of EBIT recovery from EBITDA improvement as volumes recover, plus lower D&A
items.quote: EBITDA in the quarter that's just passed was only 12%, which is very low for us. So we expect part of the recovery in EBIT margin for the balance of the year to be lower D&A, but the majority of it to be improvements in EBITDA as well as volume recovers.

items.statement: JLR wholesales 87,000 units in Q2 (down from 97,000); 6,000 unit quality hold to reverse in Q3; expects significantly higher H2 volumes
items.quote: we only wholesaled 87,000 units Tata Motors Limited November 08, 2024 in the quarter. Hit significantly by two effects, which are timing reversing. 6,000 units of wholesale hold , and I mentioned beforehand that we had at least 10,000 units of lower production driven by the issues we had with aluminum

items.statement: JLR H1 investment spending just under GBP1.9bn (GBP400m higher YoY) driven by BEV transition and new product cadence; engineering capitalization stable at ~65%
items.quote: Investment in H1 was just under GBP1.9 billion, about GBP400 million higher than the same period last year. This was driven by our BEV transition and our very forward and very exciting new product cadence over the next few years.

items.statement: JLR FCF guidance reduced from GBP1.8bn to GBP1.3bn due to tougher market and higher investment to extend ICE portfolio while developing three BEV architectures
items.quote: There's a couple of reasons. First of all, the market is a little bit tougher than we had envisaged it to be and also the scale of the investment that's required to keep the ICE portfolio of vehicles going for longer and simultaneously to invest in three architectures worth of BEVs is a little bit higher than we had originally envisaged.

items.statement: JLR Halewood BEV facility ready for EMA architecture production starting early 2026; will reduce industrial CO2e by 40,000 tons
items.quote: This picture is the BEV lines up in Halewood. It's an amazing facility dedicated to BEV production, and it'll eliminate tailpipe emissions, but also you'll see near the bottom of the text on the right, it will also reduce our own emissions. So we're taking maybe 40,000 tons of CO2e out of Halewood's industrial footprint.

items.statement: JLR variable marketing expense (VME) rose to 4% in Q2 from 1.1% YoY; expects VME to flatten at current rates and rise slightly in H2
items.quote: Net pricing was also negative for us. So, variable marketing expense or sales support on an incurred basis was 4% in the quarter versus 1.1% in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: CV business maintained disciplined pricing despite volume decline; focuses on value proposition beyond price including Fleetedge, AMC, cost of ownership
items.quote: We continue to have a very disciplined approach with price being only one part of the value proposition. The many other aspects and attributes which add value to the customer, starting from product, cost of ownership, the entire annual maintenance contract package, the Fleetedge and the kind of benefits that Fleetedge delivers.

items.statement: PV business cut prices instead of heavy discounting to protect brand; EV price cuts driven by cell price reductions and localization to bring EV prices closer to ICE
items.quote: Frankly, the discounting in the first quarter had gone up for all the manufacturers and we took a conscious decision to rather cut the prices rather than keep the discount very heavy because it impacts the brand. That is on the PV side. But as far as EV is concerned, we have taken the price cut because as one of the levers for mainstreaming EVs, it was also needed that the EV prices come closer to

items.statement: JLR strategy shifted from volume to value focus; will not return to old model but focus on Range Rover, Range Rover Sport, Defender, new Jaguar and Discovery
items.quote: It's the result of our new strategy. So many years ago we were very focused on volume and very focused on the car lines that deliver us the volume. Now we're very focused on value and the car lines that deliver the value. So we will not be returning to the old model.

items.statement: PV EV portfolio expansion: Harrier EV by end FY25, Sierra EV and ICE in FY26; targeting 70% SUV salience in 2 years, 80% by FY30
items.quote: What we have announced so far is beyond Curvv. Some of the EV models that we talked about, which is Harrier EV, which is going to come at the end of this financial year. But also Sierra, both in EV as well as ICE version is what is going to be launched. So in the next two financial years, we should start reaching a penetration level of about 70%. And we have said 80% by FY30 is what we have commit

items.statement: PV dealer inventory reduced to 30-31 days median after October festive season; highest ever monthly registrations of 68,500 units in October
items.quote: And we focused on reducing the dealer inventory levels to normal level. And therefore, we moderated our offtake also to do that in October and even in the earlier months. So now it is down to 30, 31 days, as I said.

items.statement: CV Ace EV has 62 anchor corporate customers (added 8 in Q2); working with municipalities for intracity decarbonization; capacity can produce thousands per month
items.quote: We have total 62 anchor customers who are our repeat buyers. So, they are essentially corporates who are deploying electric vehicles for their last mile distribution to meet their decarbonization target. In the last quarter, we have added eight such anchor customers.

items.statement: JLR sees intense NEV (PHEV/EREV/BEV) competition in lower price segments in China; top-end segments (Range Rover, Defender) not yet facing local BEV competition
items.quote: In the lower segments, absolutely, there is very strong competition from the new entry BEVs impacting the available market for ICE vehicles. In the top end, there really isn't yet. So there are no local BEVs competing at the price points. All the performance, all the brand that we have with Range Rover, Range Rover Sport, Defender.

items.statement: PLI applications filed by Sept 30 deadline; government accepted submissions; physical verification underway; disbursement expected within 60 days from Sept 30
items.quote: The government has already looked at all the submissions , that's been accepted. The various agencies will now be visiting our factories to confirm and go through the physical verification. The timelines intended for the government for disbursement of PLI funds are 60 days from 30 th September

items.statement: JLR H1 free cash flow flat due to working capital hit from lower production (payables fell to ~GBP900m vs normal GBP1.2bn); expects reversal in H2 as volumes recover
items.quote: If you look through the balance sheet where we ended up the quarter is with payables of just under GBP900 million, whereas in the normal circumstance, they would be north of GBP 1.2 billion. So that will also reverse.

items.statement: Tata Motors consolidated net debt marginally inched up; expects to reverse and become net cash by year-end as working capital normalizes
items.quote: Net debt marginally inched up, not particularly concerned about it. We should expect to see this reverse and go into net cash by end of the year.

items.statement: JLR RCF term loan refinanced; ratings continue to improve at both domestic and JLR levels
items.quote: From a financing side, of course, both the RCF term refinanced and as well as the ratings continue to keep improving.

items.statement: CV business ROCE at ~37.4% in H1 FY25; double-digit EBITDA sustained with 120bps YoY improvement in H1
items.quote: EBITDA has improved by 120 bps, and this is leading to a strong PBT, resulting in a good ROCE at around 37.4%.

items.statement: PV business CAFE compliance with 25g/km headroom below threshold due to multi-powertrain strategy
items.quote: Our CAFE compliance is very below threshold, and we have a headroom of 25 gram per kilometer, which goes to show the impact of our multi-powertrain strategy.

items.statement: CV Fleetedge platform has 710,000 active vehicles with 78% monthly and 52% weekly active users; Mileage Sarathi delivering 4.8% median fuel efficiency improvement on 340,000+ vehicles
items.quote: Fleetedge now has more than 710,000 active vehicles on the platform and a very healthy daily, weekly and monthly active usage, almost 78% monthly active users and 52% weekly active users. Our machine learning based fuel efficiency solution, the Mileage Sarathi is now live on more than 340,000 vehicles and we continue to deliver a median fuel efficiency improvement of around 4.8%.

items.statement: Key risk to JLR guidance is China deterioration; also watching global demand; inventory levels under control in other markets providing buffer
items.quote: What can get this go off track? I think ensuring that China stays and improves from where it is today, is an important one. If things deteriorate there dramatically, then that could skew the pitch. Other markets that are currently holding on for us in the current levels, we have not dramatically shifted volumes over the last few years and therefore it has been a gradual increase, as long as that t

items.statement: Q2 saw muted demand with volumes at base and value down 6.7%; urban centres stressed, rural recovering; extended monsoon and floods in August-September hurt demand; Diwali season weaker than expected
items.quote: We saw a real muted quarter for us in terms of the overall demand conditions, which were impacted. We looked at achieving base volumes. We were just about the base in terms of the overall volume achievement. But I think the effect was more at the value level where we were negative of about 6.7%.

items.statement: Expect single-digit volume growth for FY25 (H1 at 3.3%); aim to maintain 5-6% realization decline band for the year; target H2 EBITDA margin in 18-20% band
items.quote: Based on that, I think we should really maintain single digit volume growth numbers for the year.

items.statement: Standalone gross margin fell 280 bps YoY in Q2; PBDIT margin dropped 530 bps to 16.4% due to price cuts last year, weaker mix, material inflation, higher employee cost %, and higher discounting; H1 PBDIT at 18.5%
items.quote: If you look at gross margins, there is 280 points decline over Q2 of the last year, given the fact that we had taken a price decrease last year. Also, the product mix this year has been weaker and we have seen material inflation in the current year. Similarly, the PBDIT margins have come down and this is a concern area for us. Come down to 16.4%, almost a dip of about 530 points.

items.statement: Took 1.2% price increase in Q2; full realization expected in Q3; Q2 saw 1.5% material inflation vs 4% deflation in Q2 FY24; anticipating part deflation but depends on crude prices and geopolitics
items.quote: Overall, we have taken a price increase of 1.2% in this quarter. But I think the full realization of this price increase will come in Q3. I think this is something which we are clearly seeing going forward. We are expecting that there should be some deflation. But it all depends on how the crude prices behave given the geopolitical situation which is underway.

items.statement: Industrial business grew ~6% in Q2 (auto OEM/refinishes +6%, protective +6%); contributes 6-7% of total vs 20-45% for peers; PPGAP JV PBT margin 15.7%, protective JV PBT margin fell to 7% from 11.3%
items.quote: If you see from the point of view of PPGAP, which is the auto OEM and the refinishes business which we have, we got almost about 6% overall growth at the quarter level and about 8% at the H1 level. Profitability has also been fairly good. We have maintained stable margins, and the PBT is quite high overall at about 15.7%.

items.statement: Most brownfield expansion capex complete; backward integration projects on track - VAM-VAE at Dahej, Gujarat and white cement at Fujairah, Dubai
items.quote: Most of the capex which we had committed for brownfield expansion projects is now complete. Now we are looking at all our backward integration projects, which seem to be online. Whether it was the VAM-VAE which we are doing at Dahej in Gujarat or the white cement in Fujairah, Dubai. I think these projects are also well on track.

items.statement: Retail touchpoints now ~1.67 lakh; adding 5,000-8,000 retailers annually; tinting machine multiplicity increasing as new competitors give machines free
items.quote: Overall, now 7 | P a g e talking of almost about 1.67 lakh retail touchpoints which is very strong, and we are looking at continuance of this market

items.statement: Mix slightly more inferior in Q2; 12% revenue from new products; launched Advance range (2-3% higher dealer margins) targeting 15-30% of dealer sales; Ultima Protek with graphene/PU serum/nano block launching November; Chroma Cosm colour sy
items.quote: We see that today 12% of the revenue contribution still comes from new products and this is something which we are continuing taking forward in a very strong way.

items.statement: Urban centres stressed, rural/T3-T4 performing better; B2B projects segment better than retail but construction slow and government spending muted post-elections; painter loyalty programs focus on higher business volume not just per-litre r
items.quote: Overall, if you were to dissect the performance of the urban centres, definitely we are seeing more stress in case of our business. We saw that the rural areas to some extent have performed relatively better.

items.statement: Competitive intensity up across segments, especially economy; new entrants giving free tinting machines; existing players discounting more; not expecting intensity to ease in medium term; market share variation of 1-1.5% typical for leader
items.quote: We see it almost across segments. Whether it is the area of waterproofing or it is the area of emulsions, we are seeing it possibly across the economy and the premium set as well. As well as on ancillaries like putty and primers and so on and so forth.

items.statement: Calibrating primary sales to weaker secondary; conscious of dealer ROI - balancing margins and inventory rotation; avoiding inventory push that blocks dealer working capital given market liquidity crunch
items.quote: We balance the primary and the secondary. The secondary has been weaker to that extent. And therefore, we are trying to calibrate the primary according to that.

items.statement: No specific debt commentary; exceptional items: ₹200 cr impairment on White Teak/Weatherseal (₹124 cr goodwill impairment) and ₹56 cr forex loss from Ethiopia currency devaluation
items.quote: Therefore, I think we have taken an impairment, which is totalling up to almost about ₹ 200 crores. And this is also covering the fair valuation loss on the derivative contracts for future stake purchases in White Teak and Weatherseal which are in the offing.

items.statement: Interim dividend ₹4.25/share, lower than last year in line with reduced H1 profits; final dividend to be decided later
items.quote: We have looked at really calibrating the overall dividend for the year. We have got a dividend of about ₹4.25. This is a little bit lower than what we gave as an interim dividend 24 | P a g e last year, but this is in line with the reduced profits in the first half of the year

items.statement: Employee cost up due to frontline hiring for dealer expansion (5,000-8,000 retailers/year); absolute cost flat QoQ but % higher due to depressed top line; expect to normalize when value growth returns
items.quote: As far as employee costs are concerned, as I mentioned in Q1 as well, I think the numbers have gone up because we are looking at possibly, in the front line catering to our dealers very strongly. We are adding almost about 5,000 to 8,000 retailers easily every year.

items.statement: Global business +8.7% constant currency; ₹56 cr forex loss from Ethiopia devaluation; Middle East double-digit growth; Bangladesh turmoil dragged Asia; Nepal improving after 2-year liquidity crunch
items.quote: When you look at the performance here, from constant currency terms, was still quite good. It was almost about 8.7%. However, it got impacted very strongly. Given the fact that we saw a currency devaluation in Ethiopia, which was a big kind of impact which came in a t about ₹ 56 crores in terms of forex loss

items.statement: Home Decor: #1 in lighting, modular kitchens, wall coverings; #2 in fabric/furnishings; Kitchen +9% Q2, +7% H1; Bath +6% H1; newer categories (White Teak, Weatherseal) growing double-digit but below plan; gross margins hit, bottom line loss
items.quote: Kitchen - we are number one as the modular kitchen leaders. We have got almost 9% growth in Q2 and that is something which is very strong and almost about 7% in H1.

items.statement: Demand recovery uncertain - higher base in Q3 (late Diwali last year), October challenging; wedding season from mid-November key; crude price volatility and geopolitical risk to material costs; Bangladesh instability; government capex picku
items.quote: Right now, you know we are sitting on a higher base of Q3 overall, given the fact that last year there was a late Diwali and October was a full month. So October has been also a little bit challenging and therefore we are not seeing too much immediate recovery in Q3, but there is a good wedding season in the offing and we will have to see how the demand really goes up from the third week of Novemb

items.statement: Full-year guidance flattish revenue (~3-4% growth) and margins similar to last year; H2 expected stronger than H1
items.quote: So, the guidance was flattish guidance. So we said at the top line level, maybe 3% - 4% we are in kind of, we are okay on that, margins obviously there will be some margin made up in Q3 and Q4 but, obviously margins are under a bit of pressure. We hope to be at a similar level like last year, but probably there will be some amount of margin that will still have to be made.

items.statement: Agrochemical investments dried up; muted for several more quarters. Pharma picking up in India with large projects. Chemical cycle bottom but no green shoots yet.
items.quote: We have seen a shortfall and where we do see a little bit more stress in the glass lined business, especially when it comes to the chemical. And when I say chemical, mainly the agrochemical sector where the investments have really dried up and it does mean that there is probably a few more quarters of, I would say muted investment, I don't see that turning around very quickly.

items.statement: Mixing ~10% of H1 FY25 revenue; Heavy Engineering, Edlon, Mixing driving growth; glass-lined slowing
items.quote: 10% is the number that we have currently in terms of mixing. And mixing is an area where we want to grow. So there is a big push for us to kind of get into new industry segments, mixing opens up petrochemical, oil and gas, food and beverage, lots of other new industries which are not currently under in a down cycle.

items.statement: Poland facility producing first equipment for Mavag; lower cost than Western Europe; English-speaking engineers and welders available
items.quote: Poland becomes an opportunity we already have India as a low cost sourcing hub. But we also wanted to have something in Europe, because some of the customers in Europe only accept European made equipment. So Poland is a nice option for us, like I mentioned to you, we made the first set of two equipment for Mavag our swiss subsidiary, and the FAT was actually done a couple of days ago, and the resu

items.statement: Unbilled revenue +₹28 cr, inventory +₹32 cr, customer advances +₹30 cr, receivables -₹21 cr vs 31 Mar; H1 FCF 50% of cash generation
items.quote: when we compare 30th September versus 31st March balance sheet, we observe our unbilled revenue and inventory have gone up by ₹ 28 and ₹ 32 crores respectively. This highlights higher activity at the production floor. As a corollary, our customer advance receipts are also up by ₹ 30 crores. On the other hand, our receivables are down by ₹ 21 crores due to correction focus, which directs us to the

items.statement: New hires: head of manufacturing, head of sales, process head in India; mixing head hired 6 months ago; international hires; engineering center in India staffed for global work
items.quote: we made a couple of important hires here in India, head of manufacturing and head of sales, the project that is being run right now has seen a lot of traction because of the new perspective that we brought in. We made some hires internationally as well. So that's ongoing, we are strengthening areas, we recently hired a process head as well. So we are, we are trying to build process as a technology

items.statement: Agrochemical downturn may last several quarters; chemical cycle turn timing uncertain; competitive pricing pressure persists; margin recovery to 17-18% will take time
items.quote: I don't see the green shoots yet, I do see some talk happening in terms of new investment coming in like I said in the pharmaceutical industry, we do see positivity, but chemical and agrochemical in particular seem to be a little bit more time before we see a complete turnaround, if you also, I am sure you follow a lot of the chemical and agrochemical companies, many of them are now also not clear

items.statement: Evaluating M&A for new industries with 3-4 years continuous double-digit growth and good margins; strategic plan review ongoing
items.quote: this would also lead into M&A and stuff and looking at new industries which can give us three, four years of continuous growth, double digit growth with good margins. So that's something that we are thinking about.

items.statement: Wallet share growing in key accounts; cross-selling incentivized within chemical/pharma; brand affinity not quantitatively measured (NPS considered)
items.quote: So, the wallet share in our key accounts has definitely grown. We are also currently working on rebooted key account management process where we will kind of have multiple touch points, but our key customers continue to buy, we continue to discuss, we talk about process, technology, all that kind of stuff so, wallet share in our key customers is growing.

items.statement: Glass-lined competitors offer 25-50% lower prices; GMM retains premium via quality/life argument; procurement departments demand multiple quotes
items.quote: The internal view might be that, GMM Pfaudler is the preferred vendor, but there cannot be a very large price gap, they cannot be at 100 and somebody else is going to be at 75 or 50, the gap should be a little bit smaller. And, so that's something that is part and parcel of the Indian market, generally the global glass line market as well. So there's always going to be competitive pressure, but th

items.statement: Participating in CPI-NCL Living Lab project for chemical industry decarbonization; only equipment provider in collaboration
items.quote: internally, we call it as CPI NCL project, so apologies for not addressing it. Yes, we are involved in that project, NCL of India, of course National Chemical Lab, and CPI as a Center for Process Improvement from the UK. We have a collaboration with them, along with leading innovative companies from the chemical space. And the idea is to set up this lab in NCL with an emphasis on figuring out ways

items.statement: Targets $200 million revenue by calendar year 2027, approximately two financial years from now
items.quote: We are hoping that the economy is going to be opening up. Interest rates will open up and like Srini said taxation will be reduced. That means that there will be quicker acceleration in the initial phases, like Srini was talking about. So, our thing is we have set ourselves certain targets for next year and in line with whatever we are progressing now, we will be on a similar path to get to the 20

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margins to improve significantly by the time $200 million revenue target is reached
items.quote: I don't want to give a specific number, but as you see quarter-on-quarter, we have been improving our margins. Because we did some realignment of our bench, realignment of some of the business offerings that we are doing. We are also targeting this is something that for the financial year, we are looking at and we have given a target to all our CEOs operations, sales related leadership that we wan

items.statement: US election uncertainty delayed 4-5 deal closures from last quarter, now expected to close this quarter
items.quote: Before we go into what Trump's Presidency might look like for Kelton, I want to say that there were about four or five opportunities that we were going to sign last quarter, but due to the uncertainty of the elections and so on, customers have pushed them to the right. So, we expect to close all of them in this quarter and hopefully start some of them before the holiday season in December.

items.statement: Expects initial US economic growth under Trump presidency to drive IT spending acceleration starting calendar 2025

items.quote: Generally, we used to spend around 4%. So this year, we have just thought about 3%, 1% lower than last year.

items.quote: Yes. That will help in the premiumization of our articles which are meant for children and others also. So we have done a slow beginning. But in the coming times, this will help us improve the ASP of the company.

items.quote: Our guidance is 12%-14%, right. And if you look at within the credit growth, our RAM growth is always around more than 18%; almost 18%.

items.quote: Overall NIM which used to hover around 2.84 to 2.86 has now touched 3.10. and what we have done to achieve this level is we have rebalanced our credit portfolio.

items.quote: Our cost of deposit peaked in December ’23 it was 4.91 now it is 4.86. Our cost of deposit has started coming down because we h ave reduced our reliance on the bulk

items.quote: So, as we speak in addition to the mandated provision by the Reserve Bank of India on Standard Asset Book may be on account of market mechani sm, may be on account of Covid or restructuring book, in addition to all those provisions we are holding around 1000 crores of provisions over and above the required provision

items.quote: RIL, we do not have any exposure and MTNL, we have already made around 50pc provision in this quarter itself and given the buffer available.

items.quote: At IT we have kept a target of around ₹1000 crores to spend. Out of that, around ₹360 crores plus we have already spent and there are many projects in pipeline currently which we are working and by, I think, March we plan to consume the entire budget also.

items.quote: Our cost to income ratio has improved because historically our cost to income ratio used to be around 60% and above and now it is 56%.

items.quote: From signing larger ISVs perspective, our overall percentage of revenue or revenue mix from customers that are greater than $500 million or greater than $1 billion has continued to move up and I think like we had said earlier, we had set up a sales motion to open large accounts and larger deals.

items.quote: We will definitely see SG&A increase as a percentage over the next quarter and the next, but those investments are already made. The cost, obviously, gets reflected in the next quarter.

items.statement: US rate cuts and election clarity improving spending intent but not yet translating to increased discretionary spend; budgeting cycles in Oct-Nov prepare for future spending.
items.quote: To increase spending directly, not yet. But intend to spend, definitely. Because I think the impact of the cuts, the last cut gave people the positivity and hope that they will be able to spend more. But then there was the election, which created uncertainty, and people were obviously cautious with the election side of things.

items.statement: Deepening partnerships with hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, Salesforce, Boomi, UiPath) and start-up ecosystem; upgraded to Salesforce Crest partner and Microsoft APAC partnership upgrade.

items.quote: Aroma products have clocked a revenue of around INR45 crores as compared to only INR13 crores in last quarter. And the antidumping action on Chinese manufacturer , war by US and Europe would augur well as Aroma business once it is levied.

items.quote: The total net impact there of was of INR116 crores on the consolidated results for this quarter. items.quote: Liquidity situation of the company remains a challenge and working capital management is very high up on our agenda. As you are aware, the management is working on launching a rights issue in a near -- very near future to address these issues.

items.statement: Working capital management high priority; liquidity remains a challenge
items.quote: Liquidity situation of the company remains a challenge and working capital management is very high up on our agenda.

items.statement: Vitafor integration underway; farm product portfolio complementary to feed focus; registrations ongoing in multiple countries

items.statement: Double-digit EBITDA margin (10.2%) achieved in Q2 FY25; management expects sustainability at current prices
items.quote: We have already hit double -digit EBITDA margin in this quarter. And we feel that this should remain and

items.quote: in Q2 of FY25, it has almost doubled to Rs. 739 million over Q1 of this financial year which was at Rs. 391 million. Our CAGR growth in the last 3.5 years is 236% as compared to the electric two-wheeler industry 3.5-year growth of 147%.

items.statement: Greenfield projects designed to be margin-accretive; only tailwinds seen from product mix; strong margin expansion trajectory expected
items.quote: aim of these new greenfield facilities is to be margin-accretive. Second question was about headwinds because of different product mix. No, we only see tailwinds. That is the kind of order acquisition which we have in the proprietary range and also some of our better product range. So, we are only seeing that mix will be benefiting our

items.statement: Assist and slip clutch SOP starting Q4 FY25 with technology from European subsidiary Adler and localization in India
items.quote: For the assist and slip clutches, we are offering technology from our European subsidiary Adler with localization of the parts in India. This SOP will start in Q4 of this financial year.

items.statement: Major FY25 order wins: Hero MotoCorp brakes, TVS brakes, Ather Energy battery part aluminum casting, Generac USA aluminum casting for stationary engines
items.quote: The major orders won till date in this financial year are for the Hero MotoCorp brakes business, TVS brakes business, Ather Energy battery part aluminum casting business and Generac USA aluminum casting business for their stationary engines.

items.statement: Europe: First Tier 1 plastic injection molding order from Volkswagen Group via Endurance Engineering division
items.quote: The importance of this acquisition is that it's the first order acquisition with Volkswagen Group as

items.statement: Alloy wheel market share 13.3% currently, expected to reach ~25% with new Bidkin plant based on existing industry volumes
items.quote: If you see our alloy wheel market share , it is 13.3%. And this will take us to ~25%.. It depends on how much growth will be there in the two-wheel er industry. So, I can say based on the existing volume that 13.3% will become 25% with the new plant coming up

items.statement: Standalone Q2 FY25: Total income Rs 23.2 billion (+16.8% YoY), Net profit Rs 1.85 billion (+29.7% YoY); Consolidated: Total income Rs 29.4 billion (+14.8% YoY), Net profit Rs 2.03 billion (+31.3% YoY)
items.quote: Our standalone and consolidated total income grew to Rs. 23.2 billion and Rs. 29.4 billion respectively, which is a 16.8% and a 14.8% year-on-year growth. Our standalone and consolidated net profits grew to Rs. 1.85 billion and Rs. 2.03 billion respectively, which is a 29.7% and 31.3% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Europe subsidiaries in Euro terms: Total income growth 6.5%, Net profit growth 12.8% YoY in Q2 FY25
items.quote: It is important to note that our European subsidiaries in Euro terms achieved a total income growth of 6.5% and net profit growth of 12.8% versus the same quarter last year, which is commendable given the market scenario in Europe.

items.statement: Carbon neutral percentage reached 35% in FY24, further improvement in FY25, aspiration >50% by FY30 via solar, wind, natural gas, LPG
items.quote: We have reached a carbon neutral percentage of 35% in FY24; we have seen further improvement in FY25 and our aspiration is to reach a carbon neutral percentage of more than 50% by FY30.

items.statement: Mega Project 2013 incentive: Rs 8 crore remaining to book of Rs 447 crore total; Rs 283 crore cash received, Rs 164 crore receivable; 2019 scheme application filed with higher entitlement
items.quote: Of the total of Rs. 447 crores which we had to book on the earlier 2013 Mega project incentives scheme, we still have another Rs. 8 crores to book . We have already received about Rs. 283 crores of cash, and we have another Rs. 164 crores to receive.

items.statement: Alfredo Altavilla inducted as Independent Director on Board of Endurance and its two European subsidiaries; former senior roles at Ferrari, Teksid, Chrysler
items.quote: We are happy to induct in the Board of Directors of Endurance and its two direct subsidiaries in Europe, Mr. Alfredo Altavilla. He is an Independent Director. He is an industry stalwart with a commendable track record serving in senior roles including Board seats in global automotive companies such as Ferrari, Teksid and Chrysler.

items.statement: Suspension capacity nearly fully utilized at Sanand, Halol, Waluj; expanding Waluj for Suzuki scooter order Rs 1,650 million/annum SOP Jan 2025
items.quote: At Waluj, our plant capacity is being fully used, and now we are further expanding to service a large suspension order for Suzuki scooters of Rs. 1,650 million per annum. The SOP is planned from January 2025.

items.statement: Braking business income doubled from Rs 5,950 million FY22 to Rs 11,610 million FY24; second Waluj brakes factory near peak volumes in 2 years, further expansion underway
items.quote: The total income from our braking business doubled in just 2 years, from Rs. 5,950 million in FY22 to Rs. 11,610 million in FY24. The higher demand made us set up a second brakes factory at the Waluj industrial area. The new factory has now reached close to peak volumes within 2 years of SOP, and now we are undergoing a further expansion.

items.statement: Transmission drive shaft capacity at Waluj fully utilized; supplying 3W OEMs, targeting 2 more OEM clients
items.quote: As far as our transmission drive shaft business is concerned, at Waluj, the capacity is now being fully used. We at present manufacture for three 3W OEMs and are targeting orders from two more OEM clients.

items.statement: Chakan casting plant constructing new building for 4W machined casting with automation; unmanned machining line added; TPM-driven efficiency improvements underway
items.quote: In our Chakan castings plant, we are constructing a new building to cater to 4W machined casting requirement. Here we will see improved quality standards and cost optimization because of automation. We have also put an unmanned machining line for a four-wheeler application.

items.statement: Electronics venture gaining traction: BMS offtake by key OEM improved Maxwell financials and SMT line utilization at Waluj; pursuing non-BMS electronics business
items.quote: Our Battery Management System offtake by a key OEM client has picked up leading to a significantly improved financials for our subsidiary Maxwell and better use of our surface mounted technology line that we have set up for BMS at our Waluj plant. Further, our pursuit for electronics business other than BMS is also progressing well.

items.statement: FSNL subsidiary sale SPA signed 24 Oct 2024; transfer expected to close within 60 business days (~15 Jan 2025)
items.quote: The transfer is supposed to be closed within 60 business days from the date of signing of SPA. The SPA was signed on 24th October 2024.

items.statement: H1 FY25 value of goods transacted via e-commerce and marketing verticals reached INR 476.16 billion
items.quote: during the H1 '24-'25, the company crossed INR 476.16 billion in terms of value of goods transacted through its e-commerce and marketing verticals.

items.statement: Standalone H1 FY25 revenue down ~19% to INR 179.27 cr, EBITDA down ~28% to INR 116.63 cr, PBT down ~30% to INR 111.50 cr, PAT down ~26% to INR 83.48 cr
items.quote: The total revenue has been lesser by 18.98% i.e. around 19% from INR 221.29 crores to INR 179.27 crores. And EBITDA is down by 28.19% from INR162.41 crores to INR116.63 crores.

items.statement: E-commerce revenue fell from INR 185.03 cr to INR 168.04 cr; e-auction/e-sale down from INR 142.6 cr to INR 120.31 cr in H1 FY25
items.quote: the basic cause of the fall of the revenue that we can see is down of the e-commerce revenue like from INR 185.03 crores to INR 168.04 crores and in which the e-auction, e-sale is down from INR 142.6 crores to INR 120.31 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated PAT up to INR 118.29 cr from INR 105.95 cr YoY in H1, driven by FSNL discontinued operations PAT rising to INR 37.58 cr
items.quote: Profit after tax from continuing and discontinued operation, INR 105.95 crores in corresponding last period and this year is up to INR 118.29 crores.

items.statement: New exclusive scrap sale contract signed with BPCL marketing division for cylinders, valves, regulators; auctions to start Q3 FY25, revenue visible from Q4 FY25
items.quote: BPCL scrap material, yes, the marketing division of BPCL, it is exclusive contract. They will not been selling it directly or through any other service provider. It will be only through MSTC portal.

items.statement: NPA listing portal for rural, cooperative, private banks developed and almost ready; will offer integrated listing plus bidding platform
items.quote: The listing portal for the NPA properties, which are not under the public sector banks, that is for the rural bank, private, cooperative banks and other institutes. That also is already almost ready, and it should be operational anytime soon.

items.statement: FM radio wavelength allocation auction expected in Q4 FY25; Kendriya Police Kalyan Bhandar digitization project likely to start by year-end; Chhattisgarh Forest timber e-auctions expected this quarter
items.quote: The upcoming projects which we have very recently backed are the important one being the FM width radio wavelength allocation that will be done by MSTC. This will happen, and it is expected to happen in the last quarter of this year.

items.statement: ERP for mineral sector developed covering pre- and post-auction activities; already deployed billing software for Konark Mines; aiming to expand to more mining clients
items.quote: Then we have created an ERP for the mineral sector, where our presence and our activities are quite large. So we are doing a lot of pre-auction activities and post-auction activities and integrating with the databases of our clients.

items.statement: Private sector contributes ~10-12% of scrap revenue; actively expanding to private sector clients beyond government
items.quote: See, it has been more or less stable at around 10% to 12% of the total revenue.

items.statement: FSNL sale proceeds utilization to be decided after board meeting post-closing (~15 Jan 2025); part will go to government as advance tax
items.quote: we will have a kind of internal management meetings and there will be, of course, board meeting to decide on that utilization of the proceeds because one of the parts will be taken by the government as an advanced tax.

items.statement: PSB Alliance developed comprehensive NPA portal mandated for public sector banks; MSTC lost IBAPI/Coal India business; competing for private/rural/cooperative banks with new integrated listing platform
items.quote: Now a comprehensive portal has been developed by PSB Alliance, and they've been mandated to use that. Otherwise, they were very happy with our services.

items.statement: Scrap prices fallen YoY impacting e-auction revenue; volumes stable; Coal India business lost but pursuing commercial mined coal clients
items.quote: First, being the market itself, especially for scrap has actually fallen compared to last year. So since we charge a percentage of the value, definitely, that affects our earnings also.

items.statement: Standalone other income down from INR 57.82 cr to INR 38.31 cr in H1 FY25 mainly due to non-receipt of FSNL dividend
items.quote: other income is down from INR 57.82 crores to INR 38.31 crores, mainly because of non-receipt of dividend from FSNL in this half year as compared to last half year.

items.statement: Employee benefit expenses flat at INR 44.71 cr vs INR 42.40 cr YoY in H1 FY25
items.quote: Employee benefit is remaining on the flatter side from INR 42.40 crores to INR 44.71 crores.

items.statement: Exceptional item of INR 1.94 cr for old arbitration award provision payment in H1 FY25
items.quote: Exceptional item is INR 1.94 crores as already disclosed in the note. This is due to the payment of a provision to a segment of an old arbitration award.

items.statement: Targets 8-10% volume growth for FY25
items.quote: We are confident of delivering 8% to 10% volume growth for FY '25.

items.statement: Targets 12% EBITDA margin ex-inventory gains/losses in normal environment
items.quote: In a normal environment, we should continue to do 12% EBITDA margin ex of inventory gain and loss.

items.statement: Targets ROCE of 15-20% over long term
items.quote: return on capital of 15% to 20% is what we have consistently delivered, and we will consistently deliver that going forward.

items.statement: FY25 capex guided at Rs.330-350 crores including Bihar, Aquel, debottlenecking and maintenance
items.quote: Total capex, including Bihar, will be in the range of Rs.330 crores to Rs.350 crores.

items.statement: Bihar plant capex Rs.170 crores in FY25; debottlenecking Rs.30-35 crores; piping maintenance Rs.80-90 crores; Aquel phase 2 Rs.43 crores; Aquel maintenance Rs.5-7 crores
items.quote: will be there. Apart from that, there will be the bottlenecking, which we have undertaken that will be around Rs.30 crores to Rs.35 crores will be there in that thing. And maintenance capex will be in the range of Rs.80 crores to Rs.90 crores for our existing plant. This is how the piping segment is there. And apart from that, we have already mentioned that Rs.43 crores is left for Aquel for Augus

items.statement: Bihar plant to reach 50,000 tonnes capacity by Q4 FY25; total Bihar capacity 55 KMT including preponed phase 2
items.quote: By the Q4 of the current fiscal, we will be putting up 50,000 ton nes. So we have pre poned the next phase as well, and we are aggressively putting up capacity

items.statement: Significant land available for debottlenecking at Jaipur (80+ acres), Telangana (50 acres), Begusarai (35 acres)
items.quote: We have more than 80 acres at Jaipur facility and around 50 acres at the Telangana facility. And at both current campuses around 20 to 30 acres only. So significant land parcels are available in the Northwest being Jaipur, which caters to both North and West India and Telangana, which is our fully integrated facility for South India. And in Begusarai as well, we have around 35 acres.

items.statement: Inventory losses in Q2 estimated at Rs.12-15 crores
items.quote: It would be around Rs.12 crores to Rs.15 crores for quarter 2.

items.statement: Passed on PVC price hikes of Rs.1/kg and Rs.2/kg; first hike passed, second to be passed by next week
items.quote: We have passed on. We have announced both the price hikes. The first part has been passed on and the second part will be passed on by next week.

items.statement: Channel destocking due to 16% PVC price fall in Q2; restocking expected from November after anti-dumping duty announcement
items.quote: the quarter witnessed a fall of about 16% in PVC prices, which led to severe destocking by channel partners and adversely impacting volume and profitability.

items.statement: End product demand strong due to real estate cycle and affordable polymer prices; optimistic on H2 recovery
items.quote: what is more important is the end product demand across plumbing and agriculture should do well because of a strong real estate cycle as well as affordability in polymer prices.

items.statement: Growth led by Plumbing and SWR segments; CPVC growing well; PVC and Agri weak in Q2
items.quote: The growth was majorly led by Plumbing.

items.statement: Channel finance program expanded to 150+ partners; receivables improved to 55 days from 83 days in March
items.quote: We continue to judicially expand our channel finance program, and we have made steady progress since the recourse has shifted to distributors and the sanction amount has significantly increased and over 150 channel partners have been enrolled under the program as we expand this initiative very judiciously.

items.statement: Overall working capital 93 days in September; inventory 88 days (up from 62 in March); receivables 55 days (down from 83); targeting below 70 days inventory and below 50 days receivables by year-end
items.quote: Our overall working capital stood at 93 days as compared to 80 days in June and 95 days in March '24. As we had guided, receivable have shown marked improvement in the past 2 quarters, and we now stand at 55 days from 83 days in March end. Inventory days have increased to 88 days as compared to 62 days in March '24.

items.statement: Inventory buildup due to weak Q2 volumes vs planned 10-15% growth; normal inventory 65-70 days
items.quote: On a normal basis, we have always guided for 65 to 70 days of inventory we are usually going to sit on. So a month of raw material and a month of finished goods or slightly more than that is typically what we maintain.

items.statement: Industry 65% organized; top 4 players gaining share; one player aggressive in Q2 but Prince avoided predatory pricing
items.quote: So long term, I believe this industry will continue to be more and more organized and big players will continue to become bigger. Having said that, yes, in Q2, everyone has been adding capacity aggressively over the past 2 years to keep up with the demand. So in these times where you have such strong headwinds from a sentiment and raw material pricing point of view, we had seen one player be more

items.statement: Provisional anti-dumping duty findings announced in November supporting PVC price reversal
items.quote: In November, we have seen a reversal of PVC prices because of the announcement of provisional findings of ADD, anti -dumping duty.

items.statement: Aquel Bathware Q2 revenue Rs.7 crores; H1 Rs.11.5 crores; targeting >Rs.25 crores for FY25; breakeven expected Q3 FY26
items.quote: Aquel reported Rs.7 crores of top line in the second quarter.

items.statement: Certified Great Place to Work; trained 1,848 plumbers under Parivartan program; 17 health camps for plumbers
items.quote: Under our Parivartan Plumber Upskilling Programme, we trained 1,848 plumbers across Delhi, NCR, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand to enhance technical skills. We also extended critical health benefits to plumbers and their families through 17 health camps.

items.statement: No natural gas or furnace dependence; extrusion and injection moulding processes using PVC, CPVC, PPR, HDPE, LLDP polymers
items.quote: So we don't have any dependence on natural gas nor do we have furnaces. Pipes is an extrusion process, which is a continuous manufacturing process, and fittings is an injection mo ulding batch processing. And our input raw material is polymers like PVC, CPVC, PPR, HDPE, LLDP

items.statement: Aquel phase 2 asset purchase (manufacturing unit, land, building, equipment) under process subject to regulatory approvals
items.quote: The second phase of Aquel's asset purchase agreement, which includes the acquisition of the manufacturing unit comprising land, building as well as the manufacturing equipment is under process, subject to regulatory approvals.

items.statement: Trade incentives may continue if weak sentiment persists; not ruling out future incentives
items.quote: It's too early to say that. We are in the middle of the quarter. I will not -- I cannot sit here and rule out trade incentives. That's a part and parcel of the industry. When it is required, we will do it.

items.statement: Steel demand in India forecast to grow 7-8% over next few years
items.quote: Steel demand in the developing world, excluding China is projected to grow 4.2% in 2025 while we are holding steady with our strong growth projection for India, forecasting 7% to 8% increase in the demand over next few years.

items.statement: Announced CAPEX of close to 10,000 crores since 2021 IPO, incurred ~5,000 crores till FY25
items.quote: We have announced the CAPEX of close to 10,000 crores since 2021 being an IPO year, we have already incurred a CAPEX close to 5000 crores till FY25 which accounts of 50% of the total CAPEX announced.

items.statement: FY25 CAPEX expected ~1,850 crores with ~1,000 crores in H2
items.quote: expect that out of 4000 crore, 800 crore, we have already incurred in the first half, Shyam Metalics and and we expect that another 1000 crore we will be incur in the second half of the current financial year

items.statement: Annual CAPEX target of 1,700-1,900 crores for FY25-27
items.quote: On an average we are targeting that we are spending close to 1700 to 1900 crores every year, seeing the cash, seeing the strong allocation, capital allocation policy.

items.statement: Remaining CAPEX of 4,551 crores: 1,000 cr in next 6 months, 2,300 cr in FY26, 1,200 cr in FY27
items.quote: the remaining CAPEX required is 4551 crore. Out of this 4551 crore in the next six month, we will be incurring 1000 crore , 2300 crore will be incur in the year 25 -26 and remaining 1200 crore will be incurred in the 26-27.

items.statement: Value-added product revenue grew at 43.2% CAGR over last 5 years
items.quote: However, the focus has been on the value added product, where the revenue has grown at a CAGR of 43.2% in last five years.

items.statement: Stainless steel capacity to grow 4x from 1.5 lakh to ~6 lakh tons in 5 years
items.quote: In the stainless steel we shall grow four folds over next five years, from our existing capacity of 1.5 lakh ton to close to 6 lakh ton capacity.

items.statement: Aluminum foil capacity to grow 2-2.5x in 5 years with niche products
items.quote: In aluminum segment and specialized foil and product, we are planning to grow two-fold to 2.5 fold in next five years, adding more multiple high niche product basket for the specialized application.

items.statement: Carbon steel capacity to grow 1.5-1.8x to 3.6 mt in 2-3 years
items.quote: We will further like to grow, and we will like to add the capacity close to 1.5 to 1.8 fold in next two to three years, from 2.32 million to close to 3.6 million tons.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin 11.2%, expect 100 bps improvement in Q3
items.quote: in the 2nd Quarter whatever the margin was around 11% , in the third quarter we should be able to at least better that by 100 basis points.

items.statement: Blast furnace, coke oven, sinter plant to improve margins from Q4 FY25 onwards
items.quote: with the implementations of coke oven, blast furnace and center plant, the margin will definitely improve from the fourth quarter onwards.

items.statement: Blast furnace project expected to add Rs 3,500-4,000/ton EBITDA on full supply chain when stabilized
items.quote: we expect that, we should be able to increase around 3.5 to Rs.4000 per ton EBITDA on the complete supply chain of this new project.

items.statement: Color coated mill to commercialize by end-Dec, target 70-80k tons in FY25
items.quote: We expect that from the next quarter onwards the December, January quarter onwards we will be able to resume complete operation and we expect that this year we should be able to do a business of close to around 70 - 80,000 tons.

items.statement: Color coated EBITDA expected Rs 5,500-6,500/ton initially, rising to Rs 6,500/ton
items.quote: We expect an EBITDA, because we will be buying HR from the market right now. We don't have our own HR, so around 3500 goes there. So we should be making anything between 5500 to 6500 that is the expected line of EBITDA right now.

items.statement: Stainless steel revenue target revised to ~Rs 1,100 cr for FY25 from earlier Rs 1,500 cr
items.quote: maybe close to around 1100 crores or so maybe we should be able to close it, but again I have to recheck and reconfirm you.

items.statement: Chinese steel exports and firm domestic iron ore prices pressuring margins
items.quote: Its aggressive export strategy, coupled with steep prices undercutting amidst its own economic crisis is disturbing the global steel export dynamics, parallelly the raw material prices India have not corrected to that extent.

items.statement: Management confident of sustained strong product growth in foreseeable future but declines to quantify
items.quote: We feel that between our efforts at driving penetration, driving innovation, creating more relevance, investing as we said earlier ahead of the curve on advertising, and of course, our execution improvement on the ground, we believe that we will be able to sustain strong product growth in the foreseeable future.

items.statement: Festive season saw clear acceleration from Pujas to Diwali with robust demand across all channels
items.quote: First, the growth that we saw from the Pujas to Dussehra to Navaratri period, to Diwali, there was a very clear acceleration. The growth picked up, the consumer, the footfalls in the markets, and the sentiment improved and there was a very clear uptick.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 106 bps YoY to 11.5% despite 40% increase in ad spend
items.quote: On the profitability side , the adjusted EBITDA margin increase d to 11.5% expanding 106 basis points on a year-on-year basis. This margin improvement was delivered despite a deliberate choice of significantly dialing up our advertising spend that I spoke about earlier

items.statement: Gross margin declined 111 bps YoY to 56.3% due to buyback offers and channel mix
items.quote: Our Q2 gross margins at 56.3% were 111 basis points lower versus previous year. This was driven by a combination of buyback offers and channel mix.

items.statement: Depreciation linked to capex investments; amortization largely from acquisition accounting intangibles
items.quote: It may be noted that while the depreciation charge is linked to CAPEX investments, amortization charge in the P&L is largely for intangible assets which were created as part of acquisition accounting.

items.statement: AMC base expanded year-on-year driven by more affordable segmented AMCs at lower ASP
items.quote: Our AMC base expanded year-on-year, driven by more affordable segmented AMCs, albeit at a lower ASP.

items.statement: No price-led growth; ASP improvement driven by premium mix in both water purifiers and vacuum cleaners
items.quote: It's important to also underline, that in neither of the categories, was there a pricing led growth. We did not take pricing; it was on the back of both volumes and ASP.

items.statement: Commodity prices remained range bound during the quarter
items.quote: Commodity prices remained range bound during the quarter.

items.statement: Premium portfolio growing faster than overall category; defined as UV >Rs12k and RO >Rs20k
items.quote: In the case of UV devices, the price point that we have is more than Rs. 12,000 for UV devices, and for RO devices is more than Rs. 20,000. Any product that we have in the price band, which is like I mentioned earlier, more than 12K or more than 20K, will be defined as a premium product.

items.statement: Growth broad based across regions with South over-indexing; tier 2/3 towns growing faster than metros
items.quote: Amongst the regions, we are seeing the South region grow faster and again, that's something that was over index on our overall growth. In terms of town class, we saw all town classes grow, but the tier 2 and tier 3 towns and the mid-tier towns actually grew faster than the metro and tier 1 towns.

items.statement: E-commerce fastest growing channel; modern trade and direct also strong; traditional trade slower
items.quote: While e-commerce was the fastest growing channel, we saw robust growth in retail and in our direct channels as well.

items.statement: Trade receivables up due to higher e-com and modern trade mix with standard credit terms; expected to unwind in H2
items.quote: Trade receivables increased due to channel mix with higher growth in e-com and modern trade. There are standard credit terms in both these channels and we expect this to unwind in H2 of this year.

items.statement: Inventory increase due to festive build-up
items.quote: Inventory increase was due to festive build up that were carried out.

items.statement: Net surplus improved to Rs 119 crore
items.quote: On the balance sheet side, the net surplus improved to Rs. 119 crore.

items.statement: 80% of consumer interactions now digital; service charges down 12% YoY due to digital AMC and leakage control
items.quote: Just to give you a data point around that, today 80% of our interactions are now happening through digital forums.

items.statement: Revenue grew 13.6% YoY to Rs 672.9 crore; continuing business up 14.7%; product business >20%
items.quote: In Q2, we reported a revenue growth of 13.6% over last year, with a revenue of Rs. 672.9 crores. Excluding the impact of discontinued operations, our Q2 revenues grew by 14.7% year-on-year.

items.statement: PAT grew 83% YoY to Rs 46.7 crore
items.quote: Our profit after tax grew 83% year-on-year to Rs. 46.7 crores for Q2.

items.statement: ESOP charges stabilized at Rs 5.7 crore vs Rs 10.7 crore YoY and Rs 8.7 crore QoQ
items.quote: Non-cash ESOP charges stood at Rs. 5.7 crores, versus Rs. 10.7 crores in Q2 last year, and Rs. 8.7 crore in Q1 FY'25. We expect ESOP charges to now stabilize at these levels.

items.statement: Service transformation phase 2 focused on growing franchise via affordable AMCs and filter go-to-market
items.quote: As part of this, our focus continued on improving the customer experience, in growing our service franchise. Our AMC base expanded year-on-year, driven by more affordable segmented AMCs, albeit at a lower ASP. In addition, we strengthened our distribution and our go-to-market system for filters to tap into the non-AMC customer base.

items.statement: Rental pilot continues on slow burn; prioritizing product sales over scaling rental to avoid distraction
items.quote: the rental pilot , the pilot continues on a slow burn, and I want to, sort of talk about that a little bit, because it's a question that has been asked earlier as well, and it’s a very fair question. The rental pilot continues, and it has delivered whatever we wanted to deliver, in terms of learnings, in terms of the KPI, the debate that we have internally is when to step it up

items.statement: Long-term vision: business designed for next 40 years with calibrated profitability expansion
items.quote: So, this is a business that we are designing and rebuilding, as we say often, for the next 40 years, building on the foundation that are being laid in the last 40. So, as we grow, as we drive innovation, as we drive penetration, one big part of that effort will also be to improve profitability.

items.statement: Consolidated top-line growth expected mid-single digit for FY25; India Engineering at least higher single digit; bottom-line growth much higher, in line with H1 FY25 run rate
items.quote: I believe that we will achieve at least higher single digit top line growth in India Engineering business but on a consolidated basis top line growth could be in a mid-single digit range for the current financial year. However, as we have indicated in the past, the bottom-line growth would be much higher, more or less in line with our current run rate what we have achieved in the first half Financ

items.statement: Europe demand softening significantly; US demand slowdown; inventory destocking by customers in India and overseas; normalization expected by Q4 FY25
items.quote: We continue to face challenges as much as Europe is concerned in this quarter and we have also seen demand from us softening significantly.

items.statement: China performance improving with steady improvement and positive profitability in Q2 and H1 FY25; expect significant growth in FY25 vs FY24
items.quote: As I mentioned earlier China is distinctly looking better with steady improvement in performance and positive profitability that we achieved in Quarter 2 and first half financial year '25. We expect China to grow significantly in current fiscal year, both in terms of top line as well as in terms of profitability as compared to last financial year.

items.statement: Romania prospects bleak; may not achieve operating breakeven in FY25 due to demand challenges and geopolitical tensions; combined subsidiary losses expected to reduce thanks to China
items.quote: However, Romania prospects continue to remain bleak, so we are working very hard on the strategy for improving the product mix in Romania by pursuing more cages, both from our existing customers as well as the new customers that we are in the process of acquiring.
