items.quote: On the contrast media, on the Iodine-based products, few of the molecules we are in qualification stages, and few of them we have already commercialized with our customers where we have even long-term contracts with them.

items.statement: USFDA inspection at Unit-II Visakhapatnam successfully concluded in Q2
items.quote: In Q2, we have successfully concluded a USFDA inspection at our Unit-II facility in Visakhapatnam.

items.statement: Exports 87% of total sales revenue H1 FY25; Europe + US combined 71%
items.quote: Exports for the half year is about 87% of the total sales revenue. Exports to Europe and United States combined are about 71% of the total sales revenue.

items.statement: Advancing shipments by 3-4 weeks, maintaining extended safety stock, diversifying supply base to mitigate Red Sea logistics disruption (transit 45→70 days)
items.quote: To mitigate the risks related to inventory management, we have adopted a proactive approach, by advancing shipments by three to four weeks, maintaining extended safety stock levels and diversifying our supply base, wherever feasible.

items.statement: Cash on books ₹3,602 crore as of Sep 30, 2024; receivables ₹2,181 crore; inventories ₹3,145 crore
items.quote: As of 30th September 2024, we have cash on book of ₹ 3,602 crores, receivables of ₹2,181 crores and inventories of ₹3,145 crores.

items.statement: Constant currency growth 21% for H1 FY25
items.quote: Our constant currency growth for the half year has been at 21%.

items.statement: Nutraceutical business ₹406 crore for H1 FY25
items.quote: Our Nutraceutical business amounted to ₹406 crores for this half year.

items.statement: Red Sea crisis extending transit times to ~70 days and raising logistics costs; mitigated by advance shipment planning
items.quote: continued disruptions in red sea have impacted global shipping lanes, with increased attack on commercial vessels prompting the routing of shipments via South Africa. This change has extended our transit times from around 45 days to approximately 70 days and raised associated logistics costs.

items.statement: Generic pricing pressure expected to stabilize in next 6-12 months
items.quote: It is very hard to answer that particular question, but that is the hope that in the next six months to a year, we should see at least some stability with respect to the pricing pressure.

items.statement: Continuous flow chemistry successfully applied in labs and pilot scale, commercial scale production in next 1-2 years
items.quote: Divi's is set to expand its use into commercial scale production in the next one to two years.

items.statement: Peptide fragments (SPPS and LPPS) for GLP-1s supplied to several innovators across Phase II, III and commercialized projects
items.quote: We are working with customers who have projects already commercialized, we are working with customers who are in phase-III, phase-II. So, we have a pipeline which is working right now.

items.statement: Market share gains in both large and small generic APIs despite pricing pressure
items.quote: I would say not just the larger molecules, but also the smaller molecules, all put together. I would say that this half year for the generic business, we have seen a good volume-based growth and it is 49% for the similar reason that in spite of having pricing pressures, we were able to sustain the generic business to that particular percentage.

items.statement: Other expenses flat/slightly down YoY due to green chemistry, efficiency improvements, backward integration
items.quote: What you have seen is mainly because we implemented a lot of green chemistry and we have improvised a lot on the efficiency front and also the backward integration that we went into.

items.statement: Reiterated FY25 revenue growth guidance of 15%+ with stable EBITDA margins at current levels; agri segment growth 10-15%
items.quote: Going forward, we would like to reiterate our earlier guidance of 15% -plus growth in cranes, material handling and construction equ ipment segments for the current year and expect agri segment to g row 10% to 15% during the year.

items.statement: Management expects FY25 revenue growth could reach up to 20% but guiding conservatively at 15%+ due to election and monsoon headwinds
items.quote: We are very hopeful of doing 15% -plus. And there is an easy chance it can reach up to 20%. But to be on the conservative side, we are saying 15%-plus.

items.statement: Expecting largest ever single defense order of INR400-420 crores from Ministry of Defense within November, executable over 3 years but targeting FY26-27
items.quote: Further, we are on track to receive our largest ever single order valued at over INR400 crores from the Ministry of Defense.

items.statement: Defense segment revenue contribution expected to exceed 5% in FY26 and FY27, aligning with medium-term goal of 5-10% share
items.quote: This milestone will drive Defense segment's revenue contribution beyond 5% for the years FY '26 and '27, aligning with our medium to long-term goal of achieving 5% to 10% share of overall revenue from the defense sector.

items.statement: Revenue capacity to increase from INR4,500 crores to over INR5,100 crores by Q4 FY25 through ongoing expansion; further INR600 crores possible with nominal capex
items.quote: The company currently has a revenue capacity of around INR4,500 crores, which is set to increase by an additional INR600 crores through the ongoing capacity expansion, bringing the total to over INR5,100 crores by quarter 4 of current financial year.

items.statement: Additional 82 acres land acquired (21 acres registered, 61 acres possession by Q4) plus 48 acres applied for in another state for future growth beyond INR6,500 crores capacity
items.quote: We have already done agreements for about 82 acres of land. These are 2 different chunks. One is about, I think, 21 acres, other is about 61 acres. So the 21 acres has already been registered in the company's name and we have possession of that land. The balance 61 acres chunk, hopefully, we should be in a position to bring it on to the books of the company and take physical possession in quarter

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin expanded 268 bps YoY to 18.04%; PBT margin 16%, PAT margin 11.97%; H1 FY25 EBITDA margin 17.94% (highest ever)
items.quote: The operational revenues grew by 12.2% on a year -on-year basis to INR754.34 crores with an EBITDA margin of 18.04%.

items.statement: Margin expansion driven equally by favorable product mix (higher tonnage cranes, NX-series) and commodity benefit (lower steel prices); steel prices strengthening post-Diwali
items.quote: Yes. First part of your question regarding -- definitely, there is an angle of product mix, which has added to our EBITDA margins in the last quarter. And going forward, this product mix benefit will be there because higher tonnages crane, even in the pick-and-carry segment, within this segment, are gaining more traction.

items.statement: Management to decide in next 2-3 quarters whether to pass operating leverage benefits to customers via price cuts or maintain margins
items.quote: But then I think as a company, we have to make a choice whether to remain competitive or cost effective in the market or continue to keep on increasing prices. So that call we will be taking over the next, I would say, 2, 3 quarters that maybe we will -- whatever is the operating leverage benefit, we start passing it out to our customers and not increase our prices further.

items.statement: Price increase of 5-6% for BS IV to BS V engines and 11-15% (avg 12%) for BS III to BS V engines effective 1st January 2025; 60% of machines affected by higher increase
items.quote: The machines which are going from BS IV to BS V, there'll be a cost impact of 5% to 6%. So from 1st January onwards, like I'll just repeat again, engines going fro m BS III to BS V, there will be a cost impact of around 12%, average. Machines going from BS IV to BS V from 1st January onwards, there will be 5% to 6% increase.

items.statement: Pre-buying started post-Diwali ahead of Jan 1 price hike; expecting 15-20% additional sales from pre-buying; 55% of annual revenue typically comes in H2
items.quote: So we are hopeful that we can expect a 15%, 20% additional sales on this account; balance, time will tell. Man pro poses, God disposes. We are ready with our inventory. We are ready with our planning.

items.statement: Higher tonnage cranes (20T+) and multi-activity NX-series cranes (patented) driving product mix improvement; NX-series adoption accelerating after COVID hesitation
items.quote: No. Again, see it is a mix. It is not only the higher tonnage crane, but some of our NX -series Cranes, which we had introduced 3, 4 years back. But obviously, they were priced a little higher. They were multi-activity cranes. And after corona around the time, people were a little hesitant in adopting technology at a higher cost, which has started happening now.

items.statement: Targeting market share increase of 1-1.5% in pick-and-carry cranes (currently 62-64%, targeting 70%) and tower cranes in FY25; backhoe loader share ~2-2.5%
items.quote: And we are very hopeful to grow our market share in the current year by at least 1%, 1.5%, if not more. And going forward, we target to reach even Cranes segment up to 70% market share with pick -and-carry, and I'm sure we'll do it.

items.statement: Kato Works 50-50 JV for bigger cranes (crawler, truck, rough terrain) definitive agreements by early Q4 FY25, production start within 6-8 months, revenue in FY26, full steam FY27
items.quote: So definitive agreements are being negotiated currently, and we are hopeful that by early quarter 4, all this process would be finished. And we would be setting up a joint venture, maybe within quarter 4 itself or early next financial year in quarter 1 FY '26. And we intend to start producing machines within 6 to 8 months of that.

items.statement: Overseas acquisition put on hold due to better opportunity emerging; may announce in Q4 FY25 or Q1 FY26; separate from Kato JV
items.quote: So as of now, that acquisition outside India has been put on hold, and we are working on even a better opportunity. So hopefully, if everything goes well, maybe in quarter 4 or quarter 1 next year, we might be able to announce this -- even a better opportunity, like I said.

items.statement: CFO/EBITDA ratio low at 8% in H1 due to preponed MSME vendor payments (creditors reduced 5-7 days); expected to normalize by March 2025
items.quote: Basically -- typically, the liability is basically the payments to MSME vendors. So we have been preponing our payments to MSME vendor, which has reduced the liabilities which is part of the current liabilities. Going forward, we expect that probably by the year -end probably the numbers will be as similar to what we did for March '24.

items.statement: Net cash position of INR610 crores (INR785 crores investments vs INR140 crores debt); short-term borrowings increased temporarily for MSME payments and land advances, to be repaid by March 2025
items.quote: Yes, we've got investment of INR785 crores and a debt of INR140 crores, so net of INR610 crores...

items.statement: BS V emission norms (stricter than Euro V) effective 1st Jan 2025: BS III to BS V (60% of machines, ~12% cost increase), BS IV to BS V (40%, 5-6% increase); all prototypes ARAI approved
items.quote: On 1st January, there is a transition. BS III engines are going directly to BS V and BS IV engines are going to BS V. And yes, there is going to be a cost increase.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 unit sales 2,863 (+9% YoY); H1 FY25 revenue INR1,488 crores (+12.5% YoY); EBITDA INR267 crores (+37.7% YoY)
items.quote: The company recorded sales of 2,863 units in the quarter, which is up by 9% year-on-year.

items.statement: Agri segment revenue INR61.27 crores (8% of total) with 3.85% margin in Q2; volume dip YoY due to discontinued rotavators and deferred African export order to H2
items.quote: The revenue contribution of agri stood at 8%, and we registered a revenue of INR61.27 crores with a margin of 3.85%.

items.statement: Electric cranes ready for launch pending CMVR notification (expected Nov-Dec 2024); ramp-up from Dec 2024/Jan 2025
items.quote: The -- see, product is already available. The only thing the regulations are missing. So again, it is expected that within November or latest by December, the notification, which has come with respect to CMVR regulations for this electric construction equipment should get notified and we can sell it and get it registered.

items.statement: Utilization at ~80% triggers capacity expansion; FY26 revenue target INR3,400-3,600 crores (15-20% growth) approaching INR5,100 crores capacity; FY23-26 revenue tripling goal (INR2,200 to INR4,400 crores) on track
items.quote: So looking at all that, I think this year, if we do a 15%, 20% growth, so that will be somewhere INR3,400 crores plus/minus. It could be INR100 crores, INR200 crores on either side. I would feel the positive side. And hopefully, we should be getting closer to our capacity that we have created within FY '26.

items.statement: BS V compliance (stricter than Euro V) positions company for developed market exports (Europe, US, Japan) in 2-3 years; upgrading aesthetics to international standards
items.quote: But going forward in the next 2 years, 3 years, even these markets, once we have totally adapted to the technology and perfected it, I'm sure these things will also come into our scheme of things, the developed markets with respect to export of our cranes or construction equipment.

items.statement: Spare parts revenue ~4% of turnover (INR50-60 crores); target to increase 50-100% via DMS, service app, and combating spurious parts; O&M revenue mainly via dealers except tower/crawler cranes
items.quote: around 4% of our turnover, sir. Sorab Agarwal: 4% of our turnove r. So I've understood your question, I'll answer it in 2 parts. We realize that the sales of our spare parts is reasonably underpenetrated in the market because over the years, a lot of spurious players and alternate parts have come up

items.statement: Election outcome and extended monsoons slowed H1 FY25 growth; H2 recovery critical for 15%+ FY25 target; sentiment affected post-elections
items.quote: unfortunately, we were expect ing the momentum to pick up post 15th August in the last quarter because the rains also started to subside, but it kept on raining, and obviously, the election results, the outcome was not as positive as was expected. So we are just planning for a

items.statement: Rental income minimal (INR8-9 crores) from crawler cranes given to OEMs; not competing with customers
items.quote: If I look at revenue for the rental income will be as low as INR8 crores to INR9 crores, that's all.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guided at 15-20% YoY and PAT growth at 12-15% YoY
items.quote: I think we are anticipating around 15% to 20% growth on the topline. And bottomline, around 12% to 15%.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin expected in 18-20% range
items.quote: Margin will be around 18. Right now, we are already at 18%. I think it'll be in that same range 18% to 20% depends on product mix and volume.

items.statement: Rs 150 crore capex for backward integration to complete by Q4 FY25
items.quote: The CAPEX expansion plan will be completed by Q4 this year. The CAPEX plan, which we have taken up, is for the backward integration of key materials for some of our critical products.

items.statement: Backward integration to reduce import dependency and improve margins by 5-8%
items.quote: Getting it manufactured at our own site will give us that leverage and confidence to our cus tomers and also that they will not have any supply issues. So, that was our main target for initiating this vertical integration. But obviously, definitely the re will be saving on the cost as well. The profitability will definitely increase by around close to around 5% to 8% to

items.statement: Solid sustained demand with 18% YoY and 20% QoQ revenue growth in Q2 FY25
items.quote: I am pleased to report an 18% year-on-year increase in revenues from operations, reaching Rs. 196.75 crores. This growth was driven by healthy volume growth across our portfolio. Sequentially, revenue from operations was higher by 20%.

items.statement: Growth led by ARV and anti-inflammatory segments; Ibuprofen sales on solid trajectory
items.quote: Our revenue growth was led by robust growth in ARVs and anti -inflammatory segment. I am pleased to report that ARV has rebounded strongly, which aligns with what we communicated earlier. Ibuprofen sales have continued on a solid growth trajectory supported by an expanding customer base

items.statement: Received EDQM certificate for Vizag facility to supply Ibuprofen to Europe
items.quote: I am proud to report that we have received the EDQM certificate for our Vizag facility to supply ibuprofen for Europe.

items.statement: Q2 gross margin 30% declined YoY and QoQ due to rising raw material costs from geopolitical tensions
items.quote: In terms of margins, our Q2 gross margin stood at 30%, showing some decline yearly and sequentially, primarily impacted by rising raw material costs due to geopolitical tensions.

items.statement: H1 FY25 PAT grew 45% YoY to Rs 30.58 crore with PAT margin at 8.5%
items.quote: For the first half of F Y25, PAT reached Rs. 30.58 crores, making a robust 45% year -on-year growth, primarily driven by better performance and lower financial costs. This improved PAT margins to 8.5% for H1 FY25 compared to 7% for H1 FY24

items.statement: 25% of capex allocated to new products in pipeline; commercialization in 2-3 years due to patents
items.quote: We have segmented around 25% of our CAPEX for new products. So, new products are still in the pipeline phase right now. They're in the pipeline, few on the validation phase. So, they're not fully commercial yet. And these products will not be commercialized now because they have some patents associated with them. So, I think it will take 2-3 years for them to commercialize them.

items.statement: Ongoing demand remains tepid due to lower consumer spending, especially in rural areas; extended monsoon affected volume offtake
items.quote: The on going demand continues to be tepid on account of lower consumer spending, especially in the rural areas of the country. extended monsoon affected our volume offtake, resulting in moderate decline of 6.6% in overall income in H1 FY25 compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: EBITDA dipped 16.3% YoY in H1 FY25 due to rise in export ocean freight expenditure and lower capacity utilization
items.quote: The EBITDA also dipped by 16.3% in H1 FY25 on a YoY basis. This decline in EBITDA is on the back of rise in export, ocean freight expenditure due to shortage of containers. Lower capacity utilization levels have also impacted resulting in low er EBITDA.

items.statement: Capacity utilization in H1 FY25 stood at 73%, slightly below last year's 77%
items.quote: The capacity utilization in the first half stood at 73%, which was slightly below, last year level of 77% u nderscoring the influence of these external factors on our operations.

items.statement: Board approved acquisition of 26% equity of Emerge Solar One Private Limited for Rs. 1.28 crore to provide captive power to Tamil Nadu plant under Group Captive Scheme
items.quote: We are pleased to share that the board has approved to acquire 26% of equity of Emerge Solar One private limited. The acquisition involves purchase of equity shares against cash consideration of Rs.1,28,00,000. The Company in undertaking this acquisition will provide captive power to its Tamil Nadu plant under the Group Captive Scheme, as per the Electricity Act 2003.

items.statement: H1 FY25 total income Rs. 324.6 crore vs Rs. 347.3 crore in H1 FY24; EBITDA Rs. 35.2 crore vs Rs. 42 crore; EBITDA margin 10.8%; PAT Rs. 14.4 crore vs Rs. 18.9 crore
items.quote: For H1 FY25, total income stood at Rs. 324.6 crores for H1 FY25 as compared to Rs. 347.3 crores in H1 FY24. EBITDA for H1 FY25 stood at Rs. 35.2 crores, against Rs. 42 crores in the corresponding period last year. EBITDA margin reported at 10.8% in H1 FY25. The Company registered profit after tax at Rs. 14.4 crore in H1 FY25 against Rs. 18.9 crore in H1 FY24.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 total income Rs. 106.8 crore vs Rs. 121.3 crore in Q2 FY24; EBITDA Rs. 10.3 crore vs Rs. 13.6 crore; EBITDA margin 9.6%; PAT Rs. 1.9 crore vs Rs. 3.8 crore
items.quote: For Q2 FY25, total income stood at Rs. 106.8 crore for Q2 FY25, compared to Rs. 121.3 crores in Q2 FY24. EBITDA for Q2 FY25 was Rs. 10.3 crores, down from Rs. 13.6 crores in the same period last year. items.statement: Company maintains target to reach Rs. 1000 crores revenue in next 5 years
items.quote: So, far the growth and that thing as we said that it's a continuous endeavor to reach to the Rs. 1000 crores in the next 5 years. That we are still maintaining.

items.statement: Value-added product share increased from 16% to 17% last year; target is 25% going forward; value-added margins are 15-20% higher than normal products
items.quote: See, as you have seen over value added, last year it was 16% now it increased to 17%. Going forward , the value added would be going to 25% that what we are maintaining, and we are working towards it. And value-added margins are better than the normal.

items.statement: Value-added product margins are around 15% to 20% higher than normal products
items.quote: Margin, it will be around 15% to 20% higher in the value added.

items.statement: Odisha asbestos plant and Palghar non-asbestos plant each allocated Rs. 95 crores; Wada plant to start in Q4 FY26, reaching 75% capacity utilization in 2 years from FY27 onwards
items.quote: It is already there, madam, if you see, we have clearly said that Odisha is asbestos and Palghar is non-asbestos. And already we have provided Rs. 95 crores each for both the facilities which are going to come.

items.statement: Wada plant will start in Q4 FY26 and take two years to reach 75% capacity utilization from FY27 onwards
items.quote: See as we mentioned , Wada plant will start somewhe re in the Q4 of FY26, and it will take two years to reach to a capacity of 75% capacity utilization. It is not going to impact our existing capacity because that's already set. So, whatever that plant capacity will come, slowly gradually we will reach to the 75% in the next 2 years, from 27 onwards.

items.statement: Management does not provide EBITDA margin forecasts; depends on rural economy and economic conditions
items.quote: Generally, we don't give forecast on EBITDA margins. It all depends on how the rural economy works, how the economics work, depends on that. But we generally don't give any forecast on the EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Raw material prices stable for past 1.5 years; only forex fluctuation impacts costs; asbestos supply smooth, no increase foreseen except forex
items.quote: As we said continuously in the last two calls that there is now stability in the pricing. There is no increase in the raw material pricing. Only there is fluctuation in the forex which is getting impacted because as you have seen the rupee is getting weak against the dollar.

items.statement: Asbestos prices increased 40-45% one and half years ago, now stable; only forex fluctuation causes variation; supply smooth, no near-term increase foreseen
items.quote: See, t here is no increase in asbestos price. Whatever the price has increased, it has already increased one and a half year before. And after that, there is a stability. So, there is no increase. Only the increase is happening on account of foreign exchange fluctuations. So, prices are now stable. There is no increase.

items.statement: Top raw materials are asbestos fiber and cement
items.quote: Main is the fiber and cement.

items.statement: Rural economy not picked up; hope for improvement post Maharashtra elections and harvest season; Q3 expected better post-Diwali
items.quote: As I mentioned that rural economy is still not picked up. Hopefully, post-election, particularly in the Maharashtra, and after this, you know that harvest that comes into the hands of farmers, hopefully, the things would be better.

items.statement: Industry de-growth of ~10% acknowledged; second half expected to be good with post-Diwali demand spike
items.quote: Yes, because we also are facing the same situation because there is a de-growth compared to what it used to be. So, the totality what they are saying may be correct.

items.statement: Price cuts minimal; 13-14% revenue drop mainly due to volume, capacity utilization, and export sea freight
items.quote: Price cut is a minimal.

items.statement: Competitors also adding capacity; company adding capacity in new regions (East) and for export (Maharashtra border); no long-term pricing pressure expected
items.quote: The point is the capacity everybody is increasing, not we only. If you see that, Visaka is also increasing and other companies are also increasing. So, we are increasing the capacity where we are not present as in the East we are coming, there we are not present. And the second capacity that is coming is only near Maharashtra border, which is mainly for the export purpose.

items.statement: No over-supply or increased competition in last 3-4 years; capacity same in markets where company operates; production adjusted to demand
items.quote: No, because both, more or less capacity is same in the market where we are working.

items.statement: Historical margin decline attributed to 40-45% raw material cost increase vs only 8-10% price pass-through (30-35% bottomline impact) and lower rural demand reducing volumes
items.quote: See, what you are comparing is correct that from 2018 to 202 2, the market situation different, dynamics was different. Now, because before two years if you see one and half years before, the raw material prices have increased around 40% to 45%. And we could pass on to the market not more than 8% to 10%. So, there is a straight impact of 30% to 35% in the bottomline, which is what you are seeing t

items.statement: Management agrees margins at bottom range (6-9% in bad times vs 20-24% historically); expects improvement from Q3 onwards on pricing front
items.quote: Yes. It has to improve.

items.statement: Emerge Solar One acquisition investment ~Rs. 1.26 crore; expected power cost saving Rs. 2.5 per unit; payback 15-24 months
items.quote: See, as we said, this is purely a solar power where we are going to invest around Rs. 1.26 crore and we are going to get the required quantity of power which is being used in our Tamil Nadu plant Perundurai. And the saving would be around Rs. 2.5 per unit. 15 to 24 months is the payback.

items.statement: Forex fluctuation (rupee depreciation) remains key risk for raw material costs
items.quote: Only the forex part, which is going to play, because if you've seen the last 15 days to 20 days, rupee devaluation is around...

items.statement: Kharif season delayed due to erratic rainfall; sprays shifted to October; Rabi outlook strong with full reservoirs
items.quote: Initially, there was paucity of rains, which delayed the sprays. And later on, there was continuous rainfall in most part of the country. So, negative that the sprays were delayed. Positive season continued even in the month of October.

items.statement: Maharatna premium products volume grew over 10%; generic products volume declined ~13% as part of tail-cutting strategy
items.quote: Again, in this quarter, we are very successfully able to increase the volumes of our Maharatna products, not less than 10%. So the growth is 10% plus, particularly in this case.

items.statement: Generic products volume degrowth of about 13% as company focuses on premium Maharatna portfolio
items.quote: And in case of generics, which are non -focused products, there is a degrowth of about 13%.

items.statement: Average year-on-year price decline of ~10%; Maharatna prices corrected 8-9%, generics saw some price improvement
items.quote: Overall, you can say the prices year-on-year has declined by almost 10%.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin 14.3% (up from 11.8% YoY); H1 margin 12.5%; management expects growth in both top and bottom line in H2 but avoids specific margin guidance
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 14.3%.

items.statement: Export order book already exceeds INR100 crores, covering last year's INR105 crores full-year export revenue; B2B order book routine but showing recovery signals
items.quote: We have already collected orders for INR100 crores plus actually.

items.statement: Working capital days improved from 151 days (Mar'24) to 102 days (Sep'24); inventory levels kept in control
items.quote: We also reported an improved working capital days from 151 days in March '24 to 102 days in September '24.

items.statement: Sales returns of INR35-40 crores booked in Q2 (mainly herbicides); additional INR10-15 crores expected in Q3; returns primarily in Maharatna herbicide portfolio
items.quote: So volume -- value-wise, so about INR35 crores, INR40 crores of returns would have been booked in the Q2 itself majorly from herbicides.

items.statement: Raw material prices have bottomed out and are firming slightly; no major stress; changes are plus/minus 1-3%
items.quote: I think the prices have already bottomed out, and they have started firming a detail. So I don't see a downfall from here.

items.statement: Planning to dedicate additional production lines (beyond SEZ unit) to meet export order requirements
items.quote: Apart from the SEZ unit, I have to dedicate one more unit, a few lines so that we can meet up this requirement.

items.statement: Acquired Kaeros for three strategic advantages: import technicals directly, avoid B2B channel conflict, and launch second brand to access new distributor networks; targets INR100+ crores revenue next year
items.quote: So I believe that Kaeros will be a good acquisition for IIL. And in the next year, we can plan a decent business, not less than INR100 crores or so.

items.statement: Running over 300 reactors across plants; strengthening manufacturing to support new AI and formulation launches
items.quote: Today, I'm running more than 300 reactors in my plants actually.

items.statement: Premium (Maharatna) products contribute 68% of B2C sales in Q2 (64% in H1); 4-7 new launches planned in H2, with 3+ expected to qualify as Maharatna
items.quote: In quarter 2 of FY '25, the premium products contribution is around 68% of the total B2C sales and 32% from the generic products.

items.statement: Topline growth guidance of 15% for FY25 unlikely; major season (60% of revenue) impacted; some recovery possible in remaining 40% but maintaining growth percentage difficult
items.quote: There might be a little decline actually. So difficult because major part of the season is one where we do 60%. So now 40% is left. We have to make some recovery in 40%.

items.statement: Export growth signals from regular markets (Middle East, Africa, Asia, CIS) plus new Latam business starting in Q2; order book already covers last year's full export revenue
items.quote: Like from our regular markets only because there are no -- many new countries which we are going to start about -- except some business in Latam is going to begin this year in the Q2.

items.statement: Investing in team building across functions; launched new training module for all employees (not just sales) to improve farmer engagement and product knowledge
items.quote: Today also, we are launching one more training module for our team members. The idea is that it's not only the sales team, but the development team, the entire team of the company, which is working with the farmer.

items.quote: This quarter has been a very healthy quarter with a revenue growth of 32% year-on-year despite having 25% of the Grand Hyatt Mumbai room inventory under renovation. We have achieved the EBITDA of ₹ 73 crores which is 21% YoY growth. We achieved the PBT of ₹ 20 crores in the quarter compared to a loss of ₹ 27 crores over comparable period last year.

items.statement: Cash balance ₹247 crore; strong net free cash flow generation; ₹64 crore used post-Sept for Bangalore plus ₹280 crore debt
items.quote: On the balance sheet side, we had a cash balance of ₹ 247 crores. We are generating very strong net-free cash flows, and we have utilized ₹ 64 crores of cash post the September 30th to acquire Bengaluru in addition to ₹ 280 crores of debt that we have onboarded.

items.statement: One-time tax charge of ₹49 crore in H1 FY25 from Finance Bill 2024 capital gains amendments; remeasured deferred tax liabilities
items.quote: And as Mr. Saraf was saying that there is a charge that we have taken which is notional of 49 crores in the first half, which basically reflects the amendments that were made in the Finance Bill 2024 relating to the capital gains. JHL has remeasured its deferred tax liabilities on items which were subject to capital gains, and this is a cumulat ive one-time charge that has been taken on

items.statement: Bangalore hotel ramp-up expected fast: operational in 9 months, healthy occupancy/ARR within 3-6 months post opening
items.quote: So, for our Bangalore asset, we expect it to be operational in about nine months. Post that, the ramp up would actually be quite fast according to us. The market is already there and we would assume that within the next three to six months we would be able to actually achieve a good healthy occupancy and ARR.

items.statement: Expects better growth in Q3 and Q4 FY25 vs H1 due to Dadri ramp-up and consolidation of Balaji and Bansal High Carbon
items.quote: So, we are expecting a little better growth as compared to the first 2 quarters in the next 2 quarters.

items.statement: Targets 80% EBITDA growth in FY25 driven by full consolidation of BSPL, Balaji, Bansal High Carbon and Dadri ramp-up to 6 lakh tons
items.quote: Therefore, all of these three factors combined, we are looking at a good growth.

items.statement: Strong demand across automotive, construction and general engineering drove highest ever quarterly revenue in Q2 FY25
items.quote: In the 2nd Quarter of FY'25 also, we have achieved our highest ever quarterly revenue driven by strong demand across all our key segments like automotive, construction and general engineering.

items.statement: Two-wheeler industry growth and market share gains driving automotive demand
items.quote: Other than that, the two-wheeler industry has been doing well. Therefore, we see a good growth, in which the growth has also come from acquiring market share.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin expanded 192 bps YoY and net profit margin expanded 183 bps YoY
items.quote: We are happy to report that EBITDA and net profit margins for Quarter 2 has expanded by 192 basis points and 183 basis points on year-on-year basis.

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA margin up 224 bps and net profit margin up 127 bps YoY
items.quote: For the first half too, our margins have risen by 224 basis points for EBITDA and 127 basis points for the net profit.

items.statement: High carbon EBITDA ~Rs 10/kg; mild steel Rs 4-7/kg; stainless steel Rs 7-8/kg
items.quote: Sir, in general, we look at high carbon to be about Rs. 10 per kg EBITDA business. Mild steel and stainless-steel to range between Rs. 4-7 per kg EBITDA.

items.statement: Specialty wire (steel cord, lead wire) to improve margin mix from Q4 FY25
items.quote: So, as and when we are able to ramp up the Speciality Wire vertical, our mix of margin will completely change.

items.statement: Consolidation of Balaji and Bansal High Carbon volumes to be 100% in Bansal Wire from Q3 FY25
items.quote: Therefore, in Quarter 3, we are looking at almost all volumes and revenue from Balaji and Bansal High Carbon to come into Bansal Wire.

items.statement: Dadri capex Rs 500-550 crore; funded partly from internal accruals
items.quote: Sir, the total CAPEX that we are doing in Dadri was about Rs. 500-550 crores.

items.statement: Dadri facility 3.5 lakh tons; at ~20% utilization end Q2; targeting 100% capacity operational by end FY25
items.quote: Sir, Dadri as a whole is 3.5 lakh tons, out of which till about last month of last quarter, we were already at close to 20% capacity utilization and we are looking at bringing this whole capacity or at least being able to operationalize this whole capacity within this financial year.

items.statement: Total capacity to reach 6 lakh tons by end FY25 from 2.5 lakh tons at start
items.quote: So, the starting of this year we started with 2.5 lakh tons and we will end with 6 lakh tons.

items.statement: Bead wire 30,000 tons annual capacity to be operationalized this month
items.quote: Bead wire we are adding about 30,000 tons annual capacity which will be completely operationalized within this month.

items.statement: Steel prices fell ~10% in Q2 FY25 boosting margins despite flat revenue
items.quote: From a very basic number, if you see, our volume has grown by about 10% whereas our revenue is flat. So, there is definitely a difference of at least 10% that has come there.

items.statement: Raw materials sourced domestically; natural hedge via simultaneous order booking and raw material procurement
items.quote: So, sir, we have what we would like to call a kind of a natural hedge in our business model. Because whatever orders or whatever raw material we buy, we also book orders with that simultaneously.

items.statement: Specialty wire vertical (steel cord, lead wire, hose wire) to start production in Q4 FY25; steel cord approvals take 1-1.5 years
items.quote: From the last quarter of this year, we should be seeing some production and some sales happening there and for the future also, we are depending on this segment very aggressively and we want to grow with this product, steel cord.

items.statement: Over 5,000 customers; diversified across sectors; B2C model in Gujarat for agriculture wires
items.quote: Our commitment to quality and customization has helped us build a diverse and loyal customer base of over 5,000 customers.

items.statement: Exports ~10% of revenue in H1 FY25; geopolitical issues slowed growth but momentum improving
items.quote: During the first half, export accounted for about 10% of our total revenue.

items.statement: Vendor financing and bill discounting limits tied up; will be utilized from Q3 FY25 as consolidated revenues increase
items.quote: we have already tied up some limits for discounting and other various tools. We are only waiting for the revenue, which will come in the third quarter of this year to increase from Balaji 7 and Bansal High Carbon, and then we will start utilizing those limits as well

items.statement: Debt-equity ratio 0.21x as of September 30, 2024
items.quote: As on September 30, 2024, we had a comfortable debt-equity ratio at 0.21 times.

items.statement: 100% acquisition of Bansal Steel and Power completed; Balaji and Bansal High Carbon consolidation ~100% by end Q2
items.quote: In the last quarter, we have done 100% acquisition of Bansal Steel and Power and by the end of last quarter itself, we have done almost 100% consolidation of Bansal High Carbon and Balaji.

items.statement: Formed subsidiary Bansal BWI Steels for stainless steel rod backward integration; land parcels identified in Rajasthan and Ahmedabad; targeting finalization Nov-Dec 2024
items.quote: So, sir, in the last quarter, we have formed a new subsidiary, a volume subsidiary for this particular project that is Bansal BWI Steels and we are actively looking for land parcels in the area of Rajasthan as well as Ahmedabad.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 volume 80,000 tons (high carbon 30,000, mild steel 27,000, stainless 21,000-22,000)
items.quote: On the volume front, we did about 80,000 tons this quarter, in which high carbon was about 30,000 tons, low carbon was 27,000 tons and stainless-steel was around 21,000 tons.

items.statement: H1 FY25 volume 1.56 lakh tons including ~8,000 tons from Dadri
items.quote: Sir, even in the first quarter, we had a little bit of volume coming from Dadri, which was 2,000 tons. In this quarter also, we had about 6-7,000 tons coming from Dadri.

items.statement: Steel cord approvals take 1-1.5 years; hose wire approvals faster (1 month or less)
items.quote: After that, we will start inviting customers for the approval process, which will take another one, one and a half years to get us an approval in steel cord. But the by-product of steel cord, which is hose wire, is what we will start off with in the last quarter of this year.

items.statement: Management expects H2 FY25 demand trends to be largely similar to H1, with potential upside if API prices improve and industry volumes pick up.
items.quote: Looking ahead we expect demand trends in the second half to be largely similar to the first half. There could be some upside potential if we see some improvement in API prices and uptake in industry volumes, but that remains to be seen.

items.statement: Management expects API prices to average or normalize in Q3 or Q4 FY25, which would positively impact revenue.
items.quote: An update on to it is while we saw the API prices softening in Q3, most of the intermediates of the KSM have started showing some solidification. So, either in Q3 or Q4, I expect the API prices will at least average or normalize.

items.statement: Management does not expect API business to turn EBITDA positive in Q4 FY25; timeline shifted by 6 months with review starting April.
items.quote: I don't think that in the Q4 this will turn around, or it would not be EBITDA positive. I think we will have to give it 6 months from here and we will revisit our business plans starting April.

items.statement: CDMO volume declined roughly 11% in Q2 FY25; management attributes this to industry cycle and advance ordering patterns.
items.quote: Yes, we did not experience the volume growth. We had a volume decline of roughly 11% this quarter.

items.statement: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin was 12.9% in Q2 FY25 vs 15.8% a year ago; CDMO margin 15.4%, branded/generic 10.3%, API margin negative Rs 14 crore.
items.quote: All these impacted our adjusted EBITDA margin which is down to 12.9% versus 15.8% in the prior year.

items.statement: Gross margin improved to 42.3% in Q2 FY25 from 40.6% a year ago.
items.quote: Gross margins on consolidated basis in Q2 were at 42.3% similar to Q1, but higher than Q2 last year which was 40.6%.

items.statement: Received 10 DCGI and 86 FSSAI approvals in H1 FY25; total export dossiers filed at 367 with 350 in pipeline.
items.quote: We received 10 DCGI and 86 FSSAI approvals in H1 of the current fiscal.

items.statement: Spent Rs 150 crore on capex in H1 FY25; new injectable facility at Haridwar started commercial production in Q2.
items.quote: In H1 we spent around Rs. 150 crore in CAPEX. In Q2 we started commercial production at our new injectable facility in Haridwar.

items.statement: Falling API prices (Amoxicillin, Cephalosporins, Paracetamol, Telmisartan) caused revenue deflation in cost-plus CDMO model and delayed customer inventory build-up.
items.quote: Prices of several key API's including Amoxicillin, Cephalosporins, Paracetamol, Telmisartan etc., continues to fall. As you are aware, our CDMO business is a cost-plus model, so when input costs fall, we experience revenue deflation as well.

items.statement: CDMO revenue share 79% in Q2; branded/generic 16%; API 5%. Branded portfolio reshaping driving higher profitability in branded/generic segment.
items.quote: If we were to break the segment-wise revenue, CDMO remains our driving force with almost 79% of the revenue share in Q2, followed by branded and generic with a 16% and API business adding to 5% of the revenue.

items.statement: Caters to over 1,500 clients including 26 of top 30 Indian pharma companies; long-standing relationships with Indian and MNC pharma.
items.quote: Our company caters to over 1,500 clients both Indian and MNC Pharma companies with whom we have long-standing relations. Today 26 out of top 30 Pharma companies in India are our partners.

items.statement: Cash flow from operations H1 FY25 was Rs 71 crore positive; free cash flow post investments was negative Rs 65 crore; net cash surplus Rs 341 crore including IPO proceeds.
items.quote: Cash flow from operations for H1 September 24 was Rs. 71 crore positive and the free cash flow post investment activities was Rs. (-) 65 crore. The company's long-term rating sort of improved, we got AA Stable from ICRA on long-term basis and the short-term rating continues to be A1+ as in that is from our side.

items.statement: Long-term rating upgraded to AA Stable by ICRA; short-term rating A1+ maintained.
items.quote: The company's long-term rating sort of improved, we got AA Stable from ICRA on long-term basis and the short-term rating continues to be A1+ as in that is from our side.

items.statement: Government MSME compliance deadline 8th January; uncertainty on enforcement; management supports compliance but sees no immediate commercial impact.
items.quote: See in the Indian scenario although the date is till 8 th January, but the government has not confirmed yet how it will behave, so our wish is each and every company of our country should follow the system which is under Indian law and grow

items.statement: Continued API price volatility and muted industry volumes pose risk to revenue and margins; API business EBITDA loss may persist beyond Q4 FY25.
items.quote: Muted demand resulting in lower volume growth. Prices of several key API's including Amoxicillin, Cephalosporins, Paracetamol, Telmisartan etc., continues to fall. As you are aware, our CDMO business is a cost-plus model, so when input costs fall, we experience revenue deflation as well.

items.statement: Ethanol production target for ethanol year Nov 2024-Oct 2025 is around 25 crore litres from cane and maize plus 3 crore litres ENA
items.quote: For the ethanol year, which has begun from 1st of November and will run up to 31st October, we are expecting on the basis of current cane availability estimate around 25-odd crore liter, including the maize, we would be in a position to do. In addition to this, it is around 3 crore liter on account of ENA.

items.statement: PLA project commissioning targeted for October 2026
items.quote: And this plant is on track for commissioning in October 2026. Vivek Saraogi: Yes, October 2026

items.statement: PLA plant expected to reach full capacity utilization within 6 months of commercial production
items.quote: We feel that the goods will be sold the day you start your commercial production. So, capacity utilization sales, our best guess today is 6 months.

items.statement: UP Government announced 50% capex subsidy over seven years, 5% interest subvention, and SGST net reimbursement for PLA project
items.quote: The UP Government has announced a policy for bioplastics for this project, which is a 50% capex subsidy over seven years, a 5% interest subvention, and then SGST net reimbursement.

items.statement: Central Government Cabinet approved Bio E3 policy to promote biomanufacturing including biopolymers
items.quote: In August of 2024 the Central Government Cabinet approved a policy called the Bio E3 policy. The policy is meant to give impetus to biomanufacturing, including biopolymers, in which our project also falls.

items.statement: Net sugar production estimated at 28.3 million tonnes for upcoming season after 3.7 million tonnes diversion; domestic consumption forecast at 29 million tonnes
items.quote: Gross production forecasted for the upcoming season is in the range of 32 million tonnes in our mind, ISMA's view is 33 million tonnes. After accounting for diversion of 3.7 million tonnes, the net sugar production is expected to be 28.3 million tonnes as compared to 32 million tonnes last year.

items.statement: Industry estimates scope for nearly 2 million tonnes sugar exports given current inventory and production estimates
items.quote: So, even if the Government is looking at a 60 lakhs tonnes inventory, there is scope of almost 2 million tonnes exports, which can be announced.

items.statement: Sugar prices at Rs 38.5/kg considered low after Rs 20/quintal cane price increase; industry seeks MSP revision, ethanol price revision, and export permission
items.quote: So, first of all, Rs. 38.50 per kg is not a price after Rs. 20 per quintal increase in cane price. The pricing should be a little higher to our mind.

items.statement: Government lifted all restrictions on sugar diversion for ethanol production; ethanol price revision expected soon
items.quote: Following a brief policy shift in the previous year, that is the election year, the Government has lifted all restrictions on sugar diversion for ethanol production. The industry is also awaiting the announcement of revision of ethanol prices which is expected in the coming days.

items.statement: Received full juice allocation and ~6 crore litres B-Heavy molasses allocation for Q1 of ethanol year
items.value: full juice allocation, ~6 crore litres B-Heavy
items.quote: Entire juice we have received. Vivek Saraogi: B-Heavy we have received almost 6-odd crore liter

items.statement: Distillation capacity can handle 11.5-12 crore quintals cane; current cane availability ~10 crore quintals
items.value: 11.5-12 crore quintals capacity, ~10 crore quintals current
items.quote: Our existing distillation capacity can handle cane of around. 11.5 crore to 12 crore quintal of cane. Currently we are in the region of around 10 crore quintal of cane.

items.statement: No further capex planned for co-generation; current capacity 175 MW
items.quote: So, we have no further capex expansion program in this segment.

items.statement: Power export realization to UP grid at Rs 3.46/unit; average annual realization including open access at Rs 5.82/unit
items.quote: Power which we are exporting to grid, the Uttar Pradesh grid, we are getting realization of around Rs. 3.46 per unit. Plus, open access, so average realization should be on an annual basis Rs. 5.82 per unit.

items.statement: Board announced interim dividend of Rs 3 per share
items.quote: We are pleased to announce that the Board of Directors has announced an interim dividend of Rs. 3 per share.

items.statement: UP Government made electricity free for irrigation in March 2024, benefiting farmers in East UP where company has eight factories
items.quote: The benefits it was very heartening to see that the farmers were able to irrigate without having to think of cost, especially our East UP farmers, where we have eight of our factories.

items.statement: Ethanol production mix for ethanol year: ~9 crore litres from juice, 10-11 crore litres from B-Heavy, 1-1.5 crore litres from C-Heavy, rest from maize
items.value: ~9 crore litres juice, 10-11 crore litres B-Heavy, 1-1.5 crore litres C-Heavy, rest maize
items.quote: Within this 25 crore liter, maybe around 9 crore liter on account of juice and around 10-11 crore liter on B-Heavy, may be 1 -1.5 crore liter C-Heavy and the rest is maize.

items.statement: Cane yield uncertainty due to late planting in 2-3 factories and dependence on winter rains; new varieties still acclimatizing
items.quote: Due to some late planting in 2-3 factories, we might have slightly lower cane availability due to yields having a month less to grow. But having said that, there is a tailwind on the fact that the diversion should be much lower than last year.

items.statement: Sugar Control Act draft has zero impact per management; Government already had powers under Essential Commodities Act
items.quote: So, first of all, the Government always has all powers under the act regarding essential commodities. So, there was just zero impact of that in my mind on anything at all.

items.statement: Management asserts Balrampur's distillation capacity is properly sized for 320-day utilization; competitor's higher ethanol output attributed to lower asset sweating
items.quote: We build our capacity on 320 days capacity utilization. Hence that is the ratio for 320. So, if you want to sweat your assets less that is your options.

items.statement: India ethanol blending reached ~15% in 2024, on track for 20% by 2025; current bid for 18%
items.quote: Ethanol production from cane has played a pivotal role in supporting the Government's blending target. This diversion remains essential as India has reached ~15% in 2024 and is on track to meet 20% by 2025. Right now, the bid is for 18%.

items.statement: UP sugar production expected stable at ~10.8 million tonnes; Maharashtra and Karnataka may see a dip
items.quote: Regionally, UP is expected to remain stable at a production of about 10.8 million tonnes, similar to last year's level. Maharashtra and Karnataka, however, may see a bit of a dip.

items.statement: PLA project subsidies (capital and interest) payable after commercial production commencement; land portion accrues earlier
items.quote: So, you are saying, and I am clarifying that to the best of our understanding anything which is payable will be payable after commercial production except the land portion of the subsidy. It will accrue.

items.statement: PLA offtake depends on enforcement of existing single-use plastic ban; 19 items already banned but enforcement is grey
items.quote: I think the only lacuna here is that the single use plastic ban needs to be enforced properly because though the regulation exists, the enforcement is sometimes grey this is what we want from the Government.

items.statement: Full marketing team already working on PLA product sales ahead of commissioning
items.quote: There is a full team working on marketing already. So, we would not go into more detail. One would hope to sell the day you produce and stabilize also very quickly.

items.statement: No raw sugar produced or sold; raw sugar cannot be sold to customers in India

items.statement: UP Government encouraging more cane diversion to sugar sector; no levy molasses requirement for Gur/Khandsari units yet
items.quote: The effect I am telling you and they are encouraging more diversion towards the sugar sector. So, the Government of UP is interested that sugar industry crushes more cane. And they are working indirectly towards it. On Gur and Khandsari molasses, there is no restriction till now.

items.statement: Next investor call will provide better visibility on cane crushing estimates after plant yield assessment in February
items.quote: Definitely, the next investor call for sure.

items.quote: As a result, overall sales have grown at a modest rate of 4% in the quarter 2 and 5% in H1.

items.statement: Gross profit margin increased YoY and QoQ driven by favourable product mix and lead price movement; EBITDA margin 11.3% in Q2 vs 11.8% YoY due to lower fixed overhead absorption; H1 EBITDA margin 11.4% vs 11.2% YoY
items.quote: If we look at margin, our gross profit margin in the current quarter increased both on year -on-year as well as on quarter -on-quarter basis. items.quote: At Exide, we have recently undertaken an organi sation realignment with a focus on strengthening and consolidating the go -to-market strategy in both B2C and B2B markets. items.statement: Margin drivers: cost excellence project (2 years, savings back-ended), mix improvement (aftermarket robust, motorcycle OEM production up 16% in H1, top 4W OEM capacity expansion 80% with 60% IC engines), profitable exports, debottlenecking
