items.statement: Launched full range of E-Rickshaw parts: motors, controllers, DC/DC converters, tyres
items.quote: We launched several new products targeting the E-Rickshaw segment covering now a full range of motors, controllers, DC/DC converters and other vehicle parts like tyres.

items.statement: EV launched new products Nexus and Eltra City; Eltra City registered 225 km single-charge record
items.quote: Our electric 3-wheeler, Greaves 'Eltra City' is registered in India Book of Records for the longest ride on a single charge by an EV three-wheeler covering 225 kilometers.

items.statement: Signed financing partnerships including Shriram Finance for L5 vehicles
items.quote: We have been developing our financial retail partnerships and we have signed up with multiple financing partners, including Shriram Finance, to enhance nationwide financing options for our L5 vehicles.

items.statement: Mechanic loyalty program has over 8,000 active scanning mechanics monthly
items.quote: Our mechanic loyalty program has now over 8,000 active scanning mechanics on a monthly basis.

items.statement: EV market share in Eastern region at least double the 3% national average; building share in North and West
items.quote: In fact, our market share in the Eastern region is at least double the number you've mentioned. We are actively building our market share and volume trends in the North and Western parts of India as well.

items.statement: Onboarded new business head for EV and mobility (Mr. Ramachandra) as part of retail strategy
items.quote: The new business head for EV and mobility business essentially is part of our overall retail strategy to grow the business.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue Rs 705 crore in Q2; standalone Rs 468 crore; Excel Rs 61 crore
items.quote: During the quarter, we recorded consolidated revenue of Rs. 705 crore while on a standalone basis our revenue reached Rs. 468 crore. Excel recorded revenue of Rs. 61 crore to reach Rs. 124 crore in H1 with double digit EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Electric Mobility revenue Rs 175 crore in Q2, Rs 302 crore in H1
items.quote: Our Electric Mobility division also delivered impressive results, generating Rs. 175 crore in Q2 and Rs. 302 crore in H1.

items.statement: External uncertainties exist but internal focus on profitability and strategic execution continues
items.quote: Despite external uncertainties, our internal focus on profitability and strategic execution continues to drive our success.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 consolidated revenue grew 4% YoY; H1 FY25 grew 13% YoY.
items.quote: We have reported a marginal growth of 4% year-on-year in Q2 of Financial Year '25 and a 13% growth for the first half of Financial Year '25 on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin was 19% in Q2 FY25 vs 21% in Q2 FY24.
items.quote: Our consolidated EBITDA margins for Q2 Financial Year '25 stood at 19% compared to 21% in the corresponding last quarter.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margins reduced both YoY and QoQ due to product mix change and higher operating expenses.
items.quote: On a standalone basis, we have witnessed a reduction in our EBITDA margins both year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Margin pressure driven by softer EV and export demand; subsidiary Quantum Magnetics boosted consolidated margin via a one-time purchase order.
items.quote: The primary factor which has influenced our performance this quarter and the margin reduction in the recent quarters is mainly the change in the product mix coupled with some higher operating expenses related to our ongoing business expansion.

items.statement: Domestic smart metering demand was sluggish in H1 2024 due to lower customer orders.
items.quote: Additionally, Q2 also proved to be sluggish for our domestic smart metering business. It is mainly due to lesser demand from our customers in the first half of 2024.

items.statement: Expect better top-line growth in FY26 vs FY25 with new projects contributing commercial sales and improved margins.
items.quote: My expectation is in terms of growth on the top line, we should expect next year some better growth as compared to this financial year.

items.statement: Quantum Magnetics undergoing customer audit; expects additional orders by end of FY25.
items.quote: We are currently undergoing customer audit and we are anticipating that this will be over soon and we will secure additional orders in this area towards the end of this fiscal year.

items.statement: Quantum Magnetics FY25 revenue minimal; FY26 estimated at Rs 10-20 crore; sustainable margins judged at 15-20%.
items.quote: In FY '26, we can expect, it is still a judgment. It could be one product we may be able to do, maybe 10 crores to 15-20 crores, something like that.

items.statement: Quantum Magnetics sustainable margins judged at 15-20%; Phase-2 backward integration expected to improve margins further.
items.quote: Judgment is about 15% to 20%. But right now, we are having much more fixed costs. Until we reach a breakeven point, we don't make money in this business.

items.statement: Quantum Magnetics Phase-2 capex estimated at Rs 20-25 crore over 6-12 months; Phase-3 initially planned at Rs 200 crore but undecided.
items.quote: We are still deciding at the moment, but approximate number is about 20 to 25 crores is roughly what we are seeing today, but we have still not decided that as yet.

items.statement: Alloys business running slow in FY25; expects significant improvement in FY26 with PSU tender business continuing.
items.quote: My expectation is that it should do much better quite well in the next coming financial year.

items.statement: Alloys scale-up to Rs 100 crore top line may require Rs 10-15 crore capex, could be more.
items.quote: 10 to 15 crore you can say, tentatively what we look at. It could be more also.

items.statement: Smart meter business concentrated in 2-3 key clients; developing own-design modular product to expand customer base.
items.quote: We have multiple clients, but mainly the sale goes for two or three different clients. Mainly that is what we are doing. We are building a product category which will cater to multiple more clients and that we will announce when it is done, we will announce it shortly.

items.statement: Quantum Magnetics Phase-2 implementation expected within 6-12 months; Phase-3 decision after Phase-2 completion.
items.quote: Phase-2 we are making progress. So, it should happen within next, I would say, six months to one year we should implement.

items.statement: H1 FY25 revenue mix: 50% electricity meter, 25% automotive, 12% magnets & alloys, 17% others.
items.quote: First half, I can break it down by application wise. So, application wise, about 50% was electricity meter business, about 25% was automotive, and magnets and alloys were about 12%, and others was about 17%.

items.statement: Alloys used in cobalt-nickel superalloys for high-temp, oil & gas, powder metallurgy, defense applications.
items.quote: We are generally doing Cobalt-nickel alloys, which is used for high temperature application, super alloys, oil and gas, powder metallurgy, defense application, these are the applications.

items.statement: Module business for heavy commercial vehicles: small growth in FY26, significant contribution expected from FY27.
items.quote: I feel that may be the year after next FY '26-'27 could be much, much bigger, just on the module side. FY '25-'26 could be small growth.

items.statement: Chinese EV market protected; no breakthrough supplying Chinese EV makers yet; developing low-cost solutions for future entry.
items.quote: Chinese EV manufacturers. We have a direction that we are working on for future to build very low cost solutions, which could be applicable there, but it is too early to say that

items.statement: EV demand forecasts from European/US customers reduced; customers using existing platforms to absorb volumes.
items.quote: Whatever products we had built, the forecast that they had given us initially got reduced much more. So, what they are doing is that same platform, whatever products we developed, they are trying to use for their other cars, whatever they are developing.

items.statement: EV demand recovery timing uncertain; management believes structural EV growth will resume as cost parity improves.
items.quote: EV companies are going through this period, and they will ultimately reinvent themselves in terms of their cost structure whatever to align with the market, how the market wants, and I believe ultimately they will be successful.

items.statement: Aspiration to reach Rs 500 crore top line; timing depends on 1-2 large breakthroughs across segments.
items.quote: Our next step will be to achieve a top line of 500 crores and then from grew there. But I feel that the potential that we have in all the segments that we are present, the market size or whatever we are catering to is very, very large and we are nothing.

items.statement: Added PSU relationships in alloys via tenders; limited new client additions in EV and metering recently.
items.quote: On the metering and EV, not many. I don't think we have added much, but in the alloy side, we got some business from big PSUs, so on that front we have developed relationships with them.

items.statement: Motor/generator development progressing; stator/rotor subcomponents ready; first project sales slowly increasing.
items.quote: Stator rotor is a part of the motor only, not generator, we have not done anything till now. But motor we are progressing because all the subcomponents we are already doing like stamping, winding, molding and magnet we already have a plan.

items.statement: Project funnel increasing; management wants faster funnel growth to reduce segment concentration risk.
items.quote: No, no, that funnel is increasing only. In fact, the learning for us is that that funnel should be much more bigger, so that we don't get impacted by these segment changes.

items.statement: PSU alloy orders are price-driven L1 tenders; one executed order worth Rs 70-80 lakh, another under execution.
items.quote: I think 70-80 lakhs was the order for the one order that we got, with one PSU. But that business is a, I mean, regularly they are buying. They are going through tendering process and it is all price driven.

items.statement: Expects 20-25% dip in students traveling overseas this year vs ~8 lakh last year
items.quote: We expect this time there will be a dip from 8 lakhs figure to maybe 650,000 or 6 lakhs. There will be a 20%, 25% dip in the number of people traveling is an expectation, considering what is happening as of now.

items.statement: Canada student market down significantly due to visa restrictions and GIC scheme withdrawal
items.quote: Canada market is down. In fact, it's down in a big way, and that is going to definitely impact the students

items.statement: Corporate segment showing quarter-on-quarter improvement and market share gains
items.quote: As far as corporate is concerned, it has been slow growth post COVID, but it is growing. We have seen quarter-on-quarter, things have improved.

items.statement: Leisure travel growing rapidly as overseas travel cheaper than domestic
items.quote: Leisure is something which is growing by leaps and bounds. Everyone is traveling. In fact, the thing is that Indi a is more expensive. traveling within India is more expensive than going overseas

items.statement: Average net yield per transaction ranges 0.5% to 1.5%
items.quote: Average yield goes anywhere from 0.5% to 1% when we talk of net yield. So it can even go to 0.5% to 1%, 1.5%.

items.statement: H1 FY25 PBT of INR4.18 cr surpasses full FY24 PBT of INR4.12 cr
items.quote: We are very happy to say for the first half year, we ended up with a PBT of INR4.18 crores, surpassing our annual PBT of last year of INR4.12 crores.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 gross turnover INR2,151 cr, H1 FY25 INR3,482 cr
items.quote: In Q2, we did INR2,151 crores of turnover. For the half year, it was around INR3,482 crores.

items.statement: Student segment serviced 36,000+ students, 63,000+ remittances, 73% YoY growth
items.quote: Last year, we serviced around 36,000-plus students. We did some 63,000-plus remittances. We have 250-plus consultants who give business to us. And we had a 73% growth year-on-year.

items.statement: Retail segment 53% YoY growth
items.quote: And here also, we have shown around 53% growth year-on- year

items.statement: Forex cards 106% YoY growth
items.quote: Year-on-year, we have grown by 106% in this segment.

items.statement: Outward remittances 637% growth since 2018-19 base, 60-65% of business
items.quote: From a base year, which was in 2018, '19, we have shown 637% growth. So this has been a major success story for us with around 60%, 65% of our business coming from remittances.

items.statement: Opened two new branches in Panjim and Vijayawada in H1 FY25
items.quote: We also opened two branches, one in Panjim and one in Vijayawada.

items.statement: WSFx Global Pay card launch by Christmas with Visa partnership
items.quote: We are very happy to launch our WSFx Global Pa y card. This should be available to public by Christmas. This is one card where we are doing it in association with

items.statement: Received PCI DSS certification for card issuance
items.quote: We got our PCI DSS certification, which is very important as a card issuer.

items.statement: Board approved application for PACB license for trade remittances
items.quote: We are also going to apply for a license, which gives us a kind of a stake in terms of the trade remittance. This is an application which we plan to apply. Board has approved for that.

items.statement: PACB license approval timeline uncertain, could take 3-12 months
items.quote: It's a process. We don't know. see, with RBI, they will do their own scrutiny. It's a process. A lot of steps are involved, maybe anywhere between -- it may take 3 months, 6 months, 9 months, 12 months also.

items.statement: Receivables jump due to seasonal peak volumes, credit cycle 1-2 days
items.quote: See, whenever there is a peak season, there is always a time difference before -- as I said, we handle huge amount of remittances. We handle huge amount of corporate business. So these are all short-term credits which come in.

items.statement: Creditors and advances from customers also high, matching receivables cycle
items.quote: If you see the creditor side, the creditors and advances from customers are also huge. So it is just the cycle which takes that 1 or 2 days, which takes for pr ocessing, it is only that amount

items.statement: 57% of GTO through digital channels
items.quote: We are happy to say that 57% of our GTO is through digital channels and process automation.

items.statement: Student segment market share 10-15% of LRS remittances
items.quote: Last year, if you seriously look at it from an LRS perspective, we command a significant share, maybe around 10% to 12% or around 12% to 15% of the market we would be covering.

items.statement: Stopped wholesale business 3 years ago (30% of revenue), now 2x GTO without it
items.quote: Today -- we stopped wholesale 3 years back, and we are happy to say that today, without wholesale, we have crossed around 2x of our GTO when we look at it from that perspective.

items.statement: Canadian student business impact may continue 6-12 months depending on geopolitics
items.quote: So we do feel that Canadian business will leave an impact on the next 6 months. or it may continue for the next 12 months also depending on the geopolitical situation.

items.statement: Digital channels drive 57% of GTV with scalable model reducing costs
items.quote: We have also kept a tight control on cost, thanks to a highly sca lable digital model where the stress is on digital platforms and process automation

items.statement: Order book ~₹800 crore executable over 8-12 months; customer forecasts used for capacity planning
items.quote: Overall, if I have to just give you a number on order book, it should be about ₹800-odd crores of revenue, worth of order book executable over the next 8 to 12 months. However, we do the customer forecast, which are qu ite accurate. So that's not exactly order book. It is a forecast that we received from custom ers based on which we do our capacity

items.statement: No slowdown in renewable, mining, locomotive, data centers; slight slowdown in industrial low-voltage motors due to price competition
items.quote: We are not seeing any kind of slowdown per se in any of our customer segments. If you look at renewable energy that is growing Mining is growing, locomotive part of the business also is growing. So only it is on the industrial motor side, where you have seen a slight amount of slowdown, purely on account of price.

items.statement: Inventories to reduce through integration synergies; trade payables and receivables stable
items.quote: We should see a reduction from here on. If you see we've kind of just recently bought Bagadia and recently bought Dakshin. So as we integrate the se companies, we shall be reducing the overall working capital at all our facilities, through our synergy process. So going forward, you should see the inventories coming down. Trade payab les more or less remaining stable as well as your trade receivabl

items.statement: Exporting locomotive to North America, renewable to Europe and North America; growth in green energy and transportation investment
items.quote: Coming to the global scenario, we are predominantl y exporting for locomotive business in North America and renewable business in Europe and North America. So there, we continue to see growth as those countries are investing in green energy as well as their transportation networks

items.statement: H2 FY25 volume targets: standalone sheetmetal 25,000 tons; Pitti Industries sheetmetal 6,500 tons; consolidated casting 5,000 tons
items.value: 25,000 tons standalone sheetmetal; 6,500 tons Pitti Industries sheetmetal; 5,000 tons consolidated casting
items.quote: So in H2, we would look to do about 25,000 tons fro m our own standalone basis sheetmetal. And at Pitti Industries sheetmetal volume should be roughly about 6,500 for H2. In terms of casting sales, consolidated casting sales should be about 5,000 tons for H2

items.statement: Low-voltage motor prices at rock bottom; Chinese import competition due to lower raw material costs in China
items.quote: So the prices of those motors continue to remain at rock bottom and therefore, the customer expectation on pricing also remains . We are seeing a lot of import possibilities from China, the raw material prices have kind of fallen off in Chin a, and that typically affects this segment because this is more of a

items.statement: Revised FY25 volume guidance of 110-115 million meters; expects to achieve lower end
items.quote: we are on track at the moment for the guidance, which may result into achieving the lower end of the guidance.

items.statement: Revised EBITDA margin guidance to 15-16% for FY25 due to 150 bps impact from new business investments
items.quote: we have given a revised margin guidance of 15% to 16% because we were impacted in this current H1 to the extent of 150 bps.

items.statement: FY25 capex revised to Rs 413 crores from Rs 165 crores due to strategic acquisitions; funded equally by internal accruals and debt
items.quote: CAPEX estimated for FY25 was originally Rs. 165 crores. However, due to the additional strategic acquisitions and investments, we have revised this CAPEX for FY '25 to Rs. 413 crores.

items.statement: Solar energy projects and zero liquid discharge system implementation deferred to FY26
items.quote: The solar energy projects and zero liquid discharge system will be taken up for implementation in FY '26.

items.statement: Acquired Fluvitex Inc. and Modern Home Textiles in US utility bedding; combined annual revenue potential of US$85 million at full capacity
items.quote: These acquisitions establish our manufacturing footprint in U.S. to 13 million pillows and 1.5 million quilts with a combined annual revenue potential of US$85 million at full capacity.

items.statement: Branded business expected to add US$100 million annually to top line over next three years
items.quote: We expect the contribution from the brands to add almost US$100 million to our top line annually over the next three years.

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA margin 16.03%; impacted by 150 bps from upfront costs for new utility bedding business
items.quote: On account of upfront costs and additional expenses related to human resources, brand promotion and creation of necessary infrastructure for new utility bedding business, there has been an impact of 150 bps on our overall EBITDA.

items.statement: Acquired US facilities expected to operate at similar 16% EBITDA margins; improvement expected as assets are sweated
items.quote: the margins are similar to what we are earning today. So, it will be in the range of, say, around 16% for the acquisitions as well.

items.statement: Fluvitex operating at 50% capacity, Modern Home at 35%; target 75% utilization in FY26
items.quote: So, as far as Fluvitex is concerned, it is operating at 50% capacity, and as far as Modern Home is concerned, because it started this year only, it is operating at 35% capacity. So, this we should be able to ramp up to 75% in FY '26.

items.statement: Indian capacity of 153 million meters; expects full utilization by March 2027 (FY27)
items.quote: we are confident that, say, by FY '27 we should be able to utilize the capacity till March '27.

items.statement: Threshold for Indian expansion at 90-95% utilization (~144-145 million meters); Board to decide after FY26
items.quote: It should be in the range of around 145 million in textiles. You can't reach 153. So, it should be in the range of, say, 144, 145 should be considered in my view depending upon again the product mix.

items.statement: Net debt Rs 1,045 crores (0.48x debt/equity) as of Sep 2024; increased due to acquisition funding and higher working capital; expects normalization by year-end
items.quote: As of 30 th September 2024, our net debt stood at Rs. 1,045 crores with a net debt-to-equity ratio of 0.48x. The debt levels have increased to the funding secured for recent acquisitions in addition to funding the higher working capital requirement of the business.

items.statement: Inventory spike due to Red Sea transit delays (25 extra days), container shortages, pre-poned shipments, and cotton stocking; expects normalization by year-end
items.quote: One is the transit time is increasing to the U.S. because of the Red Sea issue. Second is the availability of the containers at the right moment. The third is because of the volatility and geopolitical uncertainties, we are also trying to pre-pone some of the shipments.

items.statement: 2.5 million meters of shipments deferred to October due to supply chain issues; Q2 volume 27.8M meters vs potential ~30M
items.quote: it was close to around 2.5 million meters.

items.statement: Interest subvention scheme (2%) withdrawn from July 2024; interest cost increased; labor costs rising; cotton prices expected stable with new crop
items.quote: the interest cost which we were getting interest subvention 2% has been withdrawn by the government from July onwards. So, that's why the interest cost has gone up. The labor cost is moving up.

items.statement: Expect stable domestic cotton prices with new crop season; India competitive in cotton but 38% expensive in synthetics vs China
items.quote: With the ongoing new cotton crop season, we expect stable domestic cotton prices, which will support our operation and help manage input costs effectively.

items.statement: Strategic shift to utility, fashion, institutional segments (Version 2.0); targeting premium/branded categories; Wamsutta brand promotion underway
items.quote: We are building on our leadership position by investing in a diversified product portfolio, targeting premium and branded segments and enhancing our omni-channel capabilities.

items.statement: Acquisitions expand customer base without overlap; US utility bedding customers prefer onshore manufacturing near distribution centers
items.quote: These acquisitions not only strengthen our presence across critical U.S. regions including the Midwest and West Coast, but they also expand our customer base without overlapping the existing clientele of our new businesses.

items.statement: China Plus One sourcing benefiting India; China market share declining in OTEXA data; India gaining share with complete value chain
items.quote: we can all realize through the OTEXA data that their market share has reduced dramatically in various products. And plus, the overall environment to deal with China, Chinese supply chain is getting more and more difficult.

items.statement: FTAs with Australia and UAE supporting India's textile growth; government focus on trade enhancement
items.quote: Free trade agreements with key markets such as the Australia and the UAE along with the growing China Plus One sourcing strategy are strengthening India's appeal as a major manufacturing hub.

items.statement: Red Sea crisis adding 25 days transit time; freight costs slightly toned down but supply chain issues persist; sales booked on DDP terms upon US delivery
items.quote: the supply chain transit time is still there due to the Red Sea issue, which has impacted everybody's working capital to the extent of almost 25 days more.

items.statement: Peak debt timing uncertain; aims to reduce debt from internal accruals as revenues ramp in FY26-27; interest rates ~7.5% post subvention withdrawal
items.quote: as we draw in internal accruals, definitely our endeavor will be to reduce our overall debt. Because the interest rate have normalized now to almost like 7.5%.

items.statement: Acquired Fluvitex (US$25M revenue, 16% EBITDA, 50% utilization) and Modern Home Textiles (started this year, 35% utilization); valuation based on assets, business, customer base
items.quote: Fluvitex as a Company is doing close to US$25 million with an EBITDA level of 16%, and MHT has just started this year. So, it is getting up to speed.

items.statement: Open to further organic/inorganic growth in utility bedding; Board will evaluate opportunities with proper returns
items.quote: we are studying the utility bedding business overall, because now we have acquired two facilities, which is one on the Midwest and the second is on the West Coast. So, we are seeing how it will pan out.

items.statement: Added human resources for US manufacturing and marketing; brand promotion expenses recurring; expenses to be absorbed by FY27
items.quote: we had hired human resources to handle the U.S. manufacturing and the marketing as well wherein these revenues also from the acquisition will start coming in FY '26.

items.statement: Geopolitical volatility, Red Sea disruption, container availability, freight costs, US policy uncertainty post-election, inflation, labor costs
items.quote: there are so many uncertainties and volatility in the world. Just now certain question was there about Red Sea, the Houthi agreement happened and there is then this container issue is there, the freight issues are there, the transit time issues are there.

items.statement: Area booked grew 193% YoY to 1,56,335 sq ft in Q2 FY25
items.quote: I'm happy to report that we have witnessed a growth of 193% year-on-year in the area booked, totalling to 1,56,335 square feet.

items.statement: Average price realization was INR 6,500 per sq ft in Q2 FY25, highest this quarter
items.quote: The average price utilization of INR6,500 per square foot of area booked was the highest in this quarter, primarily driven by the majority of bookings coming from our luxury Eldeco Trinity project.

items.statement: Booking value increased 316% YoY to INR 103 crores in Q2 FY25
items.quote: As a result of the higher area booked, and higher per sq. fi. realization, our booking value has increased by 316% compared to Q2 FY24, reaching INR103 crores in the quarter.

items.statement: Handed over 61,000 sq ft in Q2 FY25 vs 38,000 sq ft in Q2 FY24
items.quote: Coming to project delivery, we have successfully handed over about 61,000 square feet of area during the quarter compared to 38,000 square feet in Q2 of last year.

items.statement: Acquired 3.84 acres of land; total land aggregation for township projects now 63 acres
items.quote: In addition to the operational highlights, we have marginally expanded our land bank in the quarter. We acquired an additional 3.84 acres of land on the periphery of our ongoing land aggregation efforts.

items.statement: Revenue potential of new 45-acre project > INR 600 crores, could be closer to INR 800 crores; launch expected early next year
items.quote: The revenue potential of this project should be more than INR600 crores, could be closer to INRS00 crores, but that depends on the final plan which gets approved.

items.statement: Unsold inventory of ~36 lakh sq ft plus INR 800 crores sold undelivered implies ~INR 2,600 crores revenue over next 4-5 years
items.quote: So INR1,800 crores plus INRSOO crores. So that makes it INR2,600 crores. And this all has to be done in the next 4, 5 years.

items.statement: Presales run rate of INR 400+ crores sustainable for next 3-4 years
items.quote: So INR2,500 crores inventory over the next 4-5 years. So I hope that answers your question.

items.statement: Trinity is only luxury project (10-15% of portfolio); rest is upper middle-premium segment
items.quote: Trinity is an outlier in the Eldeco portfolio. That's the only luxury project we have at the moment. And it not that just because we launched our luxury projects, we have pivoted to the luxury segment completely.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin 21.8% due to Imperia Phase 1 recognition (16% margin); weighted average with Phase 2 (45-50%) brings back to 40-45%
items.quote: The consolidated EBITDA for the quarter was INR7.9 crores with an EBITDA margin of 21.8%.

items.statement: Imperia Phase 1 loaded with common costs (club, entrance, parks) causing low 16% margin; Phase 2 margin 45-50%; weighted average 40-45%
items.quote: Now when we designed Phase I, we always knew that Phase I is going to come. So we designed it in such a way that many of the cost items, which are basically common to the whole development are all loaded on to Phase 1.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin slightly lower due to Imperia Phase 1 recognition; will jump when Phase 2 recognized; 4-year weighted average remains 40-45%
items.quote: Slightly lower because the Imperia Phase I is getting recognized. But next year or whenever Imperia 2 gets recognized, you'll see a huge jump.

items.statement: Overall real estate demand slowing (inquiries down to 75-80 from 100 two quarters ago); but Eldeco's product continues selling at decent pace
items.quote: So, on the whole, there are definite signs of slowing down. And I think that is true not only for real estate, that is true for the entire economic scenario in the country

items.statement: Lucknow demand-supply mismatch favors demand for INR 1-1.2 cr ticket size; luxury segment (INR 5,000-10,000/sq ft) may face glut
items.quote: In Lucknow the kind of product that we are in, I don't see any demand-supply mismatch. In fact, there is much more demand than there is supply.

items.statement: Lucknow demand driven by end-users and long-term investors (not short-term flippers); buyers from nearby cities for education/medical facilities
items.quote: It's end-users. It's either end-users or it is what we call long-term investors pro-end-users.

items.statement: Approval timeline improved to 6-9 months (was 12 months); 45-acre project application in ~10 days; launch expected H1 next year
items.quote: It used to take about 12 months and which is down to 9 months probably from the time we are ready for our application.

items.statement: Blended realization going forward ~INR 5,500-6,000/sq ft (plots INR 4,500-5,000; group housing INR 5,500-6,500; Trinity ~INR 9,000)
items.quote: Weighted average over 4 years would be INRS,500 to INR6,000 maybe.

items.statement: 10 lakh sq ft sustenance sales from launched projects; 7-8 lakh sq ft from 3 projects under approval; 20 lakh sq ft from 3 projects under land aggregation
items.quote: We have 10 lakh square feet of sustainment sales from projects which are already launched. And then we have 3 projects which are under active approval, we should get approval quickly. So thats about 7 lakhs-8 lakhs square feet.

items.statement: Projects under approval to launch immediately after RERA approval; no delay in launches
items.quote: Once approvals come, we are done with the initial site preparation, etc. We get the RERA approval. We tend to launch immediately after that.

items.statement: Construction scale-up supported by service agreement with unlisted group company for contractors and backend; not a scale concern
items.quote: there is also a service agreement with the unlisted company and unlisted company, as you probably know, is a company on a bigger scale, and we provide all the support that is required Eldeco Housing & Industries Limited ELDECO November 13, 2024 in terms of contractors and the back

items.statement: No plans for government EPC projects; not an EPC player
items.quote: No. We are not a EPC player.

items.statement: Realization per sq ft up ~10% YoY excluding Trinity
items.quote: Yes, there is about 10% increase per square foot.

items.statement: Unsold inventory timeline may extend by 1-2 quarters due to market slowdown but not beyond; 3-4 year estimate unchanged
