items.quote: quarter on quarter, the EBITDA margins have grown from 22.1% of quarter two of FY24, 22.1% has gone up to 23.6%, and today we are talking 24.9%.

items.statement: Total order book stands at INR1,210 crores as of 30th September 2024, with 76% from geospatial and engineering services.
items.quote: Our total order book as on 30th September 2024 stood at INR1,210 crores, reflecting a robust demand across our core business segments, with geospatial and engineering services contributing to almost 76% of the total order book.

items.statement: Notable new contracts include INR206 crore IoT project and INR60 crore digital monitoring project from Maharashtra, plus INR196 crore extension from Uttar Pradesh.
items.quote: Some of the notable contracts which we have acquired during the quarter include two important contracts from the Maharashtra State Water and Sanitation Mission. The first is an IoT -based project worth INR206 crores, and the second is a digital project monitoring system project valued at INR60 crores. Additionally, we have been awarded an extension of a third -party inspection project by the Uttar

items.statement: Bid pipeline with high winnability estimated at INR400-500 crores, taking total visible pipeline to ~INR1,700 crores.
items.quote: I don't know the exact number, but roughly correct, it is about INR400 crores to INR500 crores. It's in that ballpark.

items.statement: Raised INR235 crores via equity and warrants (INR105 crores received) for organic and inorganic growth; cash surplus of INR172 crores.
items.quote: during the quarter we raised fresh equity and issued warrants worth INR235 crores during the quarter and raised INR105 crores as funds. These funds will be directed towards driving both organic and inorganic growth strategies.

items.statement: Investing in data center design capabilities; team mobilized, market research underway in Singapore and Bangalore; business plan to be presented to board soon.
items.quote: On data center, we have already started mobilizing the team. We have already had a few people. There is already some market research which is going on. We have market research happening at Singapore as well as at Bangalore. And I think we will shortly be coming out with a detailed business plan which we can then present to the board.

items.statement: Working capital cycle reduced to 108 days from 190 days at March 2024 and 237 days at March 2023.
items.quote: On the balance sheet front, we reduced our working capital cycle to 108 days, which is down from 190 days on 31st March 2024 and 237 days on 31st March 2023.

items.statement: Preferential allotment raised INR103 crores cash; operational cash surplus INR68 crores as of 30th September 2024.
items.quote: the total surplus cash, which we have is INR171 crores, of which just the cash, which we have raised because of the preferential allotment is INR103 crores, and the operational cash surplus is INR68 crores.

items.statement: Revenue split ~75% government/India geospatial, 25% international/private; target to reach 50-50 then 75-80% international over time.
items.quote: Today, our revenue split up would be 76-24, 75-25, 76-24, 26 in that range. So 75-25. Let's put it around here. Over a period of time, we are expecting it to go more of an international revenue. So there will be an entry milestone where we'll probably hit 50-50. And over a period of time, we'll build a company to get international revenue of the order of 75 %-80%.

items.statement: Win rate >90% due to 'rifle shooting' approach — bidding only on tenders matching core competency and credentials under QCBS evaluation.
items.quote: after a buckshot approach by throwing 10 stones and see what hits. Instead of that, we have got into a mode of rifle shooting. So we are not bidding for whatever is available there in the market. Let's bid and see what we win. What we have started doing is go after the tenders where we have a serious competency and serious

items.statement: Standalone revenue grew 75% YoY to INR78 crores; geospatial revenue grew from INR35 crores to INR62 crores YoY.
items.quote: If you look at this quarter, the total turnover is almost around INR90 crores, of which the subsidiary, which is Allygrow, if we remove, Ceinsys turnover is INR78 crores, of which geospatial turnover is around INR62 crores. So, from INR35 crores to INR62 crores is a healthy growth as regards specific component of geospatial.

items.statement: Higher tax rate due to INR10.7 crore dividend from JV (taxed ~INR4 crores) not reflected in top line; recurring annually but larger this quarter.
items.quote: the dividend which is received is around INR10.7 crores is also added, but for which there is no top line of that. And that is why you see the tax rate higher in this quarter. Because for that, the dividend received, we have to pay the tax while for the normal accounting, current tax, it is only on the book profit which we are accounting for.

items.statement: Segments reclassified: Geospatial & Engineering Services (76% of order book) and Technology Solutions (24%); both expected to remain substantial.
items.quote: geospatial and engineering services contributing to almost 76% of the total order book, while technology solutions make up the balance 24%.

items.statement: FY25 order inflow target INR12,000 crores across power, non-power, civil, water sectors
items.quote: So this year, we are targeting an order intake of around INR12,000 crores across various sectors, namely power, non-power, civil infrastructure and water sectors

items.statement: Total order backlog INR58,000+ crores; unexecuted order book ex-MDO INR18,402 crores as of 30 Sep 2024
items.quote: And taking the total order backlog to INR58,000 crores or a little over INR58,000 crores. And excluding both MDOs, our unexecuted ord er book stands at INR18,402 crores

items.statement: O&M order backlog up 51% to INR3,326 crores; total order booking INR3,055 crores in H1 FY25
items.quote: With the order backlog which was on O&M, which was INR2,197 crores at the beginning of the year has gone up to INR3,326 crores, almost 51% upside.

items.statement: Power sector opportunity INR86,000 crores (civil/mechanical construction) and INR2.1 lakh crores (BOP EPC) over 4-5 years; 80 GW addition by 2032
items.quote: This translates to a potential opportunity of INR86,000 crores for Power Mech in the civil and mechanical workspace and that too only the construction.

items.statement: INR24,000 crores of bids in pipeline across power, water, non-power; INR3,500 crores expected to firm up in 2-3 months
items.quote: Now on the plate, we have got about INR24,000 crores worth of various opportunities being in bidding stage and also up for submi ssion in the power plant side, in the drinking water schemes and then in various other non-power segment

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin 12.78% vs 12.57% YoY; PAT margin 6.43% vs 5.47% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA margin has gone up from 12.57% in Q2 FY '24 to 12.78% in Q2 FY '25. PAT margin has gone up from 5.47% to 6.43%.

items.statement: Expect 1-1.5% EBITDA margin improvement over 3-4 years from higher O&M and MDO share
items.quote: There is an expectation of 1% to 1.5% growth in EBITDA margin over a period of next 3 to 4 years.

items.statement: Overseas O&M EBITDA margins 17-19%; overseas O&M revenue expected INR235-240 crores FY25
items.quote: And the EBITDA margins are in the range of 17% to 19% in the overseas.

items.statement: INR100 crores regular capex increase FY25; INR690 crores washery capex for Tasra over 2 years
items.quote: Apart from that, we received the washery environmental clearance approval during the month of October 24. So, there is a requirement of INR690 crores overall capex plan for the washery setup for Tasra project , over a period of next 2 years' time, we will incur this INR690 crores overall capex in Power Mech books.

items.statement: MDO mines peak rated capacity 9 MTPA by 2028; Kotre Basantpur first coal Jan-Feb 2025; Tasra washery 3.5 MTPA clearance received
items.quote: So right now, our entire focus perhaps is to bring both of these mines to steady-state operations or peak rated capacity, which is 9 million metric tons per annum, and we expect to achieve this in 2028.

items.statement: Net working capital days increased to 147 in Q2 from 142 in Q1 due to certification delays and Water division receivables
items.quote: net current excluding cash and cash equivalents have increased from 142 days in Q1 to 147 days in Q2 due to delays in certification of the works and delays in realization of receivables mainly from the Water division

items.statement: Gross debt INR611 crores, net debt INR64 crores, debt-equity 0.34x as of 30 Sep 2024
items.quote: The debt levels are in control as on 30th September 2024, the gross debt is around INR611 crores and the net debt stands at INR64 crores. The debt-equity ratio as of 30 September '24 stands at 0.34x.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 revenue mix: Mechanical INR229 cr (+10%), Civil INR395 cr (-20%), O&M INR391 cr (+44%), Mining INR12 cr (new), Electrical INR9 cr (-47%)
items.quote: Mechanical business has contributed INR229 crores against INR148 crores in Q2 FY '24, showing an increase of 10% growth. Civil business, including railway, water distribution contributed to INR395 crores against INR496 crores in Q2 FY '24, a decrease of 20%. O&M revenues are INR391 crores against INR272 crores in corresponding period last year, registering a growth of 44%.

items.statement: Domestic 95%, International 5% in Q2; Power sector 66%, Non-power 34%; Adani ordered 10,920 MW, NTPC 11,580 MW in last year
items.quote: During the quarter 2 FY '25, the distribution between domestic business and international business is 95% and 5%, respectively. Contribution from the power sector remained at 66% and non-power contributed 34%.

items.statement: Power Mech among peers in power sector with 15,000-16,000 labor deployed; BHEL capacity 15,000 MW but annual run-rate 3,200 MW, ramping to 8,000-10,000 MW
items.quote: Perhaps very few organizations have got that capabilities. Therefore, that drives us into the front compared to the others, particularly with the private customers like Adani.

items.statement: FGD orders slow due to Supreme Court ambiguity; NTPC committed to 58,000 MW FGD implementation; Udupi project INR963 cr ongoing
items.quote: It is to some extent, yes, it is slow moving because of the ambiguity attached with the Supreme Court judgment waiting and also some of the recommendations made by some of the government agencies.

items.statement: Project delays from land access, statutory clearances, forest clearance, right-of-way issues; supply chain and working capital management critical
items.quote: We are seeing many of the projects are delayed due to access issues because the land is not fully available. There are other statutory clearances are not taken. Forest clearances are not there. Right of the way is not there.

items.statement: Organization strength up ~10% to meet new business; enhancing civil engineering capability, leadership teams, O&M skill enhancement
items.quote: In fact, the present organization strength both direct and indirect labor has gone up by about 10% to meet the new businesses, which has come not only in the power sector, but also in the O&M and other areas.

items.statement: Overseas O&M revenue INR200 cr FY24, targeting INR235-240 cr FY25; 30-35% CAGR expected over 7-8 years in Middle East, West Africa
items.quote: Last year, we did overseas O&M of around INR200 crores. And this year, we anticipate to do INR235 crores to INR240 crores. So we -- you can expect to see the same trend over the next 7 to 8 years, overseas O&M growing at a rate of 30%, 35% CAGR.

items.statement: Green hydrogen partnerships with electrolyzer manufacturers in advanced stages; targeting SECI tenders for green hydrogen derivatives
items.quote: And apart from this, we are also actively exploring a few opportunities in the green hydrogen space, especially the SECI tenders that have come up for the green h ydrogen derivatives. So this again, we have tied up with a few electrolyzer manufacturers and then we are in advanced stages of forming partnerships with them

items.statement: Steel sector opportunities: ISCO Burnpur INR30,000 cr (4.5 MT), JSPL Oman INR30,000 cr (5 MT), SAIL doubling to 50 MT; INR4,000-5,000 cr construction opportunities
items.quote: And there can be opportunities about nearly INR4,000 crores to INR5,000 crores.

items.statement: H2 FY25 revenue growth ~40% driven by FGD execution, new Mahan/Athena projects, O&M projects from Q1
items.quote: The FGD, we have done around INR52 crores during the Q2 and the remaining are the new orders we received from Mahan and Athena new projects. O&M, we received new projects during the Q1 last year, new orders we received from the various projects.

items.statement: Targets Rs 1,000 crore revenue in 2-3 years with 60-40 domestic-export mix shifting toward 50-50 long term
items.quote: in terms of market and in terms of our business, as we mentioned, I think out of that, 400 to 500 should be from domestic and 500 to 600 should be from the export market which is also private label versus branded. That should be the mix

items.statement: Expects 4-5 crore revenue from Sanand facility in current year, 100 crore peak within 3 years
items.quote: Yes, I think for the current year, we will see probably 4-5 crores coming from this facility and the 100 CR target should be hit. Hopefully, we are expecting it to hit within 3 years' time.

items.statement: Invested 75 crore of 90 crore planned for Sanand Phase 1; 20 crore Phase 2 at Ghatakpukur progressing for completion within FY25
items.quote: On the CAPEX front, the first phase of Sanand-II, Gujarat project being set-up for manufacturing of Protec is nearing completion as per the schedule and the trial run for manufacturing of Dipped Gloves is likely to commence in November 2024. The Company has already invested 75 crores against projected investment of 90 crores.

items.statement: FY26 capex limited to routine 10 crore; no major expansion planned
items.quote: Yes, so as I mentioned, this year itself we are investing around 75 Cr by March 25. And for the next year, as of now, there would be only normal capacity addition we should keep doing. So, normal CAPEX in the range of 10 Cr, which is routine CAPEX we are doing. No specific further expansion is planned as of now.

items.statement: Sanand and Ghatakpukur expansions to add 200-225 crore incremental turnover capacity
items.quote: So it should be, both the units should be giving us around additional turnover of up to 200 to 225 crore turnover in excess of what we are doing now.

items.statement: Sanand trial runs for NBR gloves underway; commercial production expected by end of month; PU gloves line in 1-2 months; helmets by December
items.quote: So, yes, the trials have commenced. So, we within like right now, as we speak, I think this week, next week is when we are doing all this trials. And so hopefully, by the end of the month, we should have successfully set up the infrastructure for the trials and the trials would have been completed and we would be ready for commercial production of NBR gloves.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin 12.24% down from prior year due to branding, consultancy, operating expenses; targets 15% EBITDA margin at scale
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was around 16 crores representing a growth of 3% year-on-year with EBITDA margin at 12.24%. The decline in EBITDA margin was mainly due to higher branding and self-promotion expenses, consultancy and other operating expenses.

items.statement: New Sanand products (gloves, helmets, eyewear) targeted at 10-15% EBITDA margin
items.quote: So, we expect it to be in the range of, see, these are all basically the synthetic glass, which we are planning and helmet we are planning initially. So, we have currently margin in the range of 10% to 15%. So, we target that. So, up to 15%, it should be, Yes.

items.statement: Export demand good except Turkey, Argentina; Europe recovering; US inquiries rising on China+1 shift
items.quote: So, the demand from the export market has been good. Barring some countries like Turkey and Argentina, where they had their own internal issues and not being very importer friendly in those countries, rest of the countries have been good.

items.statement: Domestic demand healthy; growth driven by stricter safety compliance, rising labor costs, MNC standards
items.quote: So, definitely we are seeing most of the sectors in India, in terms of compliances, they are getting better, also because the statutory norms are getting stricter. And I think, in general, because when the wages increases, the cost of labor is higher, you want to ensure that you are keeping your Mallcom ( labors

items.statement: H1 FY25 revenue mix: shoes 42%, hand safety 27-28%, garments 27-28%, helmets ~2% but growing fast
items.quote: So, as of now for the current half year, the shoe remains the leading contributor around 42%, then we have hand safety and garment equally 27%-28%, and rest coming from other products like helmets. Helmets may be 2% as of now, but it is growing fast.

items.statement: Sanand facility revenue mostly hand protection; helmets 10-20% of facility turnover
items.quote: Mostly it would be hand protection. Helmet would be on the, you know, maybe up to 10% to 20% of turnover will come from helmet. But mostly it would be hand protection.

items.statement: Added 15-20 distributors in last 4-5 years; selective criteria include cash-basis terms; targeting underserved markets
items.quote: So, that number specifically, Rishabh, I don't have it ready with me, but if I am not wrong, I think definitely we would have added anywhere between 15 to 20 or maybe more in the last four to five years.

items.statement: Branded vs private label split 40:60 currently; targeting 50:50 in 3-5 years
items.quote: So, the split is very much similar as the export versus domestic because largely, in domestic we are only doing branded and some parts of Southeast Asia and Middle East where we are doing branded. So, I think the ratio is largely 60% of private label and 40% of branded that we are doing.

items.statement: Inventory at 90-110 days range; slightly elevated due to growth and supply chain buffers; expected to normalize
items.quote: In our type of business, we are supposed to keep the inventory in the range of up to 100 days. So, this quarter and half, the inventory is basically in line with the growth also. So, we had 14% growth and there is an increase in inventory.

items.statement: ICRA reaffirmed long-term credit rating at ICRA (A) with stable outlook
items.quote: ICRA, the rating agency has once again reaffirmed the long-term credit rating of the company as ICRA (A) with a stable outlook.

items.statement: Capex funded entirely through internal cash accruals
items.quote: As stated earlier, the entire CAPEX plan to be sourced through internal cash accruals of the company.

items.statement: Open to acquisitions if opportunity arises; no active discussions currently
items.quote: Yes, definitely we are always on the lookout if an opportunity presents, we would definitely like to take a look into it. We are not discussing with anyone actively right now, but Yes, if there is a possibility, we are open to it.

items.statement: Government and BIS actively enforcing certification standards; implementation strengthening for footwear, helmets; new standards for hand protection, hi-vis clothing in progress
items.quote: And in the last four, five years, the government and BIS has been very active in ensuring that certifications are followed and ensuring the cheap, low quality uncertified products are not imported or not manufactured, or the fake and spurious products are taken out of the market or the market study is being done properly.

items.statement: Logistics challenges (Red Sea, container shortages) extend lead times and revenue cycle; sold mostly on FOB basis
items.quote: Yes, so this is almost like regular business for us. There are something or the other which is happening. Earlier it was COVID and then this Red Sea crisis, and there are container shortages in between. Also, because there are very few shipping lines who are servicing worldwide, so it's a very oligopoly kind of market and they control the prices, they control the availability.

items.statement: Advertising, sales promotion, consultancy costs ~2% of sales in H1; percentage expected to decline with revenue growth
items.quote: So, it is for the period, it is in the range of 2% almost. So, how it is happening that there is a consultant cost also in the range of 1%, and apart from that we have, as Rohit mentioned in his address, we are attending a lot of fairs and seminars, both in India, outside India.

items.statement: Launched own D2C e-commerce website; early orders received without marketing; targeting small buyers and direct consumers
items.quote: We have launched our own e-commerce website and this is in a very initial stage. The idea is to, because we saw that there was demand from direct consumers for our product as well, so we thought, okay, why not reach out to them directly? So, that's why this is primarily to cater to the D2C audience.

items.statement: Land in Kolkata: received 27 crore advance from JDA; considering outright sale instead of partnership; deal not finalized
items.quote: So, just look at the notes which we have in the account. So, this year, we have received around 27 Cr as advance from the JDA. And so, what has happened that they have approached us with the proposal for outright sale, which we are still considering and the deal is yet to be finalized.

items.statement: H1 FY25 consolidated revenue Rs 232 crore (+14% YoY), EBITDA Rs 30 crore (+2% YoY), PAT Rs 19 crore (+5% YoY)
items.value: Revenue 232 crore, EBITDA 30 crore, PAT 19 crore
items.quote: For the first half of the Financial Year 2025, the operating revenue grew by around 14% to Rs. 232 crores. EBITDA grew by 2% year-on-year to Rs. 30 crores. EBITDA margin for this period was 13%. The net profit for the period grew by 5% year-on-year to Rs. 19 crores with PAT margin reported at 8.03%.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth guided at mid-single-digit; EBITDA margin improvement of ~100 bps to 18.5-19%
items.quote: on the top line, we would be mid-sin gle-digit kind of growth as far as the overall top line is concerned. But when it comes to the overall margin, we are bullish about at least 100 basis point kind of improvement somewhere between 18.5% to 19%, I mean, a kind of EBITDA, that's the outlook that I would maintain

items.statement: Domestic India growth guidance maintained at 8-9% for FY25
items.quote: On an annualized basis, I foresee -- still I will maintain our overall expectation of close to 8% to 9% kind of growth. So that is something that we are very bull ish about. And H2 will be a lot better than H1

items.statement: US business expects H2 improvement after H1 volume degrowth of 18.7% and 6% price erosion
items.quote: But going forward, we expect that to improve -- so in the second half, we are expecting much better performance as far as the U.S. business is concerned. So that's -- and on the new launches, I think I've already answered.

items.statement: US business annual outlook: flattish to mid-single-digit erosion; H1 saw 15% degrowth
items.quote: annually, we may land at a flattish to a mid-single-digit kind of erosion in the U.S. business.

items.statement: US profitability improved in H1 vs prior year; expects further improvement in H2
items.quote: our profitability is better as compared to last year from the U.S. business, and we expect this trend to even get better in the H2.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement driven by lower API prices, lower US mix, and better product mix in ROW and domestic
items.quote: First is definitely the API prices, as you must have seen all the other pharma companies also. So we also got a benefit of lower API prices that helped us to improve our gross margin.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target: improve by at least 100 bps annually
items.quote: I have always maintained that we will work on improving our EBITDA every year by at least 100 basis points and which is what I'm giving the guidance even for the current financial year.

items.statement: Enzene US CDMO plant order book started; production expected Q4 FY25 to Q1 FY26
items.quote: We've started getting a lot of queries. We've started getting some orders. Of course, furth er details, we'll give you at an appropriate time. But that's how I'll put forward

items.statement: Enzene US plant capex ~INR 450 crore; not capitalizing pre-op expenses
items.quote: So there is a capex layout that we had specified even in the previous call, close to the tune of INR450 crores, and which I think that is what we are maintaining even from -- for now.

items.statement: MedTech and Enzene pre-op expenses revised down to INR 60-70 crore from INR 100 crore
items.quote: So as of now, we don't think we will cross at max INR 60 crores to INR70 crores for both the MedTech and the Enzene U.S. plant.

items.statement: Enzene US CDMO biologics plant production start targeted Q4 FY25 to Q1 FY26
items.quote: We maintain with our expected time lines of Q4 to -- at the most Q1 of next financial year. And we expect -- so our order book has already started. It's already started getting orders basis the progress of the plant.

items.statement: Domestic chronic portfolio outperforming in diabetes and 3 other segments; chronic to grow faster than acute
items.quote: Chronic, our focus has been in diabetes -- in actually 4 such segments. We are actually outperforming in IQVIA. Now I haven't done the calculation of the percentage to chronic, but I can clearly tell you that chronic is growing -- will grow much faster than our grow th in acute owing to 2 reasons: one, the chronic market is growing faster; second, our base is lesser, so we will outperform the mark

items.statement: Trade generic business ~20% of domestic; margins improving on better mix and pricing
items.quote: So it's around 80-20. It's around 20% of our business is trade generic, yes. But even on the trade generic business, we are seeing good improvement in the overall margins. So I think that's a point that I would like to highlight.

items.statement: US back orders reduced from 38% to 2%; inventory rebuilt to win back customers
items.quote: In fact, when we started this year, we were at 38% back orders. Our back orders are now down to 2% in U.S. So what we have done is we have improved the inventory over there, but there were certain contracts where we had lost because we were not able to supply.

items.statement: US market sees 6-7% price erosion for vanilla generics; not chasing unviable pricing
items.quote: U.S. is one perennially price erosion market for vanilla generics kind of portfolio. Like I had said and we are seeing that trend as well, we have seen 6% to 7% kind of price erosion from the U.S. market in terms of pricing.

items.statement: Sacubitril-valsartan approved in US; launch timing dependent on Novartis litigation outcome
items.quote: So we got the approval for sacubitril-valsartan. But as you know that there is a litigation going on with one of the players with Novartis. So we will -- we are just waiting and we will watch how that proceeds. And then accordingly, we will take a call on going ahead with the launch for that particular product.

items.statement: Mirabegron (generic Myrbetriq) launch only post FY26 due to settlement with innovator
items.quote: We are bound by the settlement that we have with the innovator. So others who have launched it has been -- it has been an at-risk launch for them. So we will be launching it only post '26. So that is how -- because we are already bound by the agreement that we have signed with the innovator.

items.statement: US inventory increased deliberately to avoid failure-to-supply penalties (INR 140 crore in FY24)
items.quote: And we see a lot of failure-to-supply penalties in FY '24, which was around INR140 crores. And also, we lost a few of the customers in the U.S. on account of not having adequate inventory.

items.statement: Net cash ~INR 4,250 crore as of Sep 30; cash doubled in last 18 months
items.quote: just to share that we have increased our cash by INR400 crores in this quarter. And the overall cash is around -- net cash is around INR4,250 crores as on 30th September. And in fact, just to add, if you look at last 1, 1.5 years, we've almost doubled our cash position.

items.statement: Non-current investments shifted to NCDs/mutual funds for M&A readiness; all AAA/A+ rated
items.quote: Now since we are looking for a fe w of the M&A opportunities, so we want to have investments which are marketable or tradable, and which we can encash without paying any penalties. So we have started parking a few of our investment in NCDs and mutual fund and not in bank deposits, and that is why you see increase in noncurrent investments

items.statement: M&A strategy: strategic fit, synergy, value creation; IRR hurdle 14-15% vs 12% cost of capital
items.quote: Okay. And our cost of capital is around 12%, so -- and so definitely, we'll not go anything which is lower than the 14% to 15% of IRR. As Vikas said, that all depends upon how strategic it is in terms of our portfolio and also the growth drivers...

items.statement: Domestic volume growth 1.1% in Q2 vs industry 0%; PAN brand growth 12.8% vs market 7.3% MAT
items.quote: According to IQVIA data, our company registered a positive volume growth of 1.1% in a challenging market that witnessed a 0% volume growth in Q2. PAN is growing at 12.8% compared to the market growth of 7.3% on a MAT basis.

items.statement: H1 EBITDA INR 13,615 mn, margin 21.1% vs 17.7% YoY; Net profit INR 12,338 mn, up 36%
items.quote: Key highlights for H1. The total revenue from operations saw a modest growth of 0.6%, but earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization were INR 13,615 million, resulting in an EBITDA margin of 21.1% versus 17.7% in H1 FY '24.

items.statement: Acute market weakness due to COVID base normalization, channel inventory, and zero NLEM price increase
items.quote: One, the COVID base that we have spoken about, when the -- when you see this kind of growth that happens in 1 or 1.5 years, and that happened in the acute side, it takes a while for it to really come back because there is a lot of channel buying that happens during that phase. And that channel buying takes a period of time for it to get normalized.

items.statement: Anti-infectives injectable portfolio low-margin; rationalizing unviable growth opportunities
items.quote: So what I mentioned was that the injectable piece, anyways, if you see the injectable anti-infectives market is a low margin as compared to whether your overall portfolio or whether you compare it to -- even amongst the anti-infectives that's the lowest margin portfolio. So you need a very different cost structure, and there are certain growth opportunities that you have to walk away with, right?

items.statement: Enzene biosimilars: 7 commercialized in India; 5 in global development; denosumab clinical trial completed
items.quote: So far, we have got 7 products to the market, 7 biosimilars, okay? And we are actually -- if you look at for the global markets, we are working on 5 products. But our sense is that at least 2 products to 3 products is something that we will be very clear to -- yes, and that's a long-term play.

items.statement: ROW ex-US/Chile grew ~30% in Q2; focusing on filings, partnerships, out-licensing

Looking ahead, we plan to submit bids worth 1,500 crores with an anticipated financial order book of around 800 to 1,000 crores including international projects.

items.statement: Semiconductor equipment manufacturer entry constitutes 55% of non-auto order book
items.quote: we have also added a customer in semiconductor business. So we have been able to get a good entry into this. This is for a semiconductor equipment manufacturer, and that constitutes about 55% of the non-auto order book.

items.statement: QIP INR 1,200 crores completed October; net debt INR 8,797M Sept 2024; repaying INR 700 crores by March reducing interest ~INR 55 crores annually
items.quote: we have stated that we will be repaying INR 700 crores of debt and the process has already started. By March, we should be able to complete this entire process. Approximately this should reduce our interest cost by about INR55 crores per annum on an annualized basis.

items.statement: Senior hires: Rahul Kale (COO), Madhukar Bhat (CHRO), Sridhar (COO Forging), Anil Patil (CQO), Pattabhiraman Raghuraman (CSSO), Satyanarayan Patel (Head Business Finance)
items.quote: We are also focused on expanding our professional team and have recently roped in multiple members at the senior level. To name a few, Mr. Rahul Kale, who has recently joined us as COO of the company, brings a significant amount of experience and leadershi p expertise with a demonstrated history of more than 20 years in automotive and MNC. Mr. Madhukar Bhat, CHRO, has over 2 decades of experience

items.statement: Revenue grew 10% YoY to INR 7,634M in Q2 FY25; H1 revenue up 11% to INR 15,073M
items.quote: Our revenue from operations rose by 10% to INR7,634 million. We have delivered our highest ever quarterly revenue despite the challenging macro environment in the auto industry in domestic as well as international markets.

items.statement: Net debt INR 8,797M due to higher capex and elevated inventory for festive season build-up
items.quote: our net debt stood at INR 8,797 million as of September 2024, owing to higher capex during the first half and a slightly elevated inventory which is basically to build up for the ongoing festive season.

items.statement: Steel price reduction nominal impact, offset by falling scrap rates
items.quote: Steel is not a big impact. Whatever is the nominal reduction that has happened has already been executed, but it's a very small impact. Vikas Goel: We have a similar offset of this in these scrap rates because that also has been falling. And so largely, we see a nullification of that benefit as of now

items.statement: Monitoring US policy shifts post-election for US plant expansion decisions
items.quote: with the change in government that is due to happen in U.S., we are closely watching what kind of policy shift will happen, which would also help us to take further decisions on this.

items.statement: Par VNB margin of 10.1% in H1FY25 is flat versus H1FY24 and considered sustainable
items.quote: If you look at the margin for first half yearly FY '24 of par margin compared to half yearly FY '25, it is flat. It was 10.3% at '24, and now it 10.1%.

items.statement: Non-par business growth pace to continue; participating business to grow modestly and not decline
items.quote: Our strategy is very clearly that we want to have a modest growth as far as the par growth is concerned. And in non-par, we consider that the pace of growth should continue and shall continue in this manner only.

items.statement: September saw strong business momentum partly due to intermediaries covering up for October festival season
items.quote: Naturally, intermediaries or markets seek an opportunity in which they feel enthusiast, possibly people wanted to cover up for the October month when the season for festivals are there.

items.statement: VNB grew 37.74% YoY to INR 4,551 Crore; VNB margin improved 160 bps to 16.2% driven by business mix shift
items.quote: Net VNB is INR 4,551 Crore for the six months ended September 30th 2024 as compared to INR 3,304 Crore for the six months ended September 30th 2023 registering a growth of 37.74% on Year on Year basis. Further, the net VNB margin is 16.2% for the six months ended September 30th 2024 as compared to 14.6% for the six months ended September 30th 2023 showing improvement by 160 basis points on a Year

items.statement: Non-par share of individual APE surged to 26.31% in H1FY25 from 10.76% in H1FY24, a 203% YoY growth
items.quote: Our Non Par share of Individual APE is 26.31% and Par is 73.69% for six months ended September 30th 2024. As you may recall, for the six-month period ending September 30th, 2023, our Non-Par share of total individual business, based on APE, stood at 10.76%. Since then, our Non-Par APE share has surged from INR 1,575 Crore to INR 4,778 Crore, increasing from 10.76% to 26.31%.

items.statement: Banca and alternate channel new business premium grew 30.7% YoY to INR 1,207.54 Crore; share increased to 4.09% from 3.67%
items.quote: Therefore, for the six months ended September 30th 2024, total New Business Premium collected by Banca and Alternate Channel was INR 1,207.54 Crore which was INR 923.88 Crore for the six months ended September 30th 2023 registering a growth of 30.70% on a Year on Year basis. items.statement: Added 2 major bancassurance partnerships (IDFC First Bank and Canara Bank) in H1FY25; expanding alternate channel via marketing firms and brokers
items.quote: We have added 2 major banks within first 6 months. One being IDFC first and second being Canara, which has started delivering in terms of volume. And at the same time, we have also started leveraging in the form of engaging more with the alternate side that is through marketing firms as well as broker side.

items.statement: Agent count grew 7% YoY to 14.40 lakh; agent market share declined to 47.56% from 49.35%
items.quote: As on September 30th 2024, the total number of agents was 14,39,658 as compared to 13,45,891 as on September 30th 2023. The market share by number of agents as on September 30th, 2024 stands at 47.56% as against 49.35% for September 30th 2023.

Siddhartha Mohanty: Claw back, that is an enabling provision, we are not going

items.statement: Standalone health insurance (SAHI) investment is work in progress; no composite license required; operating within investment regulations
items.quote: See, as far as a stand-alone insurance is concerned, our CEO & MD has already discussed and elaborated upon that. That's a very interesting and exciting sector for us to look at. We are looking for all the opportunities there, and it's a work in progress with great enthusiasm and focus into it.

items.statement: Total premium income grew 13.56% YoY to INR 2,33,671 Crore; individual new business premium grew 17.29% to INR 29,538 Crore
items.quote: For the six months ended September 30th, 2024 we have reported a Total Premium Income of INR 2,33,671 Crore as compared to total premium income of INR 2,05,760 Crore for the six months ending September 30th, 2023 registering a growth of 13.56% on Year on Year basis. The Individual New Business Premium Income for six months ended September 30th, 2024 was INR 29,538 Crore and for the corresponding s

items.statement: Market share by first year premium income rose to 61.07% in H1FY25 from 58.50% in H1FY24; individual share 39.79%, group share 74.77%
items.quote: Our market share by First Year Premium Income for six months ending September 30th 2024 is 61.07% (as per IRDAI data) as compared to 58.50% for the similar period ended September 30th, 2023. Once again, we have reinforced our dominant position in the Indian life insurance market and continue to be the leader in both - Individual as well as Group business segments.

items.statement: Overall expense ratio improved 240 bps YoY to 12.74% in H1FY25
items.quote: For the six months ended September 30th 2024, the overall expense ratio was 12.74% as compared to 15.14% for the first six months of last year. You will observe that there is decrease of 240 basis points on Year on Year basis.

items.statement: Persistency improved on premium basis for 25th and 49th month; on policy basis for 13th, 25th, 49th month; 13th month policy persistency 67.23% vs 66.80%
items.quote: On number of policies basis, the persistency for 13th, 25th, 37th, 49th and 61st month, upto the six months ended September 30th 2024 stands at 67.23%, 59.73%, 54.06%, 53.84% and 48.92%, respectively, as compared to 66.80%, 58.79%, 57.61%, 51.73% and 50.35%, respectively, upto the six months ended September 30th 2023.

items.statement: Annualized RoEV flat at ~11.8%; unwinding rate slightly higher at ~9.5% vs H1FY24
items.quote: Actually, the RoEV of annualized RoEV is similar to what we have reported for half year '24, which is at close to around 11.8%. The unwinding for half year '25 is slightly a notch above the -- what we have reported for half year '24, and it is around 9.5%.

So initially, we were aware and we are aware that in this month, there could be an impact,

items.statement: Digital ANANDA app policies grew 35.6% YoY to 7,23,281; active agents on app grew 32.36%
items.quote: In our digital initiative through the Agent assisted ANANDA app, we have completed 7,23,281 policies through this App during the six months ended September 30th 2024 as compared to 5,33,393 policies for the period ending September 30th 2023 thereby registering a growth of 35.60% on Year on Year basis. There is a growth of 32.36% in number of active agents in ANANDA app for six months ended Septemb

items.statement: Volume growth CAGR of 12-15% over next five years with better margins and improved volumes
items.quote: Historically, our revenues have grown at a CAGR of 9% from Financial Year '20 to '24 and we anticipate continuing this growth trajectory at a CAGR of approximately 12% to 15% with better margin and improved volume over the next five years.

items.statement: FY25 volume target of 185,000-186,000 tons
EBITDA margin guidance of 10-12% for coming years
items.quote: So, on margin front, we have already given our guidance that we are expecting to maintain this current levels of margin of 10% to 12% of EBITDA.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton target of Rs 14-15 for FY25
items.quote: So, we have already given our guidance on this, just before a couple of questions, Kothari also portrayed this that our we are targeting EBITDA per Kg of Rs.14 to Rs.15 and Rs.15 being very close right now, we have been able to achieve Rs.15-plus in this particular quarter, last quarter were close to Rs.14 on an average, it is close to Rs.4.5, but for this Financial Year we are targeting to achiev

items.statement: H2 FY25 EBITDA per ton expected around Rs 15,000
items.quote: You can expect closer to Rs.15,000 per ton basis.

items.statement: Revenue target of Rs 5,000 crore by FY30
items.quote: I can only say that whatever we committed that we will achieve a turnover of 5,000 crore by 2030, we will definitely exceed that, that is we are pretty sure.

items.statement: Strong domestic demand driven by infrastructure spending, real estate, and solar installations
items.quote: Analyzing the broad economic landscape, the demand environment across this sector remains strong. Following the general assembly elections, government spending in infrastructure investment have increased in creating positive momentum.

items.statement: Export demand challenged by high freight rates and Red Sea crisis, expected to persist in H2
items.quote: Now, on the export front, we see that this challenge would continue in the second half also because sea rates are not coming down, they are still very firm and because of that our viability to export goes down and that is the story going to be in the second half as well.

items.statement: HFFR demand strong, capacity utilization at 50% and expected to reach full utilization in 2-3 quarters
items.quote: So, as this product require approvals and approval cycle takes longer time, so by now we are having enough approval to use our 50% capacity and we see that demand is very strong and in next say two quarters by end of this year or maybe 1st Quarter of next Financial Year, our full capacity utilization will come from HFFR.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin 12%, H1 FY25 EBITDA margin 11%
items.quote: EBITDA stood at 68 crore, reflecting a 3% growth year-on-year basis with a margin of 12% on EBITDA basis.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 PAT margin close to 8%, H1 FY25 PAT margin 7%
items.quote: PAT stood at 45 crore, growth of 65% year-on-year with a margin of close to 8% for this particular quarter.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton improved to Rs 15,250 in Q2 from lower Q1 levels due to reduced export mix and freight costs
items.quote: See, if you look at the last quarter, our EBITDA went down compared to the previous quarters and we explained that it was because of higher pricing in export it went down. Now if you look at this quarter, the export share has went down. So, on account of higher sea rate has been mitigated and the local volumes, the margin level has been maintained as projected.

items.statement: H1 FY25 volumes 91,000 tons (11% YoY growth), Q2 FY25 volumes ~45,000 tons (3% YoY growth)
items.quote: In H1, we achieved 91,000 close to volumes and Q2 is close to 45,000.

items.statement: XLPE segment volumes 67,000 tons in H1 FY25, 20% YoY growth
items.quote: So, on a volume front, if you see the numbers of 82,000 last year versus 91,000 this year first half, around 67,000 for this particular year has been contributed specifically the XLPE segment. I'm not talking about detailed wire and cable; I'm just giving you a highlight which is 20% YoY growth as compared to first half last year.

items.statement: Export volumes declined 12-13% in H1 FY25 due to high freight rates and lower polymer prices
items.quote: In half yearly, the export has degrown by almost 12%, 13%. That is mainly on account of two things. One is freight rates are higher, so the export potential comparatively in few of the countries was difficult and second is the margins, average realizatio n have come down marginally due to the reduction of polymer prices

items.statement: Installed capacity 233,400 MT as of September 2024 with 78% utilization
items.quote: As of September 2024, our installed capacity stood at 2,33,400 MT with the capacity utilization of 78% approximately.

items.statement: XLPE capacity expansion line to be added in H1 FY26, Greenfield Bhilad plant in H1 FY26
items.quote: Capacity expansion, last time we discussed that we have already acquired a piece of land. Now on that, the construction is yet to start, but we are adding some capacity for XLPE side which should come in place in the first half of next year.

items.statement: Target to add 25,000 tons XLPE and 15,000 tons HFFR capacity over FY25-FY27
items.quote: On a capacity front, we are targeting to add capacity of 25,000 tons of XLPE from '25 Financial Year to '27 and 15,000 tons of HFFR in these three Financial Years.

items.statement: FY25 capex commitment of Rs 50-60 crore, FY26-27 commitment of Rs 125-150 crore, funded through internal accruals
items.quote: For the next Financial Year, we have planned to add HFFR and XLPE capacity in that plant only for some additional quantities. As far as the outlay is concerned, current year we have already committed close to 50-odd crore, the target is to add another 50 to 60 crore is the commitment, it may not be outlay in the current Financial Year, but the commitment will be there. For the next couple of years

items.statement: Polymer prices expected to remain range-bound, no significant drop unless severe oil/gas price decline
items.quote: Polymer prices, we do not see any significant drop until and unless you see a very severe drop in the oil and gas prices.

items.statement: Revenue per ton bottomed in Q2, no major further reduction expected in H2
items.quote: We expect that what has been average in Q2 will be the bottom. We don't see a major further reduction from here.

items.statement: Export share 22% of revenue and volume in H1 FY25, down from ~25% in FY24
items.quote: In value terms, it was 22%-odd on the exports, volume terms is also close to 22% only.

items.statement: US export approvals progressing: one approval in hand, second expected by end of year, third targeted
items.quote: Yes, we are having one approval in hand, another is in the process. So, we targeted to have three approvals. So, one is already there and another we hope that it takes around six months' time. We have submitted the samples in the month of November itself. So, we expect that another approval should be available by end of the year.

items.statement: XLPE growing faster (18% CAGR last 2 years) vs overall volume growth, HFFR ramping up
items.quote: We have grown at the rate of 18% for the last two years in the specific XLPE segment, while overall you see a volume growth of 16% and 5% for '23-24 respectively.

items.statement: 132 kV XLPE product launch targeted for calendar year 2025, 220 kV to follow after 132 kV commercial acceptance
items.quote: On the XLPE side, the only one product where we were looking for approval and new launch is 132 kV which we already said that it would be happening anytime in 2025.

items.statement: Net debt-free status maintained since Q4 FY24, finance cost reduced 23% YoY to under Rs 5 crore in Q2
items.quote: DDev Plastiks achieved net debt-free status in the last quarter of Financial Year 2024, and it is continuing to maintain this position into this current Financial Year also. We further reduced our finance cost by 23% on a year-on-year basis to less than 5 crore this quarter.

items.statement: US duty structure uncertainty may require recalibration of direct export plans
items.quote: Now, coming to the US market, yes, we are putting our effort, we are already doing the export through proxy for two years, but direct export effort is suffering at the moment due to very high sea rates. That is why it will take a bit of time till the freight rates come to a normal situation and now we have to watch what kind of duty structure we come up. If they put the protection duties, then our

items.statement: Export viability challenged by high sea freight rates and potential US protection duties
items.quote: We see a challenge in the form of the duties coming up on the exports to USA. If that happens, then the cable export and cable compound export both will have a viability issue.

items.statement: No commitment on bonus shares, will deliberate in future
items.quote: far as the bonus share is concerned, we have made a suggestion, we will think about it, we will deliberate on that. There is no commitment, there is no thought process on this at this moment

items.statement: Consolidated revenues grew ~76% YoY to Rs 641 cr in Q2 FY25; H1 FY25 revenue up ~50% YoY to Rs 937 cr
items.quote: Our consolidated revenues grew by around 76% year on year to 641 crores. The EBITDA for the quarter stood at 46 crores, which grew by 18% year on year.

items.statement: EBITDA grew 18% YoY to Rs 46 cr in Q2 FY25; H1 FY25 EBITDA Rs 90 cr with ~10% margin
items.quote: The EBITDA for the quarter stood at 46 crores, which grew by 18% year on year. The net profit stood at 27 crores, which witnessed a 17% growth year on year.

items.statement: AUM grew ~17% since March 31, 2024; fee income up 55% YoY in H1 FY25
items.quote: We achieved AUM growth of around 17% since March 31st, 2024 due to strong and consistent returns generated by the company enhancing investor confidence and increasing the visibility and strength of our brand.

items.statement: Loan book grew Rs 83 cr (20% YoY) in H1 FY25; lending operational profit up 25% YoY
items.quote: This strategic expansion led to an increase in our customer base with the new loan segments resulting in an 83,00,00,000 growth in the loan book compared to H1 FY24, which represents a 20% growth.

items.statement: Agency business includes subscription fees, performance fees, brokerage income, advisory income; brokerage income high due to market churn
items.quote: It includes subscription fees. So, when someone puts in new money, we charge them subscription fee in our global arbitrage fund. There's performance fee, there's brokerage income because we have our own broking companies and there is advisory income.

items.statement: Global arbitrage fund returned ~0.65% per month on average; AUM up ~12% QoQ
items.quote: So, it has performed a couple of bits better than the last quarter in terms of performance, I think it has given the performance of .65, if I'm not mistaken per month on an average.

items.statement: PMS AUM grew from Rs 66 cr (Aug 2023) to Rs 152 cr; fresh inflows Rs 35 cr from foreign fund and Rs 10 cr domestic in H1 FY25; half-year return 13% absolute (~26% annualized)
items.quote: For the portfolio management services or the PMS, we had 6 6 crores in August 23 and now our AUM stands at 152 crores and we've got fresh inflows of 35 crores during the half year from our Foreign Fund and we've got fresh inflows worth about 10 crores from India.

items.statement: New loan segments: small loans to capital market traders and loan against shares for portfolios >Rs 20 lakh; unsecured exposure Rs 5-6 lakh per investor; 250-280 loans disbursed in Q2 FY25 at 18-21% IRR; short-term, expected repayment by Ma
items.quote: We are trying to structure loan against shares in the longer run, but right now we are ok to take an unsecured exposure of 5-6 lakh rupees per investor when he or she has a portfolio of more than ₹20 lakh so this time we have done, I think 250 to 280 loans, we have dispersed in this last quarter and we've been able to earn an IRR of between 18 to 21%.

items.statement: Management expects time correction in markets; FPIs selling (Rs 1 lakh cr in Oct, Rs 22k cr in Nov YTD); AUM growing at ~40% YoY run rate
items.quote: I think time consolidation or time correction will definitely will be in the place. So even though if it doesn't go down to like 20,000 or below but time correction we are anticipating and that is why Nirbhay bhai said that it is a volatile time and we need to be on our edge and we have to manage our portfolio

items.statement: EBITDA margin compressed due to higher treasury turnover; segment-level margins improving in fee and lending income
items.quote: So, in whichever quarter we do larger turnovers in physical trade, the EBITDA margin percentage looks smaller. However, the profits for the quarter have increased, so you don't actually look at EBITDA margin as a function of an o verall sales compared to EBITDA, you should look at it from a segment point of view

items.statement: Management holds guidance of 4% manpower cost as percentage of revenue by exit of FY25
items.quote: we are holding our guidance of 4% on manpower also by exit. That's what we had said.

items.statement: Completed 21 projects across India in Q2 FY25 from internal cash flows without raising long-term debt or equity
items.quote: to complete well within time. T o complete 21 projects across India with different brands and to operationalize them simultaneously gives me immense confidence in our team for the future. It may be noteworthy to note that we executed these projects from internal cash flows without raising long-term debt or

items.statement: MG Motors Windsor EV became highest-selling electric car in first month with long wait times; Landmark at 4.2% market share targeting 5% by year-end
items.quote: JSW MG Motors recently launched the all -new Windsor EV. In its first month of sales, it has already become the highest-selling electric car model in the country and we are already seeing long wait times for this product. Landmark is already at a 4.2% market share for MG as of Q2 and are taking all efforts to re ach our expected target of 5% by the end of the year.

items.statement: BYD Atto-3 has 2-3 month wait time; eMax7 sold out till end of financial year; LOI received for Faridabad outlet
items.quote: The homologated Atto-3 has a 2 to 3 month wait time and the new eMax7, which was launched a month back , is already sold out till the end of the financial year. We have received the LOI to open a new sales outlet in Faridabad, which will be operationalized in the ongoing quarter.

items.statement: Gross margin declined to 13.2% in Q2 FY25 from 14.5% YoY due to inventory control measures forgoing wholesale incentives and new facility ramp-up
items.quote: The gross profit for the quarter is Rs. 167 crore with a 13.2% margin on pro forma revenue as against a gross profit of Rs. 162 crore in Q2 FY '24 with a 14.5% gross margin. The lower gross margin is due to our effort to keep inventory under control where we forgo some wholesale incentive and prevailing discount in the market.

items.statement: New brands currently dragging margins down due to front-loaded costs and low volumes; expect improvement as volumes ramp up
items.quote: The new brands are driving the margins down currently because our volumes have not picked up and the costs have been front loaded.

items.statement: October retail sales grew 45% YoY for Landmark vs 32% industry growth; November showing decent traction in key markets
items.quote: The month of October has been a blockbuster month for the industry with the highest ever retail of 4,84,000 passenger cars, which is approximately 32% higher year-on-year. For us, the month has seen a 45% increase year-on-year as what we have reported in our presentation.

items.statement: Long-term outlook for luxury and premium car segment remains positive with sustained growth anticipated
items.quote: The long-term outlook for the private car industry, especially the luxury and premium car segment, remains positive with sustained growth anticipated.

items.statement: Operational cash flow improved significantly in H1 FY25; momentum expected to continue
items.quote: If you look at the cash flow, most of the things is, the out cash flow is the investing activity, which is the CAPEX of the new outlet. But our operational cash flow has improved a lot. And we see that momentum will continue.

items.statement: Executed 21 projects from internal cash flows without raising long-term debt or equity
items.quote: It may be noteworthy to note that we executed these projects from internal cash flows without raising long-term debt or equity.

items.statement: ASP marginally dropped due to portfolio mix with new mass-market brands (MG, Mahindra, Kia); still ~2.25x industry average
items.quote: Yes, Ritvik, so there has been a marginal drop in the ASP . We are still some maybe 2.25x the industry average.

items.statement: Received LOI for Mercedes-Benz dealerships in Jharkhand and Bihar (Patna); operations expected to start by end of FY25
items.quote: We are in the process of further increasing ou r footprint with Mercedes -Benz as we have received the letter of intent for the states of Jharkhand as well as Bihar with operations expected to start towards the end of the financial year.

items.statement: Vehicle scrappage policy remains voluntary with no compulsory policy yet; state-level incentives vary and are not yet meaningful
items.quote: So, what has happened is that each state has come in with their own benefits. So, let me just first say that there is no compulsory vehicle scrappage policy as yet. It is a voluntary thing which is in place

items.statement: Industry discounts high from OEMs to clear inventory; expected to remain high at least till January due to year-end discounts
items.quote: Now most of the m oney is going out of the OE 's pocket and not the dealer pocket. So , the discounts level are high. I believe they will be high for another quarter or so, not quarter, at least till January, because we have a year -end coming and December, as you know, always comes up with the best of discounts.

items.statement: Creating shared service company to move ~1,400 back-office employees for cost reduction; front-loading of hiring for new outlets impacting employee cost ratio
items.quote: One is that we have made last quarter, we said that we are making a shared service company where all our back-office employees, which were give or take around 1 ,400 people are getting moved right now and where we will be able to kind of, we will have the fungible pool of after sales of support people, which will then reduce the cost because we will not need so many people.

items.statement: Proforma revenue grew 13.2% YoY to Rs 1,268 crore in Q2 FY25; new car proforma sales Rs 1,039 crore, after-sales revenue Rs 229 crore
items.quote: Our total proforma revenue for the quarter stands Rs . 1,268 crore as compared to Rs. 1,120 crore in the same quarter of the previous year with a growth of 13.2% year-on-year.

items.statement: EBITDA at Rs 54.8 crore in Q2 FY25 vs Rs 49.8 crore in Q1 FY25 and Rs 57.1 crore in Q2 FY24
items.quote: In spite of these challenges, we are happy to report EBITDA of Rs. 54.8 crore versus Rs. 49.8 crore in the previous quarter and Rs. 57.1 crore in Q2 FY '24.

items.statement: Paused used car business aggressively buying/selling until new car prices stabilize; temporary pause
items.quote: For the pre -owned car business, we have taken a proactive decision to not be aggressive in buying and selling of our own brand cars till the time the prices of new cars do not stabilize.

items.statement: Mercedes-Benz agreement includes loss protection clause where OEM makes good any losses in sales operations
items.quote: In fact, they are one of the only OEs who are so much fixated on your breakeven point because our agreements basically, Amar, say that in case, God forbid, if we were to make a loss, that loss will be made good by Mercedes-Benz in sales operations.

items.statement: Targets 16-18% revenue CAGR over next 3-5 years
items.quote: Yes, sir, the overall long -term growth t rajectory will be in that range of 16% to 18% revenue growth is what we are targeting and fairly on track

items.statement: Expects better than H1 growth in H2 FY25
items.quote: We are expecting better than the first half growth.

items.statement: Targets 250 cash vans by end of FY25

items.quote: One area we are degrowing is our air supply unit which used to supply to the NASCAR, primarily BMW type of customers because of their global maybe volume reduction in the EV site. items.quote: The demand conditions in urban remained sluggish, while rural is seeing some signs of recovery.

items.quote: Yes. I think if you look at the mid term, I would not like to modify the forecast because I think now that both rural slowly coming back, urban now bottoming out, we don't feel that it will continue to bottom out and there is a bottomless pit so we don't think so.

I think it should be in triple digits this growth rate, and that is what we are targeting.

items.statement: Premium specialty pickup in H2 FY25 to aid EBITDA/MT improvement; driven by Europe and North America; pipeline building well as inflation eases and interest rates reduce
items.quote: So, premium specialties are driven majorly by Europe and North America. Okay? So, the reason why we are saying because we are seeing that the products in pipeline are getting built and customers are engaging pretty well.

items.statement: New products in pipeline: mild surfactants, non-toxic preservatives, emollients and esters for leave-on skincare; launching in coming quarters
items.quote: So, the products, yes, it will be essentially on any new product that we are looking at, we have had our mild surfactants, non-toxic preservatives, and there are some emollients and esters that we are working on in the pipeline which we will be launching shortly

items.statement: D2C brands volume grew 30-50% over last 2-3 years; wallet share improved significantly; but D2C still small fraction of overall market
items.quote: I think I would say it has gone up by about 30% to 50% what we sell, what is the volume we do with that, which tells you in terms of the intensity of what work we do, and what is the sort of action that is happening as well, that is the D2C brands.

items.statement: H1 FY25 India sales: ~50% Tier 1 (global MNCs), balance Tier 2 (regional majors) and Tier 3 (local players)
items.quote: So, basis of that if you see, D2C, our thing is like overall, we are at about, if you look at H1, 50% was the Tier 1 customers, the balance was Tier 2 and Tier 3 customers.

items.statement: In Egypt, global MNCs lost share to local players due to high inflation (100% depreciation, 28-30% interest rates); situation improving but not significantly better
items.quote: In Egypt, one of the major customers, global multinationals lost share to local players because of the highly inflationary situation. So, that situation, because even today, Egypt after having a 100% depreciation , interest rates of 28%, 30%, is still settling down.

items.statement: Incorporated subsidiaries in Europe and Mexico as part of go-to-market strategy to focus on specialty ingredients growth in those regions
items.quote: That is the reason why we have actually incorporated subsidiaries in Europe and in Mexico. So, that is essentially to prepare ourselves in terms of the business development agenda that we have for these locations.

items.statement: Supply chain into Egypt elevated to ~30 days due to Red Sea blockade; improving from ~15 days into current quarter

items.statement: Key risk: geopolitical escalation causing severe supply chain disruption and price volatility; not high raw material prices per se but volatility (prices moving up/down frequently)
items.quote: The risk to these numbers can only be any huge escalation in the geopolitical situation leading to significantly problematic supply chain situation. The prices going up is fine, but when you do not want to see a situation where it becomes so volatile that your price moving up and down, up and down, because that's more of a risk.

items.statement: If raw material prices correct significantly downward, exposure exists but risk management framework provides confidence to manage it
items.quote: The bigger risk isnot only for me, but for even my co-players is that, if you have significant corrections happening downward for the prices, then you have an exposure, and that is where our risk management framework gives us the confidence that even if the prices correct significantly downwards, we have the ability to manage it

items.quote: There is no structural change that is happening, okay? One thing that even you would know is that people are trying to access more through the quick commerce channels. But for us that doesn't matter because what we do is we serve all the customers

items.statement: Startup funding slowdown continues; focus shifted to corporate segment

items.statement: Revenue expected to gradually gain traction over next few quarters

items.statement: Operating costs expected to remain stable from current levels
items.quote: We expect our operating cost to be stable from hereon.

items.statement: Targeting EBITDA profitability at earliest but will take several quarters
items.quote: We are working towards becoming EBITDA profitable at the earliest. It will take some quarters for said profitability to materialize.

items.statement: Revenue mix shifted to 90% corporate and 9% startup in Q2 FY25

items.quote: Our team size is about 49 including employees, interns, consultants as compared to 63 in Q1 FY '25.

items.quote: The fair value of our investment in portfolio companies stood approximately INR572.8 million as of 30th September 2024, as compared to INR533.9 million on 30th September 2023.

items.quote: And now we are operating at a significant revenue scale or exploring other options, including strategic M&A.

items.quote: The Board had approved cancellation of proposal of incorporation of a subsidiary company in Mumbai Maharashtra, which was proposed to be i nvolved in the age- tech industry

items.quote: We have not come to that level of regularity yet, okay? So we have to watch for a few quarters. That's the reason we said that, that is something we're looking at 2, 3 quarters down.

items.statement: Short-term revenue CAGR guidance of 15-20% assuming no major external shocks

items.statement: Strong H1 FY25 revenue growth of 19.4% year-over-year despite challenging demand environment

items.quote: In our glassware segment, which includes borosilicate microwavables, serving ware, glass tumblers, lunchbox and storage solutions, we saw an exceptional year-over-year growth of 32.6% with revenues reaching INR 116.7 crores in H1 FY '25 compared to INR 88 crores in H1 FY '24.

items.statement: ESOP cost from 2015 policy vesting completes in next 2 quarters and Q1 FY26; new policy will have similar cost trend; no incremental impact beyond what's baked in

items.statement: Revenue target of INR 900-1,000 crores in next 3-3.5 years reaffirmed

items.quote: SSSG, H1 is trending lower. This is for all mature stores which is more than 18 months. Again, it's about in lower, negative, it's a negative zone in H1.

items.statement: Export share 33% of revenue in Q2 (up from 12% last year); expect >25% going forward
items.quote: Definitely yes, it has been significantly high 33% and see the order book is quite heavy on the side of export but it will be always more than 25% what we believe for the coming quarter.

Definitely it helps in a way from the way the welded pipe which we used to come in the country will be coming significantly less.

items.quote: the oil and gas companies just like Aramco and others approval is under process. Arun Kothari: Hopefully every month or every quarter we are getting some of the approval from the some of the new company. So, I believe that most of the oil and gas companies, or particular what segment we

items.statement: Oil & gas currently <10% of mix; target double-digit share in coming year
items.quote: We don't give any specific sector wise data but again it's not currently double digit for oil and gas. But we believe going forward with many of the approvals coming in and again supplying to the larger pla yer in the country also we should be touching double digit in coming year to come.

items.statement: Appointed Neelanjan as Chief Strategy Officer and Mark Light as Business Development Officer (Energy)
items.quote: In our journey to become a global leader, we have appointed Mr. Neelanjan as our Chief Strategy Officer and Mr. Mark Light as our Business Development Officer (Energy).

items.statement: Seamless revenue up 21% YoY in Q2 & H1; welded revenue down 2% in Q2 but up 13% in H1; both volumes >30% in H1
items.quote: Sales from seamless pipes showed strong growth increasing by 21% year-on-year for both the quarter and the first half of FY25 . Welded pipe however show ed a slight dip of the 2% in Q2 though for H1FY25 sales grew by 13% . In terms of volume growth remained robust and with both seamless and welded pipe s achieving over 30% growth in the first half .

items.statement: Domestic stainless pipe market FY24: 3.2 lakh tons (seamless 1.1L, welded 2.1L); market growth 6-8% expected
items.quote: The domestic market size has expanded from 2.2 lakh metric tons per annum to 3.2 lakh metric tons per annum from FY20-24 and we have increased our market share from 3.7% in FY20 to 6.2% in FY24.

items.statement: Domestic stainless pipe market FY24: 3.2 lakh tons (seamless 1.1L, welded 2.1L); market growth 6-8% expected
items.quote: But we believe going forward there should be 6% to 8% growth in the market on an overall basis.

items.statement: Ocean freight costs rose sharply in Q2, compressing margins; expected to normalize
items.quote: But what has happened is right, there had been good export growth but in the last quarter there was a hefty increase on the side of ocean freights being paid on while you export the goods to various part of the world. That has rose by quite significant number. So, that is slightly soft en the margins. But I think we believe it should be maintainable going forward. Those trades should also subsidiz

items.statement: Aim to produce in excess of 20,000 metric tons of bromine for FY25 including captive use
items.quote: We aim to produce in excess of 20,000 metric tons for the year of bromine, including requirements for our own use.

items.statement: Expect more than 1 million ton quarterly run rate for industrial salt in coming quarters
items.quote: H2 is generally better for our business, and we expect more than a million ton volume run rate in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Target bromine production of 20,000-25,000 tons for FY26
items.quote: Sir, next year are likely to be at around 20,000, 25,000 tons.

items.statement: Capex of INR 50-75 crores expected over next 6 months till March 2025 for existing initiatives including Oren Hydrocarbons and derivatives
items.quote: I think our initial year after this outflow of investment on the equity side, for the next 6 months, we don't see too much of capex apart from what we're doing with Oren, I think maybe I would broadly put with existing initiatives, probably we will probably be between INR50 crores to INR75 crores over the next 6 months at the very most.

items.statement: No significant capex anticipated in core bromine, salt and SOP businesses even after March 2025
items.quote: I think at the moment, we've already put in money into both the derivatives as well as the Oren Hydrocarbons acquisition and our main plant in Rann of Kutch. I think we don't anticipate too much capex in these businesses even after March '25.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 standalone EBITDA margin at 36% with EBITDA of INR 898 million
items.quote: EBITDA for the company stood at around INR898 million for this quarter, Q2, with a margin of 36% and net profit stood at around INR219 million.

items.statement: H1 FY25 standalone EBITDA margin at 37% with EBITDA of INR 1,747 million
items.quote: EBITDA for the company stood at around INR1,747 million for the 6 months period with a margin at 37%.

items.statement: Bromine demand recovering in domestic market while export market remains soft; China stimulus expected to gradually improve demand
items.quote: It has been somewhat of a mixed quarter for the company as we have seen some broad recovery on the demand side, primarily from the domestic market, whereas demand from export market remains a bit soft.
