items.statement: Two Oren Hydrocarbons plants expected to be fully operational within next few weeks with meaningful contributions from Q4 FY25
items.quote: We expect two plants to be fully operational within the next few weeks with meaningful business contributions than anticipated from the Q4 of this financial year.

items.statement: SOP trials encouraging with second grade production underway; expect meaningful contributions next year
items.quote: On the SOP side, we continue to see encouraging results in our trials, and we have also taken steps to produce a second grade of Sulphate of Potash, which we're seeing encouraging inquiries from both global and domestic markets. At present, there's a work-in-progress, and we expect meaningful contributions in the next year.

items.statement: New domestic bromine capacity expansions expected in 2-3 years; company differentiating through value-enhanced chemistries and derivatives
items.quote: While the local other players expand, I think part of our derisking and diversification into further value-enhanced chemistries and products, I think this was envisaged a couple of years ago, which is what we have implemented. So I think I credit the management team and also our on-the-ground site team for implementing these projects. And I think this will probably add to our strength and distingu

items.statement: SiC wafer fab project plan submitted to government for incentives; return ratios dependent on approval outcome
items.quote: We have submitted it to government and waiting for the necessary approvals. So a lot of that will depend on what quantum of the government incentives, et cetera, we get, which will have an impact on the return ratios. So we will definitely answer the return ratios once we get the clarity on the approval process.

items.statement: Investing GBP 15 million (GBP 10 million primary, GBP 5 million secondary) for 21.33% stake in Clas-SIC Wafer Fab Limited UK
items.quote: Our company will be investing to the tune of GBP 15 million for a 21.33% equity share capital with a primary subscription of GBP 10 million and secondary purchase of GBP 5 million.

items.statement: Investing nearly USD 12 million in Series A for 21% stake in Offgrid Energy Labs Inc. Delaware US
items.quote: We will invest nearly USD12 million in series A fund for the subscription of 21% stake.

items.statement: Oren Hydrocarbons acquisition completed with NCLT order in July 2024; refurbishing plants for specialty mud chemicals and CBF products
items.quote: After receiving the NCLT order in the month of July '24, our team has been actively working on refurbishments and renovations at various production sites of the company. We expect two plants to be fully operational within the next few weeks with meaningful business contributions than anticipated from the Q4 of this financial year.

items.statement: Mr. Kannan joined as Executive Director responsible for all initiatives including parent company and subsidiaries
items.quote: Mr. Kannan has joined as Executive Director in Archean Chemical Industries, which is a parent company for all the subsidiaries that we talked about today. So the broad mandate for him is leading and being responsible for all these initiatives, including the primary company, Archean Chemical Industries.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 salt sales volume 792,000 tons vs 976,000 tons previous year; bromine sales ~4,800 tons; SOP sales ~27 tons
items.quote: For this quarter, Q2, the sale of salt is around 792,000 versus 976 in the previous year's quarter. And with respect to bromine, it's on 4,800 plus. Krishan Parwani: 4,800. Okay. SOP is nil? Raghunathan: SOP is at around

items.statement: Salt logistics mix: 92% FOB, 5-8% CIF basis
items.quote: CIF is 5% to 8%, and almost 92% really on FOB basis.

items.statement: Cyclone Asna caused loss of 472,000 metric tons of industrial salt worth INR 40.18 crores; insurance claim initiated
items.quote: We reported an exceptional item due to the impact of Asna cyclone in Gujarat that occurred in the month of August and in the beginning of September. So almost it prevailed for more than a week or so, which resulted in a loss of 472,000 metric tons of Industrial Salt, which amounts to around INR40.18 crores. We have initiated a necessary claim process with respective insurance companies.

items.statement: Flame retardant project delayed but not derailed; measured approach prioritizing return on capital for current initiatives first
items.quote: I think it's a commercial call. It's not derailed for sure. I think it's delayed, as I mentioned, I think on the previous calls as well. It's easy to always put capital, but I think we want to take a measured approach. As someone else asked earlier on the call, it's about return on capital invested. So we already have a couple of initiatives going on. We would like to first deliver on these.

items.statement: Urban discretionary demand slowdown due to inflation and cost of living; temporary disruptions in Karnataka and Delhi impacted Q2 revenues
items.quote: we are witnessing a temporary slowdown in consumer demand across discretionary categories including alcoholic beverages, particularly within urban India, which does represent more than 90% of Sula's customer base.

items.statement: Karnataka excise policy changes caused retailer hesitancy; situation mostly stabilized with sales recovery underway
items.quote: in Karnataka, retailers were initially hesitant to stock up due to recent changes in the exercise policy, which introduced pricing uncertainty. This situation has since mostly stabilized after clarity came in from the state authorities, and we have started seeing already a recovery in sales there.

items.statement: Delhi excise portal offline for most of second half of September during migration to in-house management, impacting shipments
items.quote: In Delhi, the excise portal was offline for much of the second half of September as they migrated from external management to in-house management of the portal, and which impacted sales during this transition. We were, in fact, unable to ship goods for most of the second half of September in this very important market.

items.statement: Elite and premium portfolio grew 7% YoY with double-digit gains in iconic brands; economy and popular down 18%
items.quote: Our elite and premium portfolio performed well given the current market backdrop, recording 7% growth , with double-digit gains across some of our iconic elite brands such as The Source, which I would like to say has been a particular success for us, RASA and Dindori.

items.statement: Share of elite and premium in own brands improved 500 bps to all-time high of 78.5% in Q2
items.quote: Share of elite and premium in our own brands improved 500 basis points, reaching an all-time high of 78.5% in quarter two.

items.statement: Revenue excluding Maharashtra and Karnataka grew 6% YoY, powered by Telangana with 59% growth and high double-digit growth in Himachal, MP, Chandigarh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal
items.quote: Revenue excluding our top two states of Maharashtra and Karnataka grew 6% Y-o-Y. This growth was powered chiefly by Telangana, with Himachal, MP, Chandigarh, Uttarakhand, and West Bengal, among others, also seeing high double -digit growth.

items.statement: Telangana, the third-largest market, grew more than 50% in Q2
items.quote: Telangana, our third -largest market, particularly stood out as a bright spot with more than 50% growth in Q2.

items.statement: Shifted to third-party sales model for economy and popular brands in Maharashtra starting Mumbai and Pune in Q1; rolling out to rest of Maharashtra with plan to move entire popular and economy to third party by Q1 FY26
items.quote: we decided to shift to a third -party sales model for our economy and popular brands in Maharashtra, starting with Mumbai and Pune in Q1. The early results of this have been extremely encouraging, and we have started rolling out this strategy in the rest of Maharashtra, with a plan to move our entire popular and economy to the third party by Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: Wine tourism faced challenges from road infrastructure deterioration and surge in outbound travel to Thailand and Vietnam; inbound travel not keeping pace
items.quote: Our wine tourism business also faced challenges during the quarter due to deterioration in road infrastructure and also a surge in outbound travel. A lot of our people have been traveling to foreign countries, particularly I would highlight Thailand and Vietnam with their very easy travel policies, and with extremely easy and cheap flights available today from almost every Indian city.

items.statement: Wine tourism occupancy improved to 74% vs 66% last year; spend per head up 9% YoY offsetting lower footfalls
items.quote: On the wine tourism front, we saw moderate growth in quarter two, supported by improved occupancy of 74% versus 66% last year, and increase in spend per head by 9% Y-o-Y, which helped to offset the impact of lower footfalls.

items.statement: Pan-India tastings up 6% in Q2 to over 50,000, an all-time high for Q2
items.quote: And pan-India tastings are up 6% in Q2 to over 50,000, so an all-time high for Q2.

items.statement: New expanded Dindori Tasting Room and Bottle Shop at erstwhile ND Wines now open; strategically located <50 km from Gujarat border
items.quote: our new expanded Dindori Tasting Room and Bottle Shop is now open to visitors at the erstwhile ND Wines. This facility, as some of you might be aware, is strategically located less than 50 kilometers from the Gujarat border.

items.statement: Expansion of wine tourism facilities at Domaine Sula near Bangalore slated to complete in Q3 with new tasting room and vineyard view
items.quote: the ongoing expansion of our wine tourism facilities at Domaine Sula near Bangalore is slated to complete in Q3. So, we have a beautiful new tasting room there with a beautiful vineyard view, a bit akin to our facility in Nashik, which was a bit lacking until now.

items.statement: 30-key resort coming up near York Winery in Nashik in FY26, expanding total room capacity by 30% from 104 to 134 keys with convention facilities
items.quote: next year in FY '26 we have the 30 -key resort coming up near our York Winery in Nashik, which will expand our total room capacity by 30% from 104 keys to 134 keys. And as I have mentioned previously, this will also have convention facilities for the first time on a much larger scale than what we have been able to offer so far.

items.statement: Expect wine tourism expansions and SulaFest to boost H2 performance; targeting return to healthy growth from Q4, from December onwards
items.quote: we expect these expansions, along with the upcoming SulaFest, to provide a boost to our wine tourism business and contribute positively to H2 performance. And in particular, we are looking to return to healthy growth from Q4, in fact, from December onwards.

items.statement: Reopening Andhra Pradesh after 5-year hiatus with progressive excise policy; targeting first shipment in Q3
items.quote: We are really concentrating hard on getting it out there within Q3 itself. So, at least it will give us a nice little boost in Q3 itself, because we will be going into a totally empty state in terms of wine.

items.statement: Introducing four new brands in CSD (Canteen Stores Department) including Dindori Reserve Shiraz, Source Grenache Rose, Sula Vineyards Riesling, RASA Syrah; almost doubling brands in CSD
items.quote: We will be seeing the introduction of four more brands in CSD. CSD, I should point out, has shown very strong growth over the last 18 months or so. And we will be introducing four new brands, including our Dindori Reserve Shiraz and also our Source Grenach e Rose, our Sula Vineyards Riesling, and our RASA Syrah.

items.statement: Resuming shipments to BSF after eight months; BSF performed well in H1 FY24
items.quote: We are also resuming shipments to BSF after eight months. And BSF did incredibly well for us in the first half of FY '24. So, it was a shame that due to some administrative issues we were not able to be present. We are now getting back in there, and we will get the benefit of that in H2.

items.statement: Gross margins at 74%, up 78 bps YoY supported by higher elite and premium share; gross profit flat at Rs 104 crores
items.quote: Our gross margins stood at 74%, 78 basis points better versus last year, supported by higher share of elite and premium. Gross profit stood flat at Rs. 104 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA decreased 24% to Rs 34 crores due to increased market spending impacting profitability amid muted sales growth
items.quote: Continuing on, our EBITDA for quarter two decreased by 24% to Rs. 34 crores as increased market spending impacted profitability in a period of muted sales growth.

items.statement: Total borrowings grew from Rs 260 crores to Rs 330 crores YoY due to higher receivables; Telangana's higher DSO primary factor but collections improved 2.5x QoQ
items.quote: Total borrowings grew from Rs. 260 crores in September '23 to Rs. 330 crores as of September 2024. The higher utilization of working capital was driven by an increase in receivables. A significant rise in revenue contribution from Telangana, which has a relatively higher DSO, was the primary factor behind the increase in receivables. However, the collection situation in Telangana has significantly

items.statement: Net debt-to-EBITDA comfortable at 1.8x, well below internal benchmark of 2x
items.quote: While borrowing has increased, our net debt -to-EBITDA continues to be comfortable at 1.8x, well below our own benchmark of 2x.

items.statement: WIPS receivable was Rs 73 crores as of 1 April 2024; Rs 20 crores accrued in H1, Rs 10 crores from unwinding; received Rs 10 crores in July and Rs 22 crores in October, bringing balance to Rs 73 crores; expect to realize balance in FY25
items.quote: Our outstanding WIPS balance, which is the Wine Industry Promotion Scheme, as of 1 April, '24, was Rs. 73 crores, with Rs. 20 crores being accrued during H1 and Rs. 10 crores led by the unwinding of the previous accumulated WIPS. We subsequently received Rs. 10 crores in July 2024, taking the WIPS receivable in our balance sheet to Rs. 94 crores. We are happy to report that we received a further p

items.statement: COO Karan Vasani resigned for personal reasons, moving on in December after 11 years; smooth handover underway
items.quote: Karan Vasani, our COO, has resigned for personal reasons and will be moving on in December. I would like to take this opportunity to express my sincere thanks to Karan. We greatly appreciate all his contributions to the success of the company over the last 11 years, first as Chief Winemaker, and then for the past year as COO.

items.statement: Anant Iyer joins Board as Independent Director; currently Director General of CIABC with 40 years alcobev experience
items.quote: I would like to warmly welcome Anant Iyer who joins our Board as an Independent Director. Anant is currently the Director General of CIABC or the Confederation of Indian Alcoholic Beverage Companies . And he comes with a vast experience of 40 years working in senior roles in alcobev companies and will definitely be adding a lot of value to the Sula Board.

items.statement: FTA with Australia signed with reductions on wines above certain price threshold; negotiations ongoing; government cognizant of wine as sunrise agro-based farmer-friendly industry
items.quote: an early FTA was signed with Australia in which there was some reduction on wines above a certain price threshold. FTA negotiations are still going on. I mean, Australia is probably the most likely to have the second comprehensive FTA signed fairly soon. We very much have a seat at the table, and we are watching it closely.

items.statement: On wines above $15 CIF, tax may come down to 25%; above $5 CIF to 50%; below $5 CIF remains at 150%
items.quote: On wines now above $15, I think tax is going to come down as low as 25%. On wines above $5, please note, these are CIF p rices, tax is going to come down as low as 50%. But for wines below that right now, below $5 CIF, it's 150%. It remains at the 150% threshold.

items.statement: Unsustainable discounting by competitors in Maharashtra impacting net sales; market lacks depth to withstand; hope for return to normalcy
items.quote: there have also been, I would say, some kind of unsustainable discounting by some of our competitors. Unfortunately, the market does not have the kind of depth to allow it to easily withstand this. So, there is a fair amount of wine that has been produced, which is unfortunately being discounted in the market. That has very much impacted, because you see the sales in Maharashtra, we report them ne

items.statement: Successfully transitioned from SAP ECC6 to cloud-based S/4 HANA via brownfield implementation in 5 months, well below standard time; transaction processing nearly 40% faster with real-time analytics
items.quote: We successfully transitioned from SAP ECC6 to cloud-based S/4 HANA through a brownfield implementation, which was completed in a d five months well lower than standard implementation time. This upgrade will enhance operational efficiency, enabling transaction processing to be nearly 40% faster and improving access to real -time analytics, positioning us to make more data-driven decisions with grea

items.statement: SulaFest returning in February 2025 after 5 years as wine and beer festival (no spirits); likely biennial event
items.quote: We come back after five long years due to overwhelming popular demand. This was a festival that was much loved and had grown into being one of India's iconic festivals. We had to shut down due to COVID. And for various reasons, after that, we decided not to restart. But now we do believe the time is right. It will be coming back in a slightly different avatar. I should point out that SulaFest 2020

items.statement: Target revenue less service cost margin of ~20% by summer next year (next three quarters)
items.quote: So by summer of next year, we should be looking at this number getting to about 20%.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin on revenue less service cost is ~15% this quarter
items.quote: This INR13.6 crores of adjusted EBITDA margin is on INR93 crores of revenue less service cost, which is almost a 15% margin.

items.statement: Long-term hotel & packages gross margin expected to settle at 9-10%
items.quote: Over the next three years, given that the business would be largely focused on corporate and mice, I would expect this number to be range bound between nin e and 10

items.statement: Onboarded 29 new corporate clients with INR1.2B annual billing potential
items.quote: In the second quarter of FY25, we onboarded 29 new corporate clients, collectively adding an annual billing potential of INR1.2 billion.

items.statement: Acquired Globe Travels for INR1.28B cash; adds 360 corporate clients and INR470M adjusted revenue at >30% EBITDA margin
items.quote: On September 11th, 2024, we completed the acquisition of Globe for INR1.28 billion in cash.

items.statement: Identified INR60M annual synergies from Globe acquisition; expect to realize slightly ahead of target
items.quote: As part of the combination of Yatra and Globe, we had identified synergies of approximately INR60 million per year. And as we move forward, we expect that we should be able to realize synergies slightly ahead of this initial target.

items.statement: Corporate air volumes growing healthy double-digits; B2C air volumes stabilized and gradually increasing
items.quote: We continue to see healthy double-digit plus kind of volume growth on the air ticketing side on the corporate front. On the B2C front as well, as I mentioned, we've reached a point where we've been able to stabilize the volumes and the last couple of months we've started seeing a

items.statement: B2B now ~60% of gross bookings; hotels & packages B2B ~65%; air ticketing B2B ~50%
items.quote: So in terms of gross bookings, now almost 60% of our gross bookings are coming from the corporate travel business, from the B2B business.

items.statement: Investing in talent for mid-market, MICE, Visa, expense management; annual appraisal cycle partially impacted Q2
items.quote: Our personal expenses, excluding share-based payment, increased by 20% Y-o-Y as we continue to invest in talent to build out our mid-market, MICE, Visa, expense management, and other businesses. This also includes a partial impact of our annual appraisal cycle.

items.statement: Integrated NDC (New Distribution Capability) for richer booking experience and special fares
items.quote: We've become one of the first travel management companies in India to integrate the new distribution capabilities that the airlines are offering.

items.statement: Globe adds 360 non-overlapping mid-market corporate clients (INR2-5Cr spend) vs Yatra's large corporates (INR25Cr+ avg)
items.quote: Globe's customers will typically be between the INR2 crores to the INR5 crores kind of annual corporate travel spend space, whereas Yatra's customers will be much more closer to like on average about INR25-plus crores.

items.statement: Other current assets up INR57Cr due to vendor advances for MICE business; dissolve as trips complete
items.quote: These are advances given to vendors for our MICE business. So they're recorded as other current assets. They get dissolved as the trip comes to an end and the billing is completed.

items.statement: Cash & equivalents INR2.1B; gross debt INR277M as of Sep 30, 2024
items.quote: Lastly, as of 30th September 2024, we had a cash and cash equivalent term deposits equivalent of about INR2.1 billion on our balance sheet. And we were carrying gross debt of approximately INR277 million.

items.statement: Evaluating Holdco restructuring options; restructuring committee formed in July; announcements due
items.quote: We continue to evaluate options. There was a restructuring committee which was formed in the month of July. And the committee has evaluated certain options. We do, we are working with our consultants, lawyers, e tc. To come up with a structure which is the most optimal structure for the organization and the shareholders. We will make some announcements on that in due course of time

items.statement: ESOP cost INR2.5Cr this quarter (down from INR9.7Cr); expect range-bound going forward
items.quote: The ESOP cost for this quarter is about INR2.5 crores.

items.statement: MICE seasonality: ~30% in Q2 & Q4, ~25% in Q1, ~15% in Q3 due to inventory tightness
items.quote: You would see approximately about 30% happening in Q2 and Q4, and about 25% happening in Q1 and 15% happening in Q3. Because Q3 has the tightest availability in terms of inventory.

items.statement: Q3 earnings expected range-bound; full operating leverage flow-through in Q4
items.quote: As of now, the trending seems to indicate that they shouldn't come off. They should remain range bound to what we had just reported.

items.statement: Legal/professional costs ~INR1.4Cr from Globe acquisition and EasyGo matter; non-recurring
items.quote: The combined effect of all of this would be approximately about INR1.4-odd crores. So that would not be there on an ongoing basis.

items.statement: Revenue less service cost (net revenue) grew 15% YoY organic; Q2 INR93Cr vs Q1 INR80Cr
items.quote: Revenue less service cost grew 15% year-over-year, excluding Globe.

items.statement: Payment gateway cost reduced 15bps to 0.55% of gross bookings
items.quote: Our payment gateway cost as a percentage to gross bookings has reduced by 15 basis points, from 0.7% in year-ago quarter to 0.55% in the current quarter.

items.statement: B2C air faces direct competition from airline websites/apps; stabilized via tech improvements and partnerships (e.g., Swiggy)
items.quote: The B2C business continues to face direct competition from some of the domestic air suppliers who differentiate pricing on their own website and apps. However, despite this competition on the B2C airfront, we've managed to stabilize the volumes and have focused on improving operating performance.

items.statement: Globe gross bookings split: 60% air, 40% hotels & packages
items.quote: In terms of the split of the acquisition between hotels and air, so Globe, again, being a large MICE-focused business, their business is split almost 60% of their gross bookings come from air and 40% of their gross bookings come from hotels and packages.

items.statement: Mid-market segment onboarding ongoing; material revenue impact expected H2 next year
items.quote: My sense is that for it to really start being material, we are looking at this to be maybe, in the second half of next year.

items.statement: Agent-dependent business only 10-12% of gross bookings (5-7% of revenue); unchanged post-Globe
items.quote: So in terms of business dependent on travel agents, that is just about maybe 10%-12% of our overall business. In terms of gross bookings, in terms of revenue, that would be more like 5%-7%. So it's a very, very small part of our overall business. It doesn't change materially post the acquisition of Globe either.

items.statement: Management expects gradual recovery over next few quarters, not sudden return to growth path in Q3
items.quote: So, our entire focus is on that. That's said we expect the recovery to be gradual and not sudden when it comes to sort of getting back on the growth path that you talked about.

items.statement: Urban consumption patterns changing, visible shift in consumer buying behavior
items.quote: There clearly seems to be some form or change in terms of consumer buying in patterns which are visible, but we genuinely want to see that and understand that as a structural change.

items.statement: Medium-term high double-digit EBITDA margin target for Mamaearth unchanged despite short-term investment skew
items.quote: But our view on being able to get to a high double -digit in the medium term for ME continues to hold strongly.

items.statement: Focus categories (face cleansing, serum, sunscreen) grew 28% in H1 FY25; aim to extend to 5-6 categories in next 3-4 quarters
items.quote: Our three strongest categories where we have the best shares and ambition also is the strongest in those 2-3 categories which is face cleansing, serum, and sunscreen have actually demonstrated 28% growth in half one.

items.statement: Investing in R&D capabilities and partnerships to make hero products beat competition in blind testing across focus categories

items.statement: Completed 30+ lakh trips in FY24 averaging 5,000+ trips/day
items.quote: In FY '24, through the CCR and ETS segments, we completed more than 30 lakh trips averaging at more than 5,000 trips in a day.

items.statement: Expect CCR growth to continue in H2 FY25; ETS growth driven by GCC expansion (target 2,400 by 2030) and manufacturing; no specific revenue or margin targets given
items.quote: We are expecting to see a ride on the back of this, plus the manufacturing sector's growth to complement the growth of our ETS segment in the years ahead.

items.statement: Margin compression purely from ETS mix shift (higher operating cost), not from pricing pressure or inability to pass on costs
items.quote: So, the entire effect is due to a higher operating cost of ETS per se. So, when a section of the business, which is a higher operating cost, that increases more than the other business, that is the only effect, it has nothing to do with any kind of price pressure that we are facing from clients in either of the segments.

items.statement: Organized pan-India players serve only ~20% of market; ECOS is #1 among them; market growing faster than penetration
items.quote: If you look at the industry report, only around 20% of the market has been served by the organized pan-India players. At the same time, this is growing at a higher pace. We are number one amongst those organized pan India players.

items.statement: CCR demand was muted during election period (till August) due to political uncertainty and reduced business travel; recovered from September
items.quote: Because of the elections, generally business travel was low because of the political uncertainty which may have been there at that time. Beyond that, there were no events also or international delegates etc. who were not coming in at that point, right. This is however now picked up from September onwards very well.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guided range 14% to 16%
items.quote: And as far as our margin is concerned, we always maintain the overall tramline of 14% to 16%.

items.statement: ICE EBITDA margin improved 160 bps to 16.5% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: The EBITDA margin during the quarter for ICE business improved by 160 basis points to 16.5%, driven by mix improvement, lower material costs and LEAP savings, while we continue to invest behind brand building and new business.

items.statement: Overall EBITDA margin improved 40 bps to 14.5% after EV investment of ₹175 cr
items.quote: During the quarter, after taking into account the investment behind EV business ₹175 crores, the overall EBITDA margin improved by 40 basis points to 14.5%.

items.statement: Highest-ever festival sales of 1.6 million units, 16% revenue growth in 32-day festive period
items.quote: We clocked the highest-ever festival sales of 1.6 million units this festive season, 16% revenue growth in the festive period of 32 days, reiterating the confidence customers have with Hero.

items.statement: Vahan market share improved to 31.6% during festive period
items.quote: During the period of 32 days, our Vahan market share improved to 31.6%.

items.statement: Rural and urban demand both double-digit growth in festive, rural slightly higher
items.quote: Both are double digits, yes.

items.statement: Positive outlook for next 4-8 quarters as bottom of pyramid participation increases
items.quote: I would actually say as we move forward the next 4 to 6 to 8 quarters, as the b ottom of pyramid starts participating more, this would actually benefit the economy, of course, and the -- but auto sector, in particular

items.statement: EV retail volumes scaled to 5,000 units per month in Q2, 11,600 units during festive
items.quote: Our continued efforts in the EV business has started to show encouraging results as we further scale our volumes and improve market share in the segment to now double at 5,000 units per month during the quarter.

items.statement: EV festive retail 11,600 units, 20% market share in 5 cities and 10% in 10 cities
items.quote: We further scaled up to 11,600 units during the festive and gained 20% market share in 5 cities and 10% in 10 cities during the festive period.

items.statement: EV overall market share 5.4% during festive, uniform growth across regions
items.quote: We clocked 11.6k units in retail. And we have gone to a market share of 5.4% overall. And each of the zones have fired up on this, and we see a very uniform growth happening across the country.

items.statement: Investing aggressively behind EV and Premium growth priorities
items.quote: And that allows us the flexibility to , and the headroom , to invest even more aggressively behind our growth priorities, which we have talked about earlier, namely EV and Premium specifically.

items.statement: EV investment ~200 bps impact on margin, PLI benefits expected from FY26
items.quote: Investment behind EV, of course, 200 basis points and as the cost curve keeps coming down through external factors on the sale s price as well as internal actions that we are taking.

items.statement: PLI compliance for EV products expected in FY26, benefits to start accruing
items.quote: So in FY'26, you'll see our products getting compliant with PLI, and those benefits will start to accrue.

items.statement: Premium portfolio premiumizing over last 8 quarters via Xtec series, Xtreme 125R success
items.quote: We have been premiumizing our entire portfolio over the last 8 quarters, as you have seen through Xtec series and each one of them starts adding to the margin.

items.statement: Upcoming launches: Xpulse 210, Xtreme 250R, Karizma XMR 250, Destini full body change, Xoom 125/160, EV scooter portfolio expansion covering all price points within 6 months
items.quote: So basically, by -- within 6 months, you would have covered most of the price and the customer segment as far as EV scooters is concerned, Chandra.

items.statement: Xtreme 125R capacity increased to 40,000 units per month, now extended to secondary network
items.quote: But as we saw the demand picking up and we I: increased the capacity to 40,000 a month, now it's also gone to the secondary network - It's gone there

items.statement: Premia stores: 58 activated, target 100 by year-end, breakeven expected within 12-18 months
items.quote: We already activated 58. And there is a path forward to even accelerate that.

items.statement: Finance penetration 66% during festive, Hero FinCorp share 26%
items.quote: So on the finance penetration during the festive period, the number was close to 66%, of which, HFCL was around 26%.

items.statement: Institutional sales ~30,000 units to quick commerce/food delivery players during festive
items.quote: And in fact, to these segments in this festive, we would have probably sold close to around 30,000 vehicles with big buyers being the usual ones who do quick commerce and food deliveries.

items.statement: Global business grew 30% YoY in H1 vs industry 16%, market share 6.1% in Q2 up 60 bps sequentially
items.quote: But if you look at the firs t half, we did grow 30% versus the industry growth of 16% as far as the global business is concerned. And therefore that led to an increase in the market share to 6.1% in Quarter 2, which you compare sequentially is up by almost 60 basis points.

items.statement: Colombia turned EBITDA and cash positive first time in Q2, traction in Mexico, challenges in Bangladesh, Turkey, Nigeria
items.quote: In fact, Colombia, I must say, delivered their first quarter of a bottom line turnaround. They are cash and EBITDA positive for the fir st time. And of course, then we see traction coming from Mexico and from some of the other countries as well.

items.statement: Dealer inventory reduced to 4 weeks after festive sales
items.quote: And that's how we've ensured that the sale happens, and we ended up with the inventory that we would love to, which is 4 weeks at the dealer end.

items.statement: Hero FinCorp loan book grew 16% YoY in Q2, delinquencies and collections slowed in H1 impacting profitability, recovery expected in H2
items.quote: And their loan book overall, just to supplement Vivek, has grown 16% in Quarter 2 over Quarter 2 and they're on a very strong trajectory of their AUM and the growth, which is there.

items.statement: Hero FinCorp delinquencies and collections slowed in H1, GNPAs increased but well managed, on path to IPO
items.quote: And so as a result of that, that has really impacted the profitability of HFCL, right . And so the company is really taking steps in terms of really improving the collection efforts. Hopefully, we'll see collections coming back in the second half of the year.

items.statement: Realization per unit improved ₹2,700 QoQ (two-wheelers ₹1,400, parts balance)
items.quote: You're right, our realization during this quarter compared to Quarter 1 has improved by almost ₹2,700, right. That's two-wheelers actually contributing ₹1,400 out of which and the balance coming from the parts business.

items.statement: Parts, accessories & merchandise revenue highest ever at ₹1,456 cr, up 7.5% YoY in Q2
items.quote: The company als o reported its highest ever quarterly revenue from parts, accessories and merchandise business at ₹1,456 crores, year -on-year growth of 7.5%.

items.statement: Cash from operations H1 FY25 ₹2,817 cr, up 160% YoY
items.quote: Our continued strong focus on cash management resulted in delivering cash from operations during Half-1 ₹2,817 crores, which is up by 160% over last year, strengthening our financial position even further.

items.statement: Expects 15-20% revenue growth for full year FY25
items.quote: We expect roughly between 15% to 20% growth during the current year on a full year basis.

items.statement: Engineering order book at INR 3,580 crores end of Q2 FY25
items.quote: At the end of the Q2 financial year '25, the total order book for the engineering division stood at INR 3,580 crores.

items.statement: H1 FY25 order inflow was INR 726 crores
items.quote: The order inflow for the first half was around 726 crores.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 order inflow was INR 578 crores, nearly double Q2 FY24
items.quote: Just to give you an example, the Q2 of this year we have got around 578 crores of inflow of orders, which is significantly higher than the Q2 of the previous year, which was at around 290 crores level.

items.statement: Roha plant expansion CAPEX of INR 275 crores, commercial production expected Q1 FY26
items.quote: We are expecting the plant to deliver somewhere around 2.5 times asset turn to the total CAPEX of roughly 275 crores which is on the primary production facility.

items.statement: Membrane facility expanded recently, further expansion planned
items.quote: We've just expanded capacity on our membrane facility and we are planning to expand that further.

items.statement: Chemicals capacity utilization at 65-70%, Roha plant to add capacity
items.quote: Currently, I believe in terms of reasons our capacity utilization hovers between 65%, 70%.

items.statement: Membrane facility running at 60-65% of expanded capacity
items.quote: We are running at roughly 60% to 65% of the expanded capacity level.

items.statement: One engineering contract suppressing segment margins by 150-200 bps
items.quote: The impact of this on our engineering segment margins is significantly upward of 150-200 basis points.

items.statement: Overall FY25 operating margin expected around FY24 level due to problematic contract
items.quote: Therefore, we are likely to be at around the last year's margin percentage.

items.statement: Domestic engineering enquiry robust, large value opportunities expected in next few months
items.quote: The domestic enquiry remains robust and we are hopeful for the finalization of some large value opportunities in the next few months.

items.statement: Water and wastewater segment in sweet spot globally
items.quote: The water and the wastewater segment is certainly in the sweet spot, not just in India but globally.

items.statement: Chemicals product mix optimization for revenue and profitability over nameplate capacity
items.quote: The nameplate capacity is based on a particular product mix and the actual product mix can vary based on considerations of optimum revenue and profitability.

items.statement: Roha plant securing long-term contracts and global distribution channels
items.quote: We have been working on it for quite some time now and there is a continuous effort to make sure that once the plant gets commissioned, we would have a few customers who would be having long-term contract.

items.statement: Receivable days increased due to higher EPC invoicing, expected to remain at current days level at year-end
items.quote: Our EPC segment revenue is steadily increasing. That's why we are largely seeing an increase in the number of days of the receivables for the current year.

items.statement: Indraneel Dutt appointed MD in natural progression from CEO role
items.quote: Mr. Indraneel Dutt had been appointed as a CEO for the company last year and in a natural progression he has been appointed as M.D. this year.

items.statement: Engineering division conversion rate from enquiry bank to order book at 15-20%
items.quote: Our average conversion from the enquiry bank into the order book is roughly around 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Sri Lanka project has significant uncertainty on fund allocation, ~10% invoicing remains
items.quote: But roughly around 10% or so of the invoicing still remains to be made. We can only say that there is a significant degree of uncertainty about when the funds will get allocated to it and how much.

items.statement: UP contract execution dependent on government fund flows and approvals
items.quote: The execution of the contract is quite dependent upon the flow of funds which are allocated and approved for our contract, as well as the various approvals that we receive from the government.

items.statement: Chemicals standalone FY25 growth ~15%, consolidated 12-14%
items.quote: So for the year as a whole, we are expecting to close on a standalone basis at roughly around 15% growth, and on a consolidated basis, growth of roughly between 12% to 14%.

items.statement: Chemicals faces Indian and global competition, sustained margins indicate competitive strength
items.quote: We face competition from several Indian and global competitors in both the Indian and global markets. And this has been so for several decades.

items.statement: Jal Jeevan Mission fund flows improved post-elections, October significantly better
items.quote: The fund allocations have improved in October, for example, and during a part of September, and we do hope that we will see more of this happening in the coming period of time.

items.statement: Mapril acquisition contributes substantially to chemicals, other smaller additions also
items.quote: There are some other additions also, but Mapril is the most substantial one.

items.statement: International orders improving in quality, targeting higher international growth
items.quote: The recent orders that we are picking up from the international market are also quite good both from the top line as well as the bottom line perspective.

items.statement: Consolidated operating margin was 13.6% in Q2 FY25, down 70 bps sequentially due to RM cost pressure.
items.quote: Consolidated operating margin for the quarter stood at 13.6% down about 70 basis points sequentially mainly on account of RM cost pressures.

items.statement: RM costs increased ~8% sequentially in India in Q2; expected ~1% increase in Q3 then decline from Q4.
items.quote: So Raghu, the RM went up by about 8% sequentially. Our expectation going forward is just about a 1 percent-plus increase for Q3. And then as per current expectations the RM should start coming down.

items.statement: Price hikes taken: ~2% in truck segment, larger quantum in PCR; under-recovery from last year ~6%.
items.quote: So, broadly we have taken price increase ranging from 2-odd percent in the truck segment to a larger quantum in the PCR segment. The under-recovery from last year is about 6-odd percent.

items.statement: India replacement volume grew mid-single digits YoY in Q2; exports double-digit growth; OEM double-digit decline.
items.quote: The volume for Q2, Y-o-Y Raghu, was flattish. Within that, the replacement was mid single-digit growth, exports was a double-digit growth and OEM was a double-digit negative.

items.statement: Full-year replacement demand for TBR and PCR expected around double-digit growth; OE demand to remain muted near term.
items.quote: So both for TBR and PCR full year the replacement should be around a double-digit growth. Right now, in near term, the signs of recovery from OE are not there. So in near term, it will continue to be probably in the same zone.

items.statement: India EBITDA margin 12.1% in Q2 vs 13.8% in Q1; Europe EBITDA margin 14.8% vs 13.7% sequentially.
items.quote: The EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 5.4 billion, a margin of 12.1% compared to 13.8% in the last quarter.

items.statement: Europe margin supported by lower natural rubber share, higher UHP mix (47% of PCT volumes vs 39% YoY), and lower RM proportion in mature markets.
items.quote: The reason on the margin performance is that large part of the raw material cost push was driven by natural rubber which is a much smaller proportion for the European Operations versus the Indian Operations.

items.statement: UHP segment accounted for 47% of PCT volumes in Europe in Q2 FY25, up from 39% in Q2 FY24.
items.quote: Ultra High performance segment accounted for about 47% of PCT volumes in Quarter 2 of FY25 compared to 39% in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: No change in FY25 capex guidance of INR 10 billion; only INR 3 billion spent in H1.
items.quote: There is no change in our CapEx guidance for FY25 and we will continue to focus on profitability, free cash flow generation and improvement in the return ratios as we go ahead.

items.statement: Net debt increased INR 4.6 billion since April due to short-term borrowings for inventory; inventory buildup temporary, partly seasonal for Europe winter tyres.
items.quote: We saw about I.NR 4.6 billion increase in net debt as on September '24 when compared to beginning of the year, April '24. The increase in net debt was driven by increase in short-term borrowings which was used to finance inventories and is only a short-term phenomenon.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt/EBITDA 0.8x; India net debt/EBITDA 1.1x as of September; long-term debt reduced INR 7.6 billion since March.
items.quote: The net debt-to-EBITDA for the consolidated operations was a very comfortable 0.8x as of September end.

items.statement: Commodity prices in Q2: natural rubber ~INR 210/kg, synthetic rubber ~INR 190/kg, carbon black ~INR 125/kg.
items.quote: So natural rubber was in the region of INR 210 a kg, Synthetic rubber, INR 190 a kg. Carbon black, INR 125 a kg.

items.statement: Europe energy costs hedged 60-70% for next one year.
items.quote: So, I would say over the next one year, our energy cost would be hedged about to the extent of 60% to 70%.

items.statement: Market share maintained or slightly up across categories; aspiration to reach 30% in truck and early 20s% in passenger car over next couple of years.
items.quote: On the truck side, our aspirations or vision would be to get back into the 30% in terms of market share which is where we used to be a couple of years back, and in passenger car given the more number of players and the more competitive intensity somewhere in the 20%, to early 20%.

items.statement: Other expenses run-rate ~INR 800 crore/quarter sustained near term; driven by freight, EPR, advertising.
items.quote: So Amar, the advertising part continues at a certain level and there are no immediate decisions of taking it up or down

items.statement: Expect margin improvement in Q4 if RM costs decline; Q3 RM still strong with lag effect, volume growth positive.
items.quote: I don't see it springing back in Quarter 3, but I'm very positive on my volume growth in Quarter 3. And that should release some margin. Going forward, if all goes well and RM still keeps coming down, there will be a margin increase in Quarter 4.

items.statement: Europe passenger car market grew ~3% in H1; Apollo grew in line; winter tyre demand sensing decent for current quarter.
items.quote: Europe markets for the first half, has shown a growth of about 3% on the passenger car segment which is the key segment for us. We've also grown in line with that.

items.statement: Reifencom revenue INR 45 million in Q2 with double-digit YoY growth; margins at historical breakeven range.
items.quote: So Reifencom for this quarter did INR 45 million in revenues, had a fairly healthy growth, double-digit growth over the same period last year. And margins continue to be broadly in the same range, which at an overall level, which they have been historically.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; focus on premiumisation and profitable growth strategy.
items.quote: My mantra has been profitable growth and therefore we are only looking at premiumisation of our PCR tyres and not going down on pricing.

items.statement: Freight costs volatile and macro-dependent; EPR cost now constant; advertising under control but sustained.
items.quote: The increase in the other cost is on account of freight costs where the freight rates went up. Secondly on account of the EPR which was not there last year and thirdly on account of advertising.

items.statement: EPR (Extended Producer Responsibility) cost introduced this year, adding to other expenses.
items.quote: Secondly on account of the EPR which was not there last year and thirdly on account of advertising.

items.statement: No major capex coming up; focus on cash flow and return ratios; digitalisation of supply chain live in India.
items.quote: There is no major CapEx coming up. So from a cash flow perspective or a net debt, there is nothing to worry about.

items.statement: Sustainability recognition: EcoVadis rating improved; BW Sustainability World ranked Apollo 14th overall, top in auto components.
items.quote: Furthermore, recently BW Sustainability World ranked Apollo Tyres 14th overall among India's most sustainable companies. Apollo Tyres was also ranked the top sustainable company in the automotive component segment.

items.quote: We are still working on that number. We feel that this growth is -- this muted growth is not going to go long, maybe 1 quarter more. items.statement: Long-term sustainable EBITDA margin expected around 16% plus
items.quote: I think for the less -- we should look at a number around 16% , then it will be done. That is not an issue. And margins, sometimes it's an impact of some marginal price increases, sometimes is the impact of freight, et cetera. It's a mix impact. Sometimes it go by 0.5%, 0.2% here and there. But it should be around 16% plus, it should be around that in the long term.

items.statement: New order book announcement expected within 15-20 days
items.quote: Yes, we are working on that. Hopefully, within the next 15, 20 days, we will announce the new order book we have got. We are waiting for one more order. If it comes, then it w ill be a decent amount to

items.quote: And in the joint venture of Marelli, as you are aware, we have got INR1,000 crores order from them. The supply -- there are some design changes and the new samples are in progress. items.quote: Yes, maybe we may see a slightish muted quarter 3, which would be equal to quarter 2, I would say. items.quote: Next-generation heat shield is Nimbus heat shield, which we have offered to Tata Motors. We are under product develo pment, it has started for that. items.quote: We have start supply to Mahindra and heat shield supply to Mahindra. Now we're looking at also looking at hoses and rubber as a next order category to them. It takes some time because I know that's one OEM, which has actually done better than all the other OEMs.

items.statement: Freight cost increases partially unrecovered from customers, to be recovered in subsequent quarters
items.quote: Freight also has gone increase. Some freight we have still to recover from our customers, which will come in the subsequent quarters, plus a lot of development happened in this quarter, please.

items.quote: Yes, Pune facility has started, but I think we are adding the Phase 1 of machines, we added. Now we are adding the Phase 2 of the machines. items.statement: Jaguar Land Rover EV launch delayed to July-August 2025 impacting supply start
items.quote: No, no, we are not impacted by that. But the new launches of the e -vehicle, which they have delayed by the -- until, I think, July, A ugust of next year, which was supposed to launch in January, it has impacted us that way. But supply will start a late little bit

items.statement: UK OEM launch delays and BMW schedule reduction creating near-term revenue headwinds
items.quote: One of our major OEMs with which we were looking at a large revenue base, like U.K.-based OEMs, they have delayed some launches. So there is cyclicality. But we keep adding on customers. We'll keep adding on. We'll try and add on some U.S. aftermarket customers that may be a little bit low -hanging fruits. We are working on our process. So it's nothing to really worr y about

items.statement: Expecting RBI rate cut by end of 2024 or Q1 2025 to boost auto demand
items.quote: And we are expecting by the end of this year or in the first quarter of next year, RBI will also reduce some rate of interest, which will also impact this growth.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; focus on operational team execution
items.quote: We're also very happy with our operative team to come up with the EBITDA margin of 16.9% in this kind of a situation.

items.statement: DCTL Board approved ~INR 5,000 crore investment for polycarbonate resin plant including greenfield infrastructure, funded by balanced debt-equity mix
items.quote: To proceed with the project to manufacture polycarbonate resins involving an investment of approximately INR 5,000 crore, inclusive of greenfield infrastructure and capital expenditure. This investment will be funded through a balanced mix of debt and equity, contingent upon the completion of detailed engineering.

items.statement: Polycarbonate resin plant capacity 165,000 MTPA via Trinseo asset acquisition and technology license
items.quote: Additionally, DCTL will acquire Trinseo's assets, including all proprietary equipment with an annual capacity of 165,000 metric tonnes, currently located in Stade, Germany.

items.statement: Nitric acid, photochlorination, hydrogenation, nitration blocks commissioning in H2 FY25; MIBK/MIBC and acetophenone in H1 FY26; R&D center in H2 FY25
items.quote: The nitric acid project is expected to be commissioned in H2 FY25. Our other projects, including photochlorination, hydrogenation and nitration block are also commissioning together in H2 FY25.

items.statement: India polycarbonate demand ~240,000 MTPA in 2023, projected to grow faster than GDP; currently 100% import dependent
items.quote: India's demand for polycarbonate resins was approximately 240,000 MTPA in 2023, and it is projected to grow at a rate exceeding that of India's GDP. Currently, the entire demand is met through imports.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 consolidated EBITDA INR 319 crore flat YoY; H1 FY25 EBITDA INR 647 crore up 15% YoY at 15% margin
items.quote: In terms of profitability, EBITDA at INR 319 crore in Q2 was stable on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Advanced Intermediates Q2 EBIT margin 8% (INR 47 crore); Phenolics Q2 EBIT margin 15% (INR 215 crore)
