items.quote: So, I would say things will not improve until the zero DPD bucket repayment rate goes up to at least 99%, 98.5% to 99%, which is what typically what we used to.

items.statement: Expect credit cycle recovery to take at least a year from April 2024; improvement possible by Q4 FY25
items.quote: In my experience, once a credit cycle starts, it takes at least a year for things to start getting back on track. And so if I say get this credit cycle started in April, which is when, it really kind of started surfacing very, very quickly. That would mean that by Q4 end we should start seeing things getting back on track or improving or getting better.

items.statement: High attrition rates among field staff across industry affecting collection efficiency
items.quote: Additionally, high attrition rates among the field staff across the industry have affected collection effici ency, as turnover disrupts the consistency and effectiveness of borrower interactions.

items.statement: MSME yields 28-32% due to individual doorstep collections and high operating costs
items.quote: Typically our interest rates in MSME are between 28% to 32% and as far as this segment goes, this is little par for the course, because the operating cost in MSME are much, much higher than what they are in MSME.

items.statement: Minimal overlap between MFI and MSME books; some MFI customers graduate to MSME but no cross-sell
items.quote: As far as our books are concerned, there is very little overlap or no overlap. Some microfinance customers do graduate to MSME, but there is no cross sell, so essentially, it would be one loan, one customer.

items.statement: Oversupply of credit from non-MFI players; deregulation in April 2022 led to aggressive pricing and overleveraging
items.quote: It just seems that the world is crazy for offering loans. Even the companies who have nothing to do with loans , monetize their businesses with giving out loans as a supplementary business.

items.statement: PAR 31-90 bucket ~8% in microfinance; management overlay maintained high for provisioning
items.quote: Given that we have a large power book, 30 to 90 days of almost 8% in microfinance and you mentioned that that number continues to see increase because X bucket collection fee , your collection efficiency is still low.

items.statement: Revenue target of Rs 2,900 crore by March 2027 maintained; high single-digit growth expected in FY25 and 20%+ growth in FY26 and FY27
items.quote: Regarding the first question, whether we are wanting to revise a guideline of Rs. 2,900 crore by March 2027 ; see when we were making the projections, we had already factored in that the first two quarters of the current financial year would not be going as strong.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to return to 16%-17% range in H2 FY25 from 14.3% in Q2
items.quote: No, we should be having margin in the range of 16%-17%. We had done something like 14.3% in the current quarter . With the price increase implemented in faucetware, a 6% increase happened in faucetware, 1% in sanitaryware; so, the total impact in that respect in the second quarter rather in the second half should be to the extent of 1.5%.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 revenues grew 6.3% YoY to Rs 490 crore despite extended monsoon; gradual demand uptrend vs Q1 strengthens optimism for H2 recovery
items.quote: Building on the challenges of the first quarter, Q2 FY25 continued to face market pressures, which was further intensified by an extended monsoon season. Despite these headwinds, Cera recorded revenues from operations of Rs. 490 crore and profits after tax of Rs. 68 crore for Q2 FY25, achieving a year-on-year growth of 6.3% and 19.7%, respectively.

items.statement: Sanitaryware retail demand subdued but project segment showing improvement; faucetware retail and project both growing; overall high single-digit growth expected for FY25
items.quote: The project segment has already started showing some signs of improvement in the sanitaryware segment . So, we anticipate that the H2 going forward, once the retail market also picks up, we should be ending up with stronger volumes in sanitaryware.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin 17.3%, down 110 bps YoY due to higher opex partially offset by favorable absorption; gas costs favorable at 1.55% of revenue
items.quote: EBITDA margins for the current quarter stood at 17.3% as against 18.4% in Q2 FY24, registering a decrease of 110 basis points. This decline in margin was mainly on account of increase in 'opex' cost, which is partially offset by favorable absorption.

items.statement: Price hike of 6% on faucets and 1% on sanitaryware implemented in September 2024 to offset 18% brass price increase; expected to cushion margins in upcoming quarters
items.quote: To address the impact of rising input costs, namely brass prices, wherein prices increased by 18% between March and June, we implemented a strategic price adjustment in September 2024, applying a 6% increase for faucets and 1% increase for sanitaryware.

items.statement: Premium category 41% of sales, mid 34%, entry 25% in Q2; new product development 34% of total sales; luxury segment target 10% of revenue in 3-5 years
items.quote: In Q2 FY25, 41% of our sales were in the premium category, 34% in mid category and 25% in entry-level category.

items.statement: Faucetware capacity 4 lakh units/month at 93% utilization; sanitaryware at 89% utilization; can stretch to 115-120%; greenfield sanitaryware project land acquired, construction 18 months, start date to be revisited end of FY25
items.quote: With adequate inventory levels, we have optimized our production strategy to balance production and inventory, achieving faucetware capacity utilization of 93% and sanitaryware capacity utilization at 89% in Q2 FY25.

items.statement: FY25 planned capex Rs 25 crore, Rs 11 crore deployed in H1; sanitaryware greenfield Phase 1 capex Rs 130 crore (incl Rs 25-30 cr land) for 1.2 mn pieces/annum yielding Rs 300 cr revenue from FY28
items.quote: Our planned CAPEX for FY25 stands at Rs. 25 crore, of which we have already deployed Rs. 11 crore by H1 FY25.

items.statement: B2B sales 37% of Q2 revenue, up 15% in last 6 months; retailer loyalty program enrolled 21,700+ retailers with 3.6 lakh invoices; 39% of Rs 97 cr retail sales eligible for rewards
items.quote: B2B sales contributed 37% of Q2 revenue, demonstrating our selective focus on project sales that align with our profitability and margin goals.

items.statement: Not concerned about new entrants (pipe/paint cos) as they bulk source basic products from Morbi targeting unorganized market; Cera has strong distribution, brand and ad spend
items.quote: We are not concerned about the competition because as you mentioned, like most of the other pipe companies, paint companies, etc. have also started with the sanitaryware and faucetware business. But we find that most of them are mostly bulk sourcing from Morbi and trying to sell within a very basic kind of product.

items.statement: Net working capital days increased to 72 from 60 YoY; inventory days 80 (vs 73), receivable days 33 (vs 29), payable days 41 (vs 42)
items.quote: In terms of the working capital management, inventory days increased from 73 days to 80 days, receivable days increased from 29 days to 33 days and payable days decreased from 42 days to 41 days. Consequently, the net working capital days increased from 60 days to 72 days in Q2 FY25.

items.statement: Buyback of Rs 130 crore completed (108,333 shares at Rs 12,000/share); buyback tax of ~Rs 30 crore paid by company; consistent dividend increases maintained
items.quote: During the quarter, we successfully concluded the buyback of shares amounting to Rs. 130 crore. The buyback involved purchase of 108,333 fully paid-up equity shares at Rs . 12,000 per share, effectively returning part of the surplus cash to shareholders.

items.statement: China imports reduced to 3% of revenue (~Rs 13 cr); most items internalized or sourced from Morbi; container rates normalized after Red Sea disruptions
items.quote: For Cera, we will find that we have reduced our China imports to a great extent . Most of the items that we were importing earlier from China, we have been able to internalize, and we have started manufacturing those items within our own plant.

items.statement: Sales mix: Tier-1 34%, Tier-2 21%, Tier-3 45%; South 36%, North 33%, West 21%, East 9% in Q2
items.quote: Regarding the sales distribution, Tier-1 cities accounted for 34% of the total sales, Tier-2 cities - 21% and Tier-3 cities led with 45% of total sales.

items.statement: Cash-rich with Rs 659 cr cash equivalents; CC limit Rs 100 cr but drawing only Rs 15-20 cr; interest cost increase due to IndAS lease accounting (rentals capitalized), not actual borrowings
items.quote: Our total drawing CC limit is something like Rs. 100 crore, whereas we normally draw only to the extent of Rs. 15 to 20 crore. The data has remained static in the last few quarters . That has not changed.

items.statement: Real estate delivery cycle 5-6 years; post-COVID project completions expected FY26-27 driving demand; rural sanitaryware demand not yet visible despite FMCG uptick
items.quote: So, typically a real estate project would take five years to six years to reach the completion stage. So, we can now anticipate that with post-COVID the projects which have started sometime in 2021 should be getting completed by more or less next financial year '25-'26 and '26-'27.

items.statement: Expects H2 FY25 margins to be close to H1 levels
items.quote: Yes, I think at this time, we believe that the H1 margins more or less are in line with our expectations, and we believe that H2 would also be pretty close to that.

items.statement: Investing Rs 440 crore to add third Bretonstone line at Mekaguda facility, operational by March 2026
items.quote: We are expanding our state -of-the-art quartz manufacturing facility in Telangana by adding a third Bretonstone production line. Scheduled to be operational by March 2026, this new line will significantly enhanc e our capacity while maintaining high standards of sustainable manufacturing.

items.statement: Capex funded by Rs 300 crore debt and Rs 144 crore internal accruals
items.quote: In terms of the investment m ix, we expect to do about Rs.300 crore of debt and the balance Rs.144 crore we are expecting to fund with our internal accruals.

items.statement: New line expected to reach full optimal capacity in 12-15 months after commissioning
items.quote: See, the ramp up as we have had in the first line as well, we expect that the full optimal capacity would take at least 12 to 15 months to come.

items.statement: New line expected to generate Rs 145-165 crore EBITDA and Rs 100-110 crore PAT at steady state
items.quote: So, profitability is typically we expect that the EBITDA from this would be in the range of Rs.145 to Rs.165 crore is what we are foreseeing at this time and PAT also we are expecting it to be in the range of Rs.100 to Rs.110 crore is what we are expecting at this time.

items.statement: Targets 75% revenue from North America and 25% from rest of world in 3-5 years
items.quote: Now coming to the market share, yes, of course, next three to five years, our idea is also that we have a good amount of rest of the world coming in. So, whether it would be 25% or 20%, I think time would say, but definitely our target is that we have 25% definitely coming from the rest of the world and 75 % from probably. North America.

items.statement: Expects quarterly revenue run rate of Rs 200-225 crore from new facility at steady state
items.quote: And now coming to your quarterly revenue, I think we expect that the numbers should be in the range of Rs.200 to Rs.225 crore subject to of course the market conditions and the situations out there.

items.statement: Aspires to maintain 35% EBITDA margin with new facility, historically targets 30%+
items.quote: So, historically, we have maintained that our target is to be 30% -plus EBITDA. So, we think that 35% is maintainable , of course, subject to the market conditions, but that's what we are aspiring for.

items.statement: Internal target to maintain consolidated margins around 35% for new plant
items.quote: That is what our internal targets are that we have to look at that number and plus.

items.statement: Close to ideal product mix (30-35% high value, 30-35% medium, 20-25% basic plus hospitality), hospitality still lagging
items.quote: So, we are pretty close to the ideal mix except for that , the hospitality has still not picked up, but it is far better than what it was in last year same time.

items.statement: KREOS line commercialization in Q3 FY25, launches in Q4 FY25; CHROMIA line operational by Q4 FY25
items.quote: The Kreos Line is progressing toward commercialization in Q3 FY25, with exciting product launches planned for Q4 FY25. The Chromia Line, designed for high-definition digital printing, is expected to be operational by Q4 FY25.

items.statement: US demand recovery depends on mortgage rates stabilizing below current 6.9%; mid-to-top tier focus driving outperformance
items.quote: But then as we are positioned on a different footing compared to majority of our competition, we are focusing on mid-to-top tier products. So, there, our differential strategy is able to bring us the faith of customer and also the related sales out of it.

items.statement: Freight rates normalized to near pre-inflation levels across most US ports
items.quote: I think the freight rates what we are seeing, they are pretty close to the normal levels for most of the US ports and there are certain ports where there is still not there.

items.statement: Works predominantly with large distributors; their success drives company success
items.quote: Since we do not go like caesarstone to the end consumer or to the fabricator, we work predominantly with the large distributors and their success is our success.

items.statement: Domestic India market currently minuscule; targets 10% of turnover from domestic sales
items.quote: Our focus is that always has been export market. Now looking at the Indian market and Indian growth story, we feel that the market is now right to accept our kind of product in the market. So, let's hope that we at least achieve 10% of our turnover on the domestic front.

items.statement: Will take about one year to identify right business partners for India distribution
items.quote: We will take about one year to identify the right business partners , because the response was too good, but we have to evaluate who will be the right business partners for the growth.

items.statement: Gross debt Rs 228 crore as of Sep 2024; cost of funds ~9%
items.quote: So, the gross debt as on 30th September, it is Rs.228 crore, and the cost of funds is around close to 9%.

items.statement: Current US duties: 2.34% countervailing duty, anti-dumping duty zero for this POR; any Trump changes would apply across board
items.quote: There is already an anti -dumping duty on our product. So, we have approximately about 2.34% countervailing duty, the anti -dumping duty for this POR was set as zero.

items.statement: Gross margin dip from 67.6% to 64% QoQ due to raw material mix (imported sand usage), not concerning
items.quote: I think this decline is not really a big number to be concerned , because it also depends upon what type of raw materials you are using in that particular period. Because if you are using a lot of your imported sand in that particular quarter, then it would be… so I think the number is very negligible in our view.

items.statement: Expects 25% effective tax rate for full year FY25
items.quote: So, we are expecting 25% also for the full year.

items.statement: Brownfield expansion at existing Mekaguda facility with minimal disruption; space allocated during original design
items.quote: See, this facility is going to come up at our existing facility in Mekaguda, Telangana. So, when we had originally designed our Hyderabad Mekaguda facility, we had provided enough space for future expansion.

items.statement: Additional space available at Mekaguda for further expansion beyond third line
items.quote: Regarding the additional space availability for future expansion, we do have still some space available for further expansion.

items.statement: Asset turnover historically 1x-1.25x; expects similar for new line at steady state
items.quote: Historically we have maintained that the asset turn is about 1 x to 1.25x. So, depending upon that we will have revenues around Rs.450 crore to 525 crore is what we foresee at this time.

items.statement: Granite business near-term outlook remains cautious; implementing cost-control measures
items.quote: While the near-term outlook remains cautious, we are committed to addressing these challenges with a focused and measured approach.

items.statement: Competitive pricing pressure from India and Southeast Asia producers; differentiation strategy key
items.quote: However, we remain cautious in managing competitive pricing pressures from producers in India and Southeast Asia. Our strategic focus on innovation and differentiation positions us well to address these challenges.

items.statement: Net debt expected to be around 20% lower than current Rs. 553 crores by end of FY25
items.quote: Broadly, my personal estimate would be around 20% lower than where we sit today.

items.statement: Global trade expected to strengthen; Europe may take more than two quarters to revive
items.quote: I already answered that we expect the strong demand environment in some of the select countries to continue, and Europe may take more than two quarters to revive. But globally, there's a better momentum in the market.

items.statement: Express business EBITDA improved consistently over last three quarters; price increase announced to improve margins
items.quote: We have recently announced a general price increase which will align us to improve the revenues and therefore improve the profit

items.statement: Contract logistics revenue grew 45% YoY to Rs. 111 crores in Q2 FY25 driven by new client additions
items.quote: Contract logistics revenue for Q2 FY '25 stood at Rs. 111 crores as compared to Rs. 76 crores for the same period last year, representing a growth of 45%.

items.statement: No significant capex plans beyond ordinary; investments now focused on people rather than acquisitions
items.quote: There are no significant Cap ex plans. Even on the expansion one significant change which has happened, I would say, in a way in our strate gy is that we are now investing in people in a way rather than acquiring companies.

items.statement: Contract logistics white space increased from 3-4% to 10-11% to support growth in e-commerce, auto, engineering
items.quote: Historically our white space was possibly in the range of 3% to 4% now that is 10% to 11%, but that is required as we drive grow th and movement.

items.statement: Freight rates cyclical; short-term debt increases with rate spikes and deflates when rates fall
items.quote: The freight rates are cyclical in nature and the short-term debt kind of apes that from an amount perspective.

items.statement: Contract logistics now 23% chemical, auto/engineering equal to chemical, e-commerce largest segment
items.quote: Despite continued growth, chemical logistics today comprises only 23% of our business, which means that Company has been successful in expanding its business into new domains, auto and engineering which is now as big as the chemical in terms of the total revenue mix. And the largest section for us now is our e-commerce business.

items.statement: Onboarded new team in Argentina, Paraguay, Uruguay doubling business in two months; finalized JVs in Colombia, Ecuador
items.quote: Between July to September this quarter we onboarded an entire new team in Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay, which will add to the business in the region. It is already doing well in the first two months of operations, having grown the business significantly, almost doubling the business in two months itself.

items.statement: ECU Worldwide has unmatched technology and network creating flywheel of volume, market share, competitiveness
items.quote: Today, when we look at the competitive landscape, there is nobody close to our entity ECU Worldwide from a technology and network perspective, and that's something which should continue to create the flywheel of success wherein these capabilities lead to higher volume and market share.

items.statement: Restructuring scheme received exchange no-objection, filed with NCLT; demerger and separate listing by April 2025
items.quote: We believe that we would conclude the proce ss in the estimated timelines. And by April 2025 we should have the international domestic businesses demerged and listed separately.

items.statement: US business comprises both export and import; tariff restrictions may divert trade flows to Vietnam, Indonesia
items.quote: as far as our US business is concerned, it comprises both export and import. As I was mentioning earlier, we believe that any tariff restr ictions which come in particular to a certain country, those tariff restrictions could lead to diverted tariff flows, and we might see more cargo coming in from other countries as compared to China, for instance

items.statement: Net debt Rs. 553 crores up due to working capital increase from higher freight rates; temporary in nature
items.quote: The consolidated net debt for the quarter end ed September '24 stood at Rs. 553 crores. The net debt has gone up mainly on account of a working capital increase.

items.statement: Gross debt Rs. 1,362 crores (short-term ~Rs. 850 crores, long-term Rs. 495 crores); short-term debt tracks freight rate cycles
items.quote: The gross debt is Rs. 1,362 crores, short term debt is around only Rs. 850 crores out of it, or Rs. 495 crores is long term debt.

items.statement: Non-core asset monetization estimated at Rs. 75-100 crores consolidated including Allcargo and Gati
items.quote: So, across Allcargo, on a consolidated basis, which includes Allcargo and Gati as well, broadly there could be non-core cash flows coming into the extent of Rs. 75 crores to Rs. 100 crores, that's the broad estimate.

items.statement: Latin America expansion via new team onboarding and JVs in Colombia, Ecuador; no acquisitions planned
items.quote: Also this is the quarter when we finalized our joint ventures in Colombia and Ecuador, which will bring in local expertise. And combining with the global network, we expect these markets to also grow faster.

items.statement: Capital allocation focused on debt retirement and dividends; dividend distributed in recent quarter
items.quote: We have been using capital to retire debt or to provide dividends to the shareholders. And the Company has maintained distribution of cash flows by way of dividend, as you would have seen in the quarter gone by as well.

items.statement: Staff cost up Rs. 32 crores QoQ due to ~30 new hires in Argentina, bonus payments, and ~$1M severance cost this quarter
items.quote: the increase in staff cost is primarily driv en by, one, like you rightly mentioned, onboarding new people such as about 30 -plus people in the Argentina region that I mentioned about, and a few more people in other geographies as well which have been onboarded for

items.statement: ISC LCL volume 2.3M CBM (+4% YoY, +5% QoQ); FCL 164K TEUs (+7% YoY, +5% QoQ); Air 2.65M kg (+14% YoY, -4% QoQ)
items.quote: The Less-than-Container Load container volume for the quarter ended September ‘24 stood at 2.3 million CBM. Depicting a 4% growth over the quarter ended September ’23, and 5% over the previous quarter, that is the June quarter 2024. FCL volume for the quarter stood at 164K TEUs, up 7% over the same period last year and 5% over the quarter ended June ‘24. Air volume for the quarter ended September

items.statement: Geopolitical events (Russia-Ukraine, Middle East, US tariffs) could shape world trade; Europe economic environment subdued
items.quote: There are of course several geopolitical events happening around us and they would shape the future of world trade. But prima facie, we believe that global trade will only continue to strengthen from here.

items.statement: Freight rates expected to remain range-bound; Drewry projects net trade demand to absorb new capacity
items.quote: So, we believe that freight rates will remain range bound. There are various things pointing towards an upward movement and things pointing towards downward, some you appropriately mentioned. What we follow from various maritime research projections is that there is also a lot of capacity coming up for scraping. And on an overall basis, Drewry, which is the leading maritime research Company, publi

items.statement: Revenue growth target of 50% above industry growth rate over next 3-4 years
items.quote: we should be able to grow at least 50% more than the industry's growth rate

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expected to sustain at 14% for FY25
items.quote: we expect this margin to continue in Q3 and Q4 for the remaining part of the fiscal

items.statement: EBITDA margin expansion target from 14% to 15% over next 3 years
items.quote: we should be able to expand those EBITDA margins further, perhaps from 14% to 15%

items.statement: IAC EBITDA margin expected to maintain 16-18% range in H2
items.quote: we do expect a similar margin to be maintained

items.statement: Total order book INR1,050 crores with 90% new business and 40% EV contribution
items.quote: The total order book, considering the value of all product and domain categories is INR1,050 crores, out of which 90% is new business

items.statement: Order book maturity: 15% in FY25, 40% in FY26, 30% in FY27, 15% in FY28
items.quote: 15% of the order value will mature in the current financial year FY '25, 40% in FY '26, 30% in FY '27 and the remaining residual 15% in FY '28

items.statement: Capex estimated at INR120-140 crores for FY25, up from INR32 crores in H1
items.quote: the Capex outlay for the whole year is estimated to be around INR120 crores to INR140 crores

items.statement: Incremental capex of ~INR60 crores YoY expected to generate INR400 crores additional revenue in FY25
items.quote: there should be an incremental Capex of about INR60 crores. Last year was around INR80 crores. This year, we are looking at anywhere between INR120 crores to INR150 crores

items.statement: IAC capacity utilization ~85% after brownfield expansions in Pune and Nashik operational in H2
items.quote: post the investments, I would say that our capacity utilizations would still be close to around 85-odd percent

items.statement: Passenger vehicle industry expected low single-digit growth for full year
items.quote: Overall, as noted previously, we expect the passenger vehicle segment to register a low single-digit growth for the full year as an industry

items.statement: 2-wheeler segment growth momentum continuing with rural demand and premium models
items.quote: Looking ahead, we anticipate this upward trend to persist, fueled by a stronger rural economy, continued introduction of premium models and evolving consumer preferences

items.statement: Commercial vehicle demand expected to rebound in H2 with government spending resumption
items.quote: we are hopeful that the demand for CVs will rebound in the second half of the year as government spending resumes and infrastructure projects regain momentum

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 14% for Q2 and H1 FY25
items.quote: EBITDA margin stands at 14% for Q2 FY '25. Absolute EBITDA for Q2 stood at INR118 crores, growth of 18% on a year-on-year basis. H1 FY '25 margin is at 14%

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin improved ~150 bps YoY in H1 due to OEM scale and price corrections
items.quote: it has grew almost by 150 basis points and which basically includes certain economies of scale due to the higher revenue in OEM and as well as certain, you can say, the price corrections from our major OEMs

items.statement: EV contribution ~40% of total order book across passenger cars and 2-wheelers
items.quote: EV contribution is approximately 40% of the total order book

items.statement: No plans to pursue EV-specific components; focusing on CNG/alternate fuels instead
items.quote: we are currently not further pursuing any opportunity in the EV specific component space. As an alternative, as I mentioned, we are a lot more bullish on the penetration of alternate fuels like CNG

items.statement: IAC won full service supplier business for Tata Motors including ambient lighting new product category
items.quote: we have won a full service supplier business for Tata Motors, not just for the plastic interior products, but also for the ambient lighting, and that's a new product category which IAC India has ventured into

items.statement: Engaged with Maruti Suzuki to expand wallet share and with Honda Car India as new potential customer
items.quote: We are continuously engaged in discussions with OEMs like Maruti Suzuki to expand and increase our wallet share and also with new potential customers like Honda Car India

items.statement: GreenFuel acquisition expected to close in Q3 FY25 with consolidation from Q3
items.quote: This partnership, as I mentioned, should be fructified sometime in quarter 3 itself and with consolidation revenues maybe kicking in from quarter 3

items.statement: GreenFuel expected INR300-350 crores annualized revenue with stronger EBITDA margins, mainly for FY26
items.quote: on a full year basis, we are expecting anywhere between INR300 crores to INR350-odd crores of revenues with a stronger EBITDA margin than what we are looking at currently

items.statement: Mechatronics revenue to more than double in FY25 and double again in FY26 crossing INR200 crores
items.quote: mechatronics, as was explained earlier, will grow at almost close to 70% to 80% this year. And next year also, we expect the revenues of mechatronics domain to double, maybe crossing the INR200 crores mark

items.statement: Lumax Mannoh targeting 12-15% YoY growth with 60-62% gear shifter market share
items.quote: We are anticipating a year-on-year growth of about 12% to 15%, depending on the OEM demand holding up

items.statement: FAE oxygen sensor SOP January 2025 with major 2-wheeler OEM, targeting 0.5M sensors in FY26
items.quote: we are going ahead with the SOP in January with a major 2-wheeler manufacturer. We are looking at supplying almost 0.5 million sensors in the next financial year

items.statement: Free cash INR387 crores exceeds long-term debt INR363 crores as of Sep 30
items.value: INR387 crores cash vs INR363 crores debt
items.quote: The company is sitting on a healthy free cash of INR387 crores as on 30th September, which is more than the long-term debt of INR363 crores

items.statement: Annual long-term debt repayment INR75 crores, half paid in H1
items.quote: Annual repayment schedule for the whole year was -- long-term debt was INR75 crores. So out of that INR75 crores, half of it has been paid in H1

items.statement: IAC Q2 revenue included INR35 crores tooling revenue; manufacturing revenue grew 15-16% YoY
items.quote: it included a substantial amount of tooling revenue in IAC amounting to INR35 crores. If we exclude that INR35 crores as a manufacturing revenue, it has increased by almost 15% to 16%

items.statement: Aftermarket H1 flat but expecting double-digit YoY growth in H2 and high single-digit for full year
items.quote: for the full year, we still expect a high single-digit growth rate for aftermarket in the current financial

items.statement: Capex guidance of Rs 80 billion for H2FY25
items.quote: We expect capex spends of Rs. 80billion in H2FY25.

items.statement: Q2FY25 capex spend was Rs 13.6 billion
items.quote: Our capex investments are gaining momentum post fund raise and in Q2FY25 we invested Rs. 13.6 billion.

items.statement: Three-year capex plan of Rs 500-550 billion
items.quote: At the cost of repetition, I am pleased to share that in September, we concluded deals worth about Rs. 300 billion or USD3.6 billion with the three global partners, namely Nokia, Ericsson, and Samsung, for supply of network equipment over a period of three years. This is one of the key steps towards the rollout of the company's transformative three-year capex plan of Rs. 500 to 550 billion.

items.statement: 4G population coverage target of 1.1 billion by March 2025 and 1.2 billion by September 2025
items.quote: The 4G expansion is in progress and our target is to achieve 4G population coverage of 1.1 billion by March 2025 and 1.2 billion by September 2025.

items.statement: 5G rollout to start in Q4FY25 in key geographies
items.quote: The rollout of 5G in key geographies will start in Q4FY25.

items.statement: Added 42,000 4G sites in Q2FY25, largest ever quarterly addition
items.quote: During the quarter, we added almost 42,000 4G sites which is the largest ever addition of 4G sites in the Company in a quarter.

items.statement: 4G data capacity increased ~14% and population coverage increased by ~22 million over last 6 months
items.quote: Resultantly, our 4G data capacity has increased by approximately 14% and 4G population coverage increased by approximately 22 million from 1.03 billion to 1.05 billion over las t 6

items.statement: Customer ARPU ex-M2M increased 7.8% QoQ; blended price increase ~16% but ARPU impact lower due to segments with no hike and subscriber downgrades
items.quote: Our customer ARPU ex M2M has increased by 7.8% QoQ.

items.statement: Entry-level tariff hike ~10%, higher consumption tiers up to 20%; further structural correction needed with higher increases at high-usage levels
items.quote: At the entry level the tariff increase was about 10% whereas at the higher levels or higher price levels, it was more pronounced or, let's say, in some cases as much as 20%.

items.statement: Lost 5.1 million subscribers with increased port-outs to BSNL (which did not hike tariffs); port-outs declining post-August per MNP data
items.quote: We registered a loss of 5.1 million subscribers with increased port outs to one operator which has not participated in the tariff hike.

items.statement: Postpaid customer base grew QoQ and YoY, driven partly by M2M; retail postpaid consistently increasing over last year
items.quote: I am pleased to report that in the postpaid segment, we have been able to increase our customer base on QoQ as well as YoY

items.statement: Revenue Rs 109.3 billion, up 4% QoQ; customer revenue up 5.6% QoQ driven by July 4 price increases
items.quote: The revenues for the quarter stood at Rs. 109.3 billion, a growth of 4% versus last quarter. More importantly, the customer revenues for the quarter grew by 5.6% versus last quarter, driven by price increases effective from July 4th this year.

items.statement: EBITDA ex-Ind AS 116 Rs 23.2 billion, up 10.5% QoQ; margin 21.3%, highest since merger
items.quote: The EBITDA excluding Ind AS 116 for a quarter was at Rs. 23.2 billion, improving by 10.5% on a quarter-on-quarter basis. This is the highest quarterly EBITDA since merger and the margin has improved to 21.3%.

items.statement: Bank debt reduced to Rs 32.7 billion from Rs 78.3 billion a year ago; cash balance Rs 136.2 billion sufficient for H2FY25 capex
items.quote: The debt from banks stood at Rs. 32.7 billion versus 78.3 billion at Q2FY24, a reduction of Rs. 45.8 billion during the last one year. The cash and bank balances stood at Rs. 136.2 billion as of September 38, 2024.

items.statement: Actively engaged with lenders for debt funding for long-term network expansion; discussions ongoing with promoters involved
items.quote: We remain actively engaged with our lenders for tying up debt funding towards the execution of our long term network expansion. I am personally involved in these discussions alongwith the promoters.

items.statement: Bank guarantee quantum ~Rs 24,000 crore over one year; industry requested waiver; not factored in business plan; awaiting government decision
items.quote: The quantum of bank guarantees is disclosed in our financials i.e. about 24,000 crores over a period of one year.

items.statement: Conversion of AGR/spectrum dues to equity permitted under 2021 reforms package if shortfall exists post-moratorium (expires in ~12 months); disclosed in notes to accounts
items.quote: Given that the moratorium expires in the next 12 months, it was considered prudent to make this disclosure.

items.statement: Raised Rs 240 billion equity in 2024 via FPO and preferential issuance
items.quote: During 2024, the company has raised Rs. 240 billion of equity.

items.statement: Launched Vi One converged broadband+mobility+OTT bundle in Mumbai, Gujarat, Maharashtra, and Kerala (via Asianet partnership); expanding to other markets
items.quote: In July, we signed a strategic partnership with Asianet, a leading broadband player in Kerala, and launched Vi One additionally across entire Kerala.

items.statement: Vi Movies & TV relaunched as multi-OTT aggregation platform on mobile and Connected TV; Vi App offers games, eSports, bill pay, shopping, OTT subscriptions, 350+ TV channels
items.quote: We have launched Vi Movies & TV in an all new avatar with all new apps for mobile on both, Android & IOS as well as for TV across almost all major operating systems.

items.statement: Vi Guarantee program offers 130GB additional data to 5G/new 4G handset customers; RED X postpaid plan at Rs 1,201 includes unlimited data, multiple OTTs, lounge access, international roaming in 29 countries
items.quote: We have received good response for Vi Guarantee program in the prepaid segment, a unique offer that provides 130GB of additional data to all 5G and new 4G handset customers.

items.statement: Industry needs further tariff rationalization to recover cost of capital; entry-level headroom limited, future hikes skewed to high-usage tiers; 5G metering will create monetization opportunity
items.quote: Hence, further tariff rationalization is needed for the industry to recover its cost of capital.

items.statement: AGR curative petition dismissed; government engagement ongoing; bank funding discussions in wait-and-watch mode pending AGR clarity; no timeline for debt raise
items.quote: Post the curative petition, everybody is in a bit of a wait and watch situation to see that how things are evolving, and so these things will move together, the engagement with the government on AGR and the banking discussions.

items.statement: Moratorium on AGR/spectrum dues expires in ~12 months; conversion to equity would occur to extent of payment shortfall per reforms package
items.quote: conversion will happen to the extent of shortfall of pay ment between whatever we can pay and what is the requirement of payment

items.statement: CEO Akshaya Moondra and promoters personally engaged in lender and government discussions
items.quote: I am personally involved in these discussions alongwith the promoters.

items.statement: Expect strong revenue growth in FY26 and even stronger bottom-line growth due to cost cutting measures
items.quote: I think that for financial year 26, I think as the penetration of lab-grown diamonds increases, we see revenue growth accelerating, and this coupled with the cost cutting measures that we have taken in our Customer Brand segment, we expect strong revenue growth in FY '26 and even stronger growth in bottom line because of our cost cutting measures.

items.statement: Expect meaningful debt reduction by end of FY25 and zero net debt by end of FY26
items.quote: So, as I mentioned earlier, we expect it to be significantly lower by about 150 to 180 crore by the end of this year. So, the net debt which is currently at 328 should be closer to 100 crore of net debt and subsequently by FY '26, the plan would be to be zero net debt.

items.statement: Allocated around 30 crore for infrastructure upgradation from preferential fund raise
items.quote: There is, however, some amount of upgradation of infrastructure that will take place which we have allocated I think around 30 crore for.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin from continuing operations reached 10.3% in Q2 FY25, up from 7.5% year-over-year
items.quote: On the profitability front, adjusted EBITDA expanded by 42% at Rs. 40 crore in Q2 of FY '25 versus Rs. 28 crore in the same period last year with adjusted EBITDA margins of 10.3% versus 7.5% last year.

items.statement: Owned Brands EBITDA margin reached 10.3% in Q2, a 575 bps year-over-year improvement
items.quote: In Owned Brands, our revenue grew by 7% year-over-year in Q2, while the EBITDA margin in this segment reached 10.3%, reflecting a substantial year-over-year improvement of 575 basis points.

items.statement: Customer Brands EBITDA margin improved 295 bps to 9.4% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: In the Customer Brands division, revenue in Q2 stood at 293 crore with an EBITDA margin of 9.4%, making an impressive 295 basis point improvement.

items.statement: Licensed Brand business had EBITDA margin of 16.5% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: In Q2 of FY '25, our Licensed Brand business maintained stable revenues at Rs. 57 crore on account of healthy flow of orders from our retail partners as well as the Direct-to-Consumer segment. It had an EBITDA margin of 16.5%.

items.statement: Launched cost optimization initiative expected to deliver annual savings of 40 to 50 crore, with one-time restructuring expense of 3.5 crore in Q2
items.quote: We have launched an extensive cost optimization initiative towards the end of Q2, which will extend into Q3 and is expected to deliver annual savings of 40 to 50 crore. In line with the same, we incurred a one-time restructuring expense of around 3.5 crore in this quarter.

items.statement: Expect strong consumer demand in Owned Brands segment approaching holiday season
items.quote: As we approach the holiday season, we expect strong consumer demand in this segment, setting us up for a promising end to the year.

items.statement: Lab-grown diamond penetration in B2B business currently 6%, expected to grow meaningfully in coming quarters and years
items.quote: Currently the penetration is only 6%, which we expect to grow meaningfully in the coming quarters and the years to come.

items.statement: Cost cutting measures include capacity rationalization due to less labor-intensive lab-grown diamond products
items.quote: so, you know, a lot of the cost cutting measures have actually been capacity rationalizations because as a business moves to more lab grown, we see less labor intensive product being manufactured, which means that we will be able to produce more value of orders with less manufacturing capacity

items.statement: Launched new direct-to-consumer fashion jewelry brand Renaei primarily on Amazon US targeting millennial and Gen Z consumers
items.quote: We recently launched a new direct-to-consumer fashion jewelry brand, Renaei, to be primarily sold on Amazon in the U.S. The brand is uniquely designed to meet an ever-growing affordable fashion jewelry demand among millennial and Gen Z consumers.

items.statement: Tested Enchanted Star collection with major US retail partner, extending Enchanted Disney Fine Jewelry brand with lab-grown diamonds
items.quote: Recently, we tested the Enchanted Star collection with a major retail partner in the U.S. This collection is an exciting extension of our Enchanted Disney Fine Jewelry brand brings lab-grown diamonds into our offerings, featuring engagement rings and fashion jewelry pieces.

items.statement: Plan to launch Owned Brands in UK in February for geographic expansion
items.quote: Currently, a large part of our brands is in the US. We plan to launch in February in the UK, and there will be some geographic expansion, which will lead to growth.

items.statement: Exclusive licensing arrangement with Disney provides moat in branded jewelry segment
items.quote: And then in the licensed brand segment, we have an exclusive licensing arrangement with Disney which gives us a moat and helps us sort of protect the business because Disney is a very well-recognized brand in the markets in which we operate.

items.statement: Net debt-to-equity ratio at 0.27 as of September 2024, down from 0.31 in June 2024 and 0.29 in September 2023
items.quote: Our net debt-to-equity ratio stands at a healthy 0.27 as on 30th September '24 versus 0.31 in June '24 and 0.29 in September of '23.

items.statement: Total net debt at Rs. 328 crore as of September 2024, down from Rs. 370 crore in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Our total net debt stands at Rs. 328 crore against Rs. 370 crore in Q1 of FY '25.

items.statement: Completed preferential fund raise of around 168 crore, proceeds to be used for debt reduction and potential acquisitions
items.quote: So, we obviously have, we are on the lookout for an acquisition, and we have not identified any acquisition immediately. So, once a fund raise is done, debt reduction will happen immediately.

items.statement: Cash and bank balances increased to Rs. 244 crore as of September 2024, up Rs. 58 crore from June 2024 and Rs. 60 crore from March 2024
items.quote: Our cash and bank balances and current investments stand at Rs. 244 crore, which is up by Rs. 58 crore from 30th June '24.

items.statement: Inventory typically peaks in September for holiday season build, expected to reduce in December and March
items.quote: However, the absolute inventory number, obviously, this is the start of the season and September usually represents a peak in terms of our inventory numbers, because we are usually building inventory for the October, November, December holiday season. So, we would expect to see a reduction in inventory subsequently, both in December as well as in March.

items.statement: Branded segment revenue reached Rs. 92 crore in H1 FY25, up 19% from Rs. 78 crore in H1 FY24
items.quote: Our branded segment reached revenues of Rs. 92 crore during the first half of the financial year versus 78 crore in the first half of FY '24, which is upped by 19%.

items.statement: Direct-to-Consumer India brand Irasva recorded revenues of Rs. 10 crore in H1 FY25 with four stores
items.quote: Our Direct-to-Consumer India brand Irasva, with a total of four stores across Mumbai, Ahmedabad and Hyderabad, recorded revenues of Rs. 10 crore in the first half of FY '25.

items.statement: Expect significant reductions in interest rates leveraging proceeds from gold business sale and favorable rate environment from Fed rate cuts
items.quote: Additionally, we expect to see significant reductions in interest rates as we leverage the proceeds from the sale of our gold business and anticipate a more favorable interest rate environment with recent rate cuts announced by the fed.

items.statement: Acknowledge near-term challenges but remain confident in long-term potential of branded business
items.quote: While we remain mindful of near-term challenges, our outlook on the long-term potential of our branded business remains exceptionally strong.

items.statement: Seeing return to growth in all segments in Q2, anticipate trend to continue or accelerate going forward
items.quote: So, I think we are seeing sort of a return to growth in all of our segments in quarter 2. We anticipate this trend to continue or accelerate going forward.

items.statement: Expect double-digit growth in licensed brand segment in coming quarters as inflation pressures abate
items.quote: Our cadence has been to try and grow in double digits in our licensed brand segment and which we expect sort of in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 revenue growth guidance 25%-30% and EBITDA margin 17%-18%
items.quote: We are sticking to our guidance because we are expecting increase in the volumes of ductile iron pipes which are the major contributors to our topline and the bottomline.

items.statement: Target to become net term debt free within next 12 months; FY25 term debt target Rs. 225-250 crores
items.value: Rs. 225-250 crores term debt by FY25 end
items.quote: Our FY25 guidance is to reduce the term debt to Rs. 225-Rs. 250 crores of which we are very optimistic of achieving.

items.statement: Rs. 1,000 crore capex plan; Rs. 700 crores incurred; balance Rs. 300 crores over next 9 months
items.quote: Out of this, approximately Rs. 700 crores has already been incurred and the balance Rs. 300 crores is expected to be incurred over the next 9 months.

items.statement: DI pipe capacity expanding from 3 lakh to 6.6 lakh metric tons; Phase 1 (1.4 lakh tons) in FY25, Phase 2 (2.2 lakh tons) in FY26
items.quote: JBIL is expanding its DI pipes capacity from 3 lakh metric tons to 6.6 lakh metric tons. Of this, 1.4 lakh metric tons, the remaining capacity from Phase 1 that is expected to be commissioned in FY25 while the Phase 2 capacity of 2.2 lakh metric tons is expected for commissioning in FY26.

items.statement: Ferro alloy capacity increasing from 1.6 lakh to 1.9 lakh metric tons by Q1 FY26
items.quote: The ferro alloy capacity will increase from 1.6 lakh metric tons to 1.9 lakh metric tons with client capacity expansion by Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Blast furnace capacity rising from 6.3 lakh to 7.5 lakh metric tons; one revamped, second by Q1 FY26
items.quote: Additionally, 1 blast fumace has already been revamped and commissioned with the second one expected to be completed by Q1 of FY26 boosting the total capacity from 6.3 lakh metric tons to 7.5 lakh metric tons.

items.statement: Sinter capacity raised to 9 lakh tons in FY24; additional 3 lakh tons by Q1 FY26 to reach ~12 lakh tons per annum
items.quote: And the center capacity was raised to 9 lakhs tons in FY24 and an additional 3 lakh tons is expected to be commissioned in Q1 of FY26, bringing the total to approximately 12 lakh metric tons per annum.

items.statement: H1 FY25 adjusted EBITDA margin 17% vs 14% in H1 FY24
items.quote: I am also very happy to share that the adjusted EBITDA margin for HI FY25 has been increased to 17% compared to 14% in H1 FY24.

items.statement: DI pipe order book covers next 6 months; volumes to increase incrementally each quarter targeting 4 lakh tons in FY25
items.quote: Regarding volumes, we expect volumes to increase incrementally on each quarter. So we will target to achieve 4 lakh ton this year and the coming year.

items.statement: DI pipe demand robust driven by JJM, AMRUT 2.0, irrigation schemes and government infrastructure spending
items.quote: The demand for ductile pipes, it is robust and we expect it to be robust because not only are we looking at the compression of the JIM scheme, we are also looking at the AMRUT 2.0.

items.statement: Specialized ferro alloy growth slow and steady; niche market exporting to 40 countries; capacity raised to 1.9 lakh tons
items.quote: As far as the specialized ferro alloy segment, it is a very niche market. Here, we are already exporting to around 40 countries, but we are one of the only manufacturers in the country to make this product on organized basis.

items.statement: DI pipe realizations expected similar levels +/-2-3%; ferro alloy realizations similar +/-2%; pig iron, TMT, sponge iron up ~Rs. 1,000/ton in H2
items.quote: Regarding DI we expect the relations to be at similar levels, maybe plus minus 2%-3% rather because we have the order booked for the coming 6 months.

items.statement: Coking coal prices substantially down vs previous quarters; coal cooled; iron ore flat; chrome ore up substantially
items.quote: The prices of coking coal compared to the previous few quarters are substantially down. The prices of coal have cooled down and the iron prices are more or less flat, but expectation the global markets as a downward buyers. Only Chrome Ore is going up substantially.

items.statement: DI pipe exports currently <1%; target ~5% of production with capacity expansion
items.quote: Going forward, we have a plan that with the increase in the capacity expansion, here export is negligible. It s less than 5%, it is less than 1%. So we are looking at exporting around 5%. So on the export market

items.statement: Net term debt Rs. 300-350 crores currently; target net term debt free in 12 months; FY25 term debt target Rs. 225-250 crores
items.quote: The total term debt is around Rs. 300-Rs. 350 crores right now. And looking at the EBITDA and the pending CAPEX which is going to be, the pending CAPEX is around Rs. 300 crores and the total term debt pending is Rs. 300 crores.

items.statement: Deferred tax assets consumed over last 3 quarters; ~Rs. 70-75 crores pending consumption in Q3; carry forward tax losses ~Rs. 500 crores remaining
items.quote: As far as deferred tax assets, which were in our books, we have consumed it in last 3 quarters and the pending which I think in the third quarter will be consumed is around Rs. 70-Rs. 75 crores.

items.statement: Value-added products (DI pipes + ferro alloys) revenue share 45-55% currently; target 65% by FY25 end; 75-80% by Q4 FY26
items.quote: Then it should reach to 65% by the end of the current financial year, and then once the second part III of the ductile expansion is completed and it is fully operationalized, we will be north of 75, that is broad idea.

items.statement: DI pipe EBITDA Rs. 22,000/ton; ferro alloy Rs. 25,000/ton; pig iron Rs. 5,000/ton; TMT Rs. 4,000/ton; sponge iron Rs. 3,000/ton in Q2 FY25
items.value: DI pipe Rs. 22,000/t; ferro alloy Rs. 25,000/t; pig iron Rs. 5,000/t; TMT Rs. 4,000/t; sponge iron Rs. 3,000/t
items.quote: For ductile iron pipe, it was Rs. 22,000 per ton, ferro alloy was 25,000, pig iron, it was around. 5,000, TMT was 4,000 and sponge iron 3000.

items.statement: Domestic DI pipe demand estimated 6-7 million tons this year; bid pipeline extremely robust
items.quote: Our internal team is working is that the demand of ductile iron pipes, this particular year will be in the region of 6-7 million tons and the bid pipeline range with that only.

items.statement: DI pipe sales: 25-30% direct to government; balance to EPC contractors executing government projects
items.quote: In some cases, we are selling around 25%-30% of the sales, it is directed to the government. The balance is to the EPC contractors who are executing the projects for the government.

items.statement: Fund release from government slower post-election across sectors including Jal Jeevan Mission; expect robust spending in next 4-5 months
items.quote: What we are seeing is that since the funds have not been released to a great extent after in the last 15 months, actually the government has a budget requirement to meet the expenditure, so over the next 4-5 months, we are expecting very robust spending to be coming.

items.statement: No new capex plan announced beyond current Rs. 1,000 crore; future plans on drawing board; finalization by end of financial year
items.quote: Right now, there is no CAPEX plan which we have announced, but definitely we are looking at certain opportunities, but it will take time.

items.statement: Future capex finalization will take more than 3-4 months, likely by end of financial year
items.quote: It will take some time. It will take more than 3-4 months, 5 months.

items.statement: No discussion with board on capital market fundraising for larger expansion; priority is debt reduction first
items.quote: Well, we look into it. Right now, it has not been discussed over here, with the board.

items.statement: Priority last 3 years was turnaround, stabilize operations, shift to value-added products; ~90% achieved
items.quote: Last 3 years we wanted, the priority was to tum around the company, stabilize the operation, go into value added products in a big way, convert our big iron and the hot metal to ductile iron pipe and go big on ferro alloys.

items.statement: Commissioned 35 TPH blast furnace gas boiler for waste gas utilization in captive power plant, reducing carbon emissions
items.quote: Furthermore, the company has also commissioned a 35 TPH blast furnace gas boiler as part of a green energy initiative. This project integrates waste gas utilization from the blast fumace into the captive power plant, reducing carbon emissions and enhancing sustainability.

items.statement: Stock split announced: each Rs. 10 equity share divided into 5 shares of Rs. 2 face value
items.quote: When amnounced the liquidity of the stock, the company has also announced a stock split dividing each equity share value Rs. 10 into 5 equity share with a face value for Rs. 2 each.

items.statement: Signed SPA to divest 5 BOT project subsidiaries to Indian Highways Concessions Trust at enterprise value INR5,718 crore, equity value INR2,539 crore
items.quote: Ashoka Concessions Limited, a subsidiary of the company, has entered into share purchase agreement with Indian Highways Concessions Trust inter alia for divestment of its 5 subsidiaries. The aggregate enterprise value of the transaction is either INR5,718 crores, subject to adjustment of cash and debt, translating into an equity value of INR2,539 crores.

items.statement: Agreed to acquire 34% equity of ACL plus CCDs from Macquarie SBI Infrastructure Investment and SBI Macquarie Infrastructure Trust for INR1,526 crore
items.quote: The company has entered into SPA to acquire 34% of equity of ACL, along with 7,741,250 Class A CCDs and 2,00,00,000 class B CCDs from Macquarie SBI Infrastructure Investment Private Limited and SBI Macquarie Infrastructure Trust for INR1,526 crores.

items.statement: Viva Highways to acquire 26% equity in Jaora Nayagaon Toll Road Company for INR150 crore
items.quote: Viva Highways Limited, a subsidiary of the company, to acquire investments of investors totalling 7,46,20,000 equity shares, comprising of 26% equity share s held in Jaora Nayagaon Toll Road Company private Limited at an aggregate consideration of INR150 crores

items.statement: Monetized land at Hinjewadi, Pune held by Viva Highways for INR453 crore
items.quote: Monetization of land. - Land owned by Viva Highways Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary, under its real estate portfolio situated at Hinjewadi, Pune, has been monetized for a total consideration of INR453 crores.

items.statement: Order book as on Sep 30, 2024 stands at INR11,104 crore; including post-Sep orders INR4,320 crore and L1 INR265 crore, total current order book INR15,424 crore
items.quote: Coming t o the order book status. As on September 30, 2024, our balance order book stands at INR11,104 crores. This excludes additional orders received from projects post September '24 worth INR4,320 crores and also excludes L1 of INR265 crores. The total of curren t order book stands at INR15,424

items.quote: The breakup as on September ' 30 is Road and railway project compromise around INR6,582 crores, which is 59.3% of the total order book. Among the road project order book, HAM projects are to the tune of INR844 crores and EPC road projects are worth INR5,185 crores, and railway is around INR844 crores. Power T&D accounts for INR3,939 crores, which is approximately 35.5% of the total order book. The

items.statement: FY25 revenue expected flattish YoY; EBITDA margin to improve by ~50 bps in H2 to ~8.5%; double-digit margins only from Q1 FY26
items.quote: So on the execution side, keeping in view the orders which have come in and their expected date of start of activities, we believe that the revenue top line may be flattish for this year, so what we have said or thought in the last quarter. As far as EBITDA concerned, we expect at least it should improve by 0.5% for the next 2 quarters.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth target 10-15% based on current and new order book
items.quote: FY '26, based on this order book, and maybe next order book, we should definitely look at after getting new orders, to grow by 10% to 15%.

items.statement: Bid pipeline INR1 lakh crore from NHAI, participating in INR65,000 crore; bids to be opened ~INR9,000 crore; expect to win INR4,000-5,000 crore in balance FY25
items.quote: So bid pipeline is there. Around INR1 lakh crore bidding is there from NHAI. Out of which, INR65,000, we'll be participating. There are bids to be opened of around INR9,000 crores which we already bid. And bid opening is yet to balance. And we hope we should pick up around INR4,000 crores to INR5,000 crores in balance part of the year.

items.statement: New projects bid at 11-12% margins; legacy fixed-price projects impacted by inflation
items.quote: We now continue to bid at double-digit margins, 11% to 12%. So these are for orders which were taken in the past, and the impact of -- as they were fixed price contract, the impact of inflation or increase in prices have had an impact on the margins.

items.statement: Consolidated debt INR6,881 crore as on Sep 30, 2024; standalone debt INR1,317 crore (INR109 cr equipment/term loans + INR1,209 cr working capital loans)
items.quote: Total consolidated debt as on 30th September 2024, stood at INR6,881 crores. The stand-alone debt is at INR1,317 crores, which comprises of INR109 crores of equipment and term loans and INR1,209 crores for working capital loans.

items.statement: Standalone working capital debt increased INR800-950 crore in 6-12 months due to elongated power sector working capital cycle; funded by subsidiary loans (INR950 cr) and bank loans
items.quote: So it's typically as one of the point s that we've given, is that working capital on the power sector which we had won a lot of contracts in '23, have been executed largely in these 2 years, 1.5 years, wherein the working capital cycle in the power sector is longer, elongated. That is the reason these working capital cycle has increased, which has been typically funded both by loan from subsidiari

items.statement: Expect working capital debt to reduce by INR300-400 crore by Mar-Jun 2025 as power projects complete
items.quote: So what we expect is by -- these projects will come to an end by March to June next year, and where we'll see this number is going down by INR300 crores to INR400 crores at least.

items.statement: Peak standalone debt reached; expect reduction from Q1 FY26 as monetization proceeds and operating cash flows materialize
items.quote: From a turnover perspective, it's a peak debt. But from perspective of realization of monetization money and a mix of new HAM projects and BOT prices coming up, we cannot immediately say what how they could peak out. But I think we should be close to a peak.

items.statement: Consolidated debt to reduce by INR3,000-3,500 crore by Mar 2025 from BOT/HAM asset sales; balance reduction post-Mar
items.quote: So by the end of this quarter -- by end of this year, we probably -- the INR6,800 will be used by debt, which is already on the 5 BOT projects of INR2,400. If that deal happens, that will go down. Certain debt on the HAM projects also will go down, which we intend to sell. So today, it's difficult to estimate what exactly, but we expect that at least of INR3,000 crores, INR3,500-odd crores of debt

items.statement: H1 FY25 capex INR33 crore; H2 FY25 planned capex INR35-40 crore
items.quote: So in H1, we did capex of approximately INR33 crores. And in H2, we may prepare another INR35 crores to INR40 crores. That's H2, sorry. Not FY, H2.

items.quote: The company has a received a completion certificate for its HAM project: Four -laning of NH-161 from Kandi to Ramsanpalle in the State of Telangana from August 2024. items.statement: Toll collection Q2 FY25 INR316 crore vs INR297 crore YoY (+6%)
items.quote: In Q2 FY '25, in our toll collection division, the company recorded a gross toll collection of INR316 crores as against INR297 crores in Q2 FY '24, recording a growth of 6%.

items.statement: Order inflow FY25 YTD ~INR6,000 crore
items.quote: Around INR6,000 crores.

items.statement: NIIF SPA for Jaora-Nayagaon and Chennai ORR expired; Chennai ORR stake consolidated, structuring debt for sale; Jaora-Nayagaon awaiting MPRDC approval for 26% transfer, also trying to acquire balance 26% from Macquarie
items.quote: So as far as NIIF SPA was concerned, it had a long stop date which has expired quite some time back. So presently, it is not on , the SPA is not live. But we continue to engage. We -- as far as Chennai ORR is concerned, we could consolidate our stakes. And we are in the process of structuring the debt on that and then take it to the market for sale. As far as JTC L is concerned, we are still await

items.statement: Expect to sign SPA for HAM projects in next couple of weeks (Q3 FY25)
items.quote: So we are -- as we have stated in the past, an d we are constantly engaging. And we expect that in the next couple of weeks, we should be able to sign on the SPA for the HAM projects also.

items.statement: Impairment reversal expected: ~INR800 crore at ACL level, ~INR250-300 crore at ABL level post BOT asset sale
items.quote: So there will be impairment at ACL level which will be reversed once these assets are sold off, which is almost -- at ACL balance sheet of almost INR800 crores. And at ABL balance sheet, there could be a reversal of approximately INR250 crores to INR300 crores post sale.

items.statement: ACL 34% acquisition from SBI Macquarie long stop date Jun 2025; expect completion Mar-May 2025

items.quote: See I don't think if we have to have similar facility then could be about INR200 crores to INR250 crores for the similar facility, but we don't know which direction we are going to expand, what product line we are going to expand.

items.statement: Target debt/EBITDA of 3x by FY26 from current 5x
items.quote: We are expecting to come close to 3 by FY '26. And if still things change, I think we should be there.

items.statement: Volume growth target of 30%-40% for industrial chemicals to achieve sales targets
items.quote: I can say that we are seeing, has to be growth by about 30%-40% volume growth to achieve the over sales target, what we have in our mind.

items.statement: Schedule M implementation driving shift to organized CDMO players; structural change expected to continue benefiting quality-focused manufacturers

items.statement: Using cash credit lines for interim working capital instead of withdrawing invested funds; interest cost offset by investment income

So, that is why finance cost is being borne. However, rest assured, the income that we have earned which is part of other income on the money kept in investments is similar to the interest cost that we are bearing.

items.statement: Rs 48 crore capex spent in H1 FY25 funded from internal cash flows; Rs 38 crore cash outflow for capex (Plant-6 land Rs 13 crore, Plant-2 extension)
items.quote: And the money spent for Plant-2 extension that we are working on the overall CAPEX cash amount was about Rs. 48 crores for both of these, and the cash outflow out of these was Rs. 38 crores. So, this outflow was taken care of from cash generated from our operations, the profits that we made.

items.statement: Dividend of Rs 5.5 per share (Rs 11.5 crore) paid for FY24 in October 2024
items.quote: The Company has paid a dividend of Rs. 5.5 per share amounting to Rs. 11.5 crore for FY24 in October 2024.

items.statement: Employee costs increased due to injectables staffing and 25% minimum wage hike in Uttarakhand; contractual labor varies with production volumes
items.quote: Yes, so this includes of course the injectables personal cost increase and the manpower, the minimum wages increase of 25% that is part of this. You are right in addition to the increments and production related increase. So, this should be a good base for you to consider.

items.statement: GLP-1 manufacturing capability not currently available; working with developmental labs but success uncertain
items.quote: Yes, currently we don't. Most of the GLP-1s, some of them are very, very complex products. But we are working with some developmental labs who can help us, but it's still out there. It's not very sure whether we will be successful.

items.statement: Liquidity position Rs 200 crore as of September 2024 despite Rs 48 crore capex in H1 FY25
items.quote: As on 30th September, the Company's liquidity position is at Rs. 200 crores despite CAPEX of Rs. 48 crores in H1 FY25.

items.statement: Export dossier acquisition and transfer process ongoing; will update on success
items.quote: Yes, so we had updated Abhishekji in the last call that we have acquired a few dossiers. And now that process of transfer is ongoing. So, as we get success, we will definitely come back and update.

items.statement: Strong positive feedback from customer audits of injectable facility; purchase orders received but revenue recognition awaits stability data
items.quote: We have got very, very good and very strong positive reviews from customer audits that have happened. And we have already purchased orders against which we are manufacturing just because we cannot sell before the stability data is finished.

items.statement: Peer's large Jammu capacity in different dosage forms (injectable antibiotics, cephalosporins); ample room for multiple organized players given 13,000 fragmented CMOs
items.quote: So, Ankitji, I will answer that in two ways. The first is that, whatever we understand, the capacities that are being put in Jammu by this player are of dosage forms and products that we do not play in. So, we are not present in injectable antibiotics, cephalosporins, penums or any of those and so one is the clear separation of dosage forms.

items.statement: CDMO business on open cost sheet basis; API price erosion impact on revenue but not margins; domestic API sourcing limits exposure
items.quote: Most of our business, especially CDMO is open cost sheet business. So, that's why a little bit impact might be there on the revenue number, but we don't see much of an impact on our margin numbers there. And API hit has already been there and you have seen our revenue numbers. So, in fact going forward, everyone is expecting that to stabilize right. So, we don't see our business being affected a l

items.statement: API price erosion stabilizing after COVID-driven domestic capacity additions; minimal import dependence reduces risk
items.quote: After the COVID period, a lot of domestic API manufacturers have stepped in, which is leading to some price erosion also. But we feel that this is now getting to a more or less stable regime.

items.statement: Appointed Anand Sen as Additional Director designated Independent Director effective 14 Nov 2024
items.quote: I'm delighted to inform you that the Board has appointed Mr. Anand Sen, as an Additional Director of Tega Industries Limited designated as an Independent Director of the Company with effect from 14th November, 2024.

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY25 revenue growth guidance of 15% year-on-year for both consumable and equipment businesses
items.quote: We hold on to our guidance of 15% growth year-on-year. That is - We have a good H2 actually.

items.statement: Maintained FY25 EBITDA margin guidance of 20-22% for consumables and 10-12% for equipment, blended ~20-21%
items.quote: Generally, we have been able to have a consumables EBITDA margin of close to anything in the range of 20% to 22%. And then in equipment, we have set our expectation of 10% to 12%. On a blended rate, we see any EBITDA margin for the group at around 20%, 21%, and we are confident of these numbers.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin 13% vs 22% YoY due to one-time contract accounting expense of INR 17-20 cr
items.quote: The EBITDA margin has been muted due to the contract accounting, leading to a onetime expense in Q2, which has been charged off in the current quarter and shall lead performance in the subsequent period.

items.statement: One-time expense of INR 17-20 cr charged in Q2 FY25 related to inventory and installation for projects
items.quote: The onetime impact will be close to about INR 17 crores to INR 20 crores.

items.statement: Normalized EBITDA margins expected to revert from Q3 FY25 onwards
items.quote: Yes, we are confident, both our revenue estimate and the EBITDA margin estimate what we did, we shall be able to have those things going forward from Q3 onwards.

items.statement: Group order book INR 605 cr as of Sep 2024 including orders crystallizing in next 6-7 months
items.quote: We have a firm order book at a group level of INR 605 crores as at September 2024 end vis-a-vis an order without considering the long-term orders like the NMDC order in ML.

items.statement: Shipment delays and order deferments due to geopolitical issues; confident of recouping in next 2 quarters
items.quote: There have been certain delays in shipments and deferment of orders by customers, which we are confident of recouping in the next few quarters.

items.statement: Geopolitical issues causing shipment delays; teams made more agile to address disruptions
items.quote: These are mainly due to geopolitical issues, Chirag. And we would like these to get over ASAP, but we'll not be able to tell when.

items.statement: Major capex drive of $35-40 million including Chile project and Dahej plant; additional $10 million over FY25-26
items.quote: We have gone into a major capex drive of about $35 million to $40 million, which includes this capex of Chile as well as the Dahej plant.

items.statement: Chile project construction started; targeting commercialization by June-July FY26
items.quote: Earlier we had given an estimate of June, July of the next financial year. So we currently think we should be able to have the construction complete.

items.statement: Quarterly depreciation ~INR 26 cr; expected to continue at this level subject to capex capitalization
items.quote: Yes. So, these are the quarterly numbers. And for -- you should consider these are the quarterly numbers, which will be reflected in the subsequent quarters as well.

items.statement: Chinese competitors not considered serious in consumables due to service component; some Chinese-owned mines order from Tega
items.quote: Chinese competitors in the mining, have not been able to sustain products from overseas because in the mining and the consumables that we have there, there is a very large component of service and we have sales and service team all over the world.

items.statement: Consumable segment revenue grew INR 58 cr YoY in H1; equipment segment moderated to INR 82 cr from INR 91 cr
items.quote: The total revenues of the consumable business segment grew by INR 58 crores over the same period last year, whereas the equipment business segment moderated to INR 82 crores from INR 91 crores same period last year.

items.statement: Inventory increased as of Sep 30 due to shipment delays; inventory will convert to revenue in subsequent periods
items.quote: We even have an increase in the overall inventory levels, if you see as at 30th September, because of these delays what we have been speaking -- talking about. So all of this, inventory turns into revenue in the subsequent period.

items.statement: Bullish on copper demand driven by energy transition, digital trends and traditional growth; bullish on gold prices
items.quote: We believe that the copper demand shall be increasing due to a combination of three key themes that is traditional economic growth and the newer themes of energy transition and digital, that is primarily the data centers.

items.statement: Hopes to maintain ~100% revenue growth for full FY25 and expects new TPW range starting early next year to add volumes and revenue
items.quote: We have grown by almost 100% in the first half and we are hoping to maintain this kind of growth for this year. And once we add the new range that we are looking at beginning next year, we are hopeful that that will add numbers as well as revenue.

items.statement: TPW manufacturing facility investment likely around INR 3 crores, orders placed, targeting start early next year
items.quote: This particular TPW line that we are looking at, the value of this investment is likely to be in the range of about INR3 crores.

items.statement: Disclosed plan to set up new TPW manufacturing facility in North; orders placed, aiming to start early next year
items.quote: only, we have just made a disclosure to the exchange that we are looking at setting up a manufac turing facility for TPW. That's the plastic range of table, pedestal, and wall. The orders for the plant have been placed and we are hoping to start this sometime early next year

items.statement: Seasonal product leads to full booking in season and idle capacity off-season; adding machinery at different places to enhance capacity
items.quote: Utilization, you know, as I just mentioned a while ago, this being a very seasonal product, in the season we are kind of booked. But during the off-season, we have some idle capacity.

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA margin improved to 2.68%; BLDC fans give slightly better margin but overall improvement driven by volume growth and cost optimization
items.quote: Additionally, our EBITDA margins improved to 2.68%, underscoring our focus on operational efficiency and cost management.

items.statement: Added electric heaters and kettles to diversify portfolio and cushion fan off-season; first year in category, see potential but cannot commit numbers
items.quote: Products such as electric heaters and kettles have been added with a view to diversify our portfolio, as well as to cushion the off-season in fans.

items.statement: Short-term loans/advances up INR 2 crores due to new MSME payment legislation requiring reduced credit terms; funds used for vendor bill discounting
items.quote: Yes, this is actually a requirement that came to us because, you know, of the new legislation that MSME vendors have to be made payment in a certain number of days to meet that commitment of, you know, reduced credit t erms to our vendors, we had to increase limits, which are being used for bill discounting of our vendors

items.statement: Claims to be only listed player in OEM/ODM fan space; differentiates via R&D, quality, timely delivery, seasoned management
items.quote: Not out of place to report that we are perhaps one of the only listed companies in this space and that differentiates us from the competition.

items.statement: Combined production capacity over 12 million units per year across three plants spanning 3 lakh sq ft
items.quote: These plants have a combined production capacity of over 12 million units per year, making us one of the most capable fan producers in the country.

items.statement: Indian fan market growing strongly due to urbanization, residential construction, PM Awas Yojana, rising disposable income, and preference for energy-efficient BLDC fans
items.quote: The Indian fan market is experiencing strong growth, fuelled by rapid urbanization and increased residential construction. Initiatives like PM Awas Yojana, which aims to expand affordable housing, provide us with a direct opportunity to meet the rising demand for the same, particularly energy efficient options like our BLDC fans.

items.statement: Emphasizing cost optimization and operational efficiency to achieve percentage improvement in margins
items.quote: We are also emphasizing on cost optimization and looking at ways to further improve operational efficiency where possible to achieve some percentage improvement in margins.

items.statement: Seasoned management team with over five decades industry experience; next generation equally enthusiastic about growth
items.quote: With a seasoned management team bringing over fiv e decades of industry experience and a robust vendor network, we are well-posed for sustained growth and value creation for all
