items.quote: So as far as the covenant breaches are concerned, it is largely what you have said, Abhijit one is gross NPA, second is net NPA, and third is a rating downgrade which has happened by CARE, which was in the month of September .

items.quote: In Q2 FY25 we have raised 1513 crores, including direc t assignment of 435 crores , and till H1 we are able to raise INR 4060 crores, including direct assignment of 915 crores.

items.quote: The NIM of the company has reduced by 15 bps to 11.48% from and increased by 37 bps on year-on-year basis. QoQ drop is largely due to the higher write off taken in this quarter.

items.quote: Our MSME AUM has grown to Rs.620 crore, with almost 78% of portfolio being secured.

items.statement: Field officer incentive ~25-30% of salary (Rs 3,500-4,000 on Rs 15,000 base); never exceeded this proportion

items.statement: PAR 0 composition higher for customers with Fusion plus 3+ and 4+ lender relationships; 85% of customers in top 5 states current or up to 30 DPD
items.quote: We have looked at our customers in the top five states, and what we saw that 85% customers are still current. They are either current or up to 30, but they are still, in the last six months, they have not gone beyond 30.

items.quote: As on September 30th, 2024 the pre-provision operating profit is INR 284 crore s increased by 17.39% on a year-on-year basis and decreased by 4.67% on a quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.quote: The DA outstanding as of September 30, 2024 is approximately 11.70% of the total book, and we will continue to do so as per the market condition.

items.quote: We have implemented new loan origination and customer management tech pl atform, which has been built in -house, once fully rolled out, it will bring in better operational efficiency and scalability.

items.statement: Customer loyalty program in early phase showing encouraging response and improved attendance where launched
items.quote: We have been working on our customer loyalty program while it is in an early phase. We have received encouraging response from our customers, and we have seen improvement in their attendance wherever this program has been launched.

items.statement: Illegal agencies influencing borrowers in pockets of Eastern UP and other areas; sector working with state administrations to curb
items.quote: the point I am trying to drive is that, yes there are some small events here and there, which keep on happening like we have seen even in Eastern UP some of these events.

items.quote: During the quarter, we have successfully expanded our capacity by 118 beds, comprising 52 beds at Lucknow and 66 beds at Patna.

items.statement: Noida facility construction progressing, anticipated opening Q1 FY2026

items.quote: So if you look at the matured one, you will see that the margins have moved around 25%, 25.5%, 25.3%. So yes, if you look at the last several quarters, it does appear that they are reasonably stable.

items.quote: ARPOB grew by 6.2% to INR 67,059 in Q2 FY25, driven by tariff increases in Gurugram and Indore and changes in our case mix.

items.statement: Patna PPP revenue share ~11% (volumes ~19%); Lucknow scheme revenue negligible; group cash/TPA ~80-85%

items.quote: We continue to strengthen our clinical capabilities and on-boarded over 25 doctors in Q2 FY25.

items.quote: In a hospital that's 13 - 14 years old, we have still hired in very senior talen t. If I recall, that was almost somewhere around 80 senior doctors that had been hired in last year in a 13 - 14-year-old facility

Aligned with Government of India's pivotal initiatives like Startup India, Digital India, and Make in India, ISF aims to collaborate with over 50,000 startups.

items.statement: Global spend management market growing 10.2% CAGR; India market 15.5% CAGR; demand driven by efficiency, transparency, compliance needs
items.quote: As per the industry articles, the global spend management market is expanding at 10.2% annually, while the Indian market is estimated to expand at a CAGR of 15.5%.

items.statement: Pre-sales target of Rs 850 crore for FY25 with seven new project launches totalling GDV of Rs 1,150 crore
items.quote: Looking ahead, we aim for pre-sales of Rs. 850 crores for the current financial year with plans to launch seven new projects totaling to a GDV of Rs. 1,150 crores.

items.statement: Ongoing projects sold 5.39 lakh sq ft of 6.09 lakh sq ft generating Rs 1,370 crore with Rs 767 crore receivable; unsold inventory 2.71 lakh sq ft with GDV Rs 395 crore
items.quote: In our ongoing projects, we have sold 5.39 lakh square feet out of a total of 6.09 lakh square feet, generating approximately Rs. 1,370 crores with a receivable of approximately Rs. 767 crores.

items.statement: Future pipeline of 18 projects with over 9 lakh sq ft carpet area and GDV exceeding Rs 5,000 crore; 67% value luxury, 14% luxury, 7% mix, 12% commercial
items.quote: Looking at our future pipeline, we are awaiting upcoming projects with an estimated carpet area of over 9 lakh square feet for sale, approximately 67% of this is in the value luxury projects, 14% is in the luxury, and 7% is the mix of value-luxury and luxury.

items.statement: Raised Rs 343 crore via preferential allotment (Rs 243 crore) and convertible warrants (Rs 100 crore); received Rs 269 crore in Oct 2024, balance within 18 months for land acquisition, working capital, general corporate purposes
items.quote: We have raised Rs. 343 crores via preferential allotment of equity shares amounting to Rs. 243 crores and an additional Rs. 100 crores via issue of convertible share warrants.

items.statement: Approximately 40% of raised funds allocated for new business development and land acquisition to be expended before March 2025
items.quote: So, mainly the objects of the fundraise is also for business development, so a good portion of that would be, roughly around 40% would be for new BD and land acquisition.

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA grew 16% YoY to Rs 128 crore; Q2 FY25 EBITDA Rs 64 crore vs Rs 63 crore YoY; PAT grew 97% YoY in H1 and 88% YoY in Q2
items.quote: EBITDA grew 16% year-on-year to Rs. 128 crores in H1 FY '25 versus Rs. 111 crores in H1 FY '24.

items.statement: Average realization Q4 FY24 Rs 53,650/sq ft, Q1 FY25 Rs 51,116/sq ft, Q2 FY25 Rs 48,366/sq ft; unsold inventory estimated at Rs 55,500/sq ft based on last three quarters average
items.quote: So, if you see our average realization quarter-on-quarter, Q4 average realization was about 53,650, Q1 was 51,116 to be precise, and this quarter was about 48,366.

items.statement: Construction cost seeing steady labor price increases but no substantial hike; labor shortfall across industry may marginally impact costs
items.quote: In terms of construction cost, we are seeing that labor prices have been going up steadily, which obviously will impact our construction cost. But we do not see a very substantial hike in the construction cost, it's normally steady.

items.statement: Value luxury segment (Rs 1-3 crore) showing steady growth in both realization and velocity; commercial segment seeing big demand; luxury segment doing well but prices expected to stay steady
items.quote: So, the traction we are seeing right now, which has always been steady has been the value luxury concept where it is between Rs. 1 crores and Rs. 3 cores. So, that is a constant segment in which there has been steady growth.

items.statement: H1 FY25 revenue mix: 40.9% from luxury units, 59% from value luxury units; upcoming pipeline 67% value luxury, 14% luxury, 7% mix, 12% commercial
items.quote: 40.9% of revenue came from sales of luxury units and 59% of revenue from sales of value luxury units.

items.statement: Marinagar project: first phase approvals received with live IoD for two buildings, five more buildings planned, design underway, targeting big launch next year; Girgaonkarwadi to commence following year
items.quote: In terms of Marinagar we have already got the first phase of approvals where we already have live IoD in two upcoming buildings there. There would be slight minor amendments in the plan in terms of adding five more buildings in the redevelopment phase.

items.statement: Bandra project: first phase approvals received, design and technical details being worked out, targeting launch between Q2 and Q3 next year
items.quote: So, things are moving positively in the Bandra planning. I think like we informed earlier, we already have the first phase of approvals. We are looking at the larger piece, so design and a lot of technical details are getting worked out as we speak.

items.statement: Suraj Vibe commercial project on Tulsi Pipe Road: ~1 lakh sq ft, RERA underway, part of launch pipeline for this year, good client interest
items.quote: So, on Tulsi Pipe Road we have approximately 1 lakh of square feet. The RERA is underway, which is also part of our launch pipeline for this year.

items.statement: RERA approvals taking longer due to increased compliances from recent circular, extending timelines for project launches
items.quote: Normally RERA approvals take some time. The number of compliances from RERA standpoint also has increased in the recent circular. So, normally it does take time to get that approval compared to earlier.

items.statement: Weighted average cost of debt at 13%; debt increased as of September due to approval-related costs for upcoming launches (Tulsi Pipe Road and Parkview 1); fundraise completed after September
items.quote: To answer your question, the cost of debt remains at the same level, 13% weighted average cost of capital.

items.statement: Collections grew 90% YoY in Q2 FY25 and 46% YoY in H1 FY25 due to new project launches and higher sales volume
items.quote: Collections grew 90% year-on-year in quarter two FY '25 and 46% year-on-year in H1 FY '25 on account of new project launches and higher sales volume.

items.statement: Pre-sales grew 26% YoY in Q2 FY25 and 13% YoY in H1 FY25 despite seasonally weak quarter; realizations grew 10% YoY in Q2 and 12% YoY in H1
items.quote: Pre-sales grew growth rate of 26% year-on-year in Q2 FY '25 and 13% in H1 FY '25 despite a seasonally weak quarter and the occurrence of some inauspicious period during the quarter.

items.statement: Combined receivables of Rs 1,162 crore from sold and unsold ongoing portfolio expected to materialize between FY25 and FY29
items.quote: The combined receivables of Rs. 1,162 crores from sold and unsold portion of our current ongoing portfolio are expected to materialize between FY '25 and FY '29.

items.statement: MMR inventory overhang steady at 14 months as of Q3 2024; affordable segment 32% of Mumbai inventory; peripheral central suburbs 30% of Mumbai available units
items.quote: Compared to the previous quarter, the inventory overhang in the MMR remained steady at 14 months by the end of Q3 2024.

items.statement: Targets ROE 20% and ROCE 25% for full year FY25
items.quote: We continue to remain on track to achieve the return on equity of 20% and ROCE of 25% for the full year with ROE of 11% and ROCE of 15% for the half-year ended September 30, 2024.

items.statement: Aims to become 1,000-bed hospital chain within next 2-3 years
items.quote: As previously announced, we are steadfast to become a 1,000-bed hospital chain within the next 2-3 years.

items.statement: Raipur Hospital to commence operations in Q4 FY25
items.quote: The Raipur Hospital, a 160-bed facility, will commence operations from Q4 FY25.

items.statement: Expects double-digit revenue growth in H2 FY25 after flat H1
items.quote: Hopefully, we should be able to deliver on that. First half was slightly out of our control because of the local issues and the floods in Tripura. Hopefully, we should be able to deliver in the second half, and especially with the Raipur hospital being commissioned in Q4, that should add more flip to the functioning.

items.statement: Maintenance capex runs INR 8-10 crore annually
items.quote: The current maintenance capex varies between INR8 crores to INR10 crores on an annual basis. This is more or less standard.

items.statement: Agartala oncology block PET CT commissioned Nov 2024; LINAC by Feb 2025; full ops 6-8 months after
items.quote: We have already started with the PET scan for this department and we are awaiting the installation of the LINAC. Once the oncology department is in full-fledged operations, we expect it to give a revenue of almost 20 crores annually after its maturity. Siddhi Gandhi: And when will it start working full-fledged? Any timeline for that? Management: So, as I said, the PET scan is already on and the LI

items.statement: Howrah orthopedic surgical robot to be available by end of year
items.quote: We are in the process of procuring an orthopedic surgical robot for this hospital as well. The facility shall be available by the end of the year.

items.statement: Dum Dum plans full-fledged cardiothoracic surgery setup and clinical revamp
items.quote: The company intends to commence a full-fledged cardiothoracic surgery setup and is revamping its other clinical offerings in this hospital as well to further strengthen its scope of service.

items.statement: Group ARPOB INR 36,700 in H1 FY25
items.quote: Notably, our ARPOB stands at INR36,700, aligned with our commitment to serving the aspiring population of the society with higher disposable income in the middle to higher income segment.

items.statement: Group bed occupancy 54% on amalgamated basis
items.quote: The company-level bed occupancy rates stood at 54% on an amalgamated basis.

items.statement: Group ALOS reduced to 3.51 days in H1 FY25 from 3.98 in H1 FY24
items.quote: The ALOS has reduced from 3.98 in H1 last year to 3.51 in H1 2025. The same is on account of our continuous efforts towards changing the case mix.

items.statement: Salt Lake ARPOB rose to ~INR 39,500 in H1 FY25 from INR 33,850; inpatient volume up 13% vs trailing H2
items.quote: ILS Hospital Salt Lake is an 85-bed surgical excellence hospital. The ARPOB for this hospital has risen from INR33,850 to almost INR39,500 in H1 FY25. Additionally, there has been a 13% increase in patient volume in comparison to trailing H2.

items.statement: Salt Lake ALOS reduced to 2.77 days from 3.19 YoY
items.quote: In our pursuit of optimizing services, we have been able to reduce our length of stay to 2.77 days from 3.19 on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Agartala inpatient volumes up 12% QoQ; ALOS down to 3.08 from 3.35 days
items.quote: The inpatient volumes have increased by 12% on a quarter-and-quarter basis, combined with a reduction of length of stay to 3.08 days from 3.35 days.

items.statement: Dum Dum ARPOB ~INR 41,400 in Q2; ALOS down to 4.43 from 5.22 days YoY
items.quote: The Dum Dum Hospital has recorded an ARPOB of approximately INR41,400 for the quarter. In line with our intent to reduce the length of stay of this hospital, the length of stay has reduced to 4.43 days compared to 5.22 in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Howrah inpatient volume up ~22.8% QoQ; ARPOB up 21% YoY in H1; ALOS down to 3.31 from 3.87 days
items.quote: The inpatient volume has seen an increase of almost 22.8% from the previous quarter. ARPOB of H1 FY25 has increased by 21% on a Y-o-Y basis and the length of stay has also come down to 3.31 days compared to 3.87 days in the previous fiscal.

items.statement: Bangladesh patient flow (~5% of Agartala volumes) disrupted in Aug-Sep; recovering from Nov
items.quote: So, roughly, Bangladesh volumes in our Agartala Hospital is almost 5% of our patient volumes, which was impacted in the month of August and September. It is in November that we are seeing a re-trickling of that again.

items.statement: Local issues and floods in Tripura impacted Q2 volumes; expecting uptick from Q3
items.quote: Unfortunately, in the previous quarter, because of local issues and some natural calamities in the areas where we end up operating in, we could not get the volumes which we generally end up getting in quarter 2. But hopefully, with the situation having been corrected, we can see an uptick in the volumes from this quarter which will end up giving you that effect you are wanting to see.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 revenue INR 106 cr, EBITDA INR 26 cr, margin 24%; H1 PAT INR 25 cr, PAT margin 12%, EBITDA margin 24.2% (+80 bps)
items.quote: Revenues for Q2 FY25 stood at INR106 crores with EBITDA of INR26 crores and a margin of 24%. PAT for H1 stood at INR25 crores with a 12% PAT margin and the first six months witnessed a 5.2% year-on-year growth. EBITDA margin has increased by 80 basis points to 24.2% with a slight increase of 2% in EBITDA for the quarter to INR26.3 crores.

items.statement: Finance costs down 58% YoY due to debt reduction
items.quote: Finance costs have come down by 58% on account of reduction of debt reflecting our efficient financial management.

items.statement: 94% of patient business from cash and insurance-paying patients
items.quote: Moreover, due to our neighbourhood model, approximately 94% of our patient business continues to be from cash and insurance-paying patients only.

items.statement: Top 10 specialties contribute 80% revenue; key: gastroenterology, general surgery, nephrology, cardiology
items.quote: So, the top 10 specialties are diversified. 80% of our revenue comes from the, from 10 departments, a majority of which are gastroenterology, general surgery, nephrology, cardiology.

items.statement: Focusing on short-stay departments (gastro, urology, orthopedics, cardiology) to raise ARPOB and volumes
items.quote: We are focusing on other short-stay departments like gastroenterology, urology, and are ramping up numbers. Overall, the length of the stay coming down is a good phenomenon for us as we will be in a position to take more patients across all our hospitals.

items.statement: Manipal acquired AMRI and Medical Hospitals, becoming major force in East; no other landscape changes
items.quote: So, there has been a change in the competitive landscape with the acquisition of AMRI hospitals by Manipal. That is the only change which we have seen in the eastern part of the country. Apart from that, Manipal has also acquired Medical Hospitals. So, Manipal has become a force in the eastern part of the country over the past one or two years. Apart from that, there has not been any other change

items.statement: Ranchi expansion awaiting Jharkhand regulatory clearances; delayed by state elections
items.quote: No, the Ranchi expansion has not been cancelled. I think we are awaiting some regulatory clearances from the government of Jharkhand. Currently, there are elections in Jharkhand. So, that process is getting delayed. As soon as we have some clarity on the regulatory approvals, we will update the investors accordingly.

items.statement: West Bengal operates Swasthya Sathi scheme (similar to Ayushman Bharat); PMJAY applies in Agartala and Raipur
items.quote: West Bengal has a scheme called Swasthya Sathi by which is very similar to Ayushman Bharat where people under a particular income category are covered by it. So, that is what is the predominant healthcare scheme in West Bengal. Apart from that, in our other hospitals of Agartala and even in Raipur, we do have PMJAY which is applicable.

items.statement: Agartala oncology block expected INR 20 cr annual revenue at maturity
items.quote: Once the oncology department is in full-fledged operations, we expect it to give a revenue of almost 20 crores annually after its maturity.

items.statement: Raipur hospital expected to break even at EBITDA level in 15-16 months post commissioning
items.quote: Generally, our hospitals, our latest hospital of Howrah broke-even in 8 months from the rate of commissioning on an EBITDA basis on a month-on-month level, but we understand Raipur will be a new market for us. We are hoping that we will be able to break even by around the 15-16 month mark, post which it should contribute positively to the EBITDA of the hospital.

items.statement: Management will not provide forward-looking revenue or margin numbers but expects H2 to be stronger than H1 based on historical seasonality and a strong order book.
items.quote: For coming 6 months I will not be able to make any forward -looking statement, but what I can assure you is that we are looking at a good order book.

items.statement: Order book is described as very nicely placed and strong, with confirmed orders for February and March and two large orders (INR22 cr and INR7-8 cr) already intimated to the exchange.
items.quote: Our order book is looking very nicely placed. Our endeavor is to grow last year's number.

items.statement: No sign of recession; order booking is very strong and two large international orders (Switzerland, France) have been won recently.
items.quote: No. Mr. Arora, our order booking is very strong and our performance is there in front of you. So there is no recession, nothing which we, kind of, have to worry about.

items.statement: H1 EBITDA margin was ~10.6% (INR12.62 cr on INR119 cr); full-year margin historically ~15% due to fixed costs and H2 revenue skew.
items.quote: Our EBITDA has gone up by 94% from INR 6.5 crores last year to INR12.62 crores this year.

items.statement: H1 FY25 revenue INR119 cr, up 68% YoY from INR70.91 cr.
items.quote: In terms of top line, we have done about INR119 crores as our top line, which is 68% higher than the last year's number, which was around INR70 crores.

items.statement: FY24 full-year revenue was INR237 cr, with ~70% (INR167 cr) generated in H2.
items.quote: If we compare it to last year, out of INR237 crores, we only did INR70 crores in the first half of the year. The rest of the business was in the second half.

items.statement: Opened new Kolkata office with a 24-year industry veteran leading a new team to tap eastern India clients (plywood, steel, cement, hardware).
items.quote: We've opened our Kolkata office. We've hired a new team under the leadership of a gentleman who has about 24 years of work experience in the MICE industry.

items.statement: Headcount increased from 50-55 (Mar 2024) to 79-80 currently, including Kolkata team; plans to hire 2-3 more leaders in next 2-3 months.
items.quote: We have increased our manpower. We have from a number of about 50 -55 till 31st of March. We are currently about 79 -80.

items.statement: Working capital increased to >INR50 cr post-IPO from ~INR30 cr a year ago; management says current level is comfortable for growth plans.
items.quote: Sir, we have working capital more than INR50 crores. You can see the result s, INR50 crores plus

items.statement: No fixed formula linking revenue to working capital needs due to varied payment terms across domestic, international, and wedding segments.
items.quote: There is no set formula because we have different payment terms for different clients. Some international businesses have a different set of rules. Some domestic have different.

items.statement: B2C launch (Book My Yatra portal) underway: hiring CTO and tech team, targeting Kumbh Mela for religious tourism; will go slow to avoid burning profits.
items.quote: We have a portal, which is called Book My Yatra, which is, the compliance is all done. We are in a process of hiring our leadership. There is a CTO, which needs to be hired.

items.statement: ~20% of H1 revenue from new clients; 80% from existing clients; high retention due to repeat dealer/conference business.
items.quote: Just a ballpark figure maybe out of the 119, just about 20% would be new customers. Maybe, I could be wrong. Remaining would be the old customers.

items.statement: Entered cement industry with large volumes; empanelled with plywood, steel TMT, hardware companies in East; won insurance, banking, auto, cement clients.
items.quote: There are some plywood companies, the wooden companies, which have empaneled us. There are some steel TMT companies, which have empaneled us. There are other cement companies, which have empaneled us.

items.statement: Competes with large players like Thomas Cook, SOTC, MakeMyTrip, EaseMyTrip, Ebix; claims to be one of the leading pure-play listed MICE companies in India.
items.quote: Maybe it is Thomas Cook, maybe it is SOTG, maybe it is MakeMyTr ip, maybe it is EaseMyTrip, it could be Ebix. All these kinds of companies are our competitors. And I can proudly state that we are one of the leading players in the MICE industry in terms of the Indian companies.

items.statement: Airfare/crude oil changes do not affect margins because costs are hedged at quote time; ticket cost variance (INR2,000) is irrelevant to profitability.
items.quote: Frankly, I would not see any impact of reduction in crude oil in terms of air ticket business. But having said that, it does not matter really. Our profitability, when we pick up the business, we have a fixed cost of airlines.

items.statement: Management will consult merchant banker and may disclose order book by mid-next week after investor feedback that SEBI permits order-book disclosure for service companies.
items.quote: We shall by middle of next week come back to you with the order book numbers and I'm sure you'll be happy to see those numbers.

items.statement: Business is discretionary but historically resilient; only downturn was COVID; corporate incentive spend rises when sales slow.
items.quote: We have seen steady growth from the first year, apart from the two bloodshed years of COVID. We have never seen a drop. Now I would politely differ here. You know, when a company does not sell goods, they have to give more incentives so that they can motivate you as a dealer or me as a distributor to work harder.

items.statement: IPO proceeds removed working capital constraints and cost of funds, enabling larger order execution without bank borrowing.
items.quote: Once we have funds available, there is no cost of funds, the interest part is saved, because we used to take money from banks and we used to, there is a cost of money also.

items.statement: No dividend or buyback mentioned; focus on growth and execution.
items.quote: We would like to take this opportunity to thank our shareholders and we appreciate the trust you have given, you put in us and you are our shareholders and we look forward to doing well in future also.

items.statement: Wedding segment entered aggressively in FY25; two large wedding orders won (numbers to be disclosed later).
items.quote: Perhaps I can share with you, we, since you've been so sure about the forward-looking statement, we picked up two huge weddings also.

items.statement: No contract labor used; all tour managers are permanent employees; local vendors handle on-ground setup.
items.quote: We do not have any need for contract labor. For example, if we operate a group in Goa, we need to do a stage setup, sound setup and some decor. We wo uld give it to a local vendor, t hat local vendor will get his team and take care of it

items.statement: Corporate business pauses during festivals (Diwali, Christmas, New Year) as dealers travel with families; not in B2C yet.
items.quote: Whenever there is a Diwali, Holi, Karwa Chauth, New Year, Christmas, our business goes down because people do not travel on a corporate mission or the dealers do not travel.

items.statement: Subsidiary is Mach Conventions and Voyages Private Limited; Mach Films is not a subsidiary.
items.quote: We have only one subsidiary company which is Mach Conventions and Voyages Private Limited. Mach Sales is not our subsidiary company.

items.statement: Metal demand looking good from November; strong demand in FMCG, industrial chemicals, MSMEs; East and South regions picking up
items.quote: So the demand is looking good in the metal side. We are also seeing strong demand arising in FMCG, industrial chemicals, as well as MSMEs. So the demand is very strong right now, sir. And region-wise, I see that the demand in East is quite large. We see demand picking up in the South cluster also for us.

items.statement: Domestic loading affected by heavy rains in North India and Gujarat in H1; EXIM impacted by Red Sea disruption and erratic vessel schedules
items.quote: You will see that the domestic loading has been affected this year due to very heavy rains, especially in North India and Gujarat in the first half. But now the demand is picking up from this month. We are seeing very good growth. And North India and Gujarat, sir, remain major, you know, origin of loading, as you would appreciate. So that is what has been there. At the same time, sir, the internat

items.quote: An important milestone that we have achieved in this quarter is that we have secured an order from Tata Steel for their Joda sponge iron plant in which we are going to be doing their entire first mile and handling operations at their site, which is an order in excess of INR40 crores. This is going to be for both loose and bagged DRI, which is Direct Reduced Iron, which is DRI and sponge iron. This

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA grew 10.15% to INR716 million; margin improved 53 bps to 8.38% from 7.86% led by cost optimization
items.quote: EBITDA has grown quite handsomely by 10.15% to INR716 million in H1 FY25 as compared to INR650 million in H1 FY24. EBITDA margins, like I said, have improved 53 basis points to 8.38% from 7.86% in H1 FY24. This is led by cost optimization, like I said.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin improved 50 bps to 8.38% from 7.88% by reducing redundancies like detention and damage
items.quote: EBITDA margins have also improved by 50 basis points to 8.38% compared to 7.88% in Q2 of FY24. The improvement in margins is two various factors, the most important being optimization of our operations and ensuring that we reduce redundancies like detention and damage.

items.statement: Large contracts on DPVC basis (diesel price variation cost) and rail haulage pass-through; limited pricing power with large customers, more with MSMEs
items.quote: So fuel costs, what happens? I want to tell you that most of the fuel costs of all our large contracts, most of them are on a DPVC basis. DPVC is diesel price variation cost. So if the diesel price goes up, my rates will go up. And this is part of our contracting with our customers. And if the price goes down, similarly, they get the benefit. So now what has happened, sir, it's not been a very lar

items.statement: Top 5 client groups contribute ~70% revenue; key clients include Vedanta, Hindalco, HUL, Tata Steel, Jindal Stainless, PSUs, FMCG, industrial chemicals, MSMEs
items.quote: From the top five clients, ma'am, if we include all the companies, so say for example, when I say Tata Steel, I work with several of their units, right? So the five top groups, I would say, not the five top companies, would be about 70% of revenue for us.

items.statement: 80% revenue from customers with 3+ year relationships; 1,647 unique customers in FY24
items.quote: Today as we speak, about 80% of our revenues have been generated for customers who have been doing business with us for over 3 years and beyond. I'm happy to share that because of our expertise, our deep experience, and a very large bouquet of service offerings, we have been able to steadily diversify catering to customers across all industry sectors, including metals, pharma, FMCG, etc.

items.statement: Receivables increased post-COVID from 15 to 120 days; new complex supply chain projects and payment delays keep cycles high; improvement expected in 3-4 quarters
items.quote: So, sir, working capital cycles actually started increasing from the time of Corona, sir. We had customers before Corona who used to pay us within 15 days of dispatch and those same customers during Corona went up to 120 days post-dispatch, sir. This was, I would say, a pan-industry problem. That number has now started dipping for the industry. Our numbers have not dipped as much primarily because

items.statement: Working capital days expected to reduce in next 3-4 quarters, especially in MSME segment
items.quote: No, for sure, this is going to improve, sir. And the improvements, not across the company, but across several sectors, we are already seeing the improvements, especially in MSME businesses. We are seeing that our payment cycles have now started dropping very quickly. And we are hopeful that in the next three or four quarters, we will be able to see a good reduction in the number of the cycles, wor

items.statement: Borrowings doubled in 2 years due to INR67-68 cr capex for specialized containers and increased client payment terms; INR225 cr working capital borrowings; INR163.5 cr repaid from IPO proceeds
items.quote: So, ma'am, there are basically two major reasons for that. One is that we have done a capex of around INR67 crores, INR68 crores in the last two years in buying specialized containers that are not available in the market, which are customized for our customers. So, the capex is about INR67 crores, INR68 crores. And the second is increase in payment terms of clients, which is basically new clients

items.statement: Majority of borrowings (~INR225 cr) are working capital; asset-backed borrowings generating cash flows for EMI repayment; INR163.5 cr working capital debt cleared from IPO proceeds
items.quote: Majority of the borrowings, around INR225 odd crores, are related to working capital. Balance are against purchase of assets such as vehicles and containers. Such assets, basically the capex that we have done, are generating enough cash flows for us to repay their EMIs. Hence there is not much stress on the company's books in repayment of either of its debt. We also cleared out a large chunk of ou

items.statement: INR67-68 cr capex in last 2 years for specialized containers customized for customers
items.quote: One is that we have done a capex of around INR67 crores, INR68 crores in the last two years in buying specialized containers that are not available in the market, which are customized for our customers. So, the capex is about INR67 crores, INR68 crores.

items.statement: Asset-light model: 80-85% volumes from non-owned assets; only critical assets owned (commercial vehicles, reach stackers, forklifts); 50-55 branches Pan-India
items.quote: So, my business, from my owned assets would be a fraction of my total business. Though we don't salami slice our financials in the way that you are asking. But I would say that maybe 80%, 85% of my volumes would come from non-owned assets.

items.statement: Utilisation picks up in H2 post-monsoon; no exact utilisation tracking as assets deployed in complex supply chains
items.quote: So the utilisation rate is now picking up post the monsoon, sir. And we don't really track an exact number for the utilisation of our assets because our assets are all deployed in complex supply Western Carriers ( chains, sir. So we don't really salami slice our numbers in that way. But the utilisation of assets usually sees a much larger pickup in H2 for us always

items.statement: No foreign currency exposure; ~100% contracts in INR; H1 FY25: ~39,500 domestic containers, ~65,000 EXIM containers
items.quote: No, ma'am. All our contracts, almost 100% of them are in INR. And so we get paid in INR and we are not having any sort of foreign currency fluctuations at all, ma'am.

items.quote: The H1 containers that we've done is 1,03,816 containers compared to 1,02,764 in H1 of last year. In absolute terms, this is a growth of over 1,000 containers and most of this growth is coming from the domestic side of the business where we've seen a large growth.

items.statement: H1 FY25 revenue INR854 cr (+3.23% YoY); EBITDA INR716 mn (+10.15%); PAT INR378.56 mn (+5.77%); debt-to-equity 0.34%; RoE 6.13%; RoCE 7.36%
items.quote: So if you look at the console financial performance highlights for the first half of FY25, we see that despite there being very strong headwinds, especially in the EXIM trade in our country, we have still managed to grow our operations by 3.23% to over INR854 crores compared to INR827 crores in H1 of FY24. items.statement: Focus on FTL (full container loads); minimal LCL (less than container load) business; multimodal rail-road combination dominant
items.quote: So our main focus remains in the FTL business, sir, where we do full container loads only primarily. We do offhand, very small amounts of less than container loads, but our focus remains on full container loads.

items.statement: Likely largest business associate and AP for CONCOR; CONCOR payment cycle 24 hours vs monthly/quarterly billing for Western Carriers
items.quote: I don't recollect the exact percentage, sir, but I am probably their largest business associate and AP, sir. This is my gut feel.

items.statement: Expects defense revenue to grow 40-50% YoY in FY25 and substantial growth continuing next year
items.quote: Last year, we did about 1,300 crores. So, we have said that we will have close to 40% to 50% growth this year. We are hoping that we are able to keep a substantial level of growth even going forward next year.

items.statement: EV vertical expected to reach EBITDA break-even in next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: I will expect the EV vertical to be EBITDA break-even in the next two to three quarters.

items.statement: ATAGS order expected to be received by end of FY25 with revenue contribution from Q1 FY26
items.quote: So, everything you said before Q1 '26 is directionally correct. There is a process. First, the order has to get, there is a negotiation process, then you get the order, contracting is done, then you have to do FOPM supplies and then you have to start bulk supplies once the FOPM is approved.

items.statement: Executable defense order book stands at Rs 5,900 crore as of 30 September, excluding potential domestic/export orders
items.quote: And with order wins of almost Rs. 1,400 crores in H1, the executable order book as on 30th September now stands at about Rs. 5,900 crores. This order book does not include any potential orders from the domestic or export market.

items.statement: Total defense order pipeline close to Rs 6,000 crore including signed and potential orders
items.quote: It is still being delivered and we have also got, as I mentioned, we have a total order book which is already signed of 6,000 crores.

items.statement: Won Rs 2,200 crore new orders in H1 across segments, dominated by defense Rs 1,400 crore and aerospace ~Rs 300 crore
items.quote: And during the same period, across the segments, we won orders of Rs. 2,200 crores, largely dominated by defense of almost Rs. 1,400 crores, followed by JSA, aerospace and the traditional business.

items.statement: US aluminum second phase CAPEX nearly complete (~$8-10M remaining), will double capacity and go live next year
items.quote: There is not much CAPEX left in the subsidiaries. This was for our second phase in the U.S. There is hardly anything left there. Maybe about $8-10 million. The rest of it was all in India. And I think in the second half, in India, we have about significantly lower CAPEX. So, we will just have the maintenance CAPEX.

items.statement: India CAPEX in H2 FY25 will be significantly lower, mainly maintenance CAPEX
items.quote: And I think in the second half, in India, we have about significantly lower CAPEX. So, we will just have the maintenance CAPEX.

items.statement: US aluminum second phase will double capacity, operational next year
items.quote: It will double the capacity. It will come out live only next year.

items.statement: European operations expected to reach target margins in 1-2 quarters; aluminum improvements visible next year; steel side facing demand issues
items.quote: I think we are about a quarter or two away from getting to that level in Europe. On the aluminum side, we have made a lot of good progress, and I think from next year, we will have a much better situation. On the steel side, we have issues on demand and therefore we are doing a lot of work on the cost side.

items.statement: Europe demand challenging with monthly projections only; expects improvement next year; India CV market expected to improve in 1-2 quarters as government spending picks up
items.quote: We are not hearing anything from customers on a long -term basis. The projections come on a monthly basis, and that's really all. Everybody is saying that things are going to get better next month, next year. So , I think next year, re alistically I think next year things will probably

items.statement: US market strong and expected to remain strong next year
items.quote: America is strong and we expect it to remain strong next year as well.

items.statement: Aerospace order wins of ~Rs 300 crore in H1 exceed full year FY24 revenue of Rs 240 crore; expects aerospace to become multiple times current size
items.quote: Almost 300 crores of that is aerospace. Put that into context, last year our aerospace business was 240 crores. So, it's more than the entire business we did last year. And this is an annualized kind of business that we will do going forward once it fully ramps up. So, we expect to see the aerospace business grow quite substantially and become multiple times the size of its business that it is now

items.statement: Added three new customers in component business in H1 FY25
items.quote: And, sorry, I forgot to mention that we have added three new customers in the first half of this year in the component business.

items.statement: Seeing tremendous momentum from China Plus One and substantially increased interest from US customers post-elections
items.quote: We see multiple new customers and we also see tremendous momentum of China Plus One and movement from other parts of the world into India, and increased interest, substantially increased interest of U.S. customers, especially after the elections.

items.statement: Standalone gross debt-to-equity at 0.46x and net at 0.24x; cash on books ~Rs 2,000 crore; leverage continues to decline
items.quote: Our leverage continues to go down while we repay our debt with our gross debt-to-equity ratio now at 0.46x and 0.24x on a net basis. A stronger balance sheet and cash on books of almost Rs. 2,000 crore put us in an enviable position to tap newer opportunities as they arise, both at organic and inorganic front.

items.statement: Actively pursuing M&A opportunities in India that are synergistic, complementary, enable components-to-systems transition, new products/sectors/geographies, and expand Make in India strategy
items.quote: In terms of M&A opportunities there are plenty of opportunities, but we are looking at opportunities which are synergistic, which are complementary and where we can significantly add value and go from components to systems, get into new products, new sectors, new geographies and also where we can expand the Make in India strategy that we have. So, we will pursue this opportunity, but please rememb

items.statement: Standalone ROCE net of cash improved to 20.5% from 20% YoY
items.quote: The return ratios continue to inch higher with ROCE net of cash at 20.5% from last year of 20%.

items.statement: Consolidated ROCE ~18% as of September 2024
items.quote: The consolidated balance sheet continues to remain robust with ROC E of about 18% as of September 2024, and the ba lance sheet continues to remain strong with ROC E and RONW improving amidst the strong liquidity position.

items.statement: US tariff policy uncertainty; will react once concrete policy announced; believes India well positioned to benefit
items.quote: You know, first, everybody, there is a lot of speculation about it. So, first, let the guy come into the White House. Let him make in concrete what is it that is going to happen. Then we will have to react. But the point is, I think that India is going to be in a good position.

items.statement: European and Swedish operations being downsized; committed to fixing in short period
items.quote: We are feeling some pain in our European and Swedish operations. We are downsizing these operations. And we have committed that we will fix these businesses in a short period of time, and that is what we are working on.

items.statement: Defense business lumpy quarterly; should be viewed on 3-5 year horizon and annual basis
items.quote: It is important to understand that new orders will take time to convert into revenues and may create lumpiness in quarterly performance while the business remains on the strong fundamental when dealing with the 3-to-5-year horizon.

items.statement: Domestic defense revenue expected to grow faster than exports from next year; domestic to become 30-40% of overall defense business
items.quote: I would expect our revenues in India from next year to grow at a faster rate than the revenues from export simply because we are starting from a smaller base, and eventually I think domestic will become 30% to 40% over our overall business.

items.statement: Naval systems (10-15% of defense revenue) and unmanned systems identified as key domestic growth areas for next 12-24 months
items.quote: So, the naval system right now is all domestic. And what I am saying is that is the business that will grow, first domestically and then globally.

items.statement: Management expects revenue to increase commensurately with capacity utilization improvement, subject to market realizations, but declines to give formal guidance.
items.quote: I would not like to give a formal guidance as such, but as our strive is to improve the capacity utilization if that sort of and we are aspiring and expecting that to improve. So, we're definitely going forward assuming that the sales realizations are range bound. We can expect a commensurate increase in the overall scenario, subject to improvement in capacity utilization.

items.statement: Stainless steel capacity utilization currently 55-60%; technical target is 90% achievable with existing infrastructure.
items.quote: As I just said, the capacity utilization for my stainless-steel operations currently is about 55% to 60%. This is keeping aside the TMT bar facility that we have, which we are not focusing on right now, the mild steel TMT. So, with the plant, almost all of our revenue today is coming in from stainless steel operations.

items.statement: Forward integration project for downstream stainless products capped at INR 50 crores, to be done in phases within existing premises.
items.quote: We have capped our capex plans for it to the extent of INR50 crores because that's the plan so far. We want to do it in phases. We want to do it in a manner that whatever is implemented is running at a decent capacity.

items.statement: Plan to launch stainless steel TMT bars (400 series) in retail segment by Q4 FY25, shifting from B2B to B2C; also pursuing downstream wire and bar products.
items.quote: We are awaiting a few approvals to come in and then I expect the approvals to come in soon. And hopefully in the last quarter, we are expecting to launch the SS TMT bars. That is what we plan to do.

items.statement: Stainless steel TMT bar realization around INR 90,000 per ton; current stainless sales realizations INR 90,000-95,000 per ton.
items.quote: The realization there are approximately that the present prices are in the close – in the range of around INR90,000 per ton, but this will obviously depend upon the prices being offered by other customers – sorry, the other suppliers and also the input costs, but yes they are in the range of around INR90,000 per ton currently.

items.statement: Historical EBITDA margin range 4-6%; expects 200 bps improvement in better scenario; H1 FY25 EBITDA margin 4.46%.
items.quote: If you look at the numbers for the last 3 years we have been able to consistently operate at an EBITDA level of range bound at about 4.5% to 5.5% to 6%. So, that is what is the broad range that we have been able to achieve. And going forward, our endeavour will be to sort of drive the margins further by increasing the capacity utilization and improvising a product mix.

items.statement: Cost optimization project enables direct charging of billets to wire rods, eliminating reheating, reducing fuel consumption and carbon footprint; power consumption increases slightly.
items.quote: We probably - we're definitely the first in India and the very few globally to be able to achieve direct charging of stainless-steel billets to wire rods, thereby eliminating an entire process of reheating the stainless-steel billets. So, what that helps us to do is that it helps us to reasonably, substantially reduce the fuel consumption because there is a fuel component which goes into reheating

items.statement: Stainless steel demand growing due to infrastructure push, solar, defence, auto, and replacement of carbon steel; Q3/Q4 traditionally stronger post-monsoon.
items.quote: It is with the impetus of the government and infrastructure and with the new avenues which are opening up, let's say from the solar industry, from the defence industry, from automobile. Stainless is a growing market. I believe that stainless steel's growth with the per capita consumption that we have in the country, there is a large distance to cover.

items.statement: Stainless TMT bar competitors include Sunflag, Shyam Metalics, Jindal Stainless; management sees room for multiple players.
items.quote: To name a few, I mean, from what I understand, Sunflag, which is a listed company, then there is Shyam Metalics also doing it out of the recently acquired plant which they did in Indore. Jindal Stainless is also supplying and we welcome. Rathi Steel and Power Ltd. Q2 and H1 FY 25 Earnings Conference Call November 18, 2024 I mean, the more the suppliers, the more we feel the ecosystem will grow and

items.statement: Stainless business currently almost entirely B2B via distributors and direct sales; no exclusive agreements; plans to enter B2C via TMT bars and downstream products.
items.quote: No, right now, for my stainless business, which is driving a majority of the revenues, it is almost entirely B2B currently. I mean, of course, B2B the end product being sold as B2B, it may be channelized through distributors and traders, but the end user is a B2B user currently, but going forward, the other products will help us enter into B2C segments also.

items.statement: Became zero-debt in March 2024; re-initiated banking with Kotak Mahindra Bank for need-based working capital and small term loan.
items.quote: We became a zero-debt company as on March from a banking debt perspective in March 2024, but steel being a capital-intensive industry, particularly to do with working capital, we took a conscious call or a prudent call to enter back into banking relationships because of the legacy issues, it was important to rebuild the banking relationships. So, we have availed need-based facilities from Kotak Ma

items.statement: Completed INR 114 crore preferential allotment in February 2024 at INR 32.25 (non-promoters) and INR 55 (promoter preference share conversion).
items.quote: We had also successfully completed a fundraise of almost INR114 crores through a preferential allotment sometime in the month of February 2024, which also enabled us to reduce the debt and build up working capital and need-based capex plans for increasing our growth plans going forward.

items.statement: Government mandating stainless steel TMT bars for coastal NHAI bridges and railway bridges; quality standards specify 400 series grade.
items.quote: Basically, right now there are various government announcements which have come up wherein they are encouraging or rather there are directions by the government to make the use of stainless-steel TMT bars mandatory along the coastal area which is more prone to basically corrosion. They have directed NHAI to use TMT bars across all the bridges and anything which is made over water in the coastal ar

items.statement: Chinese and Southeast Asian steel imports pressuring domestic industry; industry lobbying for government trade measures.
items.quote: There has been a lot of inflow of steel coming in from China and Southeast Asia. We the government, the industry lobby has been representing the matter to the government and we expect some measures to be taken, to be announced by the government also.

items.statement: Exceptional gain of INR 4.71 crore from UP government electricity duty refund for FY23.
items.quote: There is a UP government policy regarding electricity duty exemption, for which we are eligible to. And by virtue of that, they have refunded us approximately INR4.71 crores for the electricity duty for the period pertaining to 2022-23.

items.statement: Promoters converted redeemable preference shares to equity at INR 55; 88 lakh preference shares outstanding with redemption extended to 2034-35.

It's about 88 lakhs shares which are pending to be sort of redeemed and the mat

items.statement: SeQuent API quarterly run rate expected at INR85-95 crores steady state
items.quote: I think we are right now looking, as we had indicated earlier that between an INR85 crores to INR95 crore run rate is what should be a sort of steady state for us.

items.statement: SeQuent PAT expected to accelerate from FY26 as EBITDA growth flows through
items.quote: And therefore, FY '26 is where most of the incremental SeQuent Scientific Limited November 14, 2024 growth, which would come into margin and EBITDA would flow through straight into the PAT

items.statement: SeQuent Q2 gross margin improved 190 bps to 47%; H1 improved 265 bps to 46%
items.quote: We are pleased to report an improvement in our gross margins, which increased by 190 basis points in Q2 rising from 45.1% to 47%.

items.statement: SeQuent Q2 EBITDA margin pre-ESOP improved 452 bps to 12.1%; H1 improved 700 bps to 12.3%
items.quote: EBITDA margins pre -ESOP, which increased by 452 basis points in Q2 from 7.6% in Q2 financial year '24 to 12.1% in Q2 financial year '25.

items.statement: Viyash Q2 EBITDA margin 17.3% up ~3% YoY; H1 17.2% up 3.3% YoY
items.quote: Viyash had EBITDA margins of 73% with an improvement of almost 3% year-on-year.

items.statement: Combined entity Q2 EBITDA margin 14.7% up 380 bps YoY; H1 14.6% up 510 bps YoY
items.quote: The combined business had an EBITDA of INR108 crores with 14.7% margins with 380 basis points improvement year-on-year.

items.statement: Formulations grew double digits overall and in most geographies; Europe distribution strong; India formulations strong double-digit growth
items.quote: Our formulations business, which is spread over many countries has had a good quarter and a good first half for the fiscal year, growing in double digits overall and in most geographies.

items.statement: Turkey currency stable, government actions predictable; accelerating product launches and price increases
items.quote: We are seeing a more predictable and steady currency scenario in Turkey, and the government actions are also more calibrated and predictable.

items.statement: Brazil business growing after portfolio refresh and LatAm expansion
items.quote: Our business in Brazil, which has seen flat to declining performance last year has begun growing this quarter as we refreshed the product portfolio and expanded to other LatAm markets.

items.statement: Viyash filed 19 products globally in H1 (17 API, 2 FDF); launched 2 products; 25 products in pipeline, 9 validations completed
items.quote: First half, we are able to do 19 products globally. Of course, 17 are API and 2 FDFs we filed all over the world, start from U.S., Europe, China, everywhere in the world.

items.statement: Viyash validated and supplied validation quantities for 2 innovator products (1 API, 1 intermediate) for lifecycle management
items.quote: We are able to develop 2 more innovative business -- and after struggling last 2, 2.5 years hard work, now we are able to validate and supply validation quantities for 2 innovators.

items.statement: Viyash received 6 regulatory approvals in H1 (2 US, 3 Europe, 1 China); 2 clean EIRs from US FDA
items.quote: And first half of FY '25, we have received 6 regulatory approvals, 2 in U.S. and 3 in Europe. These are a mix of both FDA as well as a couple of CEPs.

items.statement: Viyash low capex due to existing strong infrastructure and free capacity
items.quote: As we mentioned earlier also, we have actually strong infrastructure in manufacturing and also we have some free capacity. That's how we were able to reduce capex.

items.statement: Merger brings 5x capacity increase and 10 more US FDA-approved sites
items.quote: The combined business will have, as Rajaram mentioned earlier, it's 6x larger R&D time, R&D team is almost 200 people in Viyash and 5x more capacity and 10 more U.S. FDA -approved sites.

items.statement: Viyash oncology facility refurbished and requalified this quarter; validations starting; 2 modules ready
items.quote: Oncology, one facility, we mostly used to do for contract manufacturing, one of the big companies. But other facility, we refurbished and requalified this quarter.

items.statement: SeQuent implementing targeted price increases across geographies; beginning to get price increases in Europe inflationary environment
items.quote: We are expanding phyto -solutions range to more markets and have also introduced new products for companion animals. There has been strong growth in Europe, especially in our distribution business, and we are beginning to slowly get price increases in an inflationary environment.

items.statement: SeQuent reduced operating expense 1% YoY in Q2 and H1 despite inflationary pressures
items.quote: Cost optimization, in line with our focus on improving operational efficiency, successfully reduced operating expense despite facing inflationary pressures across geographies. We achieved a 1% year -on-year reduction in our operating expense for both Q2 and H1, respectively.

items.statement: SeQuent working capital rose to INR425 million from INR4,201 million to support Turkey and Spain growth; inventory up short term
items.quote: On the balance sheet, we saw a very modest increase in working capital, which rose to INR425 million, up from INR4,201 million as of 31st March '24. This increase reflects a strategic decision to support the planned growth in our Turkey and Spain business, resulting in inventory levels for short term.

items.statement: SeQuent net debt/EBITDA improved to 2.3x from 3.55x; net debt INR3,774 million slight decrease from INR3,378 million
items.quote: In terms of leverage, our net debt -to-EBITDA ratio improved to 2.3x as on 30th September '24, compared to 3.55x as of 31st March '24. On an absolute basis, our net debt stood at INR3,774 million, a slight decrease from INR3,378 million as of 31st March '24.

items.statement: Combined entity net debt/EBITDA 1.4x and improving continuously
items.quote: So the combined net debt today, net debt -to-EBITDA ratio is 1.4x, and it's going to improve continuously.

items.statement: Merger scheme approved by Board 26 Sep 2024; filed with BSE 16 Oct, NSE 17 Oct; registered office relocation to Hyderabad started
items.quote: Board of -- Board approved the scheme on 26th September 2024. BSE filing of the scheme was done on 16th October '24, and the scheme has got listed on the BSE website. NSE filing of the scheme was done on 17th October '24, and the same is listed on NSE website.

items.statement: Merger expected to complete in 12-15 months; synergies in manufacturing, sales, R&D, indirect costs being worked on
items.quote: We expect this maybe next 12 months -- 12 to 15 months, as I explained earlier, I think it's on track.

items.statement: Open to acquisitions in animal health, companion animal, capability deepening; disciplined approach
items.quote: We are looking for growth in certain specific areas in animal health. We are looking at opportunities to deepen our capabilities. And also in terms of the entire companion animal area is the place where we would be open to taking any acquisitions.

items.statement: Viyash top 10 APIs contribute 62% of API revenue; 6 products global leaders with 50%+ market share; top 10 grew 20%+ CAGR last 2 years
items.quote: Our top 10 products contributes almost 62% of our API revenue. And this is mainly because of our products are either innovative based or a little bit complex. And also, we are able to maintain sustainable growth because of fully backward integrated and complex products.

items.statement: Viyash generated INR100 crores free cash flow in H1 driven by working capital optimization and low capex
items.quote: And we also generated INR100 crores of free cash flow. I think this is a big achievement for this year, mainly driven by optimization in working capital and also low capex.

items.statement: BIOSECURE Act Senate approval pending; Trump administration may aid passage but official approval uncertain
items.quote: I don't see the current update, but what I heard actually is still it has to be approved in one house. Since now Trump coming in, everybody is expected that it is going to approve in other house also soon.

items.statement: Viyash R&D team ~175 people in API R&D; capable of INR10-12 crores annual spend; global experienced team avg 20-25 years experience
items.quote: And of course, R&D, we have strong R&D around 175 people in AP R&D. They are capable to do at least INR10 crores, INR12 crores in a year.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 utilization: Spinning 99%, Sheeting 61%, Terry Towel 67%
items.quote: During the quarter, our utilization levels at our manufacturing facilities stood at 99% in Spinning division, 61% in Sheeting and 67% in Terry Towel divisions as you have seen.

items.statement: Recalibration initiatives to impact revenue for another 4 to 6 months
items.quote: Our recalibration initiatives are likely to impact us for another 4 to 6 months is what we estimate at this point.

items.statement: Stable demand environment currently
items.quote: We continue to see a stable demand environment at this point.

items.statement: India revenue target ~INR1,000 crores over 5 years
items.quote: We have shared with investors earlier that we are looking to grow India to approximately INR1,000 crores market over a 5-year period, and we continue to feel optimistic about the market.

items.statement: Completed INR400 crores QIP with marquee investors
items.quote: We are pleased to inform investors that during the quarter, we've completed successfully QIP offering. The same was a INR400 crores issue, which we successfully closed and have got some marquee investors on board.

items.statement: Net debt INR2,679 crores at Sep 30; QIP proceeds to substantially reduce term debt in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Our net debt at the end of the quarter ended September 30 th, was range bound and stood at INR2,679 crores versus INR2,671 crores at the end of June. There's not been any change on the debt front because the QIP was an event that occurred after the date of September 30 th, but we will deliver substantially using the proceeds of the QIP during the third quarter of this fiscal

items.statement: Revenue range-bound next quarter; major capex cycle behind; focus on balance sheet and utilization
items.quote: I think it will be range bound is what I estimate, Chandan ji. But again, directionally, we should see the uptick going forward. Our major capex cycle is behind us. And our 2 areas of focus now is delivering our balance sheet and enhancing our utilization levels, and those will be our only two primary areas of focus.

items.statement: India revenues grew significantly in H1 FY25 vs H1 FY24; optimistic on India growth
items.quote: We continue to make progress with our India businesses during the quarter. Our revenues from India have seen significant improvements during the first half of this fiscal versus the first half of the last fiscal.

items.statement: India revenue ~INR100 crores in FY25; INR300-400 crores in 2 years
items.quote: And as far as fiscal '25 is concerned, we should see revenues from this jurisdiction stand at between roughly just under INR100 crores.

items.statement: India revenue target INR300-400 crores in 2 years
items.quote: So I think that over the next -- if I take a 2 -year period as far as India is concerned, we think that India should grow to close to INR300 crores to INR400 crores over the next 2-year period from virtually a sub INR50 crore level or a sub INR25 crore level in FY '24.

items.statement: Export outlook buoyant; capacities and infrastructure available; U.S. sourcing interest continues but EU, UK, Middle East, India, Far East to lead growth
items.quote: outlook on exports and the domestic market, as I said earlier, we remain optimistic on enhancing our market share and enhancing our utilization levels as a result of that. We have been seeing some short term -- or we've been seeing some movements which -- headwinds, which have kept our utilization levels a little subdued for reasons I've outlined earlier. But this is purely transactional in nature

items.statement: Working capital cycles expanded post-COVID; priority to rein them in
items.quote: FY '25? Shrikant Himatsingka: Yes. As we have indicated to investors earlier, we are sort of working to recalibrate this as well. This is something that typically Himatsingka has a fairly lean cycle post -COVID and some of these challenges that we have gone through. Our NWC cycles have seen some expansion, and we are working on reining that in

items.statement: Branded revenue ~30% of mix (down from 40-50% two years ago); margin-neutral churn
items.quote: In context to your other question in terms of how much is our revenue stream from brands, it's approximately -- it hovers between approximately 30% thereabouts at this stage of our revenue mix vis-a-vis private label.

items.statement: EBITDA margin range 18-22%; currently swimming in 18-20% band
items.quote: I want to share with investors that our margins can move between 18% and 22%. So it's possible on account of product mix. It's possible on account of inflationary pressures. It's -- so it could move in that framework. I don't see anything specific precipitating at this point vis -a-vis us. But between quarters, it could move in this broad band, yes.

items.statement: Terry Towel debottlenecking underway; utilization to rise substantially after product mix shifts
items.quote: So the Terry division, we are working on debottlenecking of certain specs in our plant, which is currently underway. It is because of this reason that the utilization levels are range bound at this point. But once we see that ease out because of product mix shifts in our plant, we should see Terry utilizations go up substantially. We are seeing reasonably strong demand in that vertical.

items.statement: Full capacity revenue potential ~INR4,000 crores; target run rate in 18-24 months
items.quote: I've shared with investors earlier that at full capacity, our revenue potential is in the region of INR4,000 crores, and we will be working in the medium term to head in that direction.

items.statement: Target full capacity run rate in 18-24 months
items.quote: Yes. We are looking to hit that run rate in 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: QIP proceeds to reduce term debt; internal initiatives to cut another ~INR200 crores term debt
items.quote: Ranvir, so a substantial part of the QIP proceeds will be used to reduce our term debt, which will reduce our repayments substantially over the next close to, I would say, 16 to 18 months. items.statement: Ibuprofen global demand low but expected to increase soon; domestic prices bottomed out at $9-9.25/kg, export prices >$10/kg

items.statement: Non-ibu export share increased from ~10% to ~24% of non-ibu revenue over past year; target 50% export realization from non-ibu within 2-3 years
items.quote: Non-ibu segment, our target is around 50% export collection from non-ibu segment within upcoming 2 to 3 years which is presently around 23 to 24%.

items.quote: The export for 2nd Quarter of the Financial Year 2025 was Rs. 140 crore as compared to Rs. 130 crore in the corresponding period of the last year whereas it was Rs. 150 crore in the previous quarter ended June '24.

items.statement: Non-ibu exports growing in regulated European markets; US FDA inspection expected soon for facilities linked to ANDAs for Ibuprofen, Metformin, Fenofibrate
items.quote: Yes, we have regularly started exporting for our non-Ibu segment. Earlier, one year back, it was only 10% of the revenue for non-Ibu. Now, it is around 24%.

items.statement: US FDA inspection pending; they intimate 2-3 days in advance; management expects inspection soon for facilities with filed ANDAs

items.statement: Chinese approval for Metformin obtained to attract global players in China seeking alternative suppliers
items.quote: Chinese approval helps the global players in China to procure the Metformin from India. This will help us attract the global players to create the alternative to China as well.

items.statement: SI Group closing US ibuprofen facility by March 2025 due to high costs and old technology; capacity was small, not expected to materially impact IOL
items.quote: They have officially declared and informed to SEC US that they are going to close their Ibu manufacturing facilitie due to high cost of production and some old technology and they have targeted to close by March '25.

items.statement: SMS Pharma (Hyderabad) adding 12,000 ton ibuprofen capacity; IOL cites 100% backward integration as competitive strength mitigating location disadvantage
items.quote: One company based out of Hyderabad, SMS Pharmaceutical Limited. T hey have announced that around 2 two years back, we are coming with the capacity of around 12,000

items.statement: Acetic acid prices stable last 1-2 quarters; Ethyl acetate prices stable with delta maintained
items.quote: The prices of acetic acid has been stable since the last 1-2 quarters. In the last quarter, we had some inventory. Ethyl acetate prices are also stable and Delta is being maintained between the two.

items.statement: Ibuprofen domestic prices ~$9-9.25/kg, export prices >$10/kg; prices corrected from last quarter
items.quote: Export prices are more than 10 dollar. Domestic prices are around 9 to 9.25 dollar.

items.statement: Inventory markdown from lower raw material prices (acetic acid, etc. bought 2 quarters ago) and finished goods valuation at lower prices impacted Q2 FY25 net profit
items.quote: Like in the price, when the prices are coming down, the closing inventory is also valued at the lower value. So, there is little bit difference in valuation aspect also, that added to fall in the net profit also. Same is the little bit of higher cost of inventory, which we have brought around two-quarter ago from China, which, like acetic acid and other, that also part of this decline in some bott

items.statement: Consolidated cash and bank balance Rs 157 crore as of 30 Sept 2024
items.quote: The consolidated cash and bank balance stood at Rs. 157 crore as on 30th September 2024.

items.statement: No CEO appointment timeline; MD and Joint MD positions filled, CEO not mandatory
items.quote: We are looking into it and we are finalizing. We cannot comment that how much time it is going to take. Whenever any candidate is finalized, we will be coming out with the announcement.

items.statement: 15 DMFs filed; 3 ANDAs filed by customers for Ibuprofen, Metformin, Fenofibrate awaiting US FDA site inspection
items.quote: ANDA is filed against 3 US FDA approvals for Ibuprofen, Metformin, and Fenofibrate. Whenever they will come, they will approve these sites and they will also mention in their report other facilities also working therein.

items.statement: Management acknowledges inability to meet past guidance due to market volatility; quantitative production targets for 2030 on track but selling prices and raw material costs unpredictable
items.quote: As regards our discussion for 2030, as regards to our production, our quantitative figures, we are near to our projection which we have internally discussed and tried to achieve by 2030 and we are in line with all factors as regards to our internal production. But we cannot predict the exact selling price or there may be volatility in the raw material prices.

name: S H Kelkar and Company Ltd

items.statement: Full-year revenue expected around Rs 2,100 crore, implying ~14% growth, subject to no major changes
items.quote: I would expect to reach around 2,100 or something like this number, 14% odd for the full year. This is a subject that no major changes happen between now and the end of the year.

items.statement: H2 revenue expected to be better than H1; full-year growth well in excess of 12% mid-term CAGR target
items.quote: Expect our sales to be better than 12% for the full year. Whether it is 15% in the second half, a little bit more or less, in the full-year basis we will be well in excess of our 12% target.

items.statement: H2 EBITDA margin expected similar to H1 adjusted 16.8%, slightly better, with recurring Rs 20-22 crore cost for new Creative Centres
items.quote: I expect it to be in the same range, slightly better.

items.statement: Gross margin expectation for H2 remains around 40-45% as reported in H1, but raw material shortages may necessitate price adjustments
items.quote: our gross margin expectation is still around the 40%-45% that we have reported for the first half. However, there are some raw materials where acute shortages are expected in the 4th Quarter or 1st Quarter of next year.

items.statement: European EBITDA margin 20.5% vs 21% last year; gross margin improved 350 bps but EBITDA margin down 70 bps due to smaller batch sizes from new clients
items.quote: This is purely a product mix issue. When you look at the gross margin, you look at the product level. But when we have smaller batches, then our net margin is the same.

items.statement: Global MNC account execution secured for FY25 and well underway, trending as expected with potential to expand partnership
items.quote: On the global account, we are trending as expected. So, we are on track.

items.statement: H2 FY25 capex ~Rs 50 crore; H1 FY26 another ~Rs 50 crore; ~Rs 100 crore for Vashivali reinstatement; incremental capex after insurance ~Rs 60 crore
items.quote: So, I think in the second half, we would have roughly around Rs. 50 crore and the first half next year, another Rs. 50 crore of CAPEX, out of which almost Rs. 100 odd crore would be the reinstatement of the Vashivali factory itself.

items.statement: Current utilization >85%; Vanavate and Vashivali rebuild to add 2x capacity in India; one new European factory to add ~50% capacity
items.quote: So, right now, we are at more than 85% utilization of our facilities. With the rebuilding of the Vashivali and Vanavate factory, we will add almost 2x addi tional capacity. So, that is on the domestic. And we are proposing to add one more factory which would give us roughly 50% additional capacity in the European context

items.statement: Vanavate factory expected Q4 FY25 (Q1 calendar 2025); Vashivali rebuild 9-10 months after; Mulund closure post-Vashivali
items.quote: So, the new factory in Vanavate is expected to come up in the 1st Quarter calendar next year, so 4th Quarter. Vashivali which is the rebuild of the factory will still take another 9 months to 10 months before it is rebuilt.

items.statement: Acute shortages expected in Q4 FY25/Q1 FY26 for key natural oils (orange, patchouli, vetiver ~15% of purchase basket); dialogue with customers for pass-through by Feb-Mar
items.quote: Specifically products like orange oil, patchouli oil, vetiver oil these are the key components, which is roughly I would say 15% of our purchase basket. These are under threat in terms of availability and pricing as of today.

items.statement: Domestic large FMCG customers soft; strong momentum in small/mid-sized customers and new accounts; global MNC orders driving growth
items.quote: while domestic demand for large customers remains soft, we are encouraged by strong momentum across our small, mid-sized customers and new accounts.

items.statement: European revenues grew 11.5% like-for-like; favourable dynamics from trade-down and consolidation creating vacuum for mid-sized players
items.quote: Strangely not having a very strong economic growth is favo urable for us because we are not the incumbent, we are the challengers. So, when the markets are looking for a value proposition or more private labels or different offerings it helps us to continue our growth

items.statement: Q2 gross margin muted due to ~Rs 25-30 crore lower-margin backlog carried from Q1 fire disruption; H1 gross margin representative of full business
items.quote: So, roughly Rs. 25 crore-Rs. 30 crore of business was carried over to the 2nd Quarter that was at a lower margin. Theref ore, the composite margin of 2nd Quarter is muted

items.statement: Debt expected lower by year-end from operational free cash flow and insurance payouts starting Dec-Jan
items.quote: On the debt piece, I think we expect some amount of money to come in from the insurance between now and end of the year, probably December -January we expect Insurance payout to start to flow in. So, yes, we will have lower debt in the end of the year.

items.statement: Insurance claim filed; inventory payout first, then CAPEX reimbursement on reinstatement basis; substantial payments expected Dec-Jan
items.quote: So, we have filed the claim, it is in the process. Final claims we will get in wit h the insurer any time now. And we expect by December -January substantial payments to start to come in

items.statement: Antitrust investigations against global majors (Givaudan, IFF) in EU/US creating opportunities for mid-sized players like SH Kelkar
items.quote: yes, that does open up opportunities for mid-size and other players like us.

items.statement: Raw material availability/pricing storm horizon for H1 FY26; US administration policy changes from Jan 2025 uncertain impact
items.quote: there is a sort of storm on the horizon and we are just highlighting that this may hit the industry at some point in the first half of next year. items.statement: European revenue growth 11.5% like-for-like; global MNC account scaling as expected; Ingredients division turnaround continuing
items.quote: our core European segment delivered impressive performance this quarter with revenues growing by 11.5% on a like -for-like basis.

items.statement: Creative Development Centres launched in Germany (June 2024) and Manchester (early 2025); recurring Rs 20 crore/year OPEX; revenues to start in 6-8 months
items.quote: Those are all employee and OPEX costs. So, there is a recurring Rs. 20 crore order per annum.

items.statement: Order inflow guidance for FY25 maintained at INR 3,500-4,000 crore
items.quote: Again, I would say the present our guideline still remains at INR3,500 to INR4,000, but that depends on the next 2 months to 3 months how we are working

items.statement: EBITDA margin target maintained at 10% going forward
items.quote: we will try and stick to maintain our EBITDA at 10%.

items.quote: Currently we are at an order book of INR 6,546 Crore

items.quote: INR232 crores approximately

items.quote: overall that order book still remains INR 7,000 +.

items.quote: About INR700 to INR800 crores of projects we are discussing at Shantigram. About INR800 crores projects we are addressing at Adani Airport in Ahmedabad. items.quote: As per the arrangement, Adani Infra to acquire up to 30.07% stake from the founder promoter. Post the open offer for 26%; both the companies will maintain equal equity of the company.
